2.3: and let the king appoint commissioners in all the jurisdictional districts of his realm, and let them collect together all the young women, virgins, beautiful in appearance, at Shu'shan the castle, at the house of the women in charge of Heg'a·i the king's eunuch, the guardian of the women; and let there be a giving of their massages.
2.4: And that young woman who seems pleasing in the king's eyes will be queen instead of Vash'ti. " And the thing was pleasing in the king's eyes, and he proceeded to do that way.
2.5: A certain man, a Jew, happened to be in Shu'shan the castle, and his name was Mor'de·cai the son of Ja'ir the son of Shim'e·i the son of Kish a Ben'ja·min·ite,
2.6: who had been taken into exile from Jerusalem with the deported people who were taken into exile with Jec·o·ni'ah the king of Judah whom Neb·u·chad·nez'zar the king of Babylon took into exile.
2.7: And he came to be the caretaker of Ha·das'sah, that is, Esther, the daughter of his father's brother, for she had neither father nor mother; and the young woman was pretty in form and beautiful in appearance, and at the death of her father and her mother Mor'de·cai took her as his daughter.
2.8: And it came about that, when the king's word and his law were heard, and when many young women were collected together at Shu'shan the castle in charge of Heg'a·i, then Esther was taken to the king's house in charge of Heg'a·i the guardian of the women.
2.9: Now the young woman was pleasing in his eyes, so that she gained loving - kindness before him and he made haste to give her her massages and her appropriate food, and to give her seven selected young women from the king's house, and he proceeded to transfer her and her young women to the best place of the house of the women.
2.10: Esther had not told about her people or about her relatives, for Mor'de·cai himself had laid the command upon her that she should not tell.
2.11: And day after day Mor'de·cai was walking before the courtyard of the house of the women to know of Esther's welfare and what was being done with her.
2.12: And when the turn of each young woman arrived to go in to King A·has·u·e'rus after it had happened to her according to the women's regulation for twelve months, for that was the way the days of their massage procedure were gradually fulfilled, six months with oil of myrrh and six months with balsam oil and with the massages of the women;
2.13: then on these conditions the young woman herself came in to the king. Everything that she would mention would be given her, to come with her from the house of the women to the king's house.
2.14: In the evening she herself came in, and in the morning she herself returned to the second house of the women in charge of Sha·ash'gaz the king's eunuch, the guardian of the concubines. She would not come in anymore to the king unless the king had taken delight in her and she had been called by name.
2.15: And when the turn of Esther the daughter of Ab'i·ha·il the uncle of Mor'de·cai, whom he had taken as his daughter, arrived to come in to the king, she did not request anything except what Heg'a·i the king's eunuch, the guardian of the women, proceeded to mention ( all the while Esther was continually gaining favor in the eyes of everyone seeing her ).
2.16: Then Esther was taken to King A·has·u·e'rus at his royal house in the tenth month, that is, the month Te'beth, in the seventh year of his reign.
2.17: And the king came to love Esther more than all the other women, so that she gained more favor and loving - kindness before him than all the other virgins. And he proceeded to put the royal headdress upon her head and make her queen instead of Vash'ti.
2.18: And the king went on to hold a great banquet for all his princes and his servants, the banquet of Esther; and an amnesty for the jurisdictional districts he granted, and he kept giving presents according to the means of the king.
2.19: Now when virgins were collected together a second time, Mor'de·cai was sitting in the king's gate.
2.20: Esther was not telling about her relatives and her people, just as Mor'de·cai had laid the command upon her; and the saying of Mor'de·cai Esther was performing, just as when she happened to be under care by him.
2.21: In those days while Mor'de·cai was sitting in the king's gate, Big'than and Te'resh, two court officials of the king, doorkeepers, became indignant and kept seeking to lay hand on King A·has·u·e'rus.
2.22: And the thing came to be known to Mor'de·cai, and he immediately told Esther the queen. In turn Esther talked to the king in Mor'de·cai's name.
2.23: So the matter was sought out and eventually found out, and both of them got to be hanged on a stake; after which it was written in the book of the affairs of the days before the king.

3.1: After these things King A·has·u·e'rus magnified Ha'man the son of Ham·me·da'tha the Ag'ag·ite and proceeded to exalt him and to put his throne above all the other princes that were with him.
3.2: And all the king's servants that were in the king's gate were bowing low and prostrating themselves to Ha'man, for so the king had commanded respecting him. But as for Mor'de·cai, he would neither bow low nor prostrate himself.
3.3: And the king's servants who were in the king's gate began to say to Mor'de·cai: " Why are you sidestepping the king's commandment? "
3.4: And it came about that, as they talked to him day by day, and he did not listen to them, then they told Ha'man to see whether Mor'de·cai's affairs would stand; for he had told them that he was a Jew.
3.5: Now Ha'man kept seeing that Mor'de·cai was not bowing low and prostrating himself to him, and Ha'man became filled with rage.
3.6: But it was despicable in his eyes to lay hand upon Mor'de·cai alone, for they had told him about Mor'de·cai's people; and Ha'man began seeking to annihilate all the Jews who were in all the realm of A·has·u·e'rus, Mor'de·cai's people.
3.7: In the first month, that is, the month Ni'san, in the twelfth year of King A·has·u·e'rus, someone cast Pur, that is, the Lot, before Ha'man from day to day and from month to month, I [ to] the twelfth, that is, the month A'dar.
3.8: And Ha'man proceeded to say to King A·has·u·e'rus: " There is one certain people scattered and separated among the peoples in all the jurisdictional districts of your realm; and their laws are different from all other people's, and the king's own laws they are not performing, and for the king it is not appropriate to let them alone.
3.9: If to the king it does seem good, let there be a writing that they be destroyed; and ten thousand silver talents I shall pay into the hands of those doing the work by bringing I [ it] into the king's treasury. "
3.10: At that the king removed his signet ring from his own hand and gave it to Ha'man the son of Ham·me·da'tha the Ag'ag·ite, the one showing hostility to the Jews.
3.11: And the king went on to say to Ha'man: " The silver is given to you, also the people, to do with them according to what is good in your own eyes. "
3.12: The king's secretaries were then called in the first month on the thirteenth day of it, and writing went on according to all that Ha'man commanded the king's satraps and the governors who were over the different jurisdictional districts, and the princes of the different peoples, of each jurisdictional district, in its own style of writing, and each people in its own tongue; in the name of King A·has·u·e'rus it was written and it was sealed with the king's signet ring.
3.13: And there was a sending of the letters by means of couriers to all the king's jurisdictional districts, to annihilate, to kill and to destroy all the Jews, young man as well as old man, little ones and women, on one day, on the thirteenth I [ day] of the twelfth month, that is, the month A'dar, and to plunder the spoil of them.
3.14: A copy of the writing to be given as law in all the different jurisdictional districts was being published to all the peoples, I [ for them] to become ready for this day.
3.15: The couriers themselves went out, being moved to speed because of the king's word, and the law itself was given in Shu'shan the castle. As for the king and Ha'man, they sat down to drink; but as for the city of Shu'shan, it was in confusion.

4.1: And Mor'de·cai himself got knowledge of everything that had been done; and Mor'de·cai proceeded to rip his garments apart and put on sackcloth and ashes and go out into the middle of the city and cry out with a loud and bitter outcry.
4.2: Finally he came as far as in front of the king's gate, for no one was to come into the king's gate in clothing of sackcloth.
4.3: And in all the different jurisdictional districts, wherever the king's word and his law were reaching, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting and weeping and wailing. Sackcloth and ashes themselves came to be spread out as a couch for many.
4.4: And Esther's young women and her eunuchs began to come in and tell her. And the queen was very much pained. Then she sent garments to clothe Mor'de·cai and to remove his sackcloth off him. And he did not accept I [ them].
4.5: At this Esther called Ha'thach, one of the king's eunuchs, whom he had made to attend upon her, and she proceeded to give him a command concerning Mor'de·cai, to know what this meant and what this was all about.
4.6: So Ha'thach went out to Mor'de·cai into the public square of the city that was before the king's gate.
4.7: Then Mor'de·cai told him about all the things that had befallen him and the exact statement of the money that Ha'man had said to pay to the king's treasury against the Jews, to destroy them.
4.8: And a copy of the writing of the law that had been given in Shu'shan to have them annihilated he gave him to show Esther and to tell her and to lay the command upon her to come in to the king and implore favor of him and make request directly before him for her own people.
4.9: Ha'thach now came in and told Esther Mor'de·cai's words.
4.10: Then Esther said to Ha'thach and commanded him concerning Mor'de·cai:
4.11: " All the king's servants and the people of the king's jurisdictional districts are aware that, as regards any man or woman that comes in to the king at the inner courtyard who is not called, his one law is to have I [ him] put to death; only in case the king holds out to him the golden scepter, he will also certainly stay alive. As for me, I have not been called to come in to the king now for thirty days. "
4.12: And they proceeded to tell Mor'de·cai the words of Esther.
4.13: Then Mor'de·cai said to reply to Esther: " Do not imagine within your own soul that the king's household will escape any more than all the other Jews.
4.14: For if you are altogether silent at this time, relief and deliverance themselves will stand up for the Jews from another place; but as for you and your father's house, YOU people will perish. And who is there knowing whether it is for a time like this that you have attained to royal dignity? "
4.15: Accordingly Esther said to reply to Mor'de·cai:
4.16: " Go, gather all the Jews that are to be found in Shu'shan and fast in my behalf and neither eat nor drink for three days, night and day. I too with my young women, I shall fast likewise, and upon that I shall come in to the king, which is not according to the law; and in case I must perish, I must perish. "
4.17: At this Mor'de·cai passed along and proceeded to do according to all that Esther had laid in command upon him.

5.1: And it came about on the third day that Esther went dressing up royally, after which she took her stand in the inner courtyard of the king's house opposite the king's house, while the king was sitting on his royal throne in the royal house opposite the entrance of the house.
5.2: And it came about that, as soon as the king saw Esther the queen standing in the courtyard, she gained favor in his eyes, so that the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand. Esther now came near and touched the top of the scepter.
5.3: Then the king said to her: " What do you have, O Esther the queen, and what is your request? To the half of the kingship - let it even be given to you! "
5.4: In turn Esther said: " If to the king it does seem good, let the king with Ha'man come today to the banquet that I have made for him. "
5.5: Accordingly the king said: " YOU men, have Ha'man act quickly on the word of Esther. " Later the king and Ha'man came to the banquet that Esther had made.
5.6: In time the king said to Esther during the banquet of wine: " What is your petition? Let it even be granted you! And what is your request? To the half of the kingship - let it even be done! "
5.7: To this Esther answered and said: " My petition and my request is,
5.8: If I have found favor in the king's eyes and if to the king it does seem good to grant my petition and to act on my request, let the king and Ha'man come to the banquet that I shall hold for them I [ tomorrow], and tomorrow I shall do according to the king's word. "
5.9: Consequently Ha'man went out on that day joyful and merry of heart; but as soon as Ha'man saw Mor'de·cai in the king's gate and that he did not rise and did not quake on account of him, Ha'man was immediately filled with rage against Mor'de·cai.
5.10: However, Ha'man kept control of himself and came into his house. Then he sent and had his friends and Ze'resh his wife brought in;
5.11: and Ha'man proceeded to declare to them the glory of his riches and the large number of his sons and everything with which the king had magnified him and how he had exalted him over the princes and the servants of the king.
5.12: And Ha'man went on to say: " What is more, Esther the queen brought in with the king to the banquet that she had made no one but me, and tomorrow also I am invited to her with the king.
5.13: But all this - none of it suits me as long as I am seeing Mor'de·cai the Jew sitting in the king's gate. "
5.14: At that Ze'resh his wife and all his friends said to him: " Let them make a stake fifty cubits high. Then in the morning say to the king that they should hang Mor'de·cai on it. Then go in with the king to the banquet joyful. " So the thing seemed good before Ha'man, and he proceeded to have the stake made.

6.1: During that night the king's sleep fled. Therefore he said to bring the book of the records of the affairs of the times. Thus there came to be a reading of them before the king.
6.2: At length there was found written what Mor'de·cai had reported concerning Big·tha'na and Te'resh, two court officials of the king, doorkeepers, who had sought to lay hand on King A·has·u·e'rus.
6.3: Then the king said: " What honor and great thing has been done to Mor'de·cai for this? " To this the king's attendants, his ministers, said: " Nothing has been done with him. "
6.4: Later the king said: " Who is in the courtyard? " Now Ha'man himself had come into the outer courtyard of the king's house to say to the king to hang Mor'de·cai on the stake that he had prepared for him.
6.5: Accordingly the king's attendants said to him: " Here is Ha'man standing in the courtyard. " So the king said: " Let him come in. "
6.6: When Ha'man came in, the king proceeded to say to him: " What is to be done to the man in whose honor the king himself has taken a delight? " At this Ha'man said in his heart: " To whom would the king take delight in rendering an honor more than me? "
6.7: So Ha'man said to the king: " As for the man in whose honor the king himself has taken a delight,
6.8: let them bring royal apparel with which the king does clothe himself and a horse upon which the king does ride and on the head of which the royal headdress has been put.
6.9: And let there be a putting of the apparel and the horse into the charge of one of the king's noble princes; and they must clothe the man in whose honor the king himself has taken a delight, and they must make him ride on the horse in the public square of the city, and they must call out before him, 'This is how it is done to the man in whose honor the king himself has taken a delight. ' "
6.10: At once the king said to Ha'man: " Quickly, take the apparel and the horse, just as you have said, and do that way to Mor'de·cai the Jew who is sitting in the king's gate. Do not let anything go unfulfilled of all that you have spoken. "
6.11: And Ha'man proceeded to take the apparel and the horse and clothe Mor'de·cai and make him ride in the public square of the city and call out before him: " This is how it is done to the man in whose honor the king himself has taken a delight. "
6.12: Afterward Mor'de·cai returned to the king's gate. As for Ha'man, he hurried to his house, mourning and with his head covered.
6.13: And Ha'man went on to relate to Ze'resh his wife and to all his friends everything that had befallen him. At that his wise men and Ze'resh his wife said to him: " If it is from the seed of the Jews that Mor'de·cai is before whom you have started to fall, you will not prevail against him, but you will without fail fall before him. "
6.14: While they were yet speaking with him the king's court officials themselves arrived and proceeded hastily to bring Ha'man to the banquet that Esther had made.

7.1: Then the king and Ha'man came in to banquet with Esther the queen.
7.2: The king now said to Esther also on the second day during the banquet of wine: " What is your petition, O Esther the queen? Let it even be given to you. And what is your request? To the half of the kingship - let it even be done! "
7.3: At this Esther the queen answered and said: " If I have found favor in your eyes, O king, and if to the king it does seem good, let there be given me my own soul at my petition and my people at my request.
7.4: For we have been sold, I and my people, to be annihilated, killed and destroyed. Now if we had been sold for mere men slaves and for mere maidservants, I should have kept silent. But the distress is not appropriate when with damage to the king. "
7.5: King A·has·u·e'rus now said, yes, he went on to say to Esther the queen: " Who is this, and just where is the one who has emboldened himself to do that way? "
7.6: Then Esther said: " The man, the adversary and enemy, is this bad Ha'man. " As for Ha'man, he became terrified because of the king and the queen.
7.7: As for the king, he rose up in his rage from the banquet of wine I [ to go] to the garden of the palace; and Ha'man himself stood up to make request for his soul from Esther the queen, for he saw that bad had been determined against him by the king.
7.8: And the king himself returned from the garden of the palace to the house of the wine banquet; and Ha'man was fallen upon the couch on which Esther was. Consequently the king said: " Is there also to be a raping of the queen, with me in the house? " The word itself went out of the king's mouth, and Ha'man's face they covered.
7.9: Har·bo'na, one of the court officials before the king, now said: " Also, there is the stake that Ha'man made for Mor'de·cai, who had spoken good concerning the king, standing in Ha'man's house - fifty cubits high. " At that the king said: " YOU men, hang him on it. "
7.10: And they proceeded to hang Ha'man on the stake that he had prepared for Mor'de·cai; and the king's rage itself subsided.

8.1: On that day King A·has·u·e'rus gave to Esther the queen the house of Ha'man, the one showing hostility to the Jews; and Mor'de·cai himself came in before the king, because Esther had told what he was to her.
8.2: Then the king removed his signet ring that he had taken away from Ha'man and gave it to Mor'de·cai; and Esther went on to place Mor'de·cai over the house of Ha'man.
8.3: Moreover, Esther spoke again before the king and fell down before his feet and wept and implored favor of him to turn away the badness of Ha'man the Ag'ag·ite and his scheme that he had schemed against the Jews.
8.4: Then the king held the golden scepter out to Esther, at which Esther rose and stood before the king.
8.5: She now said: " If to the king it does seem good, and if I have found favor before him and the thing is proper before the king and I am good in his eyes, let it be written to undo the written documents, the scheme of Ha'man the son of Ham·me·da'tha the Ag'ag·ite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews that are in all the king's jurisdictional districts.
8.6: For how can I I [ bear it] when I must look upon the calamity that will find my people, and how can I I [ bear it] when I must look upon the destruction of my relatives? "
8.7: So King A·has·u·e'rus said to Esther the queen and to Mor'de·cai the Jew: " Look! The house of Ha'man I have given to Esther, and him they have hanged on the stake, for the reason that he thrust out his hand against the Jews.
8.8: And YOU yourselves write in behalf of the Jews according to what is good in YOUR own eyes in the king's name and seal I [ it] with the king's signet ring; for a writing that is written in the king's name and sealed with the king's signet ring it is not possible to undo. "
8.9: Accordingly the secretaries of the king were called at that time in the third month, that is, the month of Si'van, on the twenty - third I [ day] of it; and writing went on according to all that Mor'de·cai commanded to the Jews and to the satraps and the governors and the princes of the jurisdictional districts that were from In'di·a to E·thi·o'pi·a, a hundred and twenty - seven jurisdictional districts, I [ to] each jurisdictional district in its own style of writing and I [ to] each people in its own tongue, and to the Jews in their own style of writing and in their own tongue.
8.10: And he proceeded to write in the name of King A·has·u·e'rus and do the sealing with the king's signet ring and send written documents by the hand of the couriers on horses, riding post horses used in the royal service, sons of speedy mares,
8.11: that the king granted to the Jews that were in all the different cities to congregate themselves and stand for their souls, to annihilate and kill and destroy all the force of the people and jurisdictional district that were showing hostility to them, little ones and women, and to plunder their spoil,
8.12: on the one day in all the jurisdictional districts of King A·has·u·e'rus, on the thirteenth I [ day] of the twelfth month, that is, the month of A'dar.
8.13: A copy of the writing was to be given as law throughout all the different jurisdictional districts, published to all the peoples, that the Jews should become ready for this day to avenge themselves upon their enemies.
8.14: The couriers themselves, riding post horses used in the royal service, went forth, being urged forward and being moved with speed by the king's word; and the law itself was given out in Shu'shan the castle.
8.15: As for Mor'de·cai, he went forth from before the king in royal apparel of blue and linen, with a great crown of gold, and a fine - fabric cloak, even of wool dyed reddish purple. And the city of Shu'shan itself cried out shrilly and was joyful.
8.16: For the Jews there occurred light and rejoicing and exultation and honor.
8.17: And in all the different jurisdictional districts and in all the different cities wherever the word of the king and his law were reaching there were rejoicing and exultation for the Jews, a banquet and a good day; and many of the peoples of the land were declaring themselves Jews, for the dread of the Jews had fallen upon them.

9.1: And in the twelfth month, that is, the month of A'dar, on the thirteenth day of it, when the king's word and his law came due to be performed, on the day for which the enemies of the Jews had waited to domineer over them, there was even a turning to the contrary, in that the Jews themselves domineered over those hating them.
9.2: The Jews congregated themselves in their cities in all the jurisdictional districts of King A·has·u·e'rus to lay hand on those seeking their injury, and not a man stood his ground before them, for the dread of them had fallen upon all the peoples.
9.3: And all the princes of the jurisdictional districts and the satraps and the governors and the doers of the business that belonged to the king were assisting the Jews, for the dread of Mor'de·cai had fallen upon them.
9.4: For Mor'de·cai was great in the king's house and his fame was traveling throughout all the jurisdictional districts, because the man Mor'de·cai was steadily growing greater.
9.5: And the Jews went striking down all their enemies with a slaughter by the sword and with a killing and destruction, and they went doing to those hating them according to their liking.
9.6: And in Shu'shan the castle the Jews killed and there was a destroying of five hundred men.
9.7: Also, Par·shan·da'tha and Dal'phon and As·pa'tha
9.8: and Po·ra'tha and A·da'li·a and A·ri·da'tha
9.9: and Par·mash'ta and Ar'i·sai and Ar'i·dai and Vai·za'tha,
9.10: the ten sons of Ha'man the son of Ham·me·da'tha, the one showing hostility to the Jews, they killed; but on the plunder they did not lay their hand.
9.11: On that day the number of those killed in Shu'shan the castle came before the king.
9.12: And the king proceeded to say to Esther the queen: " In Shu'shan the castle the Jews have killed, and there has been a destroying of five hundred men and the ten sons of Ha'man. In the rest of the jurisdictional districts of the king what have they done? And what is your petition? Let it even be given to you. And what is your further request? Let it even be done. "
9.13: Accordingly Esther said: " If to the king it does seem good, let it be granted tomorrow also to the Jews that are in Shu'shan to do according to the law of today; and let the ten sons of Ha'man be hanged upon the stake. "
9.14: So the king said for it to be done that way. Then a law was given out in Shu'shan, and the ten sons of Ha'man were hanged.
9.15: And the Jews that were in Shu'shan proceeded to congregate themselves also on the fourteenth day of the month A'dar, and they got to kill in Shu'shan three hundred men; but on the plunder they did not lay their hand.
9.16: As for the rest of the Jews that were in the jurisdictional districts of the king, they congregated themselves, and there was a stand for their souls, and there was an avenging of themselves upon their enemies and a killing among those hating them of seventy - five thousand; but on the plunder they did not lay their hand,
9.17: on the thirteenth day of the month A'dar; and there was a rest on the fourteenth I [ day] of it, and there was a making of it a day of banqueting and of rejoicing.
9.18: As for the Jews that were in Shu'shan, they congregated themselves on the thirteenth I [ day] of it and on the fourteenth I [ day] of it, and there was a rest on the fifteenth I [ day] of it, and there was a making of it a day of banqueting and of rejoicing.
9.19: That is why the country Jews, inhabiting the cities of the outlying districts, were making the fourteenth day of the month A'dar a rejoicing and a banqueting and a good day and a sending of portions to one another.
9.20: And Mor'de·cai proceeded to write these things and send written documents to all the Jews that were in all the jurisdictional districts of King A·has·u·e'rus, the nearby and the distant ones,
9.21: to impose upon them the obligation to be regularly holding the fourteenth day of the month A'dar and the fifteenth day of it in each and every year,
9.22: according to the days on which the Jews had rested from their enemies and the month that was changed for them from grief to rejoicing and from mourning to a good day, to hold them as days of banqueting and rejoicing and sending of portions to one another and of gifts to the poor people.
9.23: And the Jews accepted what they had started to do and what Mor'de·cai had written to them.
9.24: For Ha'man the son of Ham·me·da'tha, the Ag'ag·ite, the one showing hostility to all the Jews, had himself schemed against the Jews to destroy them, and he had had Pur, that is, the Lot, cast, to disquiet them and destroy them.
9.25: But when Esther came in before the king he said with the written document: " Let his bad scheme that he has schemed against the Jews come back upon his own head "; and they hanged him and his sons upon the stake.
9.26: That is why they called these days Pu'rim, by the name of the Pur. That is why, according to all the words of this letter and what they had seen as to this and what had come upon them,
9.27: the Jews imposed and accepted upon themselves and upon their offspring and upon all those joining themselves to them, that it should not pass away, the obligation to be regularly holding these two days according to what was written concerning them and according to their appointed time in each and every year.
9.28: And these days were to be remembered and held in each and every generation, each family, each jurisdictional district and each city, and these days of Pu'rim themselves should not pass away from the midst of the Jews and the commemoration itself of them not come to an end among their offspring.
9.29: And Esther the queen, the daughter of Ab'i·ha·il, and Mor'de·cai the Jew proceeded to write with all forcefulness to confirm this second letter concerning Pu'rim.
9.30: Then he sent written documents to all the Jews in the one hundred and twenty - seven jurisdictional districts, the realm of A·has·u·e'rus, I [ in] words of peace and truth,
9.31: to confirm these days of Pu'rim at their appointed times, just as Mor'de·cai the Jew and Esther the queen had imposed upon them, and just as they had imposed upon their own soul and upon their offspring, the matters of the fasts and their cry for aid.
9.32: And the very saying of Esther confirmed these matters of Pu'rim, and it was written down in a book.

10.1: And King A·has·u·e'rus proceeded to lay forced labor upon the land and the isles of the sea.
10.2: As for all his energetic work and his mightiness and the exact statement of Mor'de·cai's greatness with which the king magnified him, are they not written in the Book of the affairs of the times of the kings of Me'di·a and Persia?
10.3: For Mor'de·cai the Jew was second to King A·has·u·e'rus and was great among the Jews and approved by the multitude of his brothers, working for the good of his people and speaking peace to all their offspring.

1.1: There happened to be a man in the land of Uz whose name was Job; and that man proved to be blameless and upright, and fearing God and turning aside from bad.
1.2: And seven sons and three daughters came to be born to him.
1.3: And his livestock got to be seven thousand sheep and three thousand camels and five hundred spans of cattle and five hundred she - asses, along with a very large body of servants; and that man came to be the greatest of all the Orientals.
1.4: And his sons went and held a banquet at the house of each one on his own day; and they sent and invited their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
1.5: And it would occur that when the banquet days had gone round the circuit, Job would send and sanctify them; and he got up early in the morning and offered up burnt sacrifices according to the number of all of them; for, said Job, " maybe my sons have sinned and have cursed God in their heart. " That is the way Job would do always.
1.6: Now it came to be the day when the sons of the I [ true] God entered to take their station before Jehovah, and even Satan proceeded to enter right among them.
1.7: Then Jehovah said to Satan: " Where do you come from? " At that Satan answered Jehovah and said: " From roving about in the earth and from walking about in it. "
1.8: And Jehovah went on to say to Satan: " Have you set your heart upon my servant Job, that there is no one like him in the earth, a man blameless and upright, fearing God and turning aside from bad? "
1.9: At that Satan answered Jehovah and said: " Is it for nothing that Job has feared God?
1.10: Have not you yourself put up a hedge about him and about his house and about everything that he has all around? The work of his hands you have blessed, and his livestock itself has spread abroad in the earth.
1.11: But, for a change, thrust out your hand, please, and touch everything he has I [ and see] whether he will not curse you to your very face. "
1.12: Accordingly Jehovah said to Satan: " Look! Everything that he has is in your hand. Only against him himself do not thrust out your hand! " So Satan went out away from the person of Jehovah.
1.13: Now it came to be the day when his sons and his daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their brother the firstborn.
1.14: And there came a messenger to Job, and he proceeded to say: " The cattle themselves happened to be plowing and the she - asses were grazing at the side of them
1.15: when the Sa·be'ans came making a raid and taking them, and the attendants they struck down with the edge of the sword; and I got to escape, only I by myself, to tell you. "
1.16: While this one was yet speaking that one came and proceeded to say: " The very fire of God fell from the heavens and went blazing among the sheep and the attendants and eating them up; and I got to escape, only I by myself, to tell you. "
1.17: While that one was yet speaking another one came and proceeded to say: " The Chal·de'ans made up three bands and went dashing against the camels and taking them, and the attendants they struck down with the edge of the sword; and I got to escape, only I by myself, to tell you. "
1.18: While this other one was yet speaking, still another one came and proceeded to say: " Your sons and your daughters were eating and drinking wine in the house of their brother the firstborn.
1.19: And, look! there came a great wind from the region of the wilderness, and it went striking the four corners of the house, so that it fell upon the young people and they died. And I got to escape, only I by myself, to tell you. "
1.20: And Job proceeded to get up and rip his sleeveless coat apart and cut the hair off his head and fall to the earth and bow down
1.21: and say: " Naked I came out of my mother's belly, And naked shall I return there. Jehovah himself has given, and Jehovah himself has taken away. Let the name of Jehovah continue to be blessed. "
1.22: In all this Job did not sin or ascribe anything improper to God.

2.1: Afterward it came to be the day when the sons of the I [ true] God entered to take their station before Jehovah, and Satan also proceeded to enter right among them to take his station before Jehovah.
2.2: Then Jehovah said to Satan: " Just where do you come from? " At that Satan answered Jehovah and said: " From roving about in the earth and from walking about in it. "
2.3: And Jehovah went on to say to Satan: " Have you set your heart upon my servant Job, that there is no one like him in the earth, a man blameless and upright, fearing God and turning aside from bad? Even yet he is holding fast his integrity, although you incite me against him to swallow him up without cause. "
2.4: But Satan answered Jehovah and said: " Skin in behalf of skin, and everything that a man has he will give in behalf of his soul.
2.5: For a change, thrust out your hand, please, and touch as far as his bone and his flesh I [ and see] whether he will not curse you to your very face. "
2.6: Accordingly Jehovah said to Satan: " There he is in your hand! Only watch out for his soul itself! "
2.7: So Satan went out away from the person of Jehovah and struck Job with a malignant boil from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.
2.8: And he proceeded to take for himself a fragment of earthenware with which to scrape himself; and he was sitting in among the ashes.
2.9: Finally his wife said to him: " Are you yet holding fast your integrity? Curse God and die! "
2.10: But he said to her: " As one of the senseless women speaks, you speak also. Shall we accept merely what is good from the I [ true] God and not accept also what is bad? " In all this Job did not sin with his lips.
2.11: And three companions of Job got to hear of all this calamity that had come upon him, and they proceeded to come, each one from his own place, El'i·phaz the Te'man·ite and Bil'dad the Shu'hite and Zo'phar the Na'a·ma·thite. So they met together by appointment to come and sympathize with him and comfort him.
2.12: When they raised their eyes from far off they did not then recognize him. And they proceeded to raise their voice and weep and rip each one his sleeveless coat apart and toss dust toward the heavens upon their heads.
2.13: And they kept sitting with him on the earth seven days and seven nights, and there was no one speaking a word to him, for they saw that the pain was very great.

3.1: It was after this that Job opened his mouth and began to call down evil upon his day.
3.2: Job now answered and said:
3.3: " Let the day perish on which I came to be born, Also the night that someone said, 'An able - bodied man has been conceived! '
3.4: As for that day, let it become darkness. Let not God look for it from above, Nor let daylight beam upon it.
3.5: Let darkness and deep shadow reclaim it. Let a rain cloud reside over it. Let the things that darken a day terrorize it.
3.6: That night - let gloom take it; Let it not feel glad among the days of a year; Among the number of the lunar months let it not enter.
3.7: Look! That night - let it become sterile; Let no joyful cry come in it.
3.8: Let cursers of the day execrate it, Those ready to awaken Le·vi'a·than.
3.9: Let the stars of its twilight grow dark; Let it wait for the light and there be none; And let it not see the beams of dawn.
3.10: For it did not close the doors of my I [ mother's] belly, And so conceal trouble from my eyes.
3.11: Why from the womb did I not proceed to die? I [ Why did I not] come forth from the belly itself and then expire?
3.12: Why was it that knees confronted me, And why breasts that I should take suck?
3.13: For by now I should have lain down that I might be undisturbed; I should have slept then; I should be at rest
3.14: With kings and counselors of the earth, Those building desolate places for themselves,
3.15: Or with princes who have gold, Those who fill their houses with silver;
3.16: Or, like a hidden miscarriage, I should not come to be, Like children that have seen no light.
3.17: There the wicked themselves have ceased from agitation, And there those weary in power are at rest.
3.18: Together prisoners themselves are at ease; They actually do not hear the voice of one driving them to work.
3.19: Small and great are there the same, And the slave is set free from his master.
3.20: Why does he give light to one having trouble, And life to those bitter of soul?
3.21: Why are there those waiting for death, and it is not, Although they keep digging for it more than for hidden treasures?
3.22: Those who are rejoicing to gleefulness, They exult because they find a burial place.
3.23: I [ Why does he give light] to able - bodied man, whose way has been concealed, And whom God hedges in?
3.24: For before my food my sighing comes, And like waters my roaring cries pour forth;
3.25: Because a dreadful thing I have dreaded, and it comes upon me; And what I have been scared of comes to me.
3.26: I have not been carefree, nor have I been undisturbed, Nor been at rest, and yet agitation comes. "

4.1: And El'i·phaz the Te'man·ite proceeded to reply and say:
4.2: " If one does try out a word to you, will you become weary? But to put a restraint on words who is able?
4.3: Look! You have corrected many, And the weak hands you used to strengthen.
4.4: Anyone stumbling, your words would raise up; And knees giving way you would make firm.
4.5: But this time it comes to you, and you become weary; It touches even you, and you get disturbed.
4.6: Is not your reverence I [ the basis of] your confidence? Is not your hope even the integrity of your ways?
4.7: Remember, please: Who that is innocent has ever perished? And where have the upright ever been effaced?
4.8: According to what I have seen, those devising what is hurtful And those sowing trouble will themselves reap it.
4.9: Through the breath of God they perish, And through the spirit of his anger they come to an end.
4.10: There is the roaring of a lion, and the voice of a young lion, But the teeth of maned young lions do get broken down.
4.11: A lion is perishing from there being no prey, And the cubs of a lion are separated from one another.
4.12: Now to me a word was stealthily brought, And my ear proceeded to get a whisper of it,
4.13: In disquieting thoughts from visions of the night, When deep sleep falls upon men.
4.14: A dread came over me, and a trembling, And the multitude of my bones it filled with dread.
4.15: And a spirit itself went passing over my face; The hair of my flesh began to bristle.
4.16: It began to stand still, But I did not recognize its appearance; A form was in front of my eyes; There was a calm, and I now heard a voice:
4.17: 'Mortal man - can he be more just than God himself? Or can able - bodied man be cleaner than his own Maker? '
4.18: Look! In his servants he has no faith, And his messengers he charges with faultiness.
4.19: How much more so with those dwelling in houses of clay, Whose foundation is in the dust! One crushes them more quickly than a moth.
4.20: From morning to evening they are crushed to pieces; Without anyone's taking I [ it to heart] they perish forever.
4.21: Has not their tent cord within them been pulled out? They die for lack of wisdom.

5.1: " Call, please! Is there anyone answering you? And to which one of the holy ones will you turn?
5.2: For the foolish one vexation will kill, And the one easily enticed envying will put to death.
5.3: I myself have seen the foolish one taking root, But suddenly I began to execrate his abiding place.
5.4: His sons remain far from salvation, And they are crushed in the gate without a deliverer.
5.5: What he harvests the hungry one eats; And even from butcher hooks one takes it, And a snare actually snaps at their means of maintenance.
5.6: For not from mere dust does what is hurtful go forth, And from mere ground trouble does not spring up.
5.7: For man himself is born for trouble, As the very sparks fly upward.
5.8: However, I myself would apply to God, And to God I would submit my cause,
5.9: I [ To the] One doing great things unsearchable, Wonderful things without number;
5.10: I [ To] the One giving rain upon the surface of the earth And sending waters upon the open fields;
5.11: I [ To] the One putting those who are low on a high place, So that those who are sad are high up in salvation;
5.12: I [ To the] One frustrating the schemes of the shrewd, So that their hands do not work with effect;
5.13: I [ To the] One catching the wise in their own cunning, So that the counsel of astute ones is carried headlong;
5.14: They encounter darkness even by day, And they grope about at midday as if at night;
5.15: And I [ to the] One saving from the sword out of their mouth, And from the hand of the strong one, a poor one,
5.16: So that for the lowly one there comes to be hope, But unrighteousness actually shuts its mouth.
5.17: Look! Happy is the man whom God reproves; And the discipline of the Almighty do not you reject!
5.18: For he himself causes pain, but binds up I [ the wound]; He breaks to pieces, but his own hands do the healing.
5.19: In six distresses he will deliver you, And in seven nothing injurious will touch you.
5.20: During famine he will certainly redeem you from death, And during war from the power of a sword.
5.21: From the whip of a tongue you will be hidden, And you will not be afraid of despoiling when it comes.
5.22: At despoiling and hunger you will laugh, And of the wild beast of the earth you need not be afraid.
5.23: For with the stones of the field your covenant will be, And the wild beast of the field himself will be made to live at peace with you.
5.24: And you will certainly know that peace itself is your tent, And you will be bound to go and see your pasture ground, and you will miss nothing.
5.25: And you will certainly know that your offspring are many And your descendants like the vegetation of the earth.
5.26: You will come in vigor to the burial place, As when sheaves pile up in their time.
5.27: Look! This is what we have investigated. So is it. Hear it, and you - know it for yourself. "

6.1: And Job proceeded to answer and say:
6.2: " O that my vexation were altogether weighed, And that at the same time my adversity they would put on scales themselves!
6.3: For now it is heavier even than the sands of the seas. That is why my own words have been wild talk.
6.4: For the arrows of the Almighty are with me, The venom of which my spirit is drinking; The terrors from God range themselves up against me.
6.5: Will a zebra cry out over grass, Or a bull low over its fodder?
6.6: Will tasteless things be eaten without salt, Or is there any taste in the slimy juice of marshmallow?
6.7: My soul has refused to touch I [ anything]. They are like disease in my food.
6.8: O that my request would come And that God would grant even my hope!
6.9: And that God would go ahead and crush me, That he would release his hand and cut me off!
6.10: Even it would still be my comfort; And I should leap I [ for joy] at I [ my] labor pains, I [ Though] he would have no compassion, for I have not hidden the sayings of the Holy One.
6.11: What is my power, that I should keep waiting? And what is my end, that I should keep prolonging my soul?
6.12: Is my power the power of stones? Or is my flesh of copper?
6.13: Is it that self - assistance is not in me, And effectual working itself has been chased away from me?
6.14: As regards anyone who withholds loving - kindness from his own fellow, He will also leave off even the fear of the Almighty.
6.15: My own brothers have dealt treacherously, like a winter torrent, Like the channel of winter torrents that keep passing away.
6.16: They are dark from ice, Upon them snow hides itself.
6.17: In due season they become waterless, they have been silenced; When it grows hot they are dried up from their place.
6.18: The paths of their way are turned aside; They go up into the empty place and perish.
6.19: The caravans of Te'ma have looked, The traveling company of Sa·be'ans have waited for them.
6.20: They certainly are ashamed because they had trusted; They have come clear to the place and they get disappointed.
6.21: For now YOU men have amounted to nothing; YOU see terror, and YOU become afraid.
6.22: Is it because I have said, 'GIVE me I [ something], Or from some of the power of YOU men make a present in my behalf;
6.23: And rescue me out of the hand of an adversary, And out of the hand of tyrants YOU men should redeem me'?
6.24: Instruct me, and I, for my part, shall be silent; And what mistake I have committed make me understand.
6.25: The sayings of uprightness have been - O not painful! But what does reproving on the part of YOU men reprove?
6.26: Is it to reprove words that YOU men scheme, When the sayings of one in despair are for mere wind?
6.27: How much more will YOU cast lots even over someone fatherless, And barter over YOUR companion!
6.28: And now GO ahead, pay attention to me, I [ And see] whether I shall lie to YOUR very faces.
6.29: Return, please - let no unrighteousness arise - Yes, return - my righteousness is yet in it.
6.30: Is there unrighteousness on my tongue, Or does my own palate not discern adversity?

7.1: " Is there not a compulsory labor for mortal man on earth, And are not his days like the days of a hired laborer?
7.2: Like a slave he pants for the shadow, And like a hired laborer he waits for his wages.
7.3: Thus I have been made to possess worthless lunar months, And nights of trouble they have counted out to me.
7.4: When I have lain down I have also said, 'When shall I get up? ' And I [ when] evening actually goes its measure, I have also been glutted with restlessness until morning twilight.
7.5: My flesh has become clothed with maggots and lumps of dust; My skin itself has formed crusts and dissolves.
7.6: My days themselves have become swifter than a weaver's shuttle, And they come to an end in hopelessness.
7.7: Remember that my life is wind; That my eye will not see good again.
7.8: The eye of him that sees me will not behold me; Your eyes will be upon me, but I shall not be.
7.9: The cloud certainly comes to its end and goes away; So he that is going down to She'ol will not come up.
7.10: He will not return anymore to his house, And his place will not acknowledge him anymore.
7.11: I, also, I shall not hold back my mouth. I will speak in the distress of my spirit; I will be concerned with the bitterness of my soul!
7.12: Am I a sea or a sea monster, That you should set a guard over me?
7.13: When I said, 'My divan will comfort me, My bed will help carry my concern, '
7.14: You even have terrified me with dreams, And by visions you make me start up in fright,
7.15: So that my soul chooses suffocation, Death rather than my bones.
7.16: I have rejected I [ it]; to time indefinite I would not live. Cease from me, for my days are an exhalation.
7.17: What is mortal man that you should rear him, And that you should set your heart upon him,
7.18: And that you should pay attention to him every morning, That every moment you should test him?
7.19: Why will you not turn your gaze from me, Nor let me alone until I swallow my saliva?
7.20: If I have sinned, what can I accomplish against you, the Observer of mankind? Why is it that you have set me as your target, so that I should become a burden to you?
7.21: And why do you not pardon my transgression And overlook my error? For now in dust I shall lie down; And you will certainly look for me, and I shall not be. "

8.1: And Bil'dad the Shu'hite proceeded to answer and say:
8.2: " How long will you keep uttering these things, When the sayings of your mouth are but a powerful wind?
8.3: Will God himself pervert judgment, Or will the Almighty himself pervert righteousness?
8.4: If your own sons have sinned against him, So that he lets them go into the hand of their revolt,
8.5: If you yourself will look for God, And I [ if] of the Almighty you will implore favor,
8.6: If you are pure and upright, By now he would awake for you And he would certainly restore your righteous abiding place.
8.7: Also, your beginning may have proved to be a small thing, But your own end afterward would grow very great.
8.8: Indeed, ask, please, of the former generation, And direct I [ your attention] to the things searched out by their fathers.
8.9: For we were only yesterday, and we know nothing, Because our days on earth are a shadow.
8.10: Will not they themselves instruct you, tell you, And from their heart will they not bring forth words?
8.11: Will a papyrus plant grow tall without a swampy place? Will a reed grow big without water?
8.12: While it is yet in its bud, not plucked off, Even ahead of all other grass it will dry up.
8.13: Thus are the pathways of all those forgetting God, And the very hope of an apostate will perish,
8.14: Whose confidence is cut off, And whose trust is a spider's house.
8.15: He will lean upon his house, but it will not keep standing; He will take hold of it, but it will not last.
8.16: He is full of sap before the sun, And in his garden his own twig goes forth.
8.17: In a stone heap his roots become interwoven, A house of stones he beholds.
8.18: If one swallows him up from his place, It will also certainly deny him, I [ saying, ] 'I have not seen you. '
8.19: Look! That is the dissolving of his way; And from the dust others spring up.
8.20: Look! God himself will not reject anyone blameless, Neither will he take hold of the hand of evildoers,
8.21: Until he fills your mouth with laughter, And your lips with joyful shouting.
8.22: The very ones hating you will be clothed with shame, And the tent of wicked ones will not be. "

9.1: And Job proceeded to answer and say:
9.2: " For a fact I do know that it is so. But how can mortal man be in the right in a case with God?
9.3: If he should find delight in contending with him, He cannot answer him once out of a thousand.
9.4: He is wise in heart and strong in power. Who can show stubbornness to him and come off uninjured?
9.5: He is moving mountains away, so that people do not even know I [ of them], He who has overthrown them in his anger.
9.6: He is making the earth go quaking from its place, So that its very pillars shudder.
9.7: He is saying to the sun that it should not shine forth, And around stars he puts a seal,
9.8: Stretching out the heavens by himself And treading upon the high waves of the sea;
9.9: Making the Ash constellation, the Ke'sil constellation, And the Ki'mah constellation and the interior rooms of the South;
9.10: Doing great things unsearchable, And wonderful things without number.
9.11: Look! He passes by me and I do not see I [ him], And he moves on and I do not discern him.
9.12: Look! He snatches away. Who can resist him? Who will say to him, 'What are you doing? '
9.13: God himself will not turn back his anger; Beneath him the helpers of a stormer must bow down.
9.14: How much more so in case I myself answer him! I will choose my words with him,
9.15: Whom I would not answer, even though I were really in the right. Of my opponent - at - law I would implore favor.
9.16: If I called him, would he answer me? I do not believe that he would give ear to my voice;
9.17: Who with a storm bruises me And certainly makes my wounds many for no reason.
9.18: He will not grant me my taking of a fresh breath, For he keeps glutting me with bitter things.
9.19: If in power anyone is strong, there I [ he is]; And if in justice I [ anyone is strong], O that I may be summoned!
9.20: If I were in the right, my own mouth would pronounce me wicked; Were I blameless, then he would declare me crooked.
9.21: Were I blameless, I would not know my soul; I would refuse my life.
9.22: One thing there is. That is why I do say, 'One blameless, also a wicked one, he is bringing to their end. '
9.23: If a flash flood itself should cause death suddenly, At the very despair of the innocent ones he would mock.
9.24: Earth itself has been given into the hand of the wicked one; The face of its judges he covers. If not, who, then, is it?
9.25: Also my own days have become swifter than a runner; They have run away, they will certainly not see good.
9.26: They have moved on like reed boats, Like an eagle that darts to and fro for something to eat.
9.27: If I have said, 'Let me forget my concern, Let me alter my countenance and brighten up, '
9.28: I have been scared of all my pains; I do know that you will not hold me innocent.
9.29: I myself am to become wicked. Why is it that I toil merely in vain?
9.30: If I actually washed myself in snow water, And I actually cleansed my hands in potash,
9.31: Then in a pit you would dip me, And my garments would certainly detest me.
9.32: For he is not a man like me I [ that] I should answer him, That we should come together in judgment.
9.33: There exists no person to decide between us, That he should put his hand upon both of us.
9.34: Let him remove his rod from upon me, And his frightfulness, let it not terrify me.
9.35: Let me speak and not be afraid of him, For I am not so disposed in myself.

10.1: " My soul certainly feels a loathing toward my life. I will give vent to my concern about myself. I will speak in the bitterness of my soul!
10.2: I shall say to God, 'Do not pronounce me wicked. Cause me to know why it is that you are contending with me.
10.3: Is it good for you that you should do wrong, That you should reject I [ the product of] the hard work of your hands, And that upon the counsel of wicked ones you should actually beam?
10.4: Do you have eyes of flesh, Or is it as a mortal man sees that you see?
10.5: Are your days like the days of mortal man, Or your years just like the days of an able - bodied man,
10.6: That you should try to find my error And for my sin you should keep looking?
10.7: This in spite of your own knowledge that I am not in the wrong, And there is no one delivering out of your own hand?
10.8: Your own hands have shaped me so that they made me In entirety round about, and yet you would swallow me up.
10.9: Remember, please, that out of clay you have made me And to dust you will make me return.
10.10: Did you not proceed to pour me out as milk itself And like cheese to curdle me?
10.11: With skin and flesh you proceeded to clothe me And with bones and sinews to weave me together.
10.12: Life and loving - kindness you have worked with me; And your own care has guarded my spirit.
10.13: And these things you have concealed in your heart. I well know that these things are with you.
10.14: If I have sinned and you have kept watching me And of my error you do not hold me innocent;
10.15: If I am actually in the wrong, too bad for me! And I [ if] I am actually in the right, I may not raise my head, Glutted with dishonor and saturated with affliction.
10.16: And I [ if] it acts haughtily, like a young lion you will hunt for me, And you will again show yourself marvelous in my case.
10.17: You will bring forth new witnesses of yours in front of me, And you will make your vexation with me greater; Hardship after hardship is with me.
10.18: So why from a womb did you bring me out? Could I have expired, that not even an eye could see me,
10.19: There as though I had not come to be I should have become; From the belly to the burial place I should have been brought. '
10.20: Are not my days few? Let him leave off, Let him turn his gaze from me, that I may brighten up a little
10.21: Before I go away - and I shall not come back - To the land of darkness and deep shadow,
10.22: To the land of obscurity like gloom, of deep shadow And disorder, where it beams no more than gloom does. "

11.1: And Zo'phar the Na'a·ma·thite proceeded to answer and say:
11.2: " Will a multitude of words go unanswered, Or will a mere boaster be in the right?
11.3: Will your empty talk itself put men to silence, And will you keep deriding without having anyone rebuke I [ you]?
11.4: Also, you say, 'My instruction is pure, And I have proved really clean in your eyes. '
11.5: Yet O if only God himself would speak And open his lips with you!
11.6: Then he would tell you the secrets of wisdom, For the things of practical wisdom are manifold. Also, you would know that God allows some of your error to be forgotten for you.
11.7: Can you find out the deep things of God, Or can you find out to the very limit of the Almighty?
11.8: It is higher than heaven. What can you accomplish? It is deeper than She'ol. What can you know?
11.9: It is longer than the earth in measure, And broader than the sea.
11.10: If he moves on and hands I [ someone] over And calls a court, then who can resist him?
11.11: For he himself well knows men who are untrue. When he sees what is hurtful, will he not also show himself attentive?
11.12: Even a hollow - minded man himself will get good motive As soon as an asinine zebra be born a man.
11.13: If you yourself will really prepare your heart And actually spread out your palms to him,
11.14: If what is hurtful is in your hand, put it far away, And let no unrighteousness dwell in your tents.
11.15: For then you will raise your face without defect And you will certainly become established, and you will not fear.
11.16: For you - you will forget trouble itself; As waters that have passed along you will remember I [ it].
11.17: And brighter than midday will I [ your] life's duration arise; Darkness will become like the morning itself.
11.18: And you will be bound to trust because there exists hope; And you will certainly look carefully around - in security you will lie down.
11.19: And you will indeed stretch yourself out, with no one to make I [ you] tremble. And many people will certainly put you in a gentle mood;
11.20: And the very eyes of the wicked will fail; And a place for flight will certainly perish from them, And their hope will be an expiring of the soul. "

12.1: And Job proceeded to answer and say:
12.2: " For a fact YOU men are the people, And with YOU wisdom will die out!
12.3: I too have a heart as well as YOU. I am not inferior to YOU, And with whom are there not things like these?
12.4: I [ One who is] a laughingstock to his fellowman I become, One calling to God that he should answer him. A laughingstock is the righteous, unblamable one.
12.5: In thought, the carefree one has contempt for extinction itself; It is made ready for those of wobbling feet.
12.6: The tents of the despoilers are unworried, And the ones enraging God have the safety Belonging to one who has brought a god in his hand.
12.7: However, ask, please, the domestic animals, and they will instruct you; Also the winged creatures of the heavens, and they will tell you.
12.8: Or show your concern to the earth, and it will instruct you; And the fishes of the sea will declare it to you.
12.9: Who among all these does not well know That the hand of Jehovah itself has done this,
12.10: In whose hand is the soul of everyone alive And the spirit of all flesh of man?
12.11: Does not the ear itself test out words As the palate tastes food?
12.12: Is there not wisdom among the aged And understanding I [ in] length of days?
12.13: With him there are wisdom and mightiness; He has counsel and understanding.
12.14: Look! He tears down, that there may be no building up; He makes it shut to man, that it may not be opened up.
12.15: Look! He puts a restraint upon the waters and they dry up; And he sends them, and they change the earth.
12.16: With him there are strength and practical wisdom; To him belong the one making a mistake and the one leading astray;
12.17: He is making counselors go barefoot, And he makes judges themselves go crazy.
12.18: The bonds of kings he actually loosens, And he binds a belt upon their hips.
12.19: He is making priests walk barefoot, And permanently seated ones he subverts;
12.20: He is removing speech from the faithful ones, And the sensibleness of old men he takes away;
12.21: He is pouring out contempt upon nobles, And the girdle of powerful ones he actually weakens;
12.22: He is uncovering deep things from the darkness, And he brings forth to the light deep shadow;
12.23: Making the nations grow great, that he may destroy them; Spreading out the nations, that he may lead them away;
12.24: Taking away the heart of the head ones of the people of the land, That he may make them wander about in an empty place, where there is no way.
12.25: They grope in darkness, where there is no light, That he may make them wander about like a drunken man.

13.1: " Look! All this my eye has seen, My ear has heard and considers it.
13.2: What YOU men know I myself well know also; I am not inferior to YOU.
13.3: However, I, for my part, would speak to the Almighty himself, And in arguing with God I would find delight.
13.4: On the other hand, YOU men are smearers of falsehood; All of YOU are physicians of no value.
13.5: If only YOU would absolutely keep silent, That it might prove to be wisdom on YOUR part!
13.6: Hear, please, my counterarguments, And to the pleadings of my lips pay attention.
13.7: Will YOU men speak unrighteousness for God himself, And for him will YOU speak deceit?
13.8: Will YOU be treating him with partiality, Or for the I [ true] God will YOU contend at law?
13.9: Would it be good that he sound YOU out? Or as one trifles with mortal man will YOU trifle with him?
13.10: He will positively reprove YOU If in secrecy YOU try to show partiality;
13.11: Will not his very dignity make YOU start up with fright, And the very dread of him fall upon YOU?
13.12: YOUR memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes; YOUR shield bosses are as shield bosses of clay.
13.13: KEEP silent before me, that I myself may speak. Then let come upon me whatever it may be!
13.14: Why do I carry my flesh in my teeth And place my own soul in my palm?
13.15: Even if he would slay me, would I not wait? I would only argue to his face for my own ways.
13.16: He would also be my salvation, For before him no apostate will come in.
13.17: HEAR my word clear through, And let my declaration be in YOUR ears.
13.18: Look! Please, I have presented a case of justice; I well know that I myself am in the right.
13.19: Who is the one that will contend with me? For now were I to become silent I should simply expire!
13.20: Only two things do not do to me; In that case I shall not conceal myself just on your account;
13.21: Put your own hand far away from upon me, And the fright of you - may it not terrify me.
13.22: Either call that I myself may answer; Or may I speak, and you return me answer.
13.23: In what way do I have errors and sins? Make me to know my own revolt and my own sin.
13.24: Why do you conceal your very face And regard me as an enemy of yours?
13.25: Will you make a mere leaf driven about quiver, Or keep chasing after mere dry stubble?
13.26: For you keep writing against me bitter things And you make me possess I [ the consequences of] the errors of my youth.
13.27: You also keep my feet put in the stocks, And you watch all my paths; For the soles of my feet you mark your own line.
13.28: And he is like something rotten that wears out; Like a garment that a moth actually eats up.

14.1: " Man, born of woman, Is short - lived and glutted with agitation.
14.2: Like a blossom he has come forth and is cut off, And he runs away like the shadow and does not keep existing.
14.3: Yes, upon this one you have opened your eye, And me you bring into judgment with you.
14.4: Who can produce someone clean out of someone unclean? There is not one.
14.5: If his days are decided, The number of his months is with you; A decree for him you have made that he may not go beyond.
14.6: Turn your gaze from upon him that he may have rest, Until he finds pleasure as a hired laborer does in his day.
14.7: For there exists hope for even a tree. If it gets cut down, it will even sprout again, And its own twig will not cease to be.
14.8: If its root grows old in the earth And in the dust its stump dies,
14.9: At the scent of water it will sprout And it will certainly produce a bough like a new plant.
14.10: But an able - bodied man dies and lies vanquished; And an earthling man expires, and where is he?
14.11: Waters do disappear from a sea, And a river itself drains off and dries up.
14.12: Man also has to lie down and does not get up. Until heaven is no more they will not wake up, Nor will they be aroused from their sleep.
14.13: O that in She'ol you would conceal me, That you would keep me secret until your anger turns back, That you would set a time limit for me and remember me!
14.14: If an able - bodied man dies can he live again? All the days of my compulsory service I shall wait, Until my relief comes.
14.15: You will call, and I myself shall answer you. For the work of your hands you will have a yearning.
14.16: For now you keep counting my very steps; You watch for nothing but my sin.
14.17: Sealed up in a bag is my revolt, And you apply glue over my error.
14.18: However, a mountain itself, falling, will fade away, And even a rock will be moved away from its place.
14.19: Water certainly rubs away even stones; Its outpouring washes off earth's dust. So you have destroyed the very hope of mortal man.
14.20: You overpower him forever so that he goes away; You are disfiguring his face so that you send him away.
14.21: His sons get honored, but he does not know I [ it]; And they become insignificant, but he does not consider them.
14.22: Only his own flesh while upon him will keep aching, And his own soul while within him will keep mourning. "

15.1: And El'i·phaz the Te'man·ite proceeded to answer and say:
15.2: " Will a wise person himself answer with windy knowledge, Or will he fill his belly with the east wind?
15.3: Merely reproving with a word will be of no use, And mere utterances will be of no benefit by themselves.
15.4: However, you yourself make fear I [ before God] to have no force, And you diminish the having of any concern before God.
15.5: For your error trains your mouth, And you choose the tongue of shrewd people.
15.6: Your mouth pronounces you wicked, and not I; And your own lips answer against you.
15.7: Were you the very first man to be born, Or before the hills were you brought forth with labor pains?
15.8: To the confidential talk of God do you listen, And do you limit wisdom to yourself?
15.9: What do you actually know that we do not know? What do you understand that is not also with us?
15.10: Both the gray - headed and the aged one are with us, The one greater than your father in days.
15.11: Are the consolations of God not enough for you, Or a word I [ spoken] gently with you?
15.12: Why does your heart carry you away, And why do your eyes flash?
15.13: For you turn your spirit against God himself, And you have caused words to go forth from your own mouth.
15.14: What is mortal man that he should be clean, Or that anyone born of a woman should be in the right?
15.15: Look! In his holy ones he has no faith, And the heavens themselves are actually not clean in his eyes.
15.16: How much less so when one is detestable and corrupt, A man who is drinking in unrighteousness just like water!
15.17: I shall declare it to you. Listen to me! Even this I have beheld, so let me relate I [ it],
15.18: That which wise ones themselves tell And which they did not hide, I [ it being] from their fathers.
15.19: To them alone the land was given, And no stranger passed through the midst of them.
15.20: All his days a wicked one is suffering torture, Even the very number of years that have been reserved for the tyrant.
15.21: The sound of dreadful things is in his ears; During peace a despoiler himself comes upon him.
15.22: He does not believe that he will come back out of darkness, And he is reserved for a sword.
15.23: He is straying about in search of bread - where is it? He well knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
15.24: Distress and anguish keep terrifying him; They overpower him like a king in readiness for the assault.
15.25: Because he stretches out his hand against God himself, And over the Almighty he tries to show himself superior;
15.26: I [ Because] he runs against him stiff - neckedly, With the thick bosses of his shields;
15.27: Because he actually covers his face with his fattiness And he puts on fat upon his loins,
15.28: He merely resides in cities that are to be effaced; In houses in which people will not keep dwelling, Which certainly prove destined for heaps of stones.
15.29: He will not grow rich and his wealth will not mount up, Nor will he spread out the acquisition of them over the earth.
15.30: He will not turn away from darkness; His twig a flame will dry up, And he will turn aside by a blast of His mouth.
15.31: Let him put no faith in worthlessness, being led astray, For mere worthlessness will prove to be what he gets in exchange;
15.32: Before his day will it be fulfilled. And his shoot itself will certainly not grow luxuriantly.
15.33: He will thrust away his unripe grapes just like a vine, And cast off his blossoms just like an olive tree.
15.34: For the assembly of apostates is sterile, And fire itself must eat up the tents of bribery.
15.35: There is a conceiving of trouble and a giving birth to what is hurtful, And their belly itself prepares deceit. "

16.1: And Job proceeded to answer and say:
16.2: " I have heard many things like these. All of YOU are troublesome comforters!
16.3: Is there an end to windy words? Or what galls you, that you answer?
16.4: I myself also could well speak as YOU men do. If only YOUR souls existed where my soul is, Would I be brilliant in words against YOU, And would I wag my head against YOU?
16.5: I would strengthen YOU with the words of my mouth, And the consolation of my own lips would hold back -.
16.6: If I do speak, my own pain is not held back, And if I do cease doing so, what goes away from me?
16.7: Only now he has made me weary; He has made all those assembling with me desolate.
16.8: You also seize me. It has become a witness, So that my leanness rises up against me. In my face it testifies.
16.9: His very anger has torn I [ me] to pieces, and he harbors animosity against me. He actually grinds his teeth against me. My adversary himself sharpens his eyes against me.
16.10: They have opened their mouth wide against me, With reproach they have struck my cheeks, In large number they mass themselves against me.
16.11: God hands me over to young boys, And into the hands of wicked ones he throws me headlong.
16.12: I had come to be at ease, but he proceeded to shake me up; And he grabbed me by the back of the neck and proceeded to smash me, And he sets me up as a target for himself.
16.13: His archers encircle me; He splits open my kidneys and feels no compassion; He pours out my gallbladder to the very earth.
16.14: He keeps breaking through me with breach after breach; He runs at me like a mighty one.
16.15: Sackcloth I have sewed together over my skin, And I have thrust my horn in the very dust.
16.16: My face itself has become reddened from weeping, And upon my eyelids there is deep shadow,
16.17: Although there is no violence upon my palms, And my prayer is pure.
16.18: O earth, do not cover my blood! And let there prove to be no place for my outcry!
16.19: Also now, look! in the heavens is one testifying about me, And my witness is in the heights.
16.20: My companions are spokesmen against me; To God my eye has looked sleeplessly.
16.21: And the decision is to be made between an able - bodied man and God, The same as between a son of man and his fellow.
16.22: For just a few years are to come, And by the path by which I shall not return I shall go away.

17.1: " My very spirit has been broken, my own days have been extinguished; The graveyard is for me.
17.2: Certainly there is mockery at me, And amid their rebellious behavior my eye lodges.
17.3: Please, do put my security with yourself. Who else is there that will shake hands with me in pledge?
17.4: For their heart you have closed to discretion. That is why you do not exalt them.
17.5: He may tell companions to take their shares, But the very eyes of his sons will fail.
17.6: And he has set me forth as a proverbial saying of peoples, So that I become someone into whose face to spit.
17.7: And from vexation my eye grows dimmer And my members are all of them like the shadow.
17.8: Upright people stare in amazement at this, And even the innocent one gets excited over the apostate.
17.9: The righteous one keeps holding fast to his way, And the one with clean hands keeps increasing in strength.
17.10: However, YOU men may all of YOU resume. So come on, please, As I do not find anyone wise among YOU.
17.11: My own days have passed along, my own plans have been torn apart, The wishes of my heart.
17.12: Night they keep putting for day: 'Light is near on account of darkness. '
17.13: If I keep waiting, She'ol is my house; In the darkness I shall have to spread out my lounge.
17.14: To the pit I shall have to call out, 'You are my father! ' To the maggot, 'My mother and my sister! '
17.15: So where, then, is my hope? And my hope - who is it that beholds it?
17.16: To the bars of She'ol they will go down, When we, all together, must descend to the very dust. "

18.1: And Bil'dad the Shu'hite proceeded to answer and say:
18.2: " How long will YOU people be at putting an end to words? YOU should understand, that afterward we may speak.
18.3: Why should we be reckoned as beasts I [ And] be regarded as unclean in YOUR eyes?
18.4: He is tearing his soul to pieces in his anger. For your sake will the earth be abandoned, Or a rock move away from its place?
18.5: The light also of wicked ones will be extinguished And the spark of his fire will not shine.
18.6: A light itself will certainly grow dark in his tent, And in it his own lamp will be extinguished.
18.7: His steps of vigor will become cramped. Even his counsel will cast him off.
18.8: For he will indeed be let go into a net by his feet, And onto a network he will walk.
18.9: A trap will seize I [ him] by the heel; A snare keeps hold upon him.
18.10: A cord for him is hidden on the earth, And a catching device for him on I [ his] pathway.
18.11: Round about, sudden terrors certainly make him start up in fright, And indeed chase him at his feet.
18.12: His vigor becomes famished, And disaster stands ready to make him limp.
18.13: It will eat the pieces of his skin; The firstborn of death will eat his limbs.
18.14: His confidence will be torn away from his own tent And it will march him to the king of terrors.
18.15: There will reside in his tent something that is not his; Sulphur will be strewed upon his own abiding place.
18.16: Underneath will his very roots dry up, And, up above, his bough will wither.
18.17: The very mentioning of him will certainly perish from the earth, And he will have no name out in the street.
18.18: They will push him out of the light into the darkness, And from the productive land they will chase him away.
18.19: He will have no posterity and no progeny among his people, And there will be no survivor in his place of alien residence.
18.20: At his day the people in the West will indeed stare in amazement, And a shudder will certainly seize even the people in the East.
18.21: Only these are the tabernacles of a wrongdoer, And this is the place of one that has not known God. "

19.1: And Job proceeded to answer and say:
19.2: " How long will YOU men keep irritating my soul And keep crushing me with words?
19.3: These ten times YOU proceeded to rebuke me; YOU are not ashamed I [ that] YOU deal so hard with me.
19.4: And, granted that I have made a mistake, It is with me that my mistake will lodge.
19.5: If for a fact against me YOU men do put on great airs, And YOU show my reproach to be proper against me,
19.6: KNOW, then, that God himself has misled me, And his hunting net he has closed in upon me.
19.7: Look! I keep crying out, 'Violence! ' but I get no answer; I keep crying for help, but there is no justice.
19.8: My very path he has blocked with a stone wall, and I cannot pass over; And upon my roadways he puts darkness itself.
19.9: My own glory he has stripped from me, And he takes away the crown of my head.
19.10: He pulls me down on all sides, and I go away; And he pulls my hope out just like a tree.
19.11: His anger also grows hot against me, And he keeps reckoning me as an adversary of his.
19.12: Unitedly his troops come and cast up their way against me, And they camp round about my tent.
19.13: My own brothers he has put far away from me, And the very ones knowing me have even turned aside from me.
19.14: My intimate acquaintances have ceased to be, And those known by me have themselves forgotten me,
19.15: Those residing as aliens in my house; and my slave girls themselves reckon me as a stranger; A real foreigner I have become in their eyes.
19.16: To my servant I have called, but he does not answer. With my own mouth I keep imploring him for compassion.
19.17: My breath itself has become loathsome to my wife, And I have become foul - smelling to the sons of my I [ mother's] belly.
19.18: Also young boys themselves have rejected me; Let me but rise up, and they begin to speak against me.
19.19: All the men of my intimate group detest me, And those whom I loved have turned against me.
19.20: To my skin and to my flesh my bones actually cleave, And I escape with the skin of my teeth.
19.21: Show me some favor, show me some favor, O YOU my companions, For God's own hand has touched me.
