19.22: Why do YOU men keep persecuting me as God does, And not become satisfied with my very flesh?
19.23: O that now my words were written down! O that in a book they were even inscribed!
19.24: With an iron stylus and I [ with] lead, Forever in the rock O that they were hewn!
19.25: And I myself well know that my redeemer is alive, And that, coming after I [ me], he will rise up over I [ the] dust.
19.26: And after my skin, I [ which] they have skinned off, - this! Yet reduced in my flesh I shall behold God,
19.27: Whom even I shall behold for myself, And I [ whom] my very eyes will certainly see, but not some stranger. My kidneys have failed deep within me.
19.28: For YOU men say, 'Why do we keep persecuting him? ' When the very root of I [ the] matter is found in me.
19.29: Be frightened for yourselves because of a sword, For the sword means a raging against errors, In order that YOU men may know there is a judge. "

20.1: And Zo'phar the Na'a·ma·thite proceeded to reply and say:
20.2: " Therefore do my own disquieting thoughts themselves answer me, Even on account of my inward excitement.
20.3: An insulting exhortation to me I hear; And a spirit without the understanding that I have replies to me.
20.4: Have you at all times known this very thing, Since man was put upon the earth,
20.5: That the joyful cry of wicked people is short And the rejoicing of an apostate is for a moment?
20.6: Although his excellency ascends to heaven itself And his very head reaches to the clouds,
20.7: Like his manure cakes he perishes forever; The very ones seeing him will say, 'Where is he? '
20.8: Like a dream he will fly off, and they will not find him; And he will be chased away like a vision of the night.
20.9: The eye that has caught sight of him will not do so again, And no more will his place behold him.
20.10: His own sons will seek the favor of lowly people, And his own hands will give back his valuable things.
20.11: His own bones have been full of his youthful vigor, But with him it will lie down in mere dust.
20.12: If what is bad tastes sweet in his mouth, If he causes it to melt away under his tongue,
20.13: If he has compassion upon it and does not leave it, And if he keeps holding it back in the midst of his palate,
20.14: His food itself will certainly be changed in his own intestines; It will be the gall of cobras within him.
20.15: Wealth he has swallowed down, but he will vomit it up; God will drive it out from his very belly.
20.16: The venom of cobras he will suck; The tongue of a viper will kill him.
20.17: He will never see the watercourses, Torrential streams of honey and butter.
20.18: He will be giving back I [ his] acquired property and will not swallow I [ it] down; Like wealth from his trade, but which he will not enjoy.
20.19: For he has crushed to pieces, he has left lowly ones; He has snatched away a house itself that he did not proceed to build.
20.20: For he will certainly know no ease in his belly; By means of his desirable things he will not escape.
20.21: There is nothing left over for him to devour; That is why his well - being will not endure.
20.22: While his plenty is at its peak he will be feeling anxious; All the power of misfortune itself will come against him.
20.23: Let it occur that, to fill his belly, He will send his burning anger upon him And will rain I [ it] upon him, into his bowels.
20.24: He will run away from armor of iron; A bow of copper will cut him up.
20.25: A missile itself will even go out through his back, And a glittering weapon out through his gall; Frightful objects will go against him.
20.26: All darkness will be reserved for his treasured things; A fire that no one fanned will eat him up; It will go badly with a survivor in his tent.
20.27: Heaven will uncover his error, And earth will be in revolt against him.
20.28: A heavy shower will roll his house away; There will be things poured forth on the day of his anger.
20.29: This is the share of the wicked man from God, Even his stated inheritance from God. "

21.1: And Job proceeded to answer and say:
21.2: " Listen, YOU men, attentively to my word, And let this become YOUR consolation.
21.3: Put up with me, and I myself shall speak; And after my speaking you may I [ each] deride.
21.4: As for me, is my concern I [ expressed] to man? Or why is it that my spirit does not get impatient?
21.5: Turn YOUR faces to me and stare in amazement, And put I [ YOUR] hand upon I [ YOUR] mouth.
21.6: And if I have remembered, I have also become disturbed, And shuddering has taken hold of my flesh.
21.7: Why is it that the wicked themselves keep living, Have grown old, also have become superior in wealth?
21.8: Their offspring are firmly established with them in their sight, And their descendants before their eyes.
21.9: Their houses are peace itself, free from dread, And the rod of God is not upon them.
21.10: His own bull actually impregnates, and it does not waste semen; His cow brings forth and suffers no abortion.
21.11: They keep sending out their young boys just like a flock, And their own male children go skipping about.
21.12: They continue raising I [ their voice] with the tambourine and harp, And keep rejoicing at the sound of the pipe.
21.13: They spend their days in good times, And in a moment down to She'ol they descend.
21.14: And they say to the I [ true] God, 'Turn away from us! And in the knowledge of your ways we have found no delight.
21.15: What does the Almighty amount to, that we should serve him, And how do we benefit ourselves in that we have come in touch with him? '
21.16: Look! Their well - being is not in their own power. The very counsel of wicked ones has kept far from me.
21.17: How many times is the lamp of the wicked ones extinguished, And I [ how many times] does their disaster come upon them? I [ How many times] in his anger does he apportion destruction?
21.18: Do they become like straw before a wind, And like chaff that a storm wind has stolen away?
21.19: God himself will store up one's hurtfulness for one's own sons; He will reward him that he may know I [ it].
21.20: His eyes will see his decay, And from the rage of the Almighty he will drink.
21.21: For what will his delight be in his house after him, When the number of his months will really be cut in two?
21.22: Will he teach knowledge even to God, When that One himself judges high ones?
21.23: This very one will die during his full self - sufficiency, When he is altogether carefree and at ease;
21.24: I [ When] his own thighs have become full of fat And the very marrow of his bones is being kept moist.
21.25: And this other one will die with a bitter soul When he has not eaten of good things.
21.26: Together in the dust they will lie down And maggots themselves will form a cover over them.
21.27: Look! I well know the thoughts of YOU men And the schemes with which YOU would act violently against me.
21.28: For YOU say, 'Where is the house of the noble one, And where is the tent, the tabernacles of wicked ones? '
21.29: Have YOU not asked those traveling over the roads? And do YOU not carefully inspect their very signs,
21.30: That at the day of disaster an evil one is spared, At the day of fury he is delivered?
21.31: Who will tell him of his way to his very face? And for what he himself has done who will reward him?
21.32: As for him, to the graveyard he will be brought, And over a tomb a vigil will be kept.
21.33: To him the clods of earth of a torrent valley will certainly become sweet, And after him he will drag all mankind, And those before him were without number.
21.34: So how vainly YOU men try to comfort me, And YOUR very replies do remain as unfaithfulness! "

22.1: And El'i·phaz the Te'man·ite proceeded to answer and say:
22.2: " Can an able - bodied man be of use to God himself, That anyone having insight should be of use toward him?
22.3: Does the Almighty have any delight in that you are righteous, Or any gain in that you make your way blameless?
22.4: For your reverence will he reprove you, Will he come with you into the judgment?
22.5: Is not your own badness too much already, And will there be no end to your errors?
22.6: For you seize a pledge from your brothers without cause, And you strip off even the garments of naked people.
22.7: You do not give the tired one a drink of water, And from the hungry one you hold back bread.
22.8: As for a man of strength, the land is his, And one who is treated with partiality himself dwells in it.
22.9: Widows you have sent away empty - handed, And the arms of fatherless boys are crushed.
22.10: That is why bird traps are all around you, And sudden dread disturbs you;
22.11: Or darkness, I [ so that] you cannot see, And a heaving mass of water itself covers you.
22.12: Is not God the height of heaven? Also see the sum total of the stars, that they are high.
22.13: And yet you have said: 'What does God really know? Through thick gloom can he judge?
22.14: Clouds are a concealment place for him so that he does not see, And on the vault of heaven he walks about. '
22.15: Will you keep to the very way of long ago That hurtful men have trodden,
22.16: I [ Men] who have been snatched away before their time, Whose foundation is poured away just as a river,
22.17: Who are saying to the I [ true] God: 'Turn away from us! And what can the Almighty accomplish against us? '
22.18: Yet he himself has filled their houses with good things; And the very counsel of wicked ones has kept far from me.
22.19: The righteous ones will see and rejoice, And the innocent one himself will hold them in derision:
22.20: 'Truly our antagonists have been effaced; And what is left of them a fire will certainly eat up. '
22.21: Acquaint yourself, please, with him, and keep peace; Thereby good things will come to you.
22.22: Take, please, the law from his own mouth, And put his sayings in your heart.
22.23: If you return to the Almighty, you will be built up; I [ If] you will keep unrighteousness far from your tent,
22.24: And I [ if] there is a placing of precious ore in the dust And gold of O'phir in the rock of torrent valleys,
22.25: The Almighty also will indeed become your precious ores, And silver, the choicest, to you.
22.26: For then in the Almighty you will find your exquisite delight, And you will raise your face to God himself.
22.27: You will make entreaty to him, and he will hear you; And your vows you will pay.
22.28: And you will decide on something, and it will stand for you; And upon your ways light will certainly shine.
22.29: For there must be a humiliation when you speak arrogantly; But one with downcast eyes he will save.
22.30: He will rescue an innocent man, And you will certainly be rescued for the cleanness of your hands. "

23.1: And Job proceeded to answer and say:
23.2: " Even today my state of concern is rebelliousness; My own hand is heavy on account of my sighing.
23.3: O that I really knew where I might find him! I would come clear to his fixed place.
23.4: I would present before him a case of justice, And my mouth I would fill with counterarguments;
23.5: I would know the words with which he answers me, And I would consider what he says to me.
23.6: Would he with an abundance of power contend with me? O no! Surely he himself would pay heed to me.
23.7: There the upright one himself will certainly set matters straight with him, And I would go safe forever from my judge.
23.8: Look! To the east I go, and he is not there; And back again, and I cannot discern him;
23.9: To the left where he is working, but I cannot behold I [ him]; He turns aside to the right, but I do not see I [ him].
23.10: For he well knows the way I take. I [ After] he has tested me out, I shall come forth as gold itself.
23.11: Of his steps my foot has laid hold; His way I have kept, and I do not deviate.
23.12: I [ From] the commandment of his lips I do not move away. I have treasured up the sayings of his mouth more than what is prescribed for me.
23.13: And he is in one I [ mind], and who can resist him? And his own soul has a desire, and he will do I [ it].
23.14: For he will carry out completely what is prescribed for me, And things like these are many with him.
23.15: That is why I feel disturbed because of him; I show myself attentive and am in dread of him.
23.16: Even God himself has made my heart timid, And the Almighty himself has disturbed me.
23.17: For I have not been put to silence because of darkness, Nor because gloom has covered my own face.

24.1: " Why is it that times have not been stored up by the Almighty himself, And the very ones knowing him have not beheld his days?
24.2: There are those who move back boundary marks; A drove they have snatched away, that they may shepherd I [ it].
24.3: They drive off even the male ass of fatherless boys; They seize the widow's bull as a pledge.
24.4: They turn aside the poor ones from the way; At the same time the afflicted of the earth have kept themselves hidden.
24.5: Look! I [ As] zebras in the wilderness They have gone forth in their activity, looking for food. The desert plain I [ gives] to each one bread for the boys.
24.6: In the field its fodder they harvest, And the vineyard of the wicked one they hastily despoil.
24.7: Naked, they pass the night without a garment, And without any covering in the cold.
24.8: From the rainstorm of the mountains they get drenched, And because there is no shelter they have to hug a rock.
24.9: They snatch away a fatherless boy even from the breast, And what is on the afflicted one they take as a pledge.
24.10: Naked, they have to go about without a garment, And, hungry, they have to carry the reaped ears.
24.11: Between the terrace walls they pass the noontime; Winepresses they have to tread, and yet they go thirsty.
24.12: From out of the city the dying keep groaning, And the soul of deadly wounded ones cries for help; And God himself considers I [ it] not as anything improper.
24.13: As for them, they proved to be among the rebels against light; They did not recognize its ways, And they did not dwell in its roadways.
24.14: At daylight the murderer gets up, He proceeds to slay the afflicted and the poor one; And during the night he becomes a regular thief.
24.15: As for the eye of the adulterer, it has watched for evening darkness, Saying, 'No eye will behold me! ' And over his face he puts a covering.
24.16: In the darkness he has dug into houses; By day they must keep themselves locked in. They have not known daylight.
24.17: For morning is the same as deep shadow for them, For they recognize what the sudden terrors of deep shadow are.
24.18: He is swift on the surface of the waters. Their tract of land will be cursed in the earth. He will not turn toward the way of the vineyards.
24.19: The drought, also the heat, snatch away the snow waters; So does She'ol those who have sinned!
24.20: The womb will forget him, the maggot will sweetly suck him, He will be remembered no more. And unrighteousness will be broken just like a tree.
24.21: He is having dealings with a barren woman who does not bear, And with a widow, to whom he does no good.
24.22: And he will certainly draw away strong people by his power; He will rise up and not be sure of his life.
24.23: He will grant him to become confident that he may support himself; And his eyes will be upon their ways.
24.24: They have become high up a little while, then they are no more, And they have been brought low; like everyone else they are plucked off, And like the head of an ear of grain they are cut off.
24.25: So really now, who will make me out a liar Or reduce my word to nothing? "

25.1: And Bil'dad the Shu'hite proceeded to answer and say:
25.2: " Rulership and dreadfulness are with him; He is making peace on his heights.
25.3: Is there any number to his troops? And upon whom does his light not rise?
25.4: So how can mortal man be in the right before God, Or how can one born of a woman be clean?
25.5: Look! There is even the moon, and it is not bright; And the stars themselves have not proved clean in his eyes.
25.6: How much less so mortal man, who is a maggot, And a son of man, who is a worm! "

26.1: And Job proceeded to answer and say:
26.2: " O how much help you have been to one without power! O I [ how] you have saved an arm that is without strength!
26.3: How much you have advised one that is without wisdom, And you have made practical wisdom itself known to the multitude!
26.4: To whom have you told words, And whose breath has come forth from you?
26.5: Those impotent in death keep trembling Beneath the waters and those residing in them.
26.6: She'ol is naked in front of him, And I [ the place of] destruction has no covering.
26.7: He is stretching out the north over the empty place, Hanging the earth upon nothing;
26.8: Wrapping up the waters in his clouds, So that the cloud mass is not split under them;
26.9: Enclosing the face of the throne, Spreading out over it his cloud.
26.10: He has described a circle upon the face of the waters, To where light ends in darkness.
26.11: The very pillars of heaven shake, And they are amazed because of his rebuke.
26.12: By his power he has stirred up the sea, And by his understanding he has broken the stormer to pieces.
26.13: By his wind he has polished up heaven itself, His hand has pierced the gliding serpent.
26.14: Look! These are the fringes of his ways, And what a whisper of a matter has been heard of him! But of his mighty thunder who can show an understanding? "

27.1: And Job proceeded again to lift up his proverbial utterance and went on to say:
27.2: " As God lives, who has taken away my judgment, And as the Almighty I [ lives], who has made my soul bitter,
27.3: While my breath is yet whole within me, And the spirit of God is in my nostrils,
27.4: My lips will speak no unrighteousness And my own tongue will mutter no deceit!
27.5: It is unthinkable on my part that I should declare YOU men righteous! Until I expire I shall not take away my integrity from myself!
27.6: On my justness I have laid hold, and I shall not let it go; My heart will not taunt I [ me] for any of my days.
27.7: Let my enemy become in every way a wicked man, And the one revolting against me really a wrongdoer.
27.8: For what is the hope of an apostate in case he cuts I [ him] off, In case God carries off his soul from him?
27.9: Will God hear an outcry of his In case distress comes upon him?
27.10: Or in the Almighty will he find exquisite delight? Will he call to God at all times?
27.11: I shall instruct YOU men by the hand of God; That which is with the Almighty I shall not hide.
27.12: Look! YOU yourselves have all of YOU seen visions; So why is it that YOU show yourselves utterly vain?
27.13: This is the share of the wicked man from God; And the inheritance of the tyrants they will receive from the Almighty himself.
27.14: If his sons become many, it is for a sword; And his descendants themselves will not have enough food.
27.15: His own survivors will be buried during a deadly plague, And their own widows will not weep.
27.16: If he should pile up silver like dust itself, And he should prepare attire just as if clay,
27.17: He would prepare, but the righteous would be the one to clothe himself, And in the silver the innocent would be the one to have a share.
27.18: He has built his house like a mere moth, And like a booth that a watchman has made.
27.19: Rich he will lie down, but nothing will be gathered; His eyes he has opened, but there will be nothing.
27.20: Like waters sudden terrors will overtake him; At night a storm wind will certainly steal him away.
27.21: An east wind will carry him off and he will go away, And it will whirl him away from his place.
27.22: And it will hurl itself at him and have no compassion; From its power he will without fail try to run away.
27.23: One will clap his hands at him And will whistle at him from his place.

28.1: " Indeed, for silver there exists a place to find it And a place for gold that they refine;
28.2: Iron itself is taken from the very dust And I [ from] stone copper is being poured out.
28.3: An end to the darkness he has set; And to every limit he is searching out Stone in the gloom and deep shadow.
28.4: He has sunk a shaft far from where I [ people] reside as aliens, Places forgotten far from the foot; Some of mortal men have swung down, they have dangled.
28.5: As for the earth, out of it food goes forth; But underneath it, it has been upturned as if by fire.
28.6: Its stones are the place of the sapphire, And it has gold dust.
28.7: A pathway - no bird of prey has known it, Nor has the eye of a black kite caught sight of it.
28.8: The majestic wild beasts have not trodden it down solid; The young lion has not paced over it.
28.9: Upon the flint he has thrust out his hand; He has overthrown mountains from I [ their] root;
28.10: Into the rocks he has channeled water - filled galleries, And all precious things his eye has seen.
28.11: The places from which rivers trickled he has dammed up, And the concealed thing he brings forth to the light.
28.12: But wisdom - where can it be found, And where, now, is the place of understanding?
28.13: Mortal man has not come to know its valuation, And it is not found in the land of those living.
28.14: The watery deep itself has said, 'It is not in me! ' The sea too has said, 'It is not with me! '
28.15: Pure gold cannot be given in exchange for it, And silver cannot be weighed out as its price.
28.16: It cannot be paid for with gold of O'phir, With the rare onyx stone and the sapphire.
28.17: Gold and glass cannot be compared to it, Nor is any vessel of refined gold an exchange for it.
28.18: Coral and rock crystal themselves will not be mentioned, But a bagful of wisdom is worth more than I [ one full of] pearls.
28.19: The topaz of Cush cannot be compared to it; It cannot be paid for even with gold in its purity.
28.20: But wisdom itself - from where does it come, And where, now, is the place of understanding?
28.21: It has been hidden even from the eyes of everyone alive, And from the flying creatures of the heavens it has been concealed.
28.22: Destruction and death themselves have said, 'With our ears we have heard a report of it. '
28.23: God is the One who has understood its way, And he himself has known its place,
28.24: For he himself looks to the very ends of the earth; Under the whole heavens he sees,
28.25: To make a weight for the wind, While he has proportioned the waters themselves by a measure;
28.26: When he made for the rain a regulation, And a way for the thunderous storm cloud,
28.27: Then it was that he saw I [ wisdom] and proceeded to tell about it; He prepared it and also searched it through.
28.28: And he went on to say to man, 'Look! The fear of Jehovah - that is wisdom, And to turn away from bad is understanding. ' "

29.1: And Job proceeded again to lift up his proverbial utterance and went on to say:
29.2: " O that I were as in the lunar months of long ago, As in the days when God was guarding me;
29.3: When he caused his lamp to shine upon my head, I [ When] I would walk I [ through] darkness by his light;
29.4: Just as I happened to be in the days of my prime, When intimacy with God was at my tent;
29.5: When the Almighty was yet with me, I [ When] my attendants were all around me!
29.6: When I washed my steps in butter, And the rock kept pouring out streams of oil for me;
29.7: When I went forth to the gate by the town, In the public square I would prepare my seat!
29.8: The boys saw me and hid themselves, And even the aged ones rose up, they stood.
29.9: Princes themselves restrained words, And the palm they would put upon their mouth.
29.10: The voice of the leaders themselves was hidden, And their very tongue cleaved to their palate.
29.11: For the ear itself listened and proceeded to pronounce me happy, And the eye itself saw and proceeded to bear witness for me.
29.12: For I would rescue the afflicted one crying for help, And the fatherless boy and anyone that had no helper.
29.13: The blessing of the one about to perish - upon me it would come, And the heart of the widow I would make glad.
29.14: With righteousness I clothed myself, and it was clothing me. My justice was like a sleeveless coat - and a turban.
29.15: Eyes I became to the blind one; And feet to the lame one I was.
29.16: I was a real father to the poor ones; And the legal case of one whom I did not know - I would examine it.
29.17: And I would break the jawbones of the wrongdoer, And from his teeth I would tear away the prey.
29.18: And I used to say, 'Within my nest I shall expire, And like the grains of sand I shall multiply I [ my] days.
29.19: My root is opened for the waters, And dew itself will stay overnight upon my bough.
29.20: My glory is fresh with me, And my bow in my hand will shoot repeatedly. '
29.21: To me they listened; and they waited, And they would keep silent for my counsel.
29.22: After my word they would not speak again, And upon them my word would drip.
29.23: And they waited for me as for the rain, And their mouth they opened wide for the spring rain.
29.24: I would smile at them - they would not believe I [ it] - And the light of my face they would not cast down.
29.25: I would choose the way for them, and I was sitting as head; And I resided as a king among I [ his] troops, As one who comforts the mourners.

30.1: " And now they have laughed at me, Those younger in days than I am, Whose fathers I would have refused To place with the dogs of my flock.
30.2: Even the power of their hands - of what use was it to me? In them vigor has perished.
30.3: Because of want and hunger they are sterile, Gnawing at a waterless region, I [ Where] yesterday there were storm and desolation.
30.4: They were plucking the salt herb by the bushes, And the root of broom trees was their food.
30.5: From the community they would be driven away; People would shout at them as at a thief.
30.6: I [ They have] to reside on the very slope of torrent valleys, In holes of the dust and in rocks.
30.7: Among the bushes they would cry out; Under the nettles they would huddle together.
30.8: Sons of the senseless one, also sons of the nameless one, They have been scourged out of the land.
30.9: And now I have become even the theme of their song, And I am to them for a byword.
30.10: They have detested me, they have kept themselves far from me; And from my face they did not hold back I [ their] spit.
30.11: For he loosened I [ my] own bowstring and proceeded to humble me, And the bridle they left loose on my account.
30.12: At I [ my] right hand they rise up as a brood; My feet they have let go, But they proceeded to cast up against me their disastrous barriers.
30.13: They have torn down my roadways; They were beneficial only for adversity to me, Without their having any helper.
30.14: As through a wide gap they proceed to come; Under a storm they have rolled along.
30.15: Sudden terrors have been turned upon me; My noble bearing is chased like the wind, And like a cloud my salvation has passed away.
30.16: And now my soul is poured out within me; Days of affliction take hold upon me.
30.17: At night my very bones have been bored through I [ and dropped] from off me, And I [ pains] gnawing me do not take any rest.
30.18: By the abundance of power my garment takes on a change; Like the collar of my long garment it engirdles me.
30.19: He has brought me down to the clay, So that I show myself like dust and ashes.
30.20: I cry to you for help, but you do not answer me; I have stood, that you might show yourself attentive to me.
30.21: You change yourself to become cruel to me; With the full might of your hand you harbor animosity toward me.
30.22: You lift me to the wind, you cause me to ride I [ it]; Then you dissolve me with a crash.
30.23: For I well know that to death you will make me turn back, And to the house of meeting for everyone living.
30.24: Only no one thrusts his hand out against a mere heap of ruins, Nor during one's decay is there a cry for help respecting those things.
30.25: Certainly I have wept for the one having a hard day; My soul has grieved for the poor one.
30.26: Although for good I waited, yet bad came; And I kept awaiting the light, but gloom came.
30.27: My own intestines were made to boil and did not keep silent; Days of affliction confronted me.
30.28: Saddened I walked about when there was no sunlight; I got up in the congregation, I kept crying for help.
30.29: A brother to jackals I became, And a companion to the daughters of the ostrich.
30.30: My very skin became black I [ and dropped] off me, And my very bones became hot from dryness.
30.31: And my harp came to be merely for mourning, And my pipe for the voice of weeping ones.

31.1: " A covenant I have concluded with my eyes. So how could I show myself attentive to a virgin?
31.2: And what portion is there from God above, Or inheritance from the Almighty from on high?
31.3: Is there not disaster for a wrongdoer, And misfortune for those practicing what is hurtful?
31.4: Does he not himself see my ways And count even all my steps?
31.5: If I have walked with I [ men of] untruth, And my foot hastens to deception,
31.6: He will weigh me in accurate scales And God will get to know my integrity.
31.7: If my stepping deviates from the way, Or my heart has walked merely after my eyes, Or any defect has stuck in my own palms,
31.8: Let me sow seed and someone else eat, And let my own descendants be rooted out.
31.9: If my heart has been enticed toward a woman, And I kept lying in wait at the very entranceway of my companion,
31.10: Let my wife do the grinding for another man, And over her let other men kneel down.
31.11: For that would be loose conduct, And that would be an error for I [ attention by] the justices.
31.12: For that is a fire that would eat clear to destruction, And among all my produce it would take root.
31.13: If I used to refuse the judgment of my slave man Or of my slave girl in their case at law with me,
31.14: Then what can I do when God rises up? And when he calls for an accounting, what can I answer him?
31.15: Did not the One making me in the belly make him, And did not just One proceed to prepare us in the womb?
31.16: If I used to hold back the lowly ones from I [ their] delight, And the eyes of the widow I would cause to fail,
31.17: And I used to eat my morsel by myself, While the fatherless boy did not eat from it
31.18: ( For from my youth he grew up with me as with a father, And from the belly of my mother I kept leading her );
31.19: If I used to see anyone perishing from having no garment, Or that the poor one had no covering;
31.20: If his loins did not bless me, Nor from the shorn wool of my young rams he would warm himself;
31.21: If I waved my hand to and fro against the fatherless boy, When I would see I [ need of] my assistance in the gate,
31.22: Let my own shoulder blade fall from its shoulder, And let my own arm be broken from its upper bone.
31.23: For disaster from God was a dread to me, And against his dignity I could not hold out.
31.24: If I have put gold as my confidence, Or to gold I have said, 'You are my trust! '
31.25: If I used to rejoice because my property was much, And because my hand had found a lot of things;
31.26: If I used to see the light when it would flash forth, Or the precious moon walking along,
31.27: And my heart began to be enticed in secrecy And my hand proceeded to kiss my mouth,
31.28: That too would be an error for I [ attention by] the justices, For I should have denied the I [ true] God above.
31.29: If I used to rejoice at the extinction of one intensely hating me, Or I felt excited because evil had found him -
31.30: And I did not allow my palate to sin By asking for an oath against his soul.
31.31: If the men of my tent did not say, 'Who can produce anyone that has not been satisfied from food of his? ' -
31.32: Outside no alien resident would spend the night; My doors I kept open to the path.
31.33: If like an earthling man I covered over my transgressions By hiding my error in my shirt pocket -
31.34: Because I would suffer a shock at a large crowd, Or the contempt itself of families would terrorize me And I would keep silent, I would not go out of the entrance.
31.35: O that I had someone listening to me, That according to my signature the Almighty himself would answer me! Or that the individual in the case at law with me had written a document itself!
31.36: Surely upon my shoulder I would carry it; I would bind it around me like a grand crown.
31.37: The number of my steps I would tell him; Like a leader I would approach him.
31.38: If against me my own ground would cry for aid, And together its furrows themselves would weep;
31.39: If its fruitage I have eaten without money, And the soul of its owners I have caused to pant,
31.40: Instead of wheat let the thorny weed go forth, And instead of barley stinking weeds. " The words of Job have come to an end.

32.1: So these three men ceased from answering Job, for he was righteous in his own eyes.
32.2: But the anger of E·li'hu the son of Bar'a·chel the Buz'ite of the family of Ram came to be hot. Against Job his anger blazed over his declaring his own soul righteous rather than God.
32.3: Also, against his three companions his anger blazed over the fact that they had not found an answer but they proceeded to pronounce God wicked.
32.4: And E·li'hu himself had waited for Job with words, because they were older than he was in days.
32.5: And E·li'hu gradually saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, and his anger kept getting hotter.
32.6: And E·li'hu the son of Bar'a·chel the Buz'ite proceeded to answer and say: " Young I am in days And YOU men are aged. That is why I drew back and was afraid To declare my knowledge to YOU men.
32.7: I said, 'Days themselves should speak, And a multitude of years are what should make wisdom known. '
32.8: Surely it is the spirit in mortal men And the breath of the Almighty I [ that] gives them understanding.
32.9: It is not those merely abundant in days that prove wise, Nor those just old that understand judgment.
32.10: Therefore I said, 'Do listen to me. I shall declare my knowledge, even I. '
32.11: Look! I have waited for the words of YOU men, I kept giving ear to YOUR reasonings, Until YOU could search for words I [ to say].
32.12: And to YOU I kept my attention turned, And here there is no one reproving Job, None of YOU answering his sayings,
32.13: That YOU may not say, 'We have found wisdom; It is God that drives him away, not a man. '
32.14: As he has not arrayed words against me, So with the sayings of YOU men I shall not reply to him.
32.15: They have been terrified, they have answered no more; Words have moved away from them.
32.16: And I have waited, for they do not continue speaking; For they stood still, they answered no more.
32.17: I shall give in answer my part, even I; I shall declare my knowledge, even I;
32.18: For I have become full of words; Spirit has brought pressure upon me in my belly.
32.19: Look! My belly is like wine that has no vent; Like new skin bottles it wants to burst open.
32.20: Let me speak that it may be a relief to me. I shall open my lips that I may answer.
32.21: Let me not, please, show partiality to a man; And on an earthling man I shall not bestow a title;
32.22: For I certainly do not know how I can bestow a title; Easily my Maker would carry me away.

33.1: " Now, however, O Job, please hear my words, And to all my speaking do give ear.
33.2: Look, please! I have to open my mouth; My tongue with my palate has to speak.
33.3: My sayings are the uprightness of my heart, And knowledge is what my lips do utter sincerely.
33.4: God's own spirit made me, And the Almighty's own breath proceeded to bring me to life.
33.5: If you are able, make reply to me, Array I [ words] before me; do take your station.
33.6: Look! I am to the I [ true] God just what you are; From the clay I was shaped, I too.
33.7: Look! No frightfulness in me will terrify you, And no pressure by me will be heavy upon you.
33.8: Only you have said in my ears, And the sound of I [ your] words I kept hearing,
33.9: 'I am pure without transgression; Clean I am, and I have no error.
33.10: Look! Occasions for opposition to me he finds, He takes me for an enemy of his.
33.11: He puts my feet in the stocks, He watches all my paths. '
33.12: Look! In this you have not been in the right, I answer you; For God is much more than mortal man.
33.13: Why is it against him that you contended, Because all your words he does not answer?
33.14: For God speaks once, And twice - though one does not regard it -
33.15: In a dream, a vision of the night, When deep sleep falls upon men, During slumbers upon the bed.
33.16: It is then that he uncovers the ear of men, And on exhortation to them he puts his seal,
33.17: To turn aside a man from his deed, And that he may cover pride itself from an able - bodied man.
33.18: He keeps his soul back from the pit And his life from passing away by a missile.
33.19: And he is actually reproved with pain upon his bed, And the quarreling of his bones is continual.
33.20: And his life certainly makes bread loathsome, And his own soul desirable food.
33.21: His flesh wastes away from sight, And his bones that were not seen certainly grow bare.
33.22: And his soul draws near to the pit, And his life to those inflicting death.
33.23: If there exists for him a messenger, A spokesman, one out of a thousand, To tell to man his uprightness,
33.24: Then he favors him and says, 'Let him off from going down into the pit! I have found a ransom!
33.25: Let his flesh become fresher than in youth; Let him return to the days of his youthful vigor. '
33.26: He will make entreaty to God that he may take pleasure in him, And he will see his face with joyful shouting, And He will restore His righteousness to mortal man.
33.27: He will sing to men and say, 'I have sinned; and what is upright I have perverted, And it certainly was not the proper thing for me.
33.28: He has redeemed my soul from passing into the pit, And my life itself will see the light. '
33.29: Look! All these things God performs, Two times, three times, in the case of an able - bodied man,
33.30: To turn his soul back from the pit, That he may be enlightened with the light of those living.
33.31: Pay attention, O Job! Listen to me! Keep silent, and I myself shall continue speaking.
33.32: If there are any words I [ to say], make reply to me; Speak, for I have taken delight in your righteousness.
33.33: If there are none, you yourself listen to me; Keep silent, and I shall teach you wisdom. "

34.1: And E·li'hu continued to answer and say:
34.2: " Listen, YOU wise ones, to my words; And YOU who know, give ear to me.
34.3: For the ear itself makes a test of words, Just as the palate tastes when eating.
34.4: Judgment let us choose for ourselves; Let us know among ourselves what is good.
34.5: For Job has said, 'I certainly am in the right, But God himself has turned aside the judgment of me.
34.6: Against my own judgment do I tell lies? My severe wound is incurable though there is no transgression. '
34.7: What able - bodied man is like Job, I [ Who] drinks up derision like water?
34.8: And he is certainly on his way to companionship with practicers of what is hurtful And to walking with men of wickedness.
34.9: For he has said, 'An able - bodied man does not profit By his taking pleasure in God. '
34.10: Therefore, YOU men of heart, listen to me. Far be it from the I [ true] God to act wickedly, And the Almighty to act unjustly!
34.11: For I [ according to] the way earthling man acts he will reward him, And according to the path of man he will cause it to come upon him.
34.12: Yes, for a fact, God himself does not act wickedly, And the Almighty himself does not pervert judgment.
34.13: Who has assigned to him the earth, And who has appointed I [ to him] the productive land, even all of it?
34.14: If he sets his heart upon anyone, I [ If] that one's spirit and breath he gathers to himself,
34.15: All flesh will expire together, And earthling man himself will return to the very dust.
34.16: So if I [ you have] understanding, do listen to this; Do give ear to the sound of my words.
34.17: Really will anyone hating justice control, And if a powerful one is righteous will you pronounce I [ him] wicked?
34.18: Shall one say to a king, 'You are good for nothing'? To nobles, 'You are wicked'?
34.19: I [ There is One] who has not shown partiality to princes And has not given more consideration to the noble one than to the lowly one, For all of them are the work of his hands.
34.20: In a moment they die, even in the middle of the night; The people shake back and forth and pass away, And powerful ones depart by no hand.
34.21: For his eyes are upon the ways of man, And all his steps he sees.
34.22: There is no darkness nor any deep shadow For those practicing what is hurtful to conceal themselves there.
34.23: For he sets no appointed time for any man To go to God in judgment.
34.24: He breaks powerful ones without any investigation, And he makes others stand up instead of them.
34.25: Therefore he recognizes what their works are, And he does overthrow I [ them] at night, and they get crushed.
34.26: As wicked ones he does slap them In the place of onlookers;
34.27: For the reason that they have turned aside from following him, And none of his ways have they considered,
34.28: So as to cause the outcry of the lowly one to come to him; And so he hears the outcry of the afflicted ones.
34.29: When he himself causes quietness, who, then, can condemn? And when he conceals I [ his] face, who can behold him, Whether it is toward a nation or toward a man, it being the same thing?
34.30: So that an apostate man may not reign, Nor there be snares of the people.
34.31: For will anyone actually say to God himself, 'I have borne, although I do not act corruptly;
34.32: Although I behold nothing, instruct me yourself; If any unrighteousness I have committed, I shall not do I [ it] again'?
34.33: Will he make good for it from your standpoint because you do refuse I [ judgment], Because you yourself choose, and not I? Even what you well know, speak.
34.34: Men of heart themselves will say to me - Even a wise able - bodied man that is listening to me,
34.35: 'Job himself speaks without knowledge, And his words are without I [ his] having insight. '
34.36: My father, let Job be tested out to the limit Over his replies among men of hurtfulness.
34.37: For on top of his sin he adds revolt; Among us he claps I [ his hands] and multiplies his sayings against the I [ true] God! "

35.1: And E·li'hu continued answering and saying:
35.2: " Is this what you have regarded as justice? You have said, 'My righteousness is more than God's. '
35.3: For you say, 'Of what use is it to you? What benefit do I have more than by my sinning? '
35.4: I myself shall reply to you And to your companions with you.
35.5: Look up to heaven and see, And behold the clouds, I [ that] they are indeed higher than you.
35.6: If you actually sin, what do you accomplish against him? And I [ if] your revolts actually increase, what do you do to him?
35.7: If you are really in the right, what do you give him, Or what does he receive from your own hand?
35.8: Your wickedness may be against a man like you, And your righteousness to a son of earthling man.
35.9: Because of the multitude of oppressions they keep calling for aid; They keep crying for help because of the arm of the great ones.
35.10: And yet no one has said, 'Where is God my Grand Maker, The One giving melodies in the night? '
35.11: He is the One teaching us more than the beasts of the earth, And he makes us wiser than even the flying creatures of the heavens.
35.12: There they keep crying out, but he does not answer, Because of the pride of the bad ones.
35.13: Only the untruth God does not hear, And the Almighty himself does not behold it.
35.14: How much less, then, when you say you do not behold him! The legal case is before him, and so you should wait anxiously for him.
35.15: And now because his anger has not called for an accounting, He has also not taken note of the extreme rashness.
35.16: And Job himself opens his mouth wide simply for nothing; Without knowledge he multiplies mere words. "

36.1: And E·li'hu proceeded to say further:
36.2: " Have patience with me a little while, and I shall declare to you That there are yet words I [ to say] for God.
36.3: I shall carry my knowledge from far off, And to my Fashioner I shall ascribe righteousness.
36.4: For my words are for a fact no falsehood; The One perfect in knowledge is with you.
36.5: Look! God is mighty and will not reject; I [ He is] mighty in power of heart;
36.6: He will not preserve anyone wicked alive, But the judgment of the afflicted ones he will give.
36.7: He will not take away his eyes from anyone righteous; Even kings on the throne - He will also seat them forever, and they will be exalted.
36.8: And if they are bound in fetters, They are captured with ropes of affliction.
36.9: Then he will tell them about the way they act And their transgressions, because they take a superior air.
36.10: And he will uncover their ear to exhortation, And he will say that they should turn back from what is hurtful.
36.11: If they obey and serve, They will finish their days in what is good And their years in pleasantness.
36.12: But if they do not obey, they will pass away even by a missile, And they will expire without knowledge.
36.13: And those apostate in heart will themselves lay up anger. They should not cry for help because he has bound them.
36.14: Their soul will die in youth itself, And their life among male temple prostitutes.
36.15: He will rescue the afflicted one in his affliction, And he will uncover their ear in the oppression.
36.16: And he will also certainly allure you from the mouth of distress! Broader space, not constraint, will be in its place, And the consolation of your table will be full of fatness.
36.17: With the judicial sentence upon the wicked one you will certainly be filled; Judicial sentence and justice will themselves take hold.
36.18: For I [ take care] that rage does not allure you into I [ spiteful] handclapping, And let not a large ransom itself lead you astray.
36.19: Will your cry for help take effect? No, nor in distress Even all I [ your] powerful efforts.
36.20: Do not pant for the night, For peoples to retreat I [ from] where they are.
36.21: Be on your guard that you do not turn to what is hurtful, For this you have chosen rather than affliction.
36.22: Look! God himself acts exaltedly with his power; Who is an instructor like him?
36.23: Who has called his way to account against him, And who has said, 'You have committed unrighteousness'?
36.24: Remember that you should magnify his activity Of which men have sung.
36.25: All mankind themselves have gazed upon it; Mortal man himself keeps looking from far off.
36.26: Behold! God is more exalted than we can know; In number his years are beyond searching.
36.27: For he draws up the drops of water; They filter as rain for his mist,
36.28: So that the clouds trickle, They drip upon mankind abundantly.
36.29: Indeed, who can understand the cloud layers, The crashings from his booth?
36.30: Look! He has spread out over it his light, And the roots of the sea he has covered.
36.31: For by them he pleads the cause of peoples; He gives food in abundance.
36.32: In his hands he has covered over the lightning, And he lays a command upon it against an assailant.
36.33: His booming tells about him, The livestock also concerning the one coming up.

37.1: " Indeed at this my heart begins to tremble, And it leaps up from its place.
37.2: Listen attentively, YOU men, to the rumbling of his voice, And the growling that goes forth from his mouth.
37.3: Under the whole heavens he lets it loose, And his lightning is to the extremities of the earth.
37.4: After it a sound roars; He thunders with the sound of his superiority, And he does not hold them back when his voice is heard.
37.5: God thunders with his voice in a wonderful way, Doing great things that we cannot know.
37.6: For to the snow he says, 'Fall earthward, ' And I [ to] the downpour of rain, even I [ to] the downpour of his strong rains.
37.7: On the hand of every earthling man he puts a seal For every mortal man to know his work.
37.8: And the wild beast comes into the ambush, And in its hiding places it dwells.
37.9: Out of the interior room comes the storm wind And out of the north winds the cold.
37.10: By the breath of God the ice is given And the breadth of waters is under constraint.
37.11: Yes, with moisture he burdens the cloud, His light scatters the cloud mass,
37.12: And it is being turned round about by his steering I [ them] for their performance Wherever he commands them upon the face of the productive land of the earth.
37.13: Whether for a rod or for his land Or for loving - kindness, he makes it produce effects.
37.14: Do give ear to this, O Job; Stand still and show yourself attentive to the wonderful works of God.
37.15: Do you know when God laid an appointment upon them, And when he caused the light of his cloud to beam?
37.16: Do you know about the poisings of the cloud, The wonderful works of the One perfect in knowledge?
37.17: How your garments are hot When the earth shows quietness from the south?
37.18: With him can you beat out the skies Hard like a molten mirror?
37.19: Let us know what we should say to him; We cannot produce I [ words] because of darkness.
37.20: Should it be related to him that I would speak? Or has any man said that it will be communicated?
37.21: And now they do not really see the light; It is brilliant in the skies, When a wind itself has passed by and proceeded to cleanse them.
37.22: Out of the north golden splendor comes. Upon God dignity is fear - inspiring.
37.23: As for the Almighty, we have not found him out; He is exalted in power, And justice and abundance of righteousness he will not belittle.
37.24: Therefore let men fear him. He does not regard any who are wise in I [ their own] heart. "

38.1: And Jehovah proceeded to answer Job out of the windstorm and say:
38.2: " Who is this that is obscuring counsel By words without knowledge?
38.3: Gird up your loins, please, like an able - bodied man, And let me question you, and you inform me.
38.4: Where did you happen to be when I founded the earth? Tell I [ me], if you do know understanding.
38.5: Who set its measurements, in case you know, Or who stretched out upon it the measuring line?
38.6: Into what have its socket pedestals been sunk down, Or who laid its cornerstone,
38.7: When the morning stars joyfully cried out together, And all the sons of God began shouting in applause?
38.8: And I [ who] barricaded the sea with doors, Which began to go forth as when it burst out from the womb;
38.9: When I put the cloud as its garment And thick gloom as its swaddling band,
38.10: And I proceeded to break up my regulation upon it And to set a bar and doors,
38.11: And I went on to say, 'This far you may come, and no farther; And here your proud waves are limited'?
38.12: Was it from your days onward that you commanded the morning? Did you cause the dawn to know its place,
38.13: To take hold on the extremities of the earth, That the wicked ones might be shaken out from it?
38.14: It transforms itself like clay under a seal, And things take their station as in clothing.
38.15: And from the wicked ones their light is held back, And the high arm itself gets broken.
38.16: Have you come to the sources of the sea, Or in search of the watery deep have you walked about?
38.17: Have the gates of death been uncovered to you, Or the gates of deep shadow can you see?
38.18: Have you intelligently considered the broad spaces of the earth? Tell, if you have come to know it all.
38.19: Where, now, is the way to where light resides? As for darkness, where, now, is its place,
38.20: That you should take it to its boundary And that you should understand the roadways to its house?
38.21: Have you come to know because at that time you were being born, And I [ because] in number your days are many?
38.22: Have you entered into the storehouses of the snow, Or do you see even the storehouses of the hail,
38.23: Which I have kept back for the time of distress, For the day of fight and war?
38.24: Where, now, is the way by which the light distributes itself, I [ And] the east wind scatters about upon the earth?
38.25: Who has divided a channel for the flood And a way for the thunderous storm cloud,
38.26: To make it rain upon the land where there is no man, I [ Upon] the wilderness in which there is no earthling man,
38.27: To satisfy storm - stricken and desolate places And to cause the growth of grass to sprout?
38.28: Does there exist a father for the rain, Or who gave birth to the dewdrops?
38.29: Out of whose belly does the ice actually come forth, And as for the hoarfrost of heaven, who indeed brings it to birth?
38.30: The very waters keep themselves hidden as by stone, And the surface of the watery deep makes itself compact.
38.31: Can you tie fast the bonds of the Ki'mah constellation, Or can you loosen the very cords of the Ke'sil constellation?
38.32: Can you bring forth the Maz'za·roth constellation in its appointed time? And as for the Ash constellation alongside its sons, can you conduct them?
38.33: Have you come to know the statutes of the heavens, Or could you put its authority in the earth?
38.34: Can you raise your voice even to the cloud, So that a heaving mass of water itself may cover you?
38.35: Can you send forth lightnings that they may go And say to you, 'Here we are! '?
38.36: Who put wisdom in the cloud layers, Or who gave understanding to the sky phenomenon?
38.37: Who can exactly number the clouds in wisdom, Or the water jars of heaven - who can tip I [ them] over,
38.38: When the dust pours out as into a molten mass, And the clods of earth themselves get stuck together?
38.39: Can you hunt prey for a lion itself And can you satisfy the lively appetite of young lions,
38.40: When they crouch in the hiding places, I [ Or] keep lying in the covert for an ambush?
38.41: Who prepares for the raven its food When its own young ones cry to God for help, I [ When] they keep wandering about because there is nothing to eat?

39.1: " Have you come to know the appointed time for the mountain goats of the crag to give birth? Do you observe just when the hinds bring forth with birth pangs?
39.2: Do you count the lunar months that they fulfill, Or have you come to know the appointed time that they give birth?
39.3: They bow down when they cast forth their young ones, I [ When] they get rid of their pangs.
39.4: Their sons become robust, they get big in the open field; They actually go forth and do not return to them.
39.5: Who sent forth the zebra free, And who loosened the very bands of the wild ass,
39.6: Whose house I have appointed the desert plain And whose dwelling places the salt country?
39.7: It laughs at the turmoil of a town; The noises of a stalker it does not hear.
39.8: It explores mountains for its pasturage And after every sort of green plant it seeks.
39.9: Does a wild bull want to serve you, Or will it spend the night by your manger?
39.10: Will you bind a wild bull fast with its ropes in the furrow, Or will it harrow low plains after you?
39.11: Will you trust in it because its power is abundant, And will you leave your toil to it?
39.12: Will you rely on it that it will bring back your seed And that it will gather to your threshing floor?
39.13: Has the wing of the female ostrich flapped joyously, Or I [ has she] the pinions of a stork and the plumage?
39.14: For she leaves her eggs to the earth itself And in the dust she keeps them warm,
39.15: And she forgets that some foot may crush them Or even a wild beast of the field may tread on them.
39.16: She does treat her sons roughly, as if not hers - In vain is her toil I [ because she has] no dread.
39.17: For God has made her forget wisdom, And he has not given her a share in understanding.
39.18: At the time she flaps I [ her wings] on high, She laughs at the horse and at its rider.
39.19: Can you give to the horse mightiness? Can you clothe its neck with a rustling mane?
39.20: Can you cause it to leap like a locust? The dignity of its snorting is frightful.
39.21: It paws in the low plain and exults in power; It goes forth to meet armor.
39.22: It laughs at dread, and is not terrified; Nor does it turn back on account of a sword.
39.23: Against it a quiver rattles, The blade of a spear and a javelin.
39.24: With pounding and excitement it swallows up the earth, And it does not believe that it is the sound of a horn.
39.25: As soon as the horn blows it says Aha! And from far off it smells the battle, The uproar of chiefs and the war cry.
39.26: Is it owing to your understanding that the falcon soars up, That it spreads its wings to the south wind?
39.27: Or is it at your order that an eagle flies upward And that it builds its nest high up,
39.28: That on a crag it resides and stays during the night Upon the tooth of a crag and an inaccessible place?
39.29: From there it has to search for food; Far into the distance its eyes keep looking.
39.30: And its young ones themselves keep sipping up blood; And where the slain are, there it is. "

40.1: And Jehovah proceeded to answer Job and say:
40.2: " Should there be any contending of a faultfinder with the Almighty? Let the reprover of God himself answer it. "
40.3: And Job went on to answer Jehovah and say:
40.4: " Look! I have become of little account. What shall I reply to you? My hand I have put over my mouth.
40.5: Once have I spoken, and I will not answer; And twice, and I will add nothing. "
40.6: And Jehovah went on to answer Job out of the windstorm and say:
40.7: " Gird up your loins, please, like an able - bodied man; I shall question you, and you inform me.
40.8: Really, will you invalidate my justice? Will you pronounce me wicked in order that you may be in the right?
40.9: Or do you have an arm like that of the I [ true] God, And with a voice like his can you make it thunder?
40.10: Deck yourself, please, with superiority and highness; And with dignity and splendor may you clothe yourself.
40.11: Let flow the furious outbursts of your anger, And see every one haughty and bring him low.
40.12: See every one haughty, humble him, And tread down the wicked right where they are.
40.13: Hide them together in the dust, Bind their very faces in the hidden place,
40.14: And I, even I, shall commend you, Because your right hand can save you.
40.15: Here, now, is Be·he'moth that I have made as well as you. Green grass it eats just as a bull does.
40.16: Here, now, its power is in its hips, And its dynamic energy in the tendons of its belly.
40.17: It bends down its tail like a cedar; The sinews of its thighs are interwoven.
40.18: Its bones are tubes of copper; Its strong bones are like wrought - iron rods.
40.19: It is the beginning of the ways of God; Its Maker can bring near his sword.
40.20: For the mountains themselves bear their produce for it, And all the wild beasts of the field themselves play there.
40.21: Under the thorny lotus trees it lies down, In the concealed place of reeds and the swampy place.
40.22: The thorny lotus trees keep it blocked off with their shadow; The poplars of the torrent valley surround it.
40.23: If the river acts violently, it does not run in panic. It is confident, although the Jordan should burst forth against its mouth.
40.24: Before its eyes can anyone take it? With snares can anyone bore I [ its] nose?

41.1: " Can you draw out Le·vi'a·than with a fishhook, Or with a rope can you hold down its tongue?
41.2: Can you put a rush in its nostrils, Or with a thorn can you bore its jaws?
41.3: Will it make many entreaties to you, Or will it say soft words to you?
41.4: Will it conclude a covenant with you, That you may take it as a slave to time indefinite?
41.5: Will you play with it as with a bird, Or will you tie it for your young girls?
41.6: Will partners barter for it? Will they divide it up among tradesmen?
41.7: Will you fill its skin with harpoons, Or its head with fish spears?
41.8: Put your hand upon it. Remember the battle. Do not do it again.
41.9: Look! One's expectation about it will certainly be disappointed. One will also be hurled down at the mere sight of it.
41.10: None is so audacious that he should stir it up. And who is it that can hold his ground before me?
41.11: Who has given me something first, that I ought to reward him? Under the whole heavens it is mine.
41.12: I shall not keep silent about its parts Or the matter of I [ its] mightiness and the grace of its proportions.
41.13: Who has uncovered the face of its clothing? Into its double jaw who will enter?
41.14: The doors of its face who has opened? Its teeth round about are frightful.
41.15: Furrows of scales are its haughtiness, Closed as with a tight seal.
41.16: One to the other they fit closely, And not even air can come in between them.
41.17: Each one to the other they are stuck together; They grasp one another and cannot be separated.
41.18: Its very sneezings flash forth light, And its eyes are like the beams of dawn.
41.19: Out of its mouth there go lightning flashes, Even sparks of fire make their escape.
41.20: Out of its nostrils smoke goes forth, Like a furnace set aflame even with rushes.
41.21: Its soul itself sets coals ablaze, And even a flame goes forth out of its mouth.
41.22: In its neck lodges strength, And before it despair leaps.
41.23: The folds of its flesh do cling together; They are as a casting upon it, immovable.
41.24: Its heart is cast like stone, Yes, cast like a lower millstone.
41.25: Due to its rising up the strong get frightened; Due to consternation they get bewildered.
41.26: Overtaking it, the sword itself does not prove equal, Nor spear, dart or arrowhead.
41.27: It regards iron as mere straw, Copper as mere rotten wood.
41.28: An arrow does not chase it away; The slingstones have been changed for it into mere stubble.
41.29: A club has been regarded I [ by it] as mere stubble, And it laughs at the rattling of a javelin.
41.30: As pointed earthenware fragments are its underparts; It spreads out a threshing instrument upon the mire.
41.31: It causes the depths to boil just like a pot; It makes the very sea like an ointment pot.
41.32: Behind itself it makes a pathway shine; One would regard the watery deep as gray - headedness.
41.33: Upon the dust there is not the like of it, The one made to be without terror.
41.34: Everything high it sees. It is king over all majestic wild beasts. "

42.1: And Job proceeded to answer Jehovah and say:
42.2: " I have come to know that you are able to do all things, And there is no idea that is unattainable for you.
42.3: 'Who is this that is obscuring counsel without knowledge? ' Therefore I talked, but I was not understanding Things too wonderful for me, which I do not know.
42.4: 'Hear, please, and I myself shall speak. I shall question you, and you inform me. '
42.5: In hearsay I have heard about you, But now my own eye does see you.
42.6: That is why I make a retraction, And I do repent in dust and ashes. "
42.7: And it came about after Jehovah had spoken these words to Job, that Jehovah proceeded to say to El'i·phaz the Te'man·ite: " My anger has grown hot against you and your two companions, for YOU men have not spoken concerning me what is truthful as has my servant Job.
42.8: And now take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams and go to my servant Job, and YOU men must offer up a burnt sacrifice in YOUR own behalf; and Job my servant will himself pray for YOU. His face only I shall accept so as not to commit disgraceful folly with YOU, for YOU have not spoken concerning me what is truthful, as has my servant Job. "
42.9: Accordingly El'i·phaz the Te'man·ite and Bil'dad the Shu'hite I [ and] Zo'phar the Na'a·ma·thite went and did just as Jehovah had spoken to them; and so Jehovah accepted Job's face.
42.10: And Jehovah himself turned back the captive condition of Job when he prayed in behalf of his companions, and Jehovah began to give in addition all that had been Job's, in double amount.
42.11: And there kept coming to him all his brothers and all his sisters and all those formerly knowing him, and they began to eat bread with him in his house and to sympathize with him and to comfort him over all the calamity that Jehovah had let come upon him; and they proceeded each one to give him a piece of money and each one a gold ring.
42.12: As for Jehovah, he blessed the end of Job afterward more than his beginning, so that he came to have fourteen thousand sheep and six thousand camels and a thousand spans of cattle and a thousand she - asses.
42.13: He also came to have seven sons and three daughters.
42.14: And he went calling the name of the first Je·mi'mah and the name of the second Ke·zi'ah and the name of the third Ker'en - hap'puch.
42.15: And no women were found as pretty as Job's daughters in all the land, and their father proceeded to give them an inheritance in among their brothers.
42.16: And Job continued living after this a hundred and forty years and came to see his sons and his grandsons - four generations.
42.17: And gradually Job died, old and satisfied with days.

1.1: Happy is the man that has not walked in the counsel of the wicked ones, And in the way of sinners has not stood, And in the seat of ridiculers has not sat.
1.2: But his delight is in the law of Jehovah, And in his law he reads in an undertone day and night.
1.3: And he will certainly become like a tree planted by streams of water, That gives its own fruit in its season And the foliage of which does not wither, And everything he does will succeed.
1.4: The wicked are not like that, But are like the chaff that the wind drives away.
1.5: That is why the wicked ones will not stand up in the judgment, Nor sinners in the assembly of righteous ones.
1.6: For Jehovah is taking knowledge of the way of righteous ones, But the very way of wicked ones will perish.

2.1: Why have the nations been in tumult And the national groups themselves kept muttering an empty thing?
2.2: The kings of earth take their stand And high officials themselves have massed together as one Against Jehovah and against his anointed one,
2.3: I [ Saying: ] " Let us tear their bands apart And cast their cords away from us! "
2.4: The very One sitting in the heavens will laugh; Jehovah himself will hold them in derision.
2.5: At that time he will speak to them in his anger And in his hot displeasure he will disturb them,
2.6: I [ Saying: ] " I, even I, have installed my king Upon Zion, my holy mountain. "
2.7: Let me refer to the decree of Jehovah; He has said to me: " You are my son; I, today, I have become your father.
2.8: Ask of me, that I may give nations as your inheritance And the ends of the earth as your own possession.
2.9: You will break them with an iron scepter, As though a potter's vessel you will dash them to pieces. "
2.10: And now, O kings, exercise insight; Let yourselves be corrected, O judges of the earth.
2.11: Serve Jehovah with fear And be joyful with trembling.
2.12: Kiss the son, that He may not become incensed And YOU may not perish I [ from] the way, For his anger flares up easily. Happy are all those taking refuge in him.

3.1: O Jehovah, why have my adversaries become many? Why are many rising up against me?
3.2: Many are saying of my soul: " There is no salvation for him by God. " Se'lah.
3.3: And yet you, O Jehovah, are a shield about me, My glory and the One lifting up my head.
3.4: With my voice I shall call to Jehovah himself, And he will answer me from his holy mountain. Se'lah.
3.5: As for me, I will lie down that I may sleep; I shall certainly awake, for Jehovah himself keeps supporting me.
3.6: I shall not be afraid of ten thousands of people Who have set themselves in array against me round about.
3.7: Do arise, O Jehovah! Save me, O my God! For you will have to strike all my enemies on the jaw. The teeth of wicked ones you will have to break.
3.8: Salvation belongs to Jehovah. Your blessing is upon your people. Se'lah.

4.1: When I call, answer me, O my righteous God. In the distress you must make broad space for me. Show me favor and hear my prayer.
4.2: YOU sons of men, how long must my glory be for insult, I [ While] YOU keep loving empty things, I [ While] YOU keep seeking to find a lie? Se'lah.
4.3: So take knowledge that Jehovah will certainly distinguish his loyal one; Jehovah himself will hear when I call to him.
4.4: BE agitated, but do not sin. Have YOUR say in YOUR heart, upon YOUR bed, and keep silent. Se'lah.
4.5: Sacrifice the sacrifices of righteousness, And trust in Jehovah.
4.6: There are many saying: " Who will show us good? " Lift up the light of your face upon us, O Jehovah.
4.7: You will certainly give a rejoicing in my heart Greater than in the time when their grain and their new wine have abounded.
4.8: In peace I will both lie down and sleep, For you yourself alone, O Jehovah, make me dwell in security.

5.1: To my sayings do give ear, O Jehovah; Do understand my sighing.
5.2: Do pay attention to the sound of my cry for help, O my King and my God, because to you I pray.
5.3: O Jehovah, in the morning you will hear my voice; In the morning I shall address myself to you and be on the watch.
5.4: For you are not a God taking delight in wickedness; No one bad may reside for any time with you.
5.5: No boasters may take their stand in front of your eyes. You do hate all those practicing what is hurtful;
5.6: You will destroy those speaking a lie. A man of bloodshed and deception Jehovah detests.
5.7: As for me, in the abundance of your loving - kindness I shall come into your house, I shall bow down toward your holy temple in fear of you.
5.8: O Jehovah, lead me in your righteousness by reason of my foes; Make your way smooth before me.
5.9: For in their mouth there is nothing trustworthy; Their inward part is adversity indeed. Their throat is an opened burial place; A smooth tongue they use.
5.10: God will certainly hold them guilty; They will fall due to their own counsels. In the multitude of their transgressions let there be a dispersing of them, Because they have rebelled against you.
5.11: But all those taking refuge in you will rejoice; To time indefinite they will cry out joyfully. And you will block approach to them, And those loving your name will exult in you.
5.12: For you yourself will bless anyone righteous, O Jehovah; As with a large shield, with approval you will surround them.

6.1: O Jehovah, do not in your anger reprove me, And do not in your rage correct me.
6.2: Show me favor, O Jehovah, for I am fading away. Heal me, O Jehovah, for my bones have been disturbed.
6.3: Yes, my own soul has been very much disturbed; And you, O Jehovah - how long?
6.4: Do return, O Jehovah, do rescue my soul; Save me for the sake of your loving - kindness.
6.5: For in death there is no mention of you; In She'ol who will laud you?
6.6: I have grown weary with my sighing; All night long I make my couch swim; With my tears I make my own divan overflow.
6.7: From vexation my eye has become weak, It has grown old because of all those showing hostility to me.
6.8: Get away from me, all YOU practicers of what is hurtful, For Jehovah will certainly hear the sound of my weeping.
6.9: Jehovah will indeed hear my request for favor; Jehovah himself will accept my own prayer.
6.10: All my enemies will be very much ashamed and disturbed; They will turn back, they will be ashamed instantly. A dirge of David that he sang to Jehovah concerning the words of Cush the Ben'ja·min·ite.

7.1: O Jehovah my God, in you I have taken refuge. Save me from all those persecuting me and deliver me,
7.2: That no one may tear my soul to pieces as a lion does, Snatching I [ me] away when there is no deliverer.
7.3: O Jehovah my God, if I have done this, If there exists any injustice in my hands,
7.4: If I have repaid the one rewarding me with what is bad, Or I [ if] I have despoiled anyone showing hostility to me without success,
7.5: Let an enemy pursue my soul And let him overtake and trample my life down to the very earth And cause my own glory to reside in the dust itself. Se'lah.
7.6: Do arise, O Jehovah, in your anger; Lift yourself up at the outbursts of fury of those showing hostility to me, And do awake for me, I [ since] you have given command for judgment itself.
7.7: And let the very assembly of national groups surround you, And against it do you return on high.
7.8: Jehovah himself will pass sentence on the peoples. Judge me, O Jehovah, according to my righteousness And according to my integrity in me.
7.9: Please, may the badness of wicked ones come to an end, And may you establish the righteous one; And God as righteous is testing out heart and kidneys.
7.10: The shield for me is upon God, a Savior of those upright in heart.
7.11: God is a righteous Judge, And God is hurling denunciations every day.
7.12: If anyone will not return, His sword he will sharpen, His bow he will certainly bend, and he will make it ready I [ for shooting].
7.13: And for himself he must prepare the instruments of death; His arrows he will make flaming ones.
7.14: Look! There is one that is pregnant with what is hurtful, And he has conceived trouble and is bound to give birth to falsehood.
7.15: A pit he has excavated, and he proceeded to dig it; But he will fall into the hole I [ that] he went making.
7.16: His trouble will return upon his own head, And upon the crown of his head his own violence will descend.
7.17: I shall laud Jehovah according to his righteousness, And I will make melody to the name of Jehovah the Most High.

8.1: O Jehovah our Lord, how majestic your name is in all the earth, You whose dignity is recounted above the heavens!
8.2: Out of the mouth of children and sucklings you have founded strength, On account of those showing hostility to you, So as to make the enemy and the one taking his vengeance desist.
8.3: When I see your heavens, the works of your fingers, The moon and the stars that you have prepared,
8.4: What is mortal man that you keep him in mind, And the son of earthling man that you take care of him?
8.5: You also proceeded to make him a little less than godlike ones, And with glory and splendor you then crowned him.
8.6: You make him dominate over the works of your hands; Everything you have put under his feet:
8.7: Small cattle and oxen, all of them, And also the beasts of the open field,
8.8: The birds of heaven and the fish of the sea, Anything passing through the paths of the seas.
8.9: O Jehovah our Lord, how majestic your name is in all the earth!

9.1: I will laud I [ you], O Jehovah, with all my heart; I will declare all your wonderful works.
9.2: I will rejoice and exult in you, I will make melody to your name, O Most High.
9.3: When my enemies turn back, They will stumble and perish from before you.
9.4: For you have executed my judgment and my cause; You have sat on the throne judging with righteousness.
9.5: You have rebuked nations, you have destroyed the wicked one. Their name you have wiped out to time indefinite, even forever.
9.6: O you enemy, I [ your] desolations have come to their perpetual finish, And the cities that you have uprooted. The very mention of them will certainly perish.
9.7: As for Jehovah, he will sit to time indefinite, Firmly establishing his throne for judgment itself.
9.8: And he himself will judge the productive land in righteousness; He will judicially try national groups in uprightness.
9.9: And Jehovah will become a secure height for anyone crushed, A secure height in times of distress.
9.10: Why, O Jehovah, do you keep standing afar off?
9.11: Make melody, YOU people, to Jehovah, who is dwelling in Zion; Tell among the peoples his deeds.
9.12: For, when looking for bloodshed, he will certainly remember those very ones; He is sure not to forget the outcry of the afflicted ones.
9.13: Show me favor, O Jehovah; see my affliction by those hating me, O you who are lifting me up from the gates of death,
9.14: In order that I may declare all your praiseworthy deeds In the gates of the daughter of Zion, That I may be joyful in your salvation.
9.15: The nations have sunk down into the pit that they have made; In the net that they hid, their own foot has been caught.
9.16: Jehovah is known by the judgment that he has executed. By the activity of his own hands the wicked one has been ensnared. Hig·ga'ion. Se'lah.
9.17: Wicked people will turn back to She'ol, Even all the nations forgetting God.
9.18: For not always will the poor one be forgotten, Nor will the hope of the meek ones ever perish.
9.19: Do arise, O Jehovah! Let not mortal man prove superior in strength. Let the nations be judged before your face.
9.20: Do put fear into them, O Jehovah, That the nations may know that they are but mortal men. Se'lah.

10.1: I [ Why] do you keep yourself hid in times of distress?
10.2: In his haughtiness the wicked one hotly pursues the afflicted one; They get caught by the ideas that they have thought up.
10.3: For the wicked has praised himself over the selfish longing of his soul, And the one making undue profit has blessed himself; He has disrespected Jehovah.
10.4: The wicked one according to his superciliousness makes no search; All his ideas are: " There is no God. "
10.5: His ways keep prospering all the time. Your judicial decisions are high up out of his range; As for all those showing hostility to him, he puffs at them.
10.6: He has said in his heart: " I shall not be made to totter; For generation after generation I [ I shall be] one who is in no calamity. "
10.7: His mouth is full of oaths and of deceptions and of oppression. Under his tongue are trouble and what is hurtful.
10.8: He sits in an ambush of settlements; From concealed places he will kill someone innocent. His eyes are on the lookout for someone unfortunate.
10.9: He keeps lying in wait in the concealed place like a lion in his covert. He keeps lying in wait to carry off some afflicted one by force. He carries off the afflicted one by force when he draws his net shut.
10.10: He is crushed, he bows down, And the army of dejected ones has to fall into his strong I [ claws].
10.11: He has said in his heart: " God has forgotten. He has concealed his face. He will certainly never see I [ it]. "
10.12: Do arise, O Jehovah. O God, lift up your hand. Do not forget the afflicted ones.
10.13: Why is it that the wicked one has disrespected God? He has said in his heart: " You will not require an accounting. "
10.14: For you yourself have seen trouble and vexation. You keep looking on, to get I [ them] into your hand. To you the unfortunate one, the fatherless boy, commits I [ himself]. You yourself have become I [ his] helper.
10.15: Break the arm of the wicked and bad one. May you search after his wickedness I [ until] you find no more.
10.16: Jehovah is King to time indefinite, even forever. The nations have perished out of his earth.
10.17: The desire of the meek ones you will certainly hear, O Jehovah. You will prepare their heart. You will pay attention with your ear,
10.18: To judge the fatherless boy and the crushed one, That mortal man who is of the earth may no more cause trembling.

11.1: In Jehovah I have taken refuge. How dare YOU men say to my soul: " Flee as a bird to YOUR mountain! "
