55.12: For it was not an enemy that proceeded to reproach me; Otherwise I could put up with it. It was not an intense hater of me that assumed great airs against me; Otherwise I could conceal myself from him.
55.13: But it was you, a mortal man who was as my equal, One familiar to me and my acquaintance,
55.14: Because we used to enjoy sweet intimacy together; Into the house of God we used to walk with the throng.
55.15: Desolations I [ be] upon them! Let them go down into She'ol alive; For during their alien residence bad things have been within them.
55.16: As for me, to God I shall call out; And Jehovah himself will save me.
55.17: Evening and morning and noontime I cannot but show concern and I moan, And he hears my voice.
55.18: He will certainly redeem I [ and put] my soul in peace from the fight that is against me, For in multitudes they have come to be against me.
55.19: God will hear and answer them, Even He that is sitting I [ enthroned] as in the past - Se'lah - Those with whom there are no changings And who have not feared God.
55.20: He has thrust out his hands against those at peace with him; He has profaned his covenant.
55.21: Smoother than butter are I [ the words of] his mouth, But his heart is disposed to fight. His words are softer than oil, But they are drawn swords.
55.22: Throw your burden upon Jehovah himself, And he himself will sustain you. Never will he allow the righteous one to totter.
55.23: But you yourself, O God, will bring them down to the lowest pit. As for bloodguilty and deceitful men, they will not live out half their days. But as for me, I shall trust in you.

56.1: Show me favor, O God, because mortal man has snapped at me. Warring all day long, he keeps oppressing me.
56.2: My foes have kept snapping all day long, For there are many warring against me high - mindedly.
56.3: Whatever day I get afraid, I, for my part, shall trust even in you.
56.4: In union with God I shall praise his word. In God I have put my trust; I shall not be afraid. What can flesh do to me?
56.5: All day long they keep hurting my personal affairs; All their thoughts are against me for bad.
56.6: They attack, they conceal themselves, They, for their part, keep observing my very steps, While they have waited for my soul.
56.7: On account of I [ their] hurtfulness cast them forth. In anger bring down even the peoples, O God.
56.8: My being a fugitive you yourself have reported. Do put my tears in your skin bottle. Are they not in your book?
56.9: At that time my enemies will turn back, on the day that I call; This I well know, that God is for me.
56.10: In union with God I shall praise I [ his] word; In union with Jehovah I shall praise I [ his] word.
56.11: In God I have put my trust. I shall not be afraid. What can earthling man do to me?
56.12: Upon me, O God, there are vows to you. I shall render expressions of thanksgiving to you.
56.13: For you have delivered my soul from death - I [ Have you] not I [ delivered] my feet from stumbling? - That I [ I] may walk about before God in the light of those alive.

57.1: Show me favor, O God, show me favor, For in you my soul has taken refuge; And in the shadow of your wings I take refuge until the adversities pass over.
57.2: I call to God the Most High, to the I [ true] God who is bringing I [ them] to an end on my account.
57.3: He will send from heaven and save me. He will certainly confuse the one snapping at me. Se'lah. God will send his loving - kindness and his trueness.
57.4: My soul is in the middle of lions; I cannot but lie down among devourers, I [ even] the sons of men, Whose teeth are spears and arrows, And whose tongue is a sharp sword.
57.5: O be exalted above the heavens, O God; Let your glory be above all the earth.
57.6: A net they have prepared for my steps; My soul has become bowed down. They excavated before me a pitfall; They have fallen into the midst of it. Se'lah.
57.7: My heart is steadfast, O God, My heart is steadfast. I will sing and make melody.
57.8: Do awake, O my glory; Do awake, O stringed instrument; you too, O harp. I will awaken the dawn.
57.9: I shall laud you among the peoples, O Jehovah; I shall make melody to you among the national groups.
57.10: For your loving - kindness is great up to the heavens, And your trueness up to the skies.
57.11: Do be exalted above the heavens, O God; Let your glory be above all the earth.

58.1: I [ In YOUR] silence can YOU really speak about righteousness itself? Can YOU judge in uprightness itself, O YOU sons of men?
58.2: How much, rather, do YOU with the heart practice outright unrighteousness in the earth, I [ And] prepare the road for the very violence of YOUR hands!
58.3: The wicked ones have been perverts from the womb; They have wandered about from the belly onward; They are speaking lies.
58.4: The venom of theirs is like the venom of the serpent, Deaf like the cobra that stops up its ear,
58.5: That will not listen to the voice of charmers, Though someone wise is binding with spells.
58.6: O God, knock out their teeth in their mouth. Break down the very jawbones of maned young lions, O Jehovah.
58.7: May they dissolve as into waters that go their way; May he bend I [ the bow for] his arrows as they collapse.
58.8: Like a snail melting away he walks; Like a miscarriage of a woman they will certainly not behold the sun.
58.9: Before YOUR pots feel the I [ kindled] bramble, The live green as well as the burning, he will carry them off as a stormy wind.
58.10: The righteous one will rejoice because he has beheld the vengeance. His steps he will bathe in the blood of the wicked one.
58.11: And mankind will say: " Surely there is fruitage for the righteous one. Surely there exists a God that is judging in the earth. "

59.1: Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; From those rising up against me may you protect me.
59.2: Deliver me from the practicers of what is hurtful, And from bloodguilty men save me.
59.3: For, look! they have lain in wait for my soul; Strong ones make an attack upon me, For no revolt on my part, nor any sin on my part, O Jehovah.
59.4: Though there is no error, they run and get themselves ready. Do rouse yourself at my calling and see.
59.5: And you, O Jehovah God of armies, are the God of Israel. Do wake up to turn your attention to all the nations. Do not show favor to any hurtful traitors. Se'lah.
59.6: They keep returning at evening time; They keep barking like a dog and go all around the city.
59.7: Look! They make a bubbling forth with their mouth; Swords are on their lips, For who is listening?
59.8: But you yourself, O Jehovah, will laugh at them; You will hold all the nations in derision.
59.9: O my Strength, toward you I will keep watch; For God is my secure height.
59.10: The God of loving - kindness to me will himself confront me; God himself will cause me to look upon my foes.
59.11: Do not kill them, that my people may not forget. By your vital energy make them wander about, And bring them down, O our shield Jehovah,
59.12: I [ For] the sin of their mouth, the word of their lips; And may they be caught in their pride, Even for the cursing and the deception that they rehearse.
59.13: Bring I [ them] to an end in rage; Bring I [ them] to an end, that they may not be; And may they know that God is ruling in Jacob to the ends of the earth. Se'lah.
59.14: And let them return at evening time; Let them bark like a dog and go all around the city.
59.15: Let those very ones wander about for something to eat; Let them not be satisfied or stay overnight.
59.16: But as for me, I shall sing of your strength, And in the morning I shall joyfully tell about your loving - kindness. For you have proved to be a secure height for me And a place to which to flee in the day of my distress.
59.17: O my Strength, to you I will make melody, For God is my secure height, the God of loving - kindness to me.

60.1: O God, you have cast us off, you have broken through us, You have become incensed. You should restore us.
60.2: You have caused the earth to rock, you have split it open. Heal its breaches, for it has tottered.
60.3: You have caused your people to see hardship. You have made us drink wine sending us reeling.
60.4: You have given to those fearing you a signal To flee zigzag on account of the bow. Se'lah.
60.5: In order that your beloved ones may be rescued, O do save with your right hand and answer us.
60.6: God himself has spoken in his holiness: " I will exult, I will give out She'chem as a portion; And the low plain of Suc'coth I shall measure off.
60.7: Gil'e·ad belongs to me and Ma·nas'seh belongs to me, And E'phra·im is the fortress of my head one; Judah is my commander's staff.
60.8: Mo'ab is my washing pot. Over E'dom I shall throw my sandal. Over Phi·lis'ti·a I shall shout in triumph. "
60.9: Who will bring me to the besieged city? Who will certainly lead me as far as E'dom?
60.10: Is it not you, O God, who have cast us off And who do not go forth with our armies as God?
60.11: Do give us assistance from distress, As salvation by earthling man is worthless.
60.12: By God we shall gain vital energy, And he himself will tread down our adversaries.

61.1: Do hear, O God, my entreating cry. Do pay attention to my prayer.
61.2: From the extremity of the earth I shall cry, even to you, when my heart grows feeble. Onto a rock that is higher than I am may you lead me.
61.3: For you have proved to be a refuge for me, A strong tower in the face of the enemy.
61.4: I will be a guest in your tent for times indefinite; I will take refuge in the concealment of your wings. Se'lah.
61.5: For you yourself, O God, have listened to my vows. You have given I [ me] the possession of those fearing your name.
61.6: Days you will add to the days of the king; His years will be like generation after generation.
61.7: He will dwell to time indefinite before God; O assign loving - kindness and trueness, that these may safeguard him.
61.8: So I will make melody to your name forever, That I may pay my vows day after day.

62.1: Indeed toward God is my soul I [ waiting in] silence. From him my salvation is.
62.2: Indeed he is my rock and my salvation, my secure height; I shall not be made to totter very much.
62.3: How long will YOU carry on frantically against the man whom YOU would murder? All of YOU are like a leaning wall, a stone wall that is being pushed in.
62.4: Indeed they give advice so as to allure from one's own dignity; They take pleasure in a lie. With their mouth they bless, but inside themselves they call down evil. Se'lah.
62.5: Indeed toward God wait silently, O my soul, Because from him is my hope.
62.6: Indeed he is my rock and my salvation, my secure height; I shall not be made to totter.
62.7: Upon God are my salvation and my glory. My strong rock, my refuge is in God.
62.8: Trust in him at all times, O people. Before him pour out YOUR heart. God is a refuge for us. Se'lah.
62.9: Indeed the sons of earthling man are an exhalation, The sons of mankind are a lie. When laid upon the scales they are all together lighter than an exhalation.
62.10: Do not put YOUR trust in defrauding, Nor become vain in sheer robbery. In case the means of maintenance should thrive, do not set YOUR heart I [ on them].
62.11: Once God has spoken, twice I have heard even this, That strength belongs to God.
62.12: Also loving - kindness belongs to you, O Jehovah, For you yourself pay back to each one according to his work.

63.1: O God, you are my God, I keep looking for you. My soul does thirst for you. For you my flesh has grown faint I [ with longing] In a land dry and exhausted, where there is no water.
63.2: Thus I have beheld you in the holy place, At seeing your strength and your glory.
63.3: Because your loving - kindness is better than life, My own lips will commend you.
63.4: Thus I shall bless you during my lifetime; In your name I shall raise my palms.
63.5: As with the best part, even fatness, my soul is satisfied, And with lips of joyful cries my mouth offers praise.
63.6: When I have remembered you upon my lounge, During the night watches I meditate on you.
63.7: For you have proved to be of assistance to me, And in the shadow of your wings I cry out joyfully.
63.8: My soul has closely followed you; On me your right hand keeps fast hold.
63.9: As for those who keep seeking my soul for I [ its] ruin, They will come into the lowest parts of the earth.
63.10: They will be delivered over to the power of the sword; They will become a mere portion for foxes.
63.11: And the king himself will rejoice in God. Every one swearing by him will boast, For the mouth of those speaking falsehood will be stopped up.

64.1: Hear, O God, my voice in my concern. From the dreadfulness of the enemy may you safeguard my life.
64.2: May you conceal me from the confidential talk of evildoers, From the tumult of practicers of hurtfulness,
64.3: Who have sharpened their tongue just like a sword, Who have aimed their arrow, bitter speech,
64.4: To shoot from concealed places at someone blameless. All of a sudden they shoot at him and do not fear.
64.5: They hold themselves down to bad speech; They make statements about hiding traps. They have said: " Who sees them? "
64.6: They keep searching out unrighteous things; They have hidden a shrewd device well searched out, And the inward part of each one, even I [ his] heart, is deep.
64.7: But God will shoot at them with an arrow suddenly. Wounds have resulted to them,
64.8: And they cause one to stumble. I [ But] their tongue is against their own selves. All those looking upon them will shake their head,
64.9: And all earthling men will become afraid; And they will tell of the activity of God, And they will certainly have insight into his work.
64.10: And the righteous one will rejoice in Jehovah and will indeed take refuge in him; And all the upright in heart will boast.

65.1: For you there is praise - silence -, O God, in Zion; And to you the vow will be paid.
65.2: O Hearer of prayer, even to you people of all flesh will come.
65.3: Things of error have proved mightier than I am. As for our transgressions, you yourself will cover them.
65.4: Happy is the one you choose and cause to approach, That he may reside in your courtyards. We will certainly be satisfied with the goodness of your house, The holy place of your temple.
65.5: With fear - inspiring things in righteousness you will answer us, O God of our salvation, The Trust of all the borders of the earth and those far away on the sea.
65.6: He is firmly establishing the mountains with his power; He is indeed girded with mightiness.
65.7: He is stilling the noise of the seas, The noise of their waves and the turmoil of the national groups.
65.8: And the inhabitants of the uttermost parts will be afraid of your signs; The goings forth of the morning and evening you cause to cry out joyfully.
65.9: You have turned your attention to the earth, that you may give it abundance; You enrich it very much. The stream from God is full of water. You prepare their grain, For that is the way you prepare the earth.
65.10: There is a drenching of its furrows, a leveling off of its clods; With copious showers you soften it; you bless its very sprouts.
65.11: You have crowned the year with your goodness, And your very tracks drip with fatness.
65.12: The pasture grounds of the wilderness keep dripping, And with joyfulness the very hills gird themselves.
65.13: The pastures have become clothed with flocks, And the low plains themselves are enveloped with grain. They shout in triumph, yes, they sing.

66.1: Shout in triumph to God, all I [ YOU people of] the earth.
66.2: Make melody to the glory of his name. Render his praise glorious.
66.3: Say to God: " How fear - inspiring your works are! Because of the abundance of your strength your enemies will come cringing to you.
66.4: All I [ people of] the earth will bow down to you, And they will make melody to you, they will make melody to your name. " Se'lah.
66.5: Come, YOU people, and see the activities of God. His dealing with the sons of men is fear - inspiring.
66.6: He has changed the sea into dry land; Through the river they went crossing over on foot. There we began to rejoice in him.
66.7: He is ruling by his mightiness to time indefinite. Upon the nations his own eyes keep watch. As for those who are stubborn, let them not be exalted in themselves. Se'lah.
66.8: Bless our God, O YOU peoples, And cause the voice of praise to him to be heard.
66.9: He is setting our soul in life, And he has not allowed our foot to totter.
66.10: For you have examined us, O God; You have refined us as when refining silver.
66.11: You have brought us into a hunting net; You have put pressure on our hips.
66.12: You have made mortal man to ride over our head; We have come through fire and through water, And you proceeded to bring us forth to relief.
66.13: I shall come into your house with whole burnt offerings; I shall pay to you my vows
66.14: That my lips have opened up to say And that my mouth has spoken when I was in sore straits.
66.15: Whole burnt offerings of fatlings I shall offer up to you, With the sacrificial smoke of rams. I shall render up a bull with he - goats. Se'lah.
66.16: Come, listen, all YOU who fear God, and I will relate What he has done for my soul.
66.17: To him I called with my mouth, And there was an extolling with my tongue.
66.18: If I have regarded anything hurtful in my heart, Jehovah will not hear I [ me].
66.19: Truly God has heard; He has paid attention to the voice of my prayer.
66.20: Blessed be God, who has not turned aside my prayer, Nor his loving - kindness from me.

67.1: God himself will show us favor and bless us; He will make his face shine upon us - Se'lah -
67.2: That your way may be known in the earth, Your salvation even among all the nations.
67.3: Let peoples laud you, O God; Let the peoples, all of them, laud you.
67.4: Let national groups rejoice and cry out joyfully, For you will judge the peoples with uprightness; And as for national groups, on the earth you will lead them. Se'lah.
67.5: Let peoples laud you, O God; Let peoples, all of them, laud you.
67.6: The earth itself will certainly give its produce; God, our God, will bless us.
67.7: God will bless us, And all the ends of the earth will fear him.

68.1: Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered, And let those who intensely hate him flee because of him.
68.2: As smoke is driven away, may you drive I [ them] away; As wax melts because of the fire, Let the wicked ones perish from before God.
68.3: But as for the righteous, let them rejoice, Let them be elated before God, And let them exult with rejoicing.
68.4: Sing YOU to God, make melody to his name; Raise up I [ a song] to the One riding through the desert plains As Jah, which is his name; and jubilate before him;
68.5: A father of fatherless boys and a judge of widows Is God in his holy dwelling.
68.6: God is causing the solitary ones to dwell in a house; He is bringing forth prisoners into full prosperity. However, as for the stubborn, they have to reside in a scorched land.
68.7: O God, when you went forth before your people, When you marched through the desert - Se'lah -
68.8: The earth itself rocked, Heaven itself also dripped because of God; This Si'nai I [ rocked] because of God, the God of Israel.
68.9: A copious downpour you began causing to fall, O God; Your inheritance, even when it was weary - you yourself reinvigorated it.
68.10: Your tent community - they have dwelt in it; With your goodness you proceeded to make it ready for the afflicted one, O God.
68.11: Jehovah himself gives the saying; The women telling the good news are a large army.
68.12: Even the kings of armies flee, they flee. As for her who abides at home, she shares in the spoil.
68.13: Although YOU men kept lying between the I [ camp] ash heaps, There will be the wings of a dove covered with silver And its pinions with yellowish - green gold.
68.14: When the Almighty One scattered abroad the kings in it, It began to snow in Zal'mon.
68.15: The mountainous region of Ba'shan is a mountain of God; The mountainous region of Ba'shan is a mountain of peaks.
68.16: Why do YOU, O YOU mountains of peaks, keep watching enviously The mountain that God has desired for himself to dwell in? Even Jehovah himself will reside I [ there] forever.
68.17: The war chariots of God are in tens of thousands, thousands over and over again. Jehovah himself has come from Si'nai into the holy place.
68.18: You have ascended on high; You have carried away captives; You have taken gifts in the form of men, Yes, even the stubborn ones, to reside I [ among them], O Jah God.
68.19: Blessed be Jehovah, who daily carries the load for us, The I [ true] God of our salvation. Se'lah.
68.20: The I [ true] God is for us a God of saving acts; And to Jehovah the Sovereign Lord belong the ways out from death.
68.21: Indeed God himself will break the head of his enemies in pieces, The hairy crown of the head of anyone walking about in his guiltiness.
68.22: Jehovah has said: " From Ba'shan I shall bring back, I shall bring I [ them] back from the depths of the sea,
68.23: In order that you may wash your foot in blood, That the tongue of your dogs may have its portion from the enemies. "
68.24: They have seen your processions, O God, The processions of my God, my King, into the holy place.
68.25: The singers went in front, the players on stringed instruments after them; In between were the maidens beating tambourines.
68.26: In congregated throngs bless God, Jehovah, I [ O YOU who are] from the Source of Israel.
68.27: There is little Benjamin subduing them, The princes of Judah with their shouting crowd, The princes of Zeb'u·lun, the princes of Naph'ta·li.
68.28: Your God has laid command upon your strength. Do show strength, O God, you who have acted for us.
68.29: Because of your temple at Jerusalem, Kings will bring gifts to you yourself.
68.30: Rebuke the wild beast of the reeds, the assembly of bulls, With the calves of the peoples, each one stamping down on pieces of silver. He has scattered the peoples that take delight in fights.
68.31: Bronzeware things will come out of Egypt; Cush itself will quickly stretch out its hands I [ with gifts] to God.
68.32: O YOU kingdoms of the earth, sing to God, Make melody to Jehovah - Se'lah -
68.33: To the One riding on the ancient heaven of heavens. Lo! He sounds with his voice, a strong voice.
68.34: ASCRIBE strength to God. Over Israel his eminence is and his strength is in the clouds.
68.35: God is fear - inspiring out of your grand sanctuary. The God of Israel he is, giving strength, even might to the people. Blessed be God.

69.1: Save me, O God, for the waters have come clear to the soul.
69.2: I have sunk down in deep mire, where there is no standing ground. I have come into profound waters, And a flowing stream itself has washed me away.
69.3: I have become tired by my calling out; My throat has become hoarse. My eyes have failed while waiting for my God.
69.4: Those hating me without a cause have become even more than the hairs of my head. Those bringing me to silence, being my enemies for no reason, have become numerous. What I had not taken by robbery I then proceeded to give back.
69.5: O God, you yourself have come to know my foolishness, And from you my own guiltiness has not been hidden.
69.6: O may those hoping in you not be ashamed because of me, O Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of armies. O may those seeking you not be humiliated because of me, O God of Israel.
69.7: For on your account I have borne reproach, Humiliation has covered my face.
69.8: I have become one estranged to my brothers, And a foreigner to the sons of my mother.
69.9: For sheer zeal for your house has eaten me up, And the very reproaches of those reproaching you have fallen upon me.
69.10: And I proceeded to weep with the fasting of my soul, But it came to be for reproaches to me.
69.11: When I made sackcloth my clothing, Then I became to them a proverbial saying.
69.12: Those sitting in the gate began concerning themselves about me, And I [ I was] the subject of the songs of drinkers of intoxicating liquor.
69.13: But as for me, my prayer was to you, O Jehovah, At an acceptable time, O God. In the abundance of your loving - kindness answer me with the truth of salvation by you.
69.14: Deliver me from the mire, that I may not sink down. O may I be delivered from those hating me and from the deep waters.
69.15: O may not the flowing stream of waters wash me away, Nor the depth swallow me up, Nor the well close its mouth over me.
69.16: Answer me, O Jehovah, for your loving - kindness is good. According to the multitude of your mercies turn to me,
69.17: And do not conceal your face from your servant. Because I am in sore straits, answer me quickly.
69.18: Do come near to my soul, reclaim it; On account of my enemies redeem me.
69.19: You yourself have come to know my reproach and my shame and my humiliation. All those showing hostility to me are in front of you.
69.20: Reproach itself has broken my heart, and I [ the wound] is incurable. And I kept hoping for someone to show sympathy, but there was none; And for comforters, but I found none.
69.21: But for food they gave I [ me] a poisonous plant, And for my thirst they tried to make me drink vinegar.
69.22: Let their table before them become a trap, And what is for their welfare a snare.
69.23: Let their eyes become darkened so as not to see; And cause their very hips to wobble constantly.
69.24: Pour out upon them your denunciation, And may your own burning anger overtake them.
69.25: Let their walled camp become desolate; In their tents may there come to be no dweller.
69.26: For the one whom you yourself have struck they have pursued, And the pains of those pierced by you they keep recounting.
69.27: Do give error upon their error, And may they not come into your righteousness.
69.28: Let them be wiped out of the book of the living ones, And with the righteous ones may they not be written in.
69.29: But I am afflicted and aching. May your own salvation, O God, protect me.
69.30: I will praise the name of God with song, And I will magnify him with thanksgiving.
69.31: This will also be more pleasing to Jehovah than a bull, Than a young bull displaying horns, splitting the hoof.
69.32: The meek ones will certainly see I [ it]; they will rejoice. YOU who are seeking God, let YOUR heart also keep alive.
69.33: For Jehovah is listening to the poor ones, And he will indeed not despise his very own prisoners.
69.34: Let heaven and earth praise him, The seas and everything moving about in them.
69.35: For God himself will save Zion And will build the cities of Judah; And they will certainly dwell there and take possession of it.
69.36: And the offspring of his servants themselves will inherit it, And those loving his name will be the ones to reside in it.

70.1: O God, to deliver me, O Jehovah, to my assistance do make haste.
70.2: May those be ashamed and abashed who are seeking my soul. May those turn back and be humiliated who are taking delight in my calamity.
70.3: May those go back by reason of their shame who are saying: " Aha, aha! "
70.4: May those exult and rejoice in you, all of whom are seeking you, And may they say constantly: " God be magnified! " - those loving your salvation.
70.5: But I am afflicted and poor. O God, do act quickly for me. You are my help and the Provider of escape for me. O Jehovah, do not be too late.

71.1: In you, O Jehovah, I have taken refuge. O may I never be ashamed.
71.2: In your righteousness may you deliver me and provide me with escape. Incline to me your ear and save me.
71.3: Become to me a rock fortress into which to enter constantly. You must command to save me, For you are my crag and my stronghold.
71.4: O my God, provide me with escape from the hand of the wicked one, From the palm of the one acting unjustly and oppressively.
71.5: For you are my hope, O Sovereign Lord Jehovah, my confidence from my youth.
71.6: Upon you I have supported myself from the belly; You are the One severing me even from the inward parts of my mother. In you my praise is constantly.
71.7: I have become just like a miracle to many people; But you are my strong refuge.
71.8: My mouth is filled with your praise, All day long with your beauty.
71.9: Do not throw me away in the time of old age; Just when my power is failing, do not leave me.
71.10: For my enemies have said in regard to me, And the very ones keeping watch for my soul have jointly exchanged counsel,
71.11: Saying: " God himself has left him. Pursue and catch him, for there is no deliverer. "
71.12: O God, do not keep far away from me. O my God, do hurry to my assistance.
71.13: May those be ashamed, may those come to their end, who are resisting my soul. May those cover themselves with reproach and humiliation who are seeking calamity for me.
71.14: But as for me, I shall wait constantly, And I will add to all your praise.
71.15: My own mouth will recount your righteousness, All day long your salvation, For I have not come to know the numbers I [ of them].
71.16: I shall come in grand mightiness, O Sovereign Lord Jehovah; I shall mention your righteousness, yours alone.
71.17: O God, you have taught me from my youth on, And until now I keep telling about your wonderful works.
71.18: And even until old age and gray - headedness, O God, do not leave me, Until I may tell about your arm to the generation, To all those who are to come, about your mightiness.
71.19: Your righteousness, O God, is up to the height; As respects the great things that you have done, O God, who is like you?
71.20: Because you have made me see many distresses and calamities, May you revive me again; And from the watery deeps of the earth may you again bring me up.
71.21: May you enlarge my greatness, And may you surround I [ and] comfort me.
71.22: I too, I shall laud you on an instrument of a stringed sort, As regards your trueness, O my God. I will make melody to you on the harp, O Holy One of Israel.
71.23: My lips will cry out joyfully when I am inclined to make melody to you, Even my soul that you have redeemed.
71.24: Also, my own tongue, all day long, will utter in an undertone your righteousness, For they have become ashamed, for they have become abashed, who are seeking calamity for me.

72.1: O God, give your own judicial decisions to the king, And your righteousness to the son of the king.
72.2: May he plead the cause of your people with righteousness And of your afflicted ones with judicial decision.
72.3: Let the mountains carry peace to the people, Also the hills, through righteousness.
72.4: Let him judge the afflicted ones of the people, Let him save the sons of the poor one, And let him crush the defrauder.
72.5: They will fear you as long as there is a sun, And before the moon for generation after generation.
72.6: He will descend like the rain upon the mown grass, Like copious showers that wet the earth.
72.7: In his days the righteous one will sprout, And the abundance of peace until the moon is no more.
72.8: And he will have subjects from sea to sea And from the River to the ends of the earth.
72.9: Before him the inhabitants of waterless regions will bow down, And his very enemies will lick the dust itself.
72.10: The kings of Tar'shish and of the islands - Tribute they will pay. The kings of She'ba and of Se'ba - A gift they will present.
72.11: And to him all the kings will prostrate themselves; All the nations, for their part, will serve him.
72.12: For he will deliver the poor one crying for help, Also the afflicted one and whoever has no helper.
72.13: He will feel sorry for the lowly one and the poor one, And the souls of the poor ones he will save.
72.14: From oppression and from violence he will redeem their soul, And their blood will be precious in his eyes.
72.15: And let him live, and to him let some of the gold of She'ba be given. And in his behalf let prayer be made constantly; All day long let him be blessed.
72.16: There will come to be plenty of grain on the earth; On the top of the mountains there will be an overflow. His fruit will be as in Leb'a·non, And those who are from the city will blossom like the vegetation of the earth.
72.17: Let his name prove to be to time indefinite; Before the sun let his name have increase, And by means of him let them bless themselves; Let all nations pronounce him happy.
72.18: Blessed be Jehovah God, Israel's God, Who alone is doing wonderful works.
72.19: And blessed be his glorious name to time indefinite, And let his glory fill the whole earth. Amen and Amen.
72.20: The prayers of David, the son of Jes'se, have come to their end.

73.1: God is indeed good to Israel, to those clean in heart.
73.2: As for me, my feet had almost turned aside, My steps had nearly been made to slip.
73.3: For I became envious of the boasters, I [ When] I would see the very peace of wicked people.
73.4: For they have no deathly pangs; And their paunch is fat.
73.5: They are not even in the trouble of mortal man, And they are not plagued the same as other men.
73.6: Therefore haughtiness has served as a necklace to them; Violence envelops them as a garment.
73.7: Their eye has bulged from fatness; They have exceeded the imaginations of the heart.
73.8: They scoff and speak about what is bad; About defrauding they speak in an elevated style.
73.9: They have put their mouth in the very heavens, And their tongue itself walks about in the earth.
73.10: Therefore he brings his people back hither, And the waters of what is full are drained out for them.
73.11: And they have said: " How has God come to know? And does there exist knowledge in the Most High? "
73.12: Look! These are the wicked, who are at ease indefinitely. They have increased I [ their] means of maintenance.
73.13: Surely it is in vain that I have cleansed my heart And that I wash my hands in innocence itself.
73.14: And I came to be plagued all day long, And my correction is every morning.
73.15: If I had said: " I will tell a story like that, " Look! against the generation of your sons I should have acted treacherously.
73.16: And I kept considering so as to know this; It was a trouble in my eyes,
73.17: Until I proceeded to come into the grand sanctuary of God. I wanted to discern their future.
73.18: Surely on slippery ground is where you place them. You have made them fall to ruins.
73.19: O how they have become an object of astonishment as in a moment! I [ How] they have reached their end, have been brought to their finish through sudden terrors!
73.20: Like a dream after awaking, O Jehovah, I [ So] when arousing I [ yourself] you will despise their very image.
73.21: For my heart was soured And in my kidneys I was sharply pained,
73.22: And I was unreasoning and I could not know; I became as mere beasts from your standpoint.
73.23: But I am constantly with you; You have taken hold of my right hand.
73.24: With your counsel you will lead me, And afterward you will take me even to glory.
73.25: Whom do I have in the heavens? And besides you I do have no other delight on the earth.
73.26: My organism and my heart have failed. God is the rock of my heart and my share to time indefinite.
73.27: For, look! the very ones keeping away from you will perish. You will certainly silence every one immorally leaving you.
73.28: But as for me, the drawing near to God is good for me. In the Sovereign Lord Jehovah I have placed my refuge, To declare all your works.

74.1: Why, O God, have you cast off forever? Why does your anger keep smoking against the flock of your pasturage?
74.2: Remember your assembly that you acquired long ago, The tribe that you redeemed as your inheritance, This Mount Zion in which you have resided.
74.3: Do lift up your steps to the long - lasting desolations. Everything the enemy has treated badly in the holy place.
74.4: Those showing hostility to you have roared in the middle of your meeting place. They have set their own signs as I [ the] signs.
74.5: One is notorious in being like him that brings up axes on high against a thicket of trees.
74.6: And now the very engravings of it, one and all, they strike even with hatchet and iron - tipped beams.
74.7: They have thrust your sanctuary into the fire itself. They have profaned the tabernacle of your name to the very earth.
74.8: They, even their offspring, have said together in their own heart: " All the meeting places of God must be burned in the land. "
74.9: Our signs we have not seen; there is no prophet anymore, And there is no one with us knowing how long.
74.10: How long, O God, will the adversary keep reproaching? Will the enemy keep treating your name with disrespect forever?
74.11: Why do you keep your hand, even your right hand, withdrawn From the midst of your bosom to make an end I [ of us]?
74.12: And yet God is my King from long ago, The One performing grand salvation in the midst of the earth.
74.13: You yourself stirred up the sea with your own strength; You broke the heads of the sea monsters in the waters.
74.14: You yourself crushed to pieces the heads of Le·vi'a·than. You proceeded to give it as food to the people, to those inhabiting the waterless regions.
74.15: You were the One that split the spring and the torrent; You yourself dried up ever - flowing rivers.
74.16: To you the day belongs; also, to you the night belongs. You yourself prepared the luminary, even the sun.
74.17: It was you that set up all the boundaries of the earth; Summer and winter - you yourself formed them.
74.18: Remember this: The enemy himself has reproached, O Jehovah, And a senseless people have treated your name with disrespect.
74.19: Do not give to the wild beast the soul of your turtledove. Do not forget the very life of your afflicted ones forever.
74.20: Take a look at the covenant, For the dark places of the earth have become full of the abodes of violence.
74.21: O may the crushed one not return humiliated. May the afflicted one and the poor one praise your name.
74.22: Do arise, O God, do conduct your own case at law. Remember your reproach from the senseless one all day long.
74.23: Do not forget the voice of those showing hostility to you. The noise of those rising up against you is ascending constantly.

75.1: We give thanks to you, O God; we give thanks to you, And your name is near. Men have to declare your wondrous works.
75.2: " For I proceeded to take a set time; I myself began judging with uprightness.
75.3: The earth and all its inhabitants being dissolved, It was I that adjusted its pillars. " Se'lah.
75.4: I said to the foolish ones: " Do not be foolish, " And to the wicked ones: " Do not exalt the horn.
75.5: Do not exalt YOUR horn on high. Do not speak with an arrogant neck.
75.6: For neither from the east nor from the west, Nor from the south is there an exalting.
75.7: For God is the judge. This one he abases, and that one he exalts.
75.8: For there is a cup in the hand of Jehovah, And the wine is foaming, it is full of mixture. And he will surely pour out its dregs from it; All the wicked ones of the earth will drain I [ them] out, drink I [ them]. "
75.9: But as for me, I shall tell I [ of it] to time indefinite; I will make melody to the God of Jacob.
75.10: And all the horns of the wicked ones I shall cut down. The horns of the righteous one will be exalted.

76.1: God is known in Judah; In Israel his name is great.
76.2: And his covert proves to be in Sa'lem itself, And his dwelling place in Zion.
76.3: There he broke the flaming shafts of the bow, The shield and the sword and the battle. Se'lah.
76.4: You are enveloped with light, more majestic than the mountains of prey.
76.5: The ones powerful in heart have been despoiled, They have drowsed away to their sleep, And none of all the valiant men have found their hands.
76.6: From your rebuke, O God of Jacob, both the charioteer and the horse have fallen fast asleep.
76.7: You - fear - inspiring you are, And who can stand before you because of the strength of your anger?
76.8: From heaven you caused the legal contest to be heard; The earth itself feared and kept quiet
76.9: When God rose up to judgment, To save all the meek of the earth. Se'lah.
76.10: For the very rage of man will laud you; The remainder of raging you will gird upon yourself.
76.11: Vow and pay to Jehovah YOUR God, all YOU who are round about him. Let them bring a gift in fear.
76.12: He will humble the spirit of leaders; Fear - inspiring he is to the kings of the earth.

77.1: With my voice I will even cry out to God himself, With my voice to God, and he will certainly give ear to me.
77.2: In the day of my distress I have searched for Jehovah himself. At night my very hand has been stretched out and does not grow numb; My soul has refused to be comforted.
77.3: I will remember God and be boisterous; I will show concern, that my spirit may faint away. Se'lah.
77.4: You have seized hold of my eyelids; I have become agitated, and I cannot speak.
77.5: I have thought upon the days of long ago, On the years in the indefinite past.
77.6: I will remember my string music in the night; With my heart I will show concern, And my spirit will carefully search.
77.7: Will it be to times indefinite that Jehovah keeps casting off, And will he no more be pleased again?
77.8: Has his loving - kindness terminated forever? Has I [ his] saying come to nothing for generation after generation?
77.9: Has God forgotten to be favorable, Or has he shut off his mercies in anger? Se'lah.
77.10: And shall I keep saying: " This is what pierces me through, The changing of the right hand of the Most High "?
77.11: I shall remember the practices of Jah; For I will remember your marvelous doing of long ago.
77.12: And I shall certainly meditate on all your activity, And with your dealings I will concern myself.
77.13: O God, your way is in the holy place. Who is a great God like God?
77.14: You are the I [ true] God, doing marvelously. Among the peoples you have made your strength known.
77.15: With I [ your] arm you have recovered your people, The sons of Jacob and of Joseph. Se'lah.
77.16: The waters have seen you, O God, The waters have seen you; they began to be in severe pains. Also, the watery deeps began to be agitated.
77.17: The clouds have thunderously poured down water; A sound the cloudy skies have given forth. Also, your own arrows proceeded to go here and there.
77.18: The sound of your thunder was like chariot wheels; Lightnings have lighted up the productive land; The earth became agitated and began to rock.
77.19: Through the sea your way was, And your path was through many waters; And your very footprints have not come to be known.
77.20: You have led your people just like a flock, By the hand of Moses and Aaron.

78.1: Do give ear, O my people, to my law; Incline YOUR ear to the sayings of my mouth.
78.2: In a proverbial saying I will open my mouth; I will cause riddles of long ago to bubble forth,
78.3: Which we have heard and know, And which our own fathers have related to us;
78.4: Which we do not hide from their sons, Relating I [ them] even to the generation to come, The praises of Jehovah and his strength And his wonderful things that he has done.
78.5: And he proceeded to raise up a reminder in Jacob, And a law he set in Israel, Things that he commanded our forefathers, To make them known to their sons;
78.6: In order that the generation to come, the sons that were to be born, might know I [ them], That they might rise up and relate I [ them] to their sons,
78.7: And that they might set their confidence in God himself And not forget the practices of God but observe his own commandments.
78.8: And they should not become like their forefathers, A generation stubborn and rebellious, A generation who had not prepared their heart And whose spirit was not trustworthy with God.
78.9: The sons of E'phra·im, though armed shooters of the bow, Retreated in the day of fight.
78.10: They did not keep the covenant of God, And in his law they refused to walk.
78.11: They also began to forget his dealings And his wonderful works that he caused them to see.
78.12: In front of their forefathers he had done marvelously In the land of Egypt, the field of Zo'an.
78.13: He split the sea, that he might let them pass over, And he caused the waters to stand like a dam.
78.14: And he continued to lead them with a cloud by day And the whole night with a light of fire.
78.15: He proceeded to split rocks in the wilderness, That he might cause I [ them] to drink an abundance just like watery deeps.
78.16: And he went bringing forth streams out of a crag And causing waters to descend just like rivers.
78.17: And they kept sinning still more against him By rebelling against the Most High in the waterless region;
78.18: And they proceeded to test God in their heart By asking for something to eat for their soul.
78.19: So they began to speak against God. They said: " Is God able to arrange a table in the wilderness? "
78.20: Look! He struck a rock That waters might flow and torrents themselves might flood forth. " Is he able also to give bread itself, Or can he prepare sustenance for his people? "
78.21: That was why Jehovah heard and began to be furious; And fire itself was kindled against Jacob, And anger also ascended against Israel.
78.22: For they did not put faith in God, And they did not trust in salvation by him.
78.23: And he proceeded to command the cloudy skies above, And he opened the very doors of heaven.
78.24: And he kept raining upon them manna to eat, And the grain of heaven he gave to them.
78.25: Men ate the very bread of powerful ones; Provisions he sent them to satisfaction.
78.26: He began making an east wind burst forth in the heavens And making a south wind blow by his own strength.
78.27: And he proceeded to make sustenance rain upon them just like dust, Even winged flying creatures just like the sand grains of the seas.
78.28: And he kept making I [ them] fall in the middle of his camp, All around his tabernacles.
78.29: And they went eating and satisfying themselves very much, And what they desired he proceeded to bring to them.
78.30: They had not turned aside from their desire, While their food was yet in their mouth,
78.31: When God's wrath itself ascended against them. And he went killing among their stout ones; And the young men of Israel he made collapse.
78.32: Despite all this they sinned some more And did not put faith in his wonderful works.
78.33: So he brought their days to an end as if a mere exhalation, And their years by the disturbance.
78.34: As often as he killed them, they also inquired for him, And they returned and looked for God.
78.35: And they began to remember that God was their Rock, And that God the Most High was their Avenger.
78.36: And they tried to fool him with their mouth; And with their tongue they tried to lie to him.
78.37: And their heart was not steadfast with him; And they did not prove faithful in his covenant.
78.38: But he was merciful; he would cover the error and not bring ruin. And many times he made his anger turn back, And he would not rouse up all his rage.
78.39: And he kept remembering that they were flesh, That the spirit is going forth and does not come back.
78.40: How often they would rebel against him in the wilderness, They would make him feel hurt in the desert!
78.41: And again and again they would put God to the test, And they pained even the Holy One of Israel.
78.42: They did not remember his hand, The day that he redeemed them from the adversary,
78.43: How he put his signs in Egypt itself And his miracles in the field of Zo'an;
78.44: And how he began changing to blood their Nile canals, So that they could not drink from their own streams.
78.45: He proceeded to send upon them gadflies, that these might eat them up; And frogs, that these might bring them to ruin.
78.46: And he began to give to the cockroaches their yield, And their toil to the locusts.
78.47: He went killing their vine even by the hail And their sycamore trees by hailstones.
78.48: And he proceeded to hand over their beasts of burden even to the hail And their livestock to the flaming fever.
78.49: He went sending upon them his burning anger, Fury and denunciation and distress, Deputations of angels bringing calamity.
78.50: He proceeded to prepare a pathway for his anger. He did not hold back their soul from death itself; And their life he handed over even to the pestilence.
78.51: Finally he struck down all the firstborn in Egypt, The beginning of their generative power in the tents of Ham.
78.52: Afterward he caused his people to depart just like a flock, And conducted them like a drove in the wilderness.
78.53: And he kept leading them in security, and they felt no dread; And the sea covered their enemies themselves.
78.54: And he proceeded to bring them to his holy territory, This mountainous region that his right hand acquired.
78.55: And because of them he gradually drove out the nations, And by the measuring line he went allotting them an inheritance, So that he caused the tribes of Israel to reside in their own homes.
78.56: And they began to test and rebel against God the Most High, And his reminders they did not keep.
78.57: They also kept turning back and acting treacherously like their forefathers; They turned around like a loose bow.
78.58: And they kept offending him with their high places, And with their graven images they kept inciting him to jealousy.
78.59: God heard and got to be furious, And so he contemned Israel very much.
78.60: And he finally forsook the tabernacle of Shi'loh, The tent in which he resided among earthling men.
78.61: And he proceeded to give his strength even to captivity And his beauty into the hand of the adversary.
78.62: And he kept handing over his people to the sword itself, And against his inheritance he became furious.
78.63: His young men a fire ate up, And his virgins were not praised.
78.64: As for his priests, they fell by the very sword, And their own widows did not give way to weeping.
78.65: Then Jehovah began to awake as from sleeping, Like a mighty one sobering up from wine.
78.66: And he went striking down his adversaries from behind; A reproach of indefinite duration he gave to them.
78.67: And he proceeded to reject the tent of Joseph; And the tribe of E'phra·im he did not choose.
78.68: But he chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loved.
78.69: And he began to build his sanctuary just like the heights, Like the earth that he has founded to time indefinite.
78.70: And so he chose David his servant And took him from the pens of the flock.
78.71: From following the females giving suck He brought him in to be a shepherd over Jacob his people And over Israel his inheritance.
78.72: And he began to shepherd them according to the integrity of his heart, And with the skillfulness of his hands he began leading them.

79.1: O God, the nations have come into your inheritance; They have defiled your holy temple; They have laid Jerusalem in a heap of ruins.
79.2: They have given the dead body of your servants as food to the fowls of the heavens, The flesh of your loyal ones to the wild beasts of the earth.
79.3: They have poured out their blood like water All around Jerusalem, and there is no one to do the burying.
79.4: We have become a reproach to our neighbors, A derision and a jeering to those round about us.
79.5: How long, O Jehovah, will you be incensed? Forever? How long will your ardor burn just like fire?
79.6: Pour out your rage upon the nations that have not known you, And upon the kingdoms that have not called upon your own name.
79.7: For they have eaten up Jacob, And they have caused his own abiding place to be desolated.
79.8: Do not remember against us the errors of ancestors. Hurry! Let your mercies confront us, For we have become greatly impoverished.
79.9: Help us, O God of our salvation, For the sake of the glory of your name; And deliver us and cover over our sins on account of your name.
79.10: Why should the nations say: " Where is their God? " Among the nations let there be known before our eyes The avenging of the blood of your servants that has been shed.
79.11: May the sighing of the prisoner come in even before you. According to the greatness of your arm preserve those appointed to death.
79.12: And repay to our neighbors seven times into their bosom Their reproach with which they have reproached you, O Jehovah.
79.13: As for us your people and the flock of your pasturage, We shall give thanks to you to time indefinite; From generation to generation we shall declare your praise.

80.1: O Shepherd of Israel, do give ear, You who are conducting Joseph just like a flock. O you who are sitting upon the cherubs, do beam forth.
80.2: Before E'phra·im and Benjamin and Ma·nas'seh do rouse up your mightiness, And do come to our salvation.
80.3: O God, bring us back; And light up your face, that we may be saved.
80.4: O Jehovah God of armies, how long must you fume against the prayer of your people?
80.5: You have made them eat the bread of tears, And you keep making them drink tears upon tears in I [ great] measure.
80.6: You set us for strife to our neighbors, And our very enemies keep deriding as they please.
80.7: O God of armies, bring us back; And light up your face, that we may be saved.
80.8: You proceeded to make a vine depart from Egypt. You kept driving out the nations, that you might plant it.
80.9: You made a clearing before it, that it might take root and fill the land.
80.10: The mountains were covered with its shadow, And the cedars of God with its boughs.
80.11: It gradually sent forth its boughs as far as the sea, And to the River its twigs.
80.12: Why have you broken down its stone walls, And I [ why] have all those passing by on the road plucked at it?
80.13: A boar out of the woods keeps eating it away, And the animal throngs of the open field keep feeding upon it.
80.14: O God of armies, return, please; Look down from heaven and see and take care of this vine,
80.15: And the stock that your right hand has planted, And I [ look] upon the son whom you have made strong for yourself.
80.16: It is burned with fire, cut off. From the rebuke of your face they perish.
80.17: Let your hand prove to be upon the man of your right hand, Upon the son of mankind whom you have made strong for yourself,
80.18: And we shall not turn back from you. May you preserve us alive, that we may call upon your own name.
80.19: O Jehovah God of armies, bring us back; Light up your face, that we may be saved.

81.1: O cry out joyfully, YOU people, to God our strength; Shout in triumph to the God of Jacob.
81.2: Strike up a melody and take a tambourine, The pleasant harp together with the stringed instrument.
81.3: On the new moon, BLOW the horn; On the full moon, for the day of our festival.
81.4: For it is a regulation for Israel, A judicial decision of the God of Jacob.
81.5: As a reminder he laid it upon Joseph himself, When he was going forth over the land of Egypt. A language that I did not know I kept hearing.
81.6: " I turned aside his shoulder even from I [ the] burden; His own hands got to be free even from the basket.
81.7: In distress you called, and I proceeded to rescue you; I began to answer you in the concealed place of thunder. I went examining you at the waters of Mer'i·bah. Se'lah.
81.8: Hear, O my people, and I will bear witness against you, O Israel, if you will listen to me.
81.9: Among you there will prove to be no strange god; And you will not bow down to a foreign god.
81.10: I, Jehovah, am your God, The One bringing you up out of the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I shall fill it.
81.11: But my people has not listened to my voice; And Israel itself has not showed any willingness toward me.
81.12: And so I let them go in the stubbornness of their heart; They went walking in their own counsels.
81.13: O that my people were listening to me, O that Israel itself would walk in my very ways!
81.14: Their enemies I would easily subdue, And against their adversaries I would turn my hand.
81.15: As for those intensely hating Jehovah, they will come cringing to him, And their time will prove to be to time indefinite.
81.16: And he will keep feeding him off the fat of the wheat, And out of the rock I shall satisfy you with honey itself. "

82.1: God is stationing himself in the assembly of the Divine One; In the middle of the gods he judges:
82.2: " How long will YOU keep on judging with injustice And showing partiality to the wicked themselves? Se'lah.
82.3: Be judges for the lowly one and the fatherless boy. To the afflicted one and the one of little means do justice.
82.4: Provide escape for the lowly one and the poor one; Out of the hand of the wicked ones deliver I [ them]. "
82.5: They have not known, and they do not understand; In darkness they keep walking about; All the foundations of the earth are made to totter.
82.6: " I myself have said, 'YOU are gods, And all of YOU are sons of the Most High.
82.7: Surely YOU will die just as men do; And like any one of the princes YOU will fall! ' "
82.8: Do rise up, O God, do judge the earth; For you yourself should take possession of all the nations.

83.1: O God, let there be no silence on your part; Do not keep speechless, and do not stay quiet, O Divine One.
83.2: For, look! your very enemies are in an uproar; And the very ones intensely hating you have raised I [ their] head.
83.3: Against your people they cunningly carry on their confidential talk; And they conspire against your concealed ones.
83.4: They have said: " Come and let us efface them from being a nation, That the name of Israel may be remembered no more. "
83.5: For with the heart they have unitedly exchanged counsel; Against you they proceeded to conclude even a covenant,
83.6: The tents of E'dom and the Ish'ma·el·ites, Mo'ab and the Hag'rites,
83.7: Ge'bal and Am'mon and Am'a·lek, Phi·lis'ti·a together with the inhabitants of Tyre.
83.8: Also, As·syr'i·a itself has become joined with them; They have become an arm to the sons of Lot. Se'lah.
83.9: Do to them as to Mid'i·an, as to Sis'e·ra, As to Ja'bin at the torrent valley of Ki'shon.
83.10: They were annihilated at En - dor; They became manure for the ground.
83.11: As for their nobles, make these like O'reb and like Ze'eb, And like Ze'bah and like Zal·mun'na all their dukes,
83.12: Who have said: " Let us take possession of the abiding places of God for ourselves. "
83.13: O my God, make them like a thistle whirl, Like stubble before a wind.
83.14: Like a fire that burns up the forest And like a flame that scorches the mountains,
83.15: In just that way may you pursue them with your tempest And may you disturb them with your own storm wind.
83.16: Fill their faces with dishonor, That people may search for your name, O Jehovah.
83.17: O may they be ashamed and be disturbed for all times, And may they become abashed and perish;
83.18: That people may know that you, whose name is Jehovah, You alone are the Most High over all the earth.

84.1: How lovely your grand tabernacle is, O Jehovah of armies!
84.2: My soul has yearned and also pined away for the courtyards of Jehovah. My own heart and my very flesh cry out joyfully to the living God.
84.3: Even the bird itself has found a house, And the swallow a nest for herself, Where she has put her young ones - Your grand altar, O Jehovah of armies, my King and my God!
84.4: Happy are those dwelling in your house! They still keep on praising you. Se'lah.
84.5: Happy are the men whose strength is in you, In whose heart are the highways.
84.6: Passing along through the low plain of the ba'ca bushes, They turn it into a spring itself; Even with blessings the instructor enwraps himself.
84.7: They will walk on from vital energy to vital energy; Each one appears to God in Zion.
84.8: O Jehovah God of armies, do hear my prayer; Do give ear, O God of Jacob. Se'lah.
84.9: O shield of ours, see, O God, And look upon the face of your anointed one.
84.10: For a day in your courtyards is better than a thousand I [ elsewhere]. I have chosen to stand at the threshold in the house of my God Rather than to move around in the tents of wickedness.
84.11: For Jehovah God is a sun and a shield; Favor and glory are what he gives. Jehovah himself will not hold back anything good from those walking in faultlessness.
84.12: O Jehovah of armies, happy is the man that is trusting in you.

85.1: You have taken pleasure, O Jehovah, in your land; You have brought back the ones taken captive of Jacob.
85.2: You have pardoned the error of your people; You have covered all their sin. Se'lah.
85.3: You have controlled all your fury; You have turned back from the heat of your anger.
85.4: Gather us back, O God of our salvation, And break off your vexation with us.
85.5: Is it to time indefinite that you will be incensed at us? Will you draw out your anger to generation after generation?
85.6: Will you yourself not enliven us again, That your people themselves may rejoice in you?
85.7: Show us, O Jehovah, your loving - kindness, And your salvation may you give to us.
85.8: I will hear what the I [ true] God Jehovah will speak, For he will speak peace to his people and to his loyal ones, But let them not return to self - confidence.
85.9: Surely his salvation is near to those fearing him, For glory to reside in our land.
85.10: As for loving - kindness and trueness, they have met each other; Righteousness and peace - they have kissed each other.
85.11: Trueness itself will sprout out of the very earth, And righteousness itself will look down from the very heavens.
85.12: Also, Jehovah, for his part, will give what is good, And our own land will give its yield.
85.13: Before him righteousness itself will walk, And it will make a way by his steppings.

86.1: Incline, O Jehovah, your ear. Answer me, For I am afflicted and poor.
86.2: O do guard my soul, for I am loyal. Save your servant - you are my God - that is trusting in you.
86.3: Show me favor, O Jehovah, For to you I keep calling all day long.
86.4: Make the soul of your servant rejoice, For to you, O Jehovah, I lift up my very soul.
86.5: For you, O Jehovah, are good and ready to forgive; And the loving - kindness to all those calling upon you is abundant.
86.6: Do give ear, O Jehovah, to my prayer; And do pay attention to the voice of my entreaties.
86.7: In the day of my distress I will call upon you, For you will answer me.
86.8: There is none like you among the gods, O Jehovah, Neither are there any works like yours.
86.9: All the nations whom you have made will themselves come, And they will bow down before you, O Jehovah, And will give glory to your name.
86.10: For you are great and are doing wondrous things; You are God, you alone.
86.11: Instruct me, O Jehovah, about your way. I shall walk in your truth. Unify my heart to fear your name.
86.12: I laud you, O Jehovah my God, with all my heart, And I will glorify your name to time indefinite,
86.13: For your loving - kindness is great toward me, And you have delivered my soul out of She'ol, its lowest place.
86.14: O God, the presumptuous ones themselves have risen up against me; And the very assembly of tyrannical ones have looked for my soul, And they have not set you in front of themselves.
86.15: But you, O Jehovah, are a God merciful and gracious, Slow to anger and abundant in loving - kindness and trueness.
86.16: Turn to me and show me favor. Do give your strength to your servant, And do save the son of your slave girl.
86.17: Work out with me a sign meaning goodness, That those hating me may see I [ it] and be ashamed. For you yourself, O Jehovah, have helped me and comforted me.

87.1: His foundation is in the holy mountains.
87.2: Jehovah is more in love with the gates of Zion Than with all the tabernacles of Jacob.
87.3: Glorious things are being spoken about you, O city of the I [ true] God. Se'lah.
87.4: I shall make mention of Ra'hab and Babylon as among those knowing me; Here are Phi·lis'ti·a and Tyre, together with Cush: " This is one who was born there. "
87.5: And respecting Zion it will be said: " Each and every one was born in her. " And the Most High himself will firmly establish her.
87.6: Jehovah himself will declare, when recording the peoples: " This is one who was born there. " Se'lah.
87.7: There will also be singers as well as dancers of circle dances: " All my springs are in you. "

88.1: O Jehovah, the God of my salvation, By day I have cried out, In the night I [ also] in front of you.
88.2: Before you my prayer will come. Incline your ear to my entreating cry.
88.3: For my soul has had enough of calamities, And my very life has come in touch even with She'ol.
88.4: I have been reckoned in among those going down to the pit; I have become like an able - bodied man without strength,
88.5: Set free among the dead themselves, Like slain ones lying in the burial place, Whom you have remembered no longer And who have been severed from your own I [ helping] hand.
88.6: You have put me in a pit of the lowest depths, In dark places, in a large abyss.
88.7: Upon me your rage has thrown itself, And with all your breaking waves you have afflicted I [ me]. Se'lah.
88.8: You have put my acquaintances far away from me; You have set me as something very detestable to them. I am under restraint and cannot go forth.
88.9: My own eye has languished because of my affliction. I have called on you, O Jehovah, all day long; To you I have spread out my palms.
88.10: For those who are dead will you do a marvel? Or will those impotent in death themselves arise, Will they laud you? Se'lah.
88.11: Will your loving - kindness be declared in the burial place itself, Your faithfulness in I [ the place of] destruction?
88.12: Will a marvel by you be known in the darkness itself, Or your righteousness in the land of oblivion?
88.13: And yet to you, O Jehovah, I myself have cried for help, And in the morning my own prayer keeps confronting you.
88.14: Why is it, O Jehovah, that you cast off my soul? Why do you keep your face concealed from me?
88.15: I am afflicted and about to expire from boyhood on; I have borne frightful things from you very much.
88.16: Over me your flashes of burning anger have passed; Terrors from you yourself have brought me to silence.
88.17: They have surrounded me like waters all day long; They have closed in upon me all at one time.
88.18: You have put far away from me friend and companion; My acquaintances are a dark place.

89.1: Jehovah's expressions of loving - kindness I will sing about even to time indefinite. For generation after generation I shall make your faithfulness known with my mouth.
89.2: For I have said: " Loving - kindness will stay built even to time indefinite; As for the heavens, you keep your faithfulness firmly established in them. "
89.3: " I have concluded a covenant toward my chosen one; I have sworn to David my servant,
89.4: 'Even to time indefinite I shall firmly establish your seed, And I will build your throne to generation after generation. ' " Se'lah.
89.5: And the heavens will laud your marvelous act, O Jehovah, Yes, your faithfulness in the congregation of the holy ones.
89.6: For who in the skies can be compared to Jehovah? Who can resemble Jehovah among the sons of God?
89.7: God is to be held in awe among the intimate group of holy ones; He is grand and fear - inspiring over all who are round about him.
89.8: O Jehovah God of armies, Who is vigorous like you, O Jah? And your faithfulness is all around you.
89.9: You are ruling over the swelling of the sea; When it raises up its waves you yourself calm them.
89.10: You yourself have crushed Ra'hab, even as someone slain. By the arm of your strength you have scattered your enemies.
89.11: Heaven is yours, the earth also is yours; The productive land and what fills it - you yourself have founded them.
89.12: The north and the south - you yourself created them; Ta'bor and Her'mon - in your name they cry out joyfully.
89.13: An arm with mightiness is yours, Your hand is strong, Your right hand is exalted.
89.14: Righteousness and judgment are the established place of your throne; Loving - kindness and trueness themselves come in before your face.
89.15: Happy are the people knowing the joyful shouting. O Jehovah, in the light of your face they keep walking.
89.16: In your name they are joyful all day long And in your righteousness they are exalted.
89.17: For you are the beauty of their strength; And by your goodwill our horn is exalted.
89.18: For our shield belongs to Jehovah, And our king belongs to the Holy One of Israel.
89.19: At that time you spoke in a vision to your loyal ones, And you proceeded to say: " I have placed help upon a mighty one; I have exalted a chosen one from among the people.
89.20: I have found David my servant; With my holy oil I have anointed him,
89.21: With whom my own hand will be firm, Whom my own arm also will strengthen.
89.22: No enemy will make exactions upon him, Neither will any son of unrighteousness afflict him.
89.23: And from before him I crushed his adversaries to pieces, And to those intensely hating him I kept dealing out blows.
89.24: And my faithfulness and my loving - kindness are with him, And in my name his horn is exalted.
89.25: And on the sea I have put his hand And on the rivers his right hand.
89.26: He himself calls out to me, 'You are my Father, My God and the Rock of my salvation. '
89.27: Also, I myself shall place him as firstborn, The most high of the kings of the earth.
89.28: To time indefinite I shall preserve my loving - kindness toward him, And my covenant will be faithful to him.
89.29: And I shall certainly set up his seed forever And his throne as the days of heaven.
89.30: If his sons leave my law And in my judicial decisions they do not walk,
89.31: If they profane my own statutes And they do not keep my own commandments,
89.32: I must also turn my attention to their transgression even with a rod And to their error even with strokes.
89.33: But my loving - kindness I shall not break off from him, Nor shall I prove false with regard to my faithfulness.
89.34: I shall not profane my covenant, And the expression out of my lips I shall not change.
89.35: Once I have sworn in my holiness, To David I will not tell lies.
89.36: His seed itself will prove to be even to time indefinite, And his throne as the sun in front of me.
89.37: As the moon it will be firmly established for time indefinite, And I [ as] a faithful witness in the skies. " Se'lah.
89.38: But you - you have cast off and you keep contemning; You have become furious toward your anointed one.
89.39: You have spurned the covenant of your servant; You have profaned his diadem to the very earth.
89.40: You have broken down all his stone pens; You have laid his fortifications in ruin.
89.41: All those passing along the way have pillaged him; He has become a reproach to his neighbors.
89.42: You have exalted the right hand of his adversaries; You have caused all his enemies to rejoice.
89.43: What is more, you again treat his sword as a foe, And you have caused him not to gain ground in the battle.
89.44: You have made I [ him] cease from his luster, And his throne you have hurled to the very earth.
89.45: You have shortened the days of his youth; You have enwrapped him with shame. Se'lah.
89.46: How long, O Jehovah, will you keep yourself concealed? For all time? Will your rage keep on burning just like a fire?
89.47: Remember of what duration of life I am. Is it all in vain that you have created all the sons of men?
89.48: What able - bodied man is there alive who will not see death? Can he provide escape for his soul from the hand of She'ol? Se'lah.
89.49: Where are your former acts of loving - kindness, O Jehovah, About which you swore to David in your faithfulness?
89.50: Remember, O Jehovah, the reproach upon your servants, My carrying in my bosom I [ the reproach of] all the many peoples,
89.51: How your enemies have reproached, O Jehovah, How they have reproached the footprints of your anointed one.
89.52: Blessed be Jehovah to time indefinite. Amen and Amen.

90.1: O Jehovah, you yourself have proved to be a real dwelling for us During generation after generation.
90.2: Before the mountains themselves were born, Or you proceeded to bring forth as with labor pains the earth and the productive land, Even from time indefinite to time indefinite you are God.
90.3: You make mortal man go back to crushed matter, And you say: " GO back, YOU sons of men. "
90.4: For a thousand years are in your eyes but as yesterday when it is past, And as a watch during the night.
90.5: You have swept them away; they become a mere sleep; In the morning I [ they are] just like green grass that changes.
90.6: In the morning it puts forth blossoms and must change; At evening it withers and certainly dries up.
90.7: For we have come to an end in your anger, And by your rage we have been disturbed.
90.8: You have set our errors right in front of you, Our hidden things before your bright face.
90.9: For all our days have come to their decline in your fury; We have finished our years just like a whisper.
90.10: In themselves the days of our years are seventy years; And if because of special mightiness they are eighty years, Yet their insistence is on trouble and hurtful things; For it must quickly pass by, and away we fly.
90.11: Who is there knowing the strength of your anger And your fury according to the fear of you?
90.12: Show I [ us] just how to count our days in such a way That we may bring a heart of wisdom in.
90.13: Do return, O Jehovah! How long will it be? And feel regret over your servants.
90.14: Satisfy us in the morning with your loving - kindness, That we may cry out joyfully and may rejoice during all our days.
90.15: Make us rejoice correspondingly to the days that you have afflicted us, The years that we have seen calamity.
90.16: May your activity appear to your own servants And your splendor upon their sons.
90.17: And let the pleasantness of Jehovah our God prove to be upon us, And the work of our hands do you firmly establish upon us. Yes, the work of our hands, do you firmly establish it.

91.1: Anyone dwelling in the secret place of the Most High Will procure himself lodging under the very shadow of the Almighty One.
91.2: I will say to Jehovah: " [ You are] my refuge and my stronghold, My God, in whom I will trust. "
91.3: For he himself will deliver you from the trap of the birdcatcher, From the pestilence causing adversities.
91.4: With his pinions he will block approach to you, And under his wings you will take refuge. His trueness will be a large shield and bulwark.
91.5: You will not be afraid of anything dreadful by night, Nor of the arrow that flies by day,
91.6: Nor of the pestilence that walks in the gloom, Nor of the destruction that despoils at midday.
91.7: A thousand will fall at your very side And ten thousand at your right hand; To you it will not come near.
91.8: Only with your eyes will you look on And see the retribution itself of the wicked ones.
91.9: Because you I [ said]: " Jehovah is my refuge, " You have made the Most High himself your dwelling;
91.10: No calamity will befall you, And not even a plague will draw near to your tent.
91.11: For he will give his own angels a command concerning you, To guard you in all your ways.
91.12: Upon their hands they will carry you, That you may not strike your foot against any stone.
91.13: Upon the young lion and the cobra you will tread; You will trample down the maned young lion and the big snake.
91.14: Because on me he has set his affection, I shall also provide him with escape. I shall protect him because he has come to know my name.
91.15: He will call upon me, and I shall answer him. I shall be with him in distress. I shall rescue him and glorify him.
91.16: With length of days I shall satisfy him, And I shall cause him to see salvation by me.

92.1: It is good to give thanks to Jehovah And to make melody to your name, O Most High;
92.2: To tell in the morning about your loving - kindness And about your faithfulness during the nights,
92.3: Upon a ten - stringed instrument and upon the lute, By resounding music on the harp.
92.4: For you have made me rejoice, O Jehovah, because of your activity; Because of the works of your hands I cry out joyfully.
92.5: How great your works are, O Jehovah! Very deep your thoughts are.
92.6: No unreasoning man himself can know I [ them], And no one stupid can understand this.
92.7: When the wicked ones sprout as the vegetation And all the practicers of what is hurtful blossom forth, It is that they may be annihilated forever.
92.8: But you are on high to time indefinite, O Jehovah.
92.9: For, look! your enemies, O Jehovah, For, look! your own enemies will perish; All the practicers of what is hurtful will be separated from one another.
92.10: But you will exalt my horn like that of a wild bull; I shall moisten I [ myself] with fresh oil.
92.11: And my eye will look on my foes; My ears will hear about the very ones who rise up against me, the evildoers.
92.12: The righteous himself will blossom forth as a palm tree does; As a cedar in Leb'a·non does, he will grow big.
92.13: Those who are planted in the house of Jehovah, In the courtyards of our God, they will blossom forth.
92.14: They will still keep on thriving during gray - headedness, Fat and fresh they will continue to be,
92.15: To tell that Jehovah is upright. I [ He is] my Rock, in whom there is no unrighteousness.

93.1: Jehovah himself has become king! With eminence he is clothed; Jehovah is clothed - with strength he has girded himself. The productive land also becomes firmly established so that it cannot be made to totter.
93.2: Your throne is firmly established from long ago; You are from time indefinite.
93.3: The rivers have raised, O Jehovah, The rivers have raised their sound; The rivers keep raising their pounding.
93.4: Above the sounds of vast waters, the majestic breaking waves of the sea, Jehovah is majestic in the height.
93.5: Your own reminders have proved very trustworthy. Holiness is befitting to your own house, O Jehovah, for length of days.

94.1: O God of acts of vengeance, Jehovah, O God of acts of vengeance, beam forth!
94.2: Raise yourself up, O Judge of the earth. Bring back a retribution upon the haughty ones.
94.3: How long are the wicked, O Jehovah, How long are the wicked themselves going to exult?
94.4: They keep bubbling forth, they keep speaking unrestrained; All the practicers of what is hurtful keep bragging about themselves.
94.5: Your people, O Jehovah, they keep crushing, And your inheritance they keep afflicting.
94.6: The widow and the alien resident they kill, And the fatherless boys they murder.
94.7: And they keep saying: " Jah does not see; And the God of Jacob does not understand I [ it]. "
94.8: Understand, YOU who are unreasoning among the people; And as for YOU stupid ones, when will YOU have any insight?
94.9: The One planting the ear, can he not hear? Or the One forming the eye, can he not look?
94.10: The One correcting the nations, can he not reprove, Even the One teaching men knowledge?
94.11: Jehovah is knowing the thoughts of men, that they are as an exhalation.
94.12: Happy is the able - bodied man whom you correct, O Jah, And whom you teach out of your own law,
94.13: To give him quietness from days of calamity, Until for the wicked one a pit is excavated.
94.14: For Jehovah will not forsake his people, Nor will he leave his own inheritance.
94.15: For judicial decision will return even to righteousness, And all the upright in heart will follow it.
