137.7: Remember, O Jehovah, regarding the sons of E'dom the day of Jerusalem, Who were saying: " Lay I [ it] bare! Lay I [ it] bare to the foundation within it! "
137.8: O daughter of Babylon, who are to be despoiled, Happy will he be that rewards you With your own treatment with which you treated us.
137.9: Happy will he be that grabs ahold and does dash to pieces Your children against the crag.

138.1: I shall laud you with all my heart. In front of other gods I shall make melody to you.
138.2: I shall bow down toward your holy temple, And I shall laud your name, Because of your loving - kindness and because of your trueness. For you have magnified your saying even above all your name.
138.3: On the day that I called, you also proceeded to answer me; You began to make me bold in my soul with strength.
138.4: All the kings of the earth will laud you, O Jehovah, For they will have heard the sayings of your mouth.
138.5: And they will sing about the ways of Jehovah, For the glory of Jehovah is great.
138.6: For Jehovah is high, and yet the humble one he sees; But the lofty one he knows only from a distance.
138.7: If I should walk in the midst of distress, you will preserve me alive. Because of the anger of my enemies you will thrust out your hand, And your right hand will save me.
138.8: Jehovah himself will complete what is in my behalf. O Jehovah, to time indefinite is your loving - kindness. Do not desert the works of your own hands.

139.1: O Jehovah, you have searched through me, and you know I [ me].
139.2: You yourself have come to know my sitting down and my rising up. You have considered my thought from far off.
139.3: My journeying and my lying outstretched you have measured off, And you have become familiar even with all my ways.
139.4: For there is not a word on my tongue, But, look! O Jehovah, you already know it all.
139.5: Behind and before, you have besieged me; And you place your hand upon me.
139.6: I [ Such] knowledge is too wonderful for me. It is so high up that I cannot attain to it.
139.7: Where can I go from your spirit, And where can I run away from your face?
139.8: If I should ascend to heaven, there you would be; And if I should spread out my couch in She'ol, look! you I [ would be there].
139.9: Were I to take the wings of the dawn, That I might reside in the most remote sea,
139.10: There, also, your own hand would lead me And your right hand would lay hold of me.
139.11: And were I to say: " Surely darkness itself will hastily seize me! " Then night would be light about me.
139.12: Even the darkness itself would not prove too dark for you, But night itself would shine just as the day does; The darkness might just as well be the light.
139.13: For you yourself produced my kidneys; You kept me screened off in the belly of my mother.
139.14: I shall laud you because in a fear - inspiring way I am wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful, As my soul is very well aware.
139.15: My bones were not hidden from you When I was made in secret, When I was woven in the lowest parts of the earth.
139.16: Your eyes saw even the embryo of me, And in your book all its parts were down in writing, As regards the days when they were formed And there was not yet one among them.
139.17: So, to me how precious your thoughts are! O God, how much does the grand sum of them amount to!
139.18: Were I to try to count them, they are more than even the grains of sand. I have awaked, and yet I am still with you.
139.19: O that you, O God, would slay the wicked one! Then even the bloodguilty men will certainly depart from me,
139.20: Who say things about you according to I [ their] idea; They have taken up I [ your name] in a worthless way - your adversaries.
139.21: Do I not hate those who are intensely hating you, O Jehovah, And do I not feel a loathing for those revolting against you?
139.22: With a complete hatred I do hate them. They have become to me real enemies.
139.23: Search through me, O God, and know my heart. Examine me, and know my disquieting thoughts,
139.24: And see whether there is in me any painful way, And lead me in the way of time indefinite.

140.1: Rescue me, O Jehovah, from bad men; May you safeguard me even from the man of deeds of violence,
140.2: Those who have schemed bad things in I [ their] heart, Who all day long keep attacking as in wars.
140.3: They have sharpened their tongue like that of a serpent; The venom of the horned viper is under their lips. Se'lah.
140.4: Keep me, O Jehovah, from the hands of the wicked one; May you safeguard me even from the man of deeds of violence, Those who have schemed to push my steps.
140.5: The self - exalted ones have hidden a trap for me; And ropes they have spread out as a net at the side of the track. Snares they have set for me. Se'lah.
140.6: I have said to Jehovah: " You are my God. Do give ear, O Jehovah, to the voice of my entreaties. "
140.7: O Jehovah the Sovereign Lord, the strength of my salvation, You have screened over my head in the day of the armed force.
140.8: Do not grant, O Jehovah, the cravings of the wicked one. Do not promote his plotting, that they may not be exalted. Se'lah.
140.9: As for the heads of those surrounding me, May the trouble of their own lips cover them.
140.10: May burning coals be dropped upon them. Let them be made to fall into the fire, into watery pits, that they may not get up.
140.11: The big talker - let him not be firmly established in the earth. The man of violence - let evil itself hunt him with repeated thrusts.
140.12: I well know that Jehovah will execute The legal claim of the afflicted one, the judgment of the poor ones.
140.13: Surely the righteous themselves will give thanks to your name; The upright ones will dwell before your face.

141.1: O Jehovah, I have called upon you. Do make haste to me. Do give ear to my voice when I call to you.
141.2: May my prayer be prepared as incense before you, The raising up of my palms as the evening grain offering.
141.3: Do set a guard, O Jehovah, for my mouth; Do set a watch over the door of my lips.
141.4: Do not incline my heart to anything bad, So as to carry on notorious deeds in wickedness With men who are practicing what is hurtful, That I may not feed myself on their dainties.
141.5: Should the righteous one strike me, it would be a loving - kindness; And should he reprove me, it would be oil upon the head, Which my head would not want to refuse. For still there would be even my prayer during their calamities.
141.6: Their judges have been thrown down by the sides of the crag, But they have heard my sayings, that they are pleasant.
141.7: As when one is doing cleaving and splitting on the earth, Our bones have been scattered at the mouth of She'ol.
141.8: However, my eyes are to you, O Jehovah the Sovereign Lord. In you I have taken refuge. Do not pour out my soul.
141.9: Keep me from the clutches of the trap that they have laid for me And from the snares of those practicing what is hurtful.
141.10: The wicked will fall into their own nets all together, While I, for my part, pass by.

142.1: With my voice, to Jehovah I proceeded to call for aid; With my voice, to Jehovah I began to cry for favor.
142.2: Before him I kept pouring out my concern; Before him I continued to tell about my own distress,
142.3: When my spirit fainted away within me. Then you yourself knew my roadway. In the path in which I walk They have hidden a trap for me.
142.4: Look to the right hand and see That there is no one giving any recognition to me. My place for flight has perished from me; There is no one inquiring for my soul.
142.5: I called to you, O Jehovah, for aid. I said: " You are my refuge, My share in the land of the living ones. "
142.6: Do pay attention to my entreating cry, For I have become very much impoverished. Deliver me from my persecutors, For they are stronger than I am.
142.7: Do bring my soul out of the very dungeon To laud your name. Around me let the righteous ones gather, Because you deal appropriately with me.

143.1: O Jehovah, hear my prayer; Do give ear to my entreaty. In your faithfulness answer me in your righteousness.
143.2: And do not enter into judgment with your servant; For before you no one alive can be righteous.
143.3: For the enemy has pursued my soul; He has crushed my life to the very earth. He has caused me to dwell in dark places like those dead for time indefinite.
143.4: And my spirit faints away within me; In the midst of me my heart shows itself numbed.
143.5: I have remembered days of long ago; I have meditated on all your activity; I willingly kept myself concerned with the work of your own hands.
143.6: I have spread out my hands to you; My soul is like an exhausted land to you. Se'lah.
143.7: O hurry, answer me, O Jehovah. My spirit has come to an end. Do not conceal your face from me, Or else I must become comparable with those going down into the pit.
143.8: In the morning cause me to hear your loving - kindness, For in you I have put my trust. Make known to me the way in which I should walk, For to you I have lifted up my soul.
143.9: Deliver me from my enemies, O Jehovah. I have taken cover even with you.
143.10: Teach me to do your will, For you are my God. Your spirit is good; May it lead me in the land of uprightness.
143.11: For the sake of your name, O Jehovah, may you preserve me alive. In your righteousness may you bring forth my soul out of distress.
143.12: And in your loving - kindness may you silence my enemies; And you must destroy all those showing hostility to my soul, For I am your servant.

144.1: Blessed be Jehovah my Rock, Who is teaching my hands for fighting, My fingers for warfare;
144.2: My loving - kindness and my stronghold, My secure height and my Provider of escape for me, My shield and the One in whom I have taken refuge, The One subduing peoples under me.
144.3: O Jehovah, what is man that you should notice him, The son of mortal man that you should take account of him?
144.4: Man himself bears resemblance to a mere exhalation; His days are like a passing shadow.
144.5: O Jehovah, bend down your heavens that you may descend; Touch the mountains that they may smoke.
144.6: Lighten with lightning that you may scatter them; Send out your arrows that you may throw them into confusion.
144.7: Thrust your hands out from the height; Set me free and deliver me from the many waters, From the hand of the foreigners,
144.8: Whose mouth has spoken what is untrue And whose right hand is a right hand of falsehood.
144.9: O God, a new song I will sing to you. On an instrument of ten strings I will make melody to you,
144.10: The One giving salvation to kings, The One setting David his servant free from the injurious sword.
144.11: Set me free and deliver me from the hand of the foreigners, Whose mouth has spoken what is untrue And whose right hand is a right hand of falsehood,
144.12: Who I [ say]: " Our sons are like little plants grown up in their youth, Our daughters like corners carved in palace style,
144.13: Our garners full, furnishing products of one sort after another, Our flocks multiplying by thousands, ten thousand to one, in our streets,
144.14: Our cattle loaded down, without any rupture and with no abortion, And with no outcry in our public squares.
144.15: Happy is the people for whom it is just like I [ that]! " Happy is the people whose God is Jehovah!

145.1: I will exalt you, O my God the King, And I will bless your name to time indefinite, even forever.
145.2: All day long I will bless you, And I will praise your name to time indefinite, even forever.
145.3: Jehovah is great and very much to be praised, And his greatness is unsearchable.
145.4: Generation after generation will commend your works, And about your mighty acts they will tell.
145.5: The glorious splendor of your dignity And the matters of your wonderful works I will make my concern.
145.6: And they will talk about the strength of your own fear - inspiring things; And as for your greatness, I will declare it.
145.7: With the mention of the abundance of your goodness they will bubble over, And I [ because of] your righteousness they will cry out joyfully.
145.8: Jehovah is gracious and merciful, Slow to anger and great in loving - kindness.
145.9: Jehovah is good to all, And his mercies are over all his works.
145.10: All your works will laud you, O Jehovah, And your loyal ones will bless you.
145.11: About the glory of your kingship they will talk, And about your mightiness they will speak,
145.12: To make known to the sons of men his mighty acts And the glory of the splendor of his kingship.
145.13: Your kingship is a kingship for all times indefinite, And your dominion is throughout all successive generations.
145.14: Jehovah is giving support to all who are falling, And is raising up all who are bowed down.
145.15: To you the eyes of all look hopefully, And you are giving them their food in its season.
145.16: You are opening your hand And satisfying the desire of every living thing.
145.17: Jehovah is righteous in all his ways And loyal in all his works.
145.18: Jehovah is near to all those calling upon him, To all those who call upon him in trueness.
145.19: The desire of those fearing him he will perform, And their cry for help he will hear, and he will save them.
145.20: Jehovah is guarding all those loving him, But all the wicked ones he will annihilate.
145.21: The praise of Jehovah my mouth will speak; And let all flesh bless his holy name to time indefinite, even forever.

146.1: Praise Jah, YOU people! Praise Jehovah, O my soul.
146.2: I will praise Jehovah during my lifetime. I will make melody to my God as long as I am.
146.3: Do not put YOUR trust in nobles, Nor in the son of earthling man, to whom no salvation belongs.
146.4: His spirit goes out, he goes back to his ground; In that day his thoughts do perish.
146.5: Happy is the one who has the God of Jacob for his help, Whose hope is in Jehovah his God,
146.6: The Maker of heaven and earth, Of the sea, and of all that is in them, The One keeping trueness to time indefinite,
146.7: The One executing judgment for the defrauded ones, The One giving bread to the hungry ones. Jehovah is releasing those who are bound.
146.8: Jehovah is opening I [ the eyes of] the blind ones; Jehovah is raising up the ones bowed down; Jehovah is loving the righteous ones.
146.9: Jehovah is guarding the alien residents; The fatherless boy and the widow he relieves, But the way of the wicked ones he makes crooked.
146.10: Jehovah will be king to time indefinite, Your God, O Zion, for generation after generation. Praise Jah, YOU people!

147.1: Praise Jah, YOU people, For it is good to make melody to our God; For it is pleasant - praise is fitting.
147.2: Jehovah is building Jerusalem; The dispersed ones of Israel he brings together.
147.3: He is healing the brokenhearted ones, And is binding up their painful spots.
147.4: He is counting the number of the stars; All of them he calls by I [ their] names.
147.5: Our Lord is great and is abundant in power; His understanding is beyond recounting.
147.6: Jehovah is relieving the meek ones; He is abasing the wicked ones to the earth.
147.7: Respond to Jehovah with thanksgiving, YOU people; Make melody to our God on the harp,
147.8: The One who is covering the heavens with clouds, The One preparing rain for the earth, The One making the mountains to sprout green grass.
147.9: To the beasts he is giving their food, To the young ravens that keep calling.
147.10: Not in the mightiness of the horse does he take delight, Nor in the legs of the man does he find pleasure.
147.11: Jehovah is finding pleasure in those fearing him, In those waiting for his loving - kindness.
147.12: Commend Jehovah, O Jerusalem. Praise your God, O Zion.
147.13: For he has made the bars of your gates strong; He has blessed your sons in the midst of you.
147.14: He is putting peace in your territory; With the fat of the wheat he keeps satisfying you.
147.15: He is sending his saying to the earth; With speed his word runs.
147.16: He is giving snow like wool; Hoarfrost he scatters just like ashes.
147.17: He is throwing his ice like morsels. Before his cold who can stand?
147.18: He sends forth his word and melts them. He causes his wind to blow; The waters trickle.
147.19: He is telling his word to Jacob, His regulations and his judicial decisions to Israel.
147.20: He has not done that way to any other nation; And as for I [ his] judicial decisions, they have not known them. Praise Jah, YOU people!

148.1: Praise Jah, YOU people! Praise Jehovah from the heavens, Praise him in the heights.
148.2: Praise him, all YOU his angels. Praise him, all YOU his army.
148.3: Praise him, YOU sun and moon. Praise him, all YOU stars of light.
148.4: Praise him, YOU heavens of the heavens, And YOU waters that are above the heavens.
148.5: Let them praise the name of Jehovah; For he himself commanded, and they were created.
148.6: And he keeps them standing forever, to time indefinite. A regulation he has given, and it will not pass away.
148.7: Praise Jehovah from the earth, YOU sea monsters and all YOU watery deeps,
148.8: YOU fire and hail, snow and thick smoke, You tempestuous wind, accomplishing his word,
148.9: YOU mountains and all YOU hills, YOU fruit trees and all YOU cedars,
148.10: YOU wild animals and all YOU domestic animals, YOU creeping things and winged birds,
148.11: YOU kings of the earth and all YOU national groups, YOU princes and all YOU judges of the earth,
148.12: YOU young men and also YOU virgins, YOU old men together with boys.
148.13: Let them praise the name of Jehovah, For his name alone is unreachably high. His dignity is above earth and heaven.
148.14: And he will exalt the horn of his people, The praise of all his loyal ones, Of the sons of Israel, the people near to him. Praise Jah, YOU people!

149.1: Praise Jah, YOU people! Sing to Jehovah a new song, His praise in the congregation of loyal ones.
149.2: Let Israel rejoice in its grand Maker, The sons of Zion - let them be joyful in their King.
149.3: Let them praise his name with dancing. With the tambourine and the harp let them make melody to him.
149.4: For Jehovah is taking pleasure in his people. He beautifies the meek ones with salvation.
149.5: Let the loyal ones exult in glory; Let them cry out joyfully on their beds.
149.6: Let the songs extolling God be in their throat, And a two - edged sword be in their hand,
149.7: To execute vengeance upon the nations, Rebukes upon the national groups,
149.8: To bind their kings with shackles And their glorified ones with fetters of iron,
149.9: To execute upon them the judicial decision written. Such splendor belongs to all his loyal ones. Praise Jah, YOU people!

150.1: Praise Jah, YOU people! Praise God in his holy place. Praise him in the expanse of his strength.
150.2: Praise him for his works of mightiness. Praise him according to the abundance of his greatness.
150.3: Praise him with the blowing of the horn. Praise him with the stringed instrument and the harp.
150.4: Praise him with the tambourine and the circle dance. Praise him with strings and the pipe.
150.5: Praise him with the cymbals of melodious sound. Praise him with the clashing cymbals.
150.6: Every breathing thing - let it praise Jah. Praise Jah, YOU people!

1.1: The proverbs of Sol'o·mon the son of David, the king of Israel,
1.2: for one to know wisdom and discipline, to discern the sayings of understanding,
1.3: to receive the discipline that gives insight, righteousness and judgment and uprightness,
1.4: to give to the inexperienced ones shrewdness, to a young man knowledge and thinking ability.
1.5: A wise person will listen and take in more instruction, and a man of understanding is the one who acquires skillful direction,
1.6: to understand a proverb and a puzzling saying, the words of wise persons and their riddles.
1.7: The fear of Jehovah is the beginning of knowledge. Wisdom and discipline are what mere fools have despised.
1.8: Listen, my son, to the discipline of your father, and do not forsake the law of your mother.
1.9: For they are a wreath of attractiveness to your head and a fine necklace to your throat.
1.10: My son, if sinners try to seduce you, do not consent.
1.11: If they keep saying: " Do go with us. Do let us lie in ambush for blood. Do let us lie in concealment for the innocent men without any cause.
1.12: Let us swallow them down alive just like She'ol, even whole, like those going down into a pit.
1.13: Let us find all sorts of precious valuables. Let us fill our houses with spoil.
1.14: Your lot you ought to cast in among us. Let there come to be just one bag belonging to all of us " -
1.15: my son, do not go in the way with them. Hold back your foot from their roadway.
1.16: For their feet are those that run to sheer badness, and they keep hastening to shed blood.
1.17: For it is for nothing that the net is spread before the eyes of anything owning wings.
1.18: Consequently they themselves lie in ambush for the very blood of these; they lie in concealment for their souls.
1.19: Thus are the paths of everyone making unjust profit. It takes away the very soul of its owners.
1.20: True wisdom itself keeps crying aloud in the very street. In the public squares it keeps giving forth its voice.
1.21: At the upper end of the noisy streets it calls out. At the entrances of the gates into the city it says its own sayings:
1.22: " How long will YOU inexperienced ones keep loving inexperience, and I [ how long] must YOU ridiculers desire for yourselves outright ridicule, and I [ how long] will YOU stupid ones keep hating knowledge?
1.23: Turn back at my reproof. Then to YOU I will cause my spirit to bubble forth; I will make my words known to YOU.
1.24: Because I have called out but YOU keep refusing, I have stretched out my hand but there is no one paying attention,
1.25: and YOU keep neglecting all my counsel, and my reproof YOU have not accepted,
1.26: I also, for my part, shall laugh at YOUR own disaster, I shall mock when what YOU dread comes,
1.27: when what YOU dread comes just like a storm, and YOUR own disaster gets here just like a storm wind, when distress and hard times come upon YOU.
1.28: At that time they will keep calling me, but I shall not answer; they will keep looking for me, but they will not find me,
1.29: for the reason that they hated knowledge, and the fear of Jehovah they did not choose.
1.30: They did not consent to my counsel; they disrespected all my reproof.
1.31: So they will eat from the fruitage of their way, and they will be glutted with their own counsels.
1.32: For the renegading of the inexperienced ones is what will kill them, and the easygoingness of the stupid is what will destroy them.
1.33: As for the one listening to me, he will reside in security and be undisturbed from dread of calamity. "

2.1: My son, if you will receive my sayings and treasure up my own commandments with yourself,
2.2: so as to pay attention to wisdom with your ear, that you may incline your heart to discernment;
2.3: if, moreover, you call out for understanding itself and you give forth your voice for discernment itself,
2.4: if you keep seeking for it as for silver, and as for hid treasures you keep searching for it,
2.5: in that case you will understand the fear of Jehovah, and you will find the very knowledge of God.
2.6: For Jehovah himself gives wisdom; out of his mouth there are knowledge and discernment.
2.7: And for the upright ones he will treasure up practical wisdom; for those walking in integrity he is a shield,
2.8: by observing the paths of judgment, and he will guard the very way of his loyal ones.
2.9: In that case you will understand righteousness and judgment and uprightness, the entire course of what is good.
2.10: When wisdom enters into your heart and knowledge itself becomes pleasant to your very soul,
2.11: thinking ability itself will keep guard over you, discernment itself will safeguard you,
2.12: to deliver you from the bad way, from the man speaking perverse things,
2.13: from those leaving the paths of uprightness to walk in the ways of darkness,
2.14: from those who are rejoicing in doing bad, who are joyful in the perverse things of badness;
2.15: those whose paths are crooked and who are devious in their general course;
2.16: to deliver you from the strange woman, from the foreign woman who has made her own sayings smooth,
2.17: who is leaving the confidential friend of her youth and who has forgotten the very covenant of her God.
2.18: For down to death her house does sink and down to those impotent in death her tracks.
2.19: None of those having relations with her will come back, nor will they regain the paths of those living.
2.20: The purpose is that you may walk in the way of good people and that the paths of the righteous ones you may keep.
2.21: For the upright are the ones that will reside in the earth, and the blameless are the ones that will be left over in it.
2.22: As regards the wicked, they will be cut off from the very earth; and as for the treacherous, they will be torn away from it.

3.1: My son, my law do not forget, and my commandments may your heart observe,
3.2: because length of days and years of life and peace will be added to you.
3.3: May loving - kindness and trueness themselves not leave you. Tie them about your throat. Write them upon the tablet of your heart,
3.4: and so find favor and good insight in the eyes of God and of earthling man.
3.5: Trust in Jehovah with all your heart and do not lean upon your own understanding.
3.6: In all your ways take notice of him, and he himself will make your paths straight.
3.7: Do not become wise in your own eyes. Fear Jehovah and turn away from bad.
3.8: May it become a healing to your navel and a refreshment to your bones.
3.9: Honor Jehovah with your valuable things and with the firstfruits of all your produce.
3.10: Then your stores of supply will be filled with plenty; and with new wine your own press vats will overflow.
3.11: The discipline of Jehovah, O my son, do not reject; and do not abhor his reproof,
3.12: because the one whom Jehovah loves he reproves, even as a father does a son in whom he finds pleasure.
3.13: Happy is the man that has found wisdom, and the man that gets discernment,
3.14: for having it as gain is better than having silver as gain and having it as produce than gold itself.
3.15: It is more precious than corals, and all other delights of yours cannot be made equal to it.
3.16: Length of days is in its right hand; in its left hand there are riches and glory.
3.17: Its ways are ways of pleasantness, and all its roadways are peace.
3.18: It is a tree of life to those taking hold of it, and those keeping fast hold of it are to be called happy.
3.19: Jehovah himself in wisdom founded the earth. He solidly fixed the heavens in discernment.
3.20: By his knowledge the watery deeps themselves were split apart, and the cloudy skies keep dripping down light rain.
3.21: My son, may they not get away from your eyes. Safeguard practical wisdom and thinking ability,
3.22: and they will prove to be life to your soul and charm to your throat.
3.23: In that case you will walk in security on your way, and even your foot will not strike against anything.
3.24: Whenever you lie down you will feel no dread; and you will certainly lie down, and your sleep must be pleasurable.
3.25: You will not need to be afraid of any sudden dreadful thing, nor of the storm upon the wicked ones, because it is coming.
3.26: For Jehovah himself will prove to be, in effect, your confidence, and he will certainly keep your foot against capture.
3.27: Do not hold back good from those to whom it is owing, when it happens to be in the power of your hand to do I [ it].
3.28: Do not say to your fellowman: " Go, and come back and tomorrow I shall give, " when there is something with you.
3.29: Do not fabricate against your fellowman anything bad, when he is dwelling in a sense of security with you.
3.30: Do not quarrel with a man without cause, if he has rendered no bad to you.
3.31: Do not become envious of the man of violence, nor choose any of his ways.
3.32: For the devious person is a detestable thing to Jehovah, but His intimacy is with the upright ones.
3.33: The curse of Jehovah is on the house of the wicked one, but the abiding place of the righteous ones he blesses.
3.34: If it has to do with ridiculers, he himself will deride; but to the meek ones he will show favor.
3.35: Honor is what the wise ones will come to possess, but the stupid ones are exalting dishonor.

4.1: Listen, O sons, to the discipline of a father and pay attention, so as to know understanding.
4.2: For good instruction is what I certainly shall give to YOU. My law DO not leave.
4.3: For I proved to be a real son to my father, tender and the only one before my mother.
4.4: And he would instruct me and say to me: " May your heart keep fast hold of my words. Keep my commandments and continue living.
4.5: Acquire wisdom, acquire understanding. Do not forget, and do not turn aside from the sayings of my mouth.
4.6: Do not leave it, and it will keep you. Love it, and it will safeguard you.
4.7: Wisdom is the prime thing. Acquire wisdom; and with all that you acquire, acquire understanding.
4.8: Highly esteem it, and it will exalt you. It will glorify you because you embrace it.
4.9: To your head it will give a wreath of charm; a crown of beauty it will bestow upon you. "
4.10: Hear, my son, and accept my sayings. Then for you the years of life will become many.
4.11: I will instruct you even in the way of wisdom; I will cause you to tread in the tracks of uprightness.
4.12: When you walk, your pace will not be cramped; and if you run, you will not stumble.
4.13: Take hold on discipline; do not let go. Safeguard it, for it itself is your life.
4.14: Into the path of the wicked ones do not enter, and do not walk straight on into the way of the bad ones.
4.15: Shun it, do not pass along by it; turn aside from it, and pass along.
4.16: For they do not sleep unless they do badness, and their sleep has been snatched away unless they cause someone to stumble.
4.17: For they have fed themselves with the bread of wickedness, and the wine of acts of violence is what they drink.
4.18: But the path of the righteous ones is like the bright light that is getting lighter and lighter until the day is firmly established.
4.19: The way of the wicked ones is like the gloom; they have not known at what they keep stumbling.
4.20: My son, to my words do pay attention. To my sayings incline your ear.
4.21: May they not get away from your eyes. Keep them in the midst of your heart.
4.22: For they are life to those finding them and health to all their flesh.
4.23: More than all else that is to be guarded, safeguard your heart, for out of it are the sources of life.
4.24: Remove from yourself the crookedness of speech; and the deviousness of lips put far away from yourself.
4.25: As for your eyes, straight ahead they should look, yes, your own beaming eyes should gaze straight in front of you.
4.26: Smooth out the course of your foot, and may all your own ways be firmly established.
4.27: Do not incline to the right hand or to the left. Remove your foot from what is bad.

5.1: My son, to my wisdom O do pay attention. To my discernment incline your ears,
5.2: so as to guard thinking abilities; and may your own lips safeguard knowledge itself.
5.3: For as a honeycomb the lips of a strange woman keep dripping, and her palate is smoother than oil.
5.4: But the aftereffect from her is as bitter as wormwood; it is as sharp as a two - edged sword.
5.5: Her feet are descending to death. Her very steps take hold on She'ol itself.
5.6: The path of life she does not contemplate. Her tracks have wandered she does not know I [ where].
5.7: So now, O sons, listen to me and do not turn away from the sayings of my mouth.
5.8: Keep your way far off from alongside her, and do not get near to the entrance of her house,
5.9: that you may not give to others your dignity, nor your years to what is cruel;
5.10: that strangers may not satisfy themselves with your power, nor the things you got by pain be in the house of a foreigner,
5.11: nor you have to groan in your future when your flesh and your organism come to an end.
5.12: And you will have to say: " How I have hated discipline and my heart has disrespected even reproof!
5.13: And I have not listened to the voice of my instructors, and to my teachers I have not inclined my ear.
5.14: Easily I have come to be in every sort of badness in the midst of the congregation and of the assembly. "
5.15: Drink water out of your own cistern, and tricklings out of the midst of your own well.
5.16: Should your springs be scattered out of doors, I [ your] streams of water in the public squares themselves?
5.17: Let them prove to be for you alone, and not for strangers with you.
5.18: Let your water source prove to be blessed, and rejoice with the wife of your youth,
5.19: a lovable hind and a charming mountain goat. Let her own breasts intoxicate you at all times. With her love may you be in an ecstasy constantly.
5.20: So why should you, my son, be in an ecstasy with a strange woman or embrace the bosom of a foreign woman?
5.21: For the ways of man are in front of the eyes of Jehovah, and he is contemplating all his tracks.
5.22: His own errors will catch the wicked one, and in the ropes of his own sin he will be taken hold of.
5.23: He will be the one to die because there is no discipline, and I [ because] in the abundance of his foolishness he goes astray.

6.1: My son, if you have gone surety for your fellowman, I [ if] you have given your handshake even to the stranger,
6.2: I [ if] you have been ensnared by the sayings of your mouth, I [ if] you have been caught by the sayings of your mouth,
6.3: take this action then, my son, and deliver yourself, for you have come into the palm of your fellowman: Go humble yourself and storm your fellowman with importunities.
6.4: Do not give any sleep to your eyes, nor any slumber to your beaming eyes.
6.5: Deliver yourself like a gazelle from the hand and like a bird from the hand of the birdcatcher.
6.6: Go to the ant, you lazy one; see its ways and become wise.
6.7: Although it has no commander, officer or ruler,
6.8: it prepares its food even in the summer; it has gathered its food supplies even in the harvest.
6.9: How long, you lazy one, will you keep lying down? When will you rise up from your sleep?
6.10: A little more sleep, a little more slumbering, a little more folding of the hands in lying down,
6.11: and your poverty will certainly come just like some rover, and your want like an armed man.
6.12: A good - for - nothing man, a man of hurtfulness, is walking with crookedness of speech,
6.13: winking with his eye, making signs with his foot, making indications with his fingers.
6.14: Perverseness is in his heart. He is fabricating something bad all the time. He keeps sending out merely contentions.
6.15: That is why suddenly there will come his disaster; in an instant he will be broken, and there will be no healing.
6.16: There are six things that Jehovah does hate; yes, seven are things detestable to his soul:
6.17: lofty eyes, a false tongue, and hands that are shedding innocent blood,
6.18: a heart fabricating hurtful schemes, feet that are in a hurry to run to badness,
6.19: a false witness that launches forth lies, and anyone sending forth contentions among brothers.
6.20: Observe, O my son, the commandment of your father, and do not forsake the law of your mother.
6.21: Tie them upon your heart constantly; bind them upon your throat.
6.22: When you walk about, it will lead you; when you lie down, it will stand guard over you; and when you have waked up, it itself will make you its concern.
6.23: For the commandment is a lamp, and a light the law is, and the reproofs of discipline are the way of life,
6.24: to guard you against the bad woman, against the smoothness of the tongue of the foreign woman.
6.25: Do not desire her prettiness in your heart, and may she not take you with her lustrous eyes,
6.26: because in behalf of a woman prostitute I [ one comes down] to a round loaf of bread; but as regards another man's wife, she hunts even for a precious soul.
6.27: Can a man rake together fire into his bosom and yet his very garments not be burned?
6.28: Or can a man walk upon the coals and his feet themselves not be scorched?
6.29: Likewise with anyone having relations with the wife of his fellowman, no one touching her will remain unpunishable.
6.30: People do not despise a thief just because he commits thievery to fill his soul when he is hungry.
6.31: But, when found, he will make it good with seven times as much; all the valuables of his house he will give.
6.32: Anyone committing adultery with a woman is in want of heart; he that does it is bringing his own soul to ruin.
6.33: A plague and dishonor he will find, and his reproach itself will not be wiped out.
6.34: For the rage of an able - bodied man is jealousy, and he will not show compassion in the day of vengeance.
6.35: He will have no consideration for any sort of ransom, neither will he show willingness, no matter how large you make the present.

7.1: My son, keep my sayings, and may you treasure up my own commandments with you.
7.2: Keep my commandments and continue living, and my law like the pupil of your eyes.
7.3: Tie them upon your fingers, and write them upon the tablet of your heart.
7.4: Say to wisdom: " You are my sister "; and may you call understanding itself " Kinswoman, "
7.5: to guard you against the woman stranger, against the foreigner who has made her own sayings smooth.
7.6: For at the window of my house, through my lattice I looked down,
7.7: that I might peer upon the inexperienced ones. I was interested in discerning among the sons a young man in want of heart,
7.8: passing along on the street near her corner, and in the way to her house he marches,
7.9: in the twilight, in the evening of the day, at the approach of the night and the gloom.
7.10: And, look! there was a woman to meet him, with the garment of a prostitute and cunning of heart.
7.11: She is boisterous and stubborn. In her house her feet do not keep residing.
7.12: Now she is outdoors, now she is in the public squares, and near every corner she lies in wait.
7.13: And she has grabbed hold of him and given him a kiss. She has put on a bold face, and she begins to say to him:
7.14: " Communion sacrifices were incumbent upon me. Today I have paid my vows.
7.15: That is why I have come out to meet you, to look for your face, that I may find you.
7.16: With coverlets I have bedecked my divan, with many - colored things, linen of Egypt.
7.17: I have besprinkled my bed with myrrh, aloes and cinnamon.
7.18: Do come, let us drink our fill of love until the morning; do let us enjoy each other with love expressions.
7.19: For the husband is not in his house; he has gone traveling on a way of some distance.
7.20: A bag of money he has taken in his hand. On the day of the full moon he will come to his house. "
7.21: She has misled him by the abundance of her persuasiveness. By the smoothness of her lips she seduces him.
7.22: All of a sudden he is going after her, like a bull that comes even to the slaughter, and just as if fettered for the discipline of a foolish man,
7.23: until an arrow cleaves open his liver, just as a bird hastens into the trap, and he has not known that it involves his very soul.
7.24: And now, O sons, listen to me and pay attention to the sayings of my mouth.
7.25: May your heart not turn aside to her ways. Do not wander into her roadways.
7.26: For many are the ones she has caused to fall down slain, and all those being killed by her are numerous.
7.27: The ways to She'ol her house is; they are descending to the interior rooms of death.

8.1: Does not wisdom keep calling out, and discernment keep giving forth its voice?
8.2: On top of the heights, by the way, at the crossing of the roadways it has stationed itself.
8.3: At the side of the gates, at the mouth of the town, at the going in of the entrances it keeps crying loudly:
8.4: " To YOU, O men, I am calling, and my voice is to the sons of men.
8.5: O inexperienced ones, understand shrewdness; and YOU stupid ones, understand heart.
8.6: Listen, for it is about the foremost things that I speak, and the opening of my lips is about uprightness.
8.7: For my palate in low tones utters truth itself; and wickedness is something detestable to my lips.
8.8: All the sayings of my mouth are in righteousness. Among them there is nothing twisted or crooked.
8.9: All of them are straight to the discerning one, and upright to the ones finding knowledge.
8.10: TAKE my discipline and not silver, and knowledge rather than choice gold.
8.11: For wisdom is better than corals, and all other delights themselves cannot be made equal to it.
8.12: " I, wisdom, I have resided with shrewdness and I find even the knowledge of thinking abilities.
8.13: The fear of Jehovah means the hating of bad. Self - exaltation and pride and the bad way and the perverse mouth I have hated.
8.14: I have counsel and practical wisdom. I - understanding; I have mightiness.
8.15: By me kings themselves keep reigning, and high officials themselves keep decreeing righteousness.
8.16: By me princes themselves keep ruling as princes, and nobles are all judging in righteousness.
8.17: Those loving me I myself love, and those looking for me are the ones that find me.
8.18: Riches and glory are with me, hereditary values and righteousness.
8.19: My fruitage is better than gold, even than refined gold, and my produce than choice silver.
8.20: In the path of righteousness I walk, in the middle of the roadways of judgment,
8.21: to cause those loving me to take possession of substance; and their storehouses I keep filled.
8.22: " Jehovah himself produced me as the beginning of his way, the earliest of his achievements of long ago.
8.23: From time indefinite I was installed, from the start, from times earlier than the earth.
8.24: When there were no watery deeps I was brought forth as with labor pains, when there were no springs heavily charged with water.
8.25: Before the mountains themselves had been settled down, ahead of the hills, I was brought forth as with labor pains,
8.26: when as yet he had not made the earth and the open spaces and the first part of the dust masses of the productive land.
8.27: When he prepared the heavens I was there; when he decreed a circle upon the face of the watery deep,
8.28: when he made firm the cloud masses above, when he caused the fountains of the watery deep to be strong,
8.29: when he set for the sea his decree that the waters themselves should not pass beyond his order, when he decreed the foundations of the earth,
8.30: then I came to be beside him as a master worker, and I came to be the one he was specially fond of day by day, I being glad before him all the time,
8.31: being glad at the productive land of his earth, and the things I was fond of were with the sons of men.
8.32: " And now, O sons, listen to me; yes, happy are the ones that keep my very ways.
8.33: Listen to discipline and become wise, and do not show any neglect.
8.34: Happy is the man that is listening to me by keeping awake at my doors day by day, by watching at the posts of my entrances.
8.35: For the one finding me will certainly find life, and gets goodwill from Jehovah.
8.36: But the one missing me is doing violence to his soul; all those intensely hating me are the ones that do love death. "

9.1: True wisdom has built its house; it has hewn out its seven pillars.
9.2: It has organized its meat slaughtering; it has mixed its wine; more than that, it has set in order its table.
9.3: It has sent forth its lady attendants, that it may call out on top of the heights of the town:
9.4: " Whoever is inexperienced, let him turn aside here. " Whoever is in want of heart - she has said to him:
9.5: " Come, feed yourselves with my bread and share in drinking the wine that I have mixed.
9.6: Leave the inexperienced ones and keep living, and walk straight in the way of understanding. "
9.7: He that is correcting the ridiculer is taking to himself dishonor, and he that is giving a reproof to someone wicked - a defect in him.
9.8: Do not reprove a ridiculer, that he may not hate you. Give a reproof to a wise person and he will love you.
9.9: Give to a wise person and he will become still wiser. Impart knowledge to someone righteous and he will increase in learning.
9.10: The fear of Jehovah is the start of wisdom, and the knowledge of the Most Holy One is what understanding is.
9.11: For by me your days will become many, and to you years of life will be added.
9.12: If you have become wise, you have become wise in your own behalf; and if you have ridiculed, you will bear I [ it], just you alone.
9.13: A woman of stupidity is boisterous. She is simplemindedness itself and has come to know nothing whatever.
9.14: And she has seated herself at the entrance of her house, upon a seat, I [ in] the high places of the town,
9.15: to call out to those passing along the way, those who are going straight ahead on their paths:
9.16: " Whoever is inexperienced, let him turn aside here. " And whoever is in want of heart - she has also said to him:
9.17: " Stolen waters themselves are sweet, and bread I [ eaten] in secrecy - it is pleasant. "
9.18: But he has not come to know that those impotent in death are there, that those called in by her are in the low places of She'ol.

10.1: Proverbs of Sol'o·mon. A wise son is the one that makes a father rejoice, and a stupid son is the grief of his mother.
10.2: The treasures of the wicked one will be of no benefit, but righteousness is what will deliver from death.
10.3: Jehovah will not cause the soul of the righteous one to go hungry, but the craving of the wicked ones he will push away.
10.4: The one working with a slack hand will be of little means, but the hand of the diligent one is what will make one rich.
10.5: The son acting with insight is gathering during the summertime; the son acting shamefully is fast asleep during the harvest.
10.6: Blessings are for the head of the righteous one, but as regards the mouth of the wicked ones, it covers up violence.
10.7: The remembrance of the righteous one is due for a blessing, but the very name of the wicked ones will rot.
10.8: The one wise in heart will accept commandments, but the one foolish with his lips will be trodden down.
10.9: He that is walking in integrity will walk in security, but he that is making his ways crooked will make himself known.
10.10: The one winking his eye will give pain, and the one foolish with his lips will be trodden down.
10.11: The mouth of the righteous one is a source of life; but as regards the mouth of the wicked ones, it covers up violence.
10.12: Hatred is what stirs up contentions, but love covers over even all transgressions.
10.13: On the lips of the understanding person wisdom is found, but the rod is for the back of one in want of heart.
10.14: The wise are the ones that treasure up knowledge, but the mouth of the foolish one is near to ruin itself.
10.15: The valuable things of a rich man are his strong town. The ruin of the lowly ones is their poverty.
10.16: The activity of the righteous one results in life; the produce of the wicked one results in sin.
10.17: He that is holding to discipline is a path to life, but he that is leaving reproof is causing to wander.
10.18: Where there is one covering over hatred there are lips of falsehood, and the one bringing forth a bad report is stupid.
10.19: In the abundance of words there does not fail to be transgression, but the one keeping his lips in check is acting discreetly.
10.20: The tongue of the righteous one is choice silver; the heart of the wicked one is worth little.
10.21: The very lips of the righteous one keep pasturing many, but for want of heart the foolish themselves keep dying.
10.22: The blessing of Jehovah - that is what makes rich, and he adds no pain with it.
10.23: To the stupid one the carrying on of loose conduct is like sport, but wisdom is for the man of discernment.
10.24: The thing frightful to the wicked one - that is what will come to him; but the desire of the righteous ones will be granted.
10.25: As when the storm wind passes over, so the wicked one is no more; but the righteous one is a foundation to time indefinite.
10.26: As vinegar to the teeth and as smoke to the eyes, so the lazy man is to those sending him forth.
10.27: The very fear of Jehovah will add days, but the years themselves of the wicked ones will be cut short.
10.28: The expectation of the righteous ones is a rejoicing, but the very hope of the wicked ones will perish.
10.29: The way of Jehovah is a stronghold for the blameless one, but ruin is for the practicers of what is hurtful.
10.30: As for the righteous one, to time indefinite he will not be caused to stagger; but as for the wicked ones, they will not keep residing on the earth.
10.31: The mouth of the righteous one - it bears the fruit of wisdom, but the tongue of perverseness will be cut off.
10.32: The lips of the righteous one - they come to know goodwill, but the mouth of the wicked ones is perverseness.

11.1: A cheating pair of scales is something detestable to Jehovah, but a complete stone - weight is a pleasure to him.
11.2: Has presumptuousness come? Then dishonor will come; but wisdom is with the modest ones.
11.3: The integrity of the upright ones is what leads them, but distortion by those dealing treacherously will despoil them.
11.4: Valuable things will be of no benefit on the day of fury, but righteousness itself will deliver from death.
11.5: The righteousness of the blameless one is what will make his way straight, but in his own wickedness the wicked one will fall.
11.6: The righteousness of the upright ones is what will deliver them, but by their craving those dealing treacherously will themselves be caught.
11.7: When a wicked man dies, I [ his] hope perishes; and even expectation I [ based] on powerfulness has perished.
11.8: The righteous is the one rescued even from distress, and the wicked one comes in instead of him.
11.9: By I [ his] mouth the one who is an apostate brings his fellowman to ruin, but by knowledge are the righteous rescued.
11.10: Because of the goodness of the righteous ones a town is elated, but when the wicked ones perish there is a joyful cry.
11.11: Because of the blessing of the upright ones a town is exalted, but because of the mouth of the wicked ones it gets torn down.
11.12: The one in want of heart has despised his own fellowman, but the man of broad discernment is one that keeps silent.
11.13: The one walking about as a slanderer is uncovering confidential talk, but the one faithful in spirit is covering over a matter.
11.14: When there is no skillful direction, the people fall; but there is salvation in the multitude of counselors.
11.15: One will positively fare badly because he has gone surety for a stranger, but the one hating handshaking is keeping carefree.
11.16: A woman of charm is the one that takes hold of glory; but the tyrants, for their part, take hold of riches.
11.17: A man of loving - kindness is dealing rewardingly with his own soul, but the cruel person is bringing ostracism upon his own organism.
11.18: The wicked one is making false wages, but the one sowing righteousness, true earnings.
11.19: The one firmly standing for righteousness is in line for life, but the one chasing after what is bad is in line for his own death.
11.20: Those crooked at heart are something detestable to Jehovah, but the ones blameless in I [ their] way are a pleasure to him.
11.21: Though hand be to hand, a bad person will not go unpunished; but the offspring of the righteous ones will certainly escape.
11.22: As a gold nose ring in the snout of a pig, so is a woman that is pretty but that is turning away from sensibleness.
11.23: The desire of the righteous ones is surely good; the hope of the wicked ones is fury.
11.24: There exists the one that is scattering and yet is being increased; also the one that is keeping back from what is right, but it results only in want.
11.25: The generous soul will itself be made fat, and the one freely watering I [ others] will himself also be freely watered.
11.26: The one holding back grain - the populace will execrate him, but there is a blessing for the head of the one letting it be bought.
11.27: He that is looking for good will keep seeking goodwill; but as for the one searching for bad, it will come upon him.
11.28: The one trusting in his riches - he himself will fall; but just like foliage the righteous ones will flourish.
11.29: As for anyone bringing ostracism upon his own house, he will take possession of wind; and a foolish person will be a servant to the one wise in heart.
11.30: The fruitage of the righteous one is a tree of life, and he that is winning souls is wise.
11.31: Look! The righteous one - in the earth he will be rewarded. How much more should the wicked one and the sinner be!

12.1: A lover of discipline is a lover of knowledge, but a hater of reproof is unreasoning.
12.2: One that is good gets approval from Jehovah, but the man of I [ wicked] ideas he pronounces wicked.
12.3: No man will be firmly established by wickedness; but as for the root - foundation of the righteous ones, it will not be caused to stagger.
12.4: A capable wife is a crown to her owner, but as rottenness in his bones is she that acts shamefully.
12.5: The thoughts of the righteous ones are judgment; the steering by the wicked ones is deception.
12.6: The words of the wicked ones are a lying in wait for blood, but the mouth of the upright ones is what will deliver them.
12.7: There is an overthrowing of the wicked ones and they are no more, but the very house of the righteous ones will keep standing.
12.8: For his mouth of discretion a man will be praised, but one who is twisted at heart will come to be for contempt.
12.9: Better is the one lightly esteemed but having a servant than the one glorifying himself but in want of bread.
12.10: The righteous one is caring for the soul of his domestic animal, but the mercies of the wicked ones are cruel.
12.11: The one cultivating his ground will himself be satisfied with bread, but the one pursuing valueless things is in want of heart.
12.12: The wicked one has desired the netted prey of bad men; but as for the root of the righteous ones, it yields.
12.13: By the transgression of the lips the bad person is ensnared, but the righteous one gets out of distress.
12.14: From the fruitage of a man's mouth he is satisfied with good, and the very doing of a man's hands will come back to him.
12.15: The way of the foolish one is right in his own eyes, but the one listening to counsel is wise.
12.16: It is a foolish person that makes known his vexation in the I [ same] day, but the shrewd one is covering over a dishonor.
12.17: He that launches forth faithfulness will tell what is righteous, but a false witness, deception.
12.18: There exists the one speaking thoughtlessly as with the stabs of a sword, but the tongue of the wise ones is a healing.
12.19: It is the lip of truth that will be firmly established forever, but the tongue of falsehood will be only as long as a moment.
12.20: Deception is in the heart of those fabricating mischief, but those counseling peace have rejoicing.
12.21: Nothing hurtful will befall the righteous one, but the wicked are the ones that will certainly be filled with calamity.
12.22: False lips are something detestable to Jehovah, but those acting in faithfulness are a pleasure to him.
12.23: A shrewd man is covering knowledge, but the heart of the stupid ones is one that calls out foolishness.
12.24: The hand of the diligent ones is the one that will rule, but the slack hand will come to be for forced labor.
12.25: Anxious care in the heart of a man is what will cause it to bow down, but the good word is what makes it rejoice.
12.26: The righteous one spies out his own pasturage, but the very way of wicked ones causes them to wander about.
12.27: Slackness will not start up one's game animals, but the diligent one is a man's precious wealth.
12.28: In the path of righteousness there is life, and the journey in its pathway means no death.

13.1: A son is wise where there is a father's discipline, but the ridiculer is one that has not heard rebuke.
13.2: From the fruitage of his mouth a man will eat good, but the very soul of those dealing treacherously is violence.
13.3: The one guarding his mouth is keeping his soul. The one opening wide his lips - he will have ruin.
13.4: The lazy one is showing himself desirous, but his soul I [ has] nothing. However, the very soul of the diligent ones will be made fat.
13.5: A false word is what the righteous hates, but the wicked ones act shamefully and cause disgrace for themselves.
13.6: Righteousness itself safeguards the one who is harmless in his way, but wickedness is what subverts the sinner.
13.7: There exists the one that is pretending to be rich and yet he has nothing at all; there is the one that is pretending to be of little means and yet I [ he has] many valuable things.
13.8: The ransom for a man's soul is his riches, but the one of little means has not heard rebuke.
13.9: The very light of the righteous ones will rejoice; but the lamp of the wicked ones - it will be extinguished.
13.10: By presumptuousness one only causes a struggle, but with those consulting together there is wisdom.
13.11: Valuable things resulting from vanity become fewer, but the one collecting by the hand is the one that makes increase.
13.12: Expectation postponed is making the heart sick, but the thing desired is a tree of life when it does come.
13.13: He that has despised the word, from him a I [ debtor's] pledge will be seized; but the one fearing the commandment is the one that will be rewarded.
13.14: The law of the wise one is a source of life, to turn one away from the snares of death.
13.15: Good insight itself gives favor, but the way of those dealing treacherously is rugged.
13.16: Everyone shrewd will act with knowledge, but the one that is stupid will spread abroad foolishness.
13.17: A messenger that is wicked will fall into bad, but a faithful envoy is a healing.
13.18: The one neglecting discipline I [ comes to] poverty and dishonor, but the one keeping a reproof is the one that is glorified.
13.19: Desire when realized is pleasurable to the soul; but it is something detestable to the stupid ones to turn away from bad.
13.20: He that is walking with wise persons will become wise, but he that is having dealings with the stupid ones will fare badly.
13.21: Sinners are the ones whom calamity pursues, but the righteous are the ones whom good rewards.
13.22: One who is good will leave an inheritance to sons of sons, and the wealth of the sinner is something treasured up for the righteous one.
13.23: Plowed ground of persons of little means I [ yields] a great deal of food, but there exists the one that is swept away for lack of judgment.
13.24: The one holding back his rod is hating his son, but the one loving him is he that does look for him with discipline.
13.25: The righteous is eating to the satisfaction of his soul, but the belly of the wicked ones will be empty.

14.1: The truly wise woman has built up her house, but the foolish one tears it down with her own hands.
14.2: The one walking in his uprightness is fearing Jehovah, but the one crooked in his ways is despising Him.
14.3: The rod of haughtiness is in the mouth of the foolish one, but the very lips of the wise ones will guard them.
14.4: Where there are no cattle the manger is clean, but the crop is abundant because of the power of a bull.
14.5: A faithful witness is one that will not lie, but a false witness launches forth mere lies.
14.6: The ridiculer has sought to find wisdom, and there is none; but to the understanding one knowledge is an easy thing.
14.7: Go away from in front of the stupid man, for you will certainly not take note of the lips of knowledge.
14.8: The wisdom of the shrewd is to understand his way, but the foolishness of stupid ones is deception.
14.9: Foolish are those who make a derision of guilt, but among the upright ones there is agreement.
14.10: The heart is aware of the bitterness of one's soul, and with its rejoicing no stranger will intermeddle.
14.11: The house of wicked people will be annihilated, but the tent of the upright ones will flourish.
14.12: There exists a way that is upright before a man, but the ways of death are the end of it afterward.
14.13: Even in laughter the heart may be in pain; and grief is what rejoicing ends up in.
14.14: The one faithless at heart will be satisfied with the results of his own ways, but the good man with the results of his dealings.
14.15: Anyone inexperienced puts faith in every word, but the shrewd one considers his steps.
14.16: The wise one fears and is turning away from badness, but the stupid is becoming furious and self - confident.
14.17: He that is quick to anger will commit foolishness, but the man of thinking abilities is hated.
14.18: The inexperienced ones will certainly take possession of foolishness, but the shrewd ones will bear knowledge as a headdress.
14.19: Bad people will have to bow down before the good ones, and the wicked people at the gates of the righteous one.
14.20: Even to his fellowman one who is of little means is an object of hatred, but many are the friends of the rich person.
14.21: The one despising his own fellowman is sinning, but happy is he who is showing favor to the afflicted ones.
14.22: Will not those devising mischief go wandering about? But there are loving - kindness and trueness as regards those devising good.
14.23: By every kind of toil there comes to be an advantage, but merely the word of the lips I [ tends] to want.
14.24: The crown of the wise is their riches; the foolishness of the stupid ones is foolishness.
14.25: A true witness is delivering souls, but a deceitful one launches forth mere lies.
14.26: In the fear of Jehovah there is strong confidence, and for his sons there will come to be a refuge.
14.27: The fear of Jehovah is a well of life, to turn away from the snares of death.
14.28: In the multitude of people there is an adornment of a king, but in the lack of population is the ruin of a high official.
14.29: He that is slow to anger is abundant in discernment, but one that is impatient is exalting foolishness.
14.30: A calm heart is the life of the fleshly organism, but jealousy is rottenness to the bones.
14.31: He that is defrauding the lowly one has reproached his Maker, but the one showing favor to the poor one is glorifying Him.
14.32: Because of his badness the wicked will be pushed down, but the righteous will be finding refuge in his integrity.
14.33: In the heart of the understanding one there rests wisdom, and in the midst of stupid ones it becomes known.
14.34: Righteousness is what exalts a nation, but sin is something disgraceful to national groups.
14.35: The pleasure of a king is in the servant who is acting with insight, but his fury comes to be toward one acting shamefully.

15.1: An answer, when mild, turns away rage, but a word causing pain makes anger to come up.
15.2: The tongue of wise ones does good with knowledge, but the mouth of the stupid ones bubbles forth with foolishness.
15.3: The eyes of Jehovah are in every place, keeping watch upon the bad ones and the good ones.
15.4: The calmness of the tongue is a tree of life, but distortion in it means a breaking down in the spirit.
15.5: Anyone foolish disrespects the discipline of his father, but anyone regarding reproof is shrewd.
15.6: In the house of the righteous one there is an abundant store, but in the produce of the wicked one there is a becoming ostracized.
15.7: The lips of the wise ones keep scattering knowledge about, but the heart of the stupid ones is not like that.
15.8: The sacrifice of the wicked ones is something detestable to Jehovah, but the prayer of the upright ones is a pleasure to him.
15.9: The way of the wicked one is something detestable to Jehovah, but the one pursuing righteousness he loves.
15.10: Discipline is bad to the one leaving the path; anyone hating reproof will die.
15.11: She'ol and I [ the place of] destruction are in front of Jehovah. How much more so the hearts of the sons of mankind!
15.12: The ridiculer does not love the one reproving him. To the wise ones he will not go.
15.13: A joyful heart has a good effect on the countenance, but because of the pain of the heart there is a stricken spirit.
15.14: The understanding heart is one that searches for knowledge, but the mouth of stupid people is one that aspires to foolishness.
15.15: All the days of the afflicted one are bad; but the one that is good at heart I [ has] a feast constantly.
15.16: Better is a little in the fear of Jehovah than an abundant supply and confusion along with it.
15.17: Better is a dish of vegetables where there is love than a manger - fed bull and hatred along with it.
15.18: An enraged man stirs up contention, but one that is slow to anger quiets down quarreling.
15.19: The way of the lazy one is like a brier hedge, but the path of the upright ones is a way cast up.
15.20: A wise son is the one that makes a father rejoice, but a stupid man is despising his mother.
15.21: Foolishness is a rejoicing to one who is in want of heart, but the man of discernment is one who goes straight ahead.
15.22: There is a frustrating of plans where there is no confidential talk, but in the multitude of counselors there is accomplishment.
15.23: A man has rejoicing in the answer of his mouth, and a word at its right time is O how good!
15.24: The path of life is upward to one acting with insight, in order to turn away from She'ol down below.
15.25: The house of the self - exalted ones Jehovah will tear down, but he will fix the boundary of the widow.
15.26: The schemes of the bad one are something detestable to Jehovah, but pleasant sayings are clean.
15.27: The one making unjust profit is bringing ostracism upon his own house, but the hater of gifts is the one that will keep living.
15.28: The heart of the righteous one meditates so as to answer, but the mouth of the wicked ones bubbles forth with bad things.
15.29: Jehovah is far away from the wicked ones, but the prayer of the righteous ones he hears.
15.30: The brightness of the eyes makes the heart rejoice; a report that is good makes the bones fat.
15.31: The ear that is listening to the reproof of life lodges right in among wise people.
15.32: Anyone shunning discipline is rejecting his own soul, but the one listening to reproof is acquiring heart.
15.33: The fear of Jehovah is a discipline toward wisdom, and before glory there is humility.

16.1: To earthling man belong the arrangings of the heart, but from Jehovah is the answer of the tongue.
16.2: All the ways of a man are pure in his own eyes, but Jehovah is making an estimate of spirits.
16.3: Roll your works upon Jehovah himself and your plans will be firmly established.
16.4: Everything Jehovah has made for his purpose, yes, even the wicked one for the evil day.
16.5: Everyone that is proud in heart is something detestable to Jehovah. Hand I [ may join] to hand, I [ yet] one will not be free from punishment.
16.6: By loving - kindness and trueness error is atoned for, and in the fear of Jehovah one turns away from bad.
16.7: When Jehovah takes pleasure in the ways of a man he causes even his enemies themselves to be at peace with him.
16.8: Better is a little with righteousness than an abundance of products without justice.
16.9: The heart of earthling man may think out his way, but Jehovah himself does the directing of his steps.
16.10: Inspired decision should be upon the lips of a king; in judgment his mouth should not prove unfaithful.
16.11: The just indicator and scales belong to Jehovah; all the stone weights of the bag are his work.
16.12: The doing of wickedness is something detestable to kings, for by righteousness is the throne firmly established.
16.13: The lips of righteousness are a pleasure to a grand king; and the speaker of upright things he loves.
16.14: The rage of a king means messengers of death, but the wise man is one that averts it.
16.15: In the light of the king's face there is life, and his goodwill is like the cloud of spring rain.
16.16: The getting of wisdom is O how much better than gold! And the getting of understanding is to be chosen more than silver.
16.17: The highway of the upright ones is to turn away from bad. One who is safeguarding his way is keeping his soul.
16.18: Pride is before a crash, and a haughty spirit before stumbling.
16.19: Better is it to be lowly in spirit with the meek ones than to divide spoil with the self - exalted ones.
16.20: He that is showing insight in a matter will find good, and happy is he that is trusting in Jehovah.
16.21: The one that is wise in heart will be called understanding, and he that is sweet in I [ his] lips adds persuasiveness.
16.22: To its owners insight is a well of life; and the discipline of the foolish ones is foolishness.
16.23: The heart of the wise one causes his mouth to show insight, and to his lips it adds persuasiveness.
16.24: Pleasant sayings are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul and a healing to the bones.
16.25: There exists a way that is upright before a man, but the ways of death are the end of it afterward.
16.26: The soul of the hard worker has worked hard for him, because his mouth has pressed him hard.
16.27: A good - for - nothing man is digging up what is bad, and upon his lips there is, as it were, a scorching fire.
16.28: A man of intrigues keeps sending forth contention, and a slanderer is separating those familiar with one another.
16.29: A man of violence will seduce his fellow, and certainly causes him to go in a way that is not good.
16.30: He is blinking with his eyes to scheme up intrigues. Pinching his lips together, he certainly brings mischief to completion.
16.31: Gray - headedness is a crown of beauty when it is found in the way of righteousness.
16.32: He that is slow to anger is better than a mighty man, and he that is controlling his spirit than the one capturing a city.
16.33: Into the lap the lot is cast down, but every decision by it is from Jehovah.

17.1: Better is a dry piece of bread with which there is quietness than a house full of the sacrifices of quarreling.
17.2: A servant that is showing insight will rule over the son who is acting shamefully, and in among the brothers he will have a share of the inheritance.
17.3: The refining pot is for silver and the furnace for gold, but Jehovah is the examiner of hearts.
17.4: The evildoer is paying attention to the lip of hurtfulness. A falsifier is giving ear to the tongue causing adversities.
17.5: He that is holding the one of little means in derision has reproached his Maker. He that is joyful at I [ another's] disaster will not be free from punishment.
17.6: The crown of old men is the grandsons, and the beauty of sons is their fathers.
17.7: For anyone senseless the lip of uprightness is not fitting. How much less so for a noble the lip of falsehood!
17.8: The gift is a stone winning favor in the eyes of its grand owner. Everywhere that he turns he has success.
17.9: The one covering over transgression is seeking love, and he that keeps talking about a matter is separating those familiar with one another.
17.10: A rebuke works deeper in one having understanding than striking a stupid one a hundred times.
17.11: Only rebellion is what the bad one keeps seeking, and cruel is the messenger that is sent against him.
17.12: Let there be an encountering by a man of a bear bereaved of its cubs rather than anyone stupid in his foolishness.
17.13: As for anyone repaying bad for good, bad will not move away from his house.
17.14: The beginning of contention is as one letting out waters; so before the quarrel has burst forth, take your leave.
17.15: Anyone pronouncing the wicked one righteous and anyone pronouncing the righteous one wicked - even both of them are something detestable to Jehovah.
17.16: Why is it that there is in the hand of a stupid one the price to acquire wisdom, when he has no heart?
17.17: A true companion is loving all the time, and is a brother that is born for when there is distress.
17.18: A man that is wanting in heart shakes hands, going full surety before his companion.
17.19: Anyone loving transgression is loving a struggle. Anyone making his entryway high is seeking a crash.
17.20: He that is crooked at heart will not find good, and he that is turned around in his tongue will fall into calamity.
17.21: Anyone becoming father to a stupid child - it is a grief to him; and the father of a senseless child does not rejoice.
17.22: A heart that is joyful does good as a curer, but a spirit that is stricken makes the bones dry.
17.23: One who is wicked will take even a bribe from the bosom to bend the paths of judgment.
17.24: Wisdom is before the face of the understanding one, but the eyes of the stupid one are at the extremity of the earth.
17.25: A stupid son is a vexation to his father and a bitterness to her that gave him birth.
17.26: Furthermore, the laying of a fine upon the righteous one is not good. To strike nobles is against what is upright.
17.27: Anyone holding back his sayings is possessed of knowledge, and a man of discernment is cool of spirit.
17.28: Even anyone foolish, when keeping silent, will be regarded as wise; anyone closing up his own lips, as having understanding.

18.1: One isolating himself will seek I [ his own] selfish longing; against all practical wisdom he will break forth.
18.2: Anyone stupid finds no delight in discernment, except that his heart should uncover itself.
18.3: When a wicked one comes in, contempt also must come in; and along with dishonor there is reproach.
18.4: The words of a man's mouth are deep waters. The well of wisdom is a torrent bubbling forth.
18.5: The showing of partiality to the wicked one is not good, nor the turning aside of the righteous one in judgment.
18.6: The lips of one who is stupid enter into quarreling, and his very mouth calls even for strokes.
18.7: The mouth of the stupid one is the ruin of him, and his lips are a snare for his soul.
18.8: The words of the slanderer are like things to be swallowed greedily, which do go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
18.9: Also, the one showing himself slack in his work - he is a brother to the one causing ruin.
18.10: The name of Jehovah is a strong tower. Into it the righteous runs and is given protection.
18.11: The valuable things of the rich are his strong town, and they are like a protective wall in his imagination.
18.12: Before a crash the heart of a man is lofty, and before glory there is humility.
18.13: When anyone is replying to a matter before he hears I [ it], that is foolishness on his part and a humiliation.
18.14: The spirit of a man can put up with his malady; but as for a stricken spirit, who can bear it?
18.15: The heart of the understanding one acquires knowledge, and the ear of wise ones seeks to find knowledge.
18.16: A man's gift will make a large opening for him, and it will lead him even before great people.
18.17: The one first in his legal case is righteous; his fellow comes in and certainly searches him through.
18.18: The lot puts even contentions to rest, and it separates even the mighty from one another.
18.19: A brother who is transgressed against is more than a strong town; and there are contentions that are like the bar of a dwelling tower.
18.20: From the fruitage of a man's mouth his belly will be satisfied; he will be satisfied even with the produce of his lips.
18.21: Death and life are in the power of the tongue, and he that is loving it will eat its fruitage.
18.22: Has one found a I [ good] wife? One has found a good thing, and one gets goodwill from Jehovah.
18.23: Entreaties the one of little means speaks out, but one that is rich answers in a strong way.
18.24: There exist companions disposed to break one another to pieces, but there exists a friend sticking closer than a brother.

19.1: Anyone of little means who is walking in his integrity is better than the one crooked in his lips, and the one that is stupid.
19.2: Also, that the soul should be without knowledge is not good, and he that is hastening with his feet is sinning.
19.3: It is the foolishness of an earthling man that distorts his way, and so his heart becomes enraged against Jehovah himself.
19.4: Wealth is what adds many companions, but one that is lowly gets separated even from his companion.
19.5: A false witness will not be free from punishment, and he that launches forth lies will not escape.
19.6: Many are those who soften the face of a noble, and everybody is a companion to the man making gifts.
19.7: The brothers of one of little means have all hated him. How much farther have his personal friends kept away from him! He is pursuing with things to say; they are not.
19.8: He that is acquiring heart is loving his own soul. He that is guarding discernment is going to find good.
19.9: The false witness will not be free from punishment, and he that launches forth lies will perish.
19.10: Luxury is not fitting for anyone stupid. How much less for a servant to rule over princes!
19.11: The insight of a man certainly slows down his anger, and it is beauty on his part to pass over transgression.
19.12: The raging of a king is a growling like that of a maned young lion, but his goodwill is like the dew upon the vegetation.
19.13: A stupid son means adversities to his father, and the contentions of a wife are as a leaking roof that drives one away.
19.14: The inheritance from fathers is a house and wealth, but a discreet wife is from Jehovah.
19.15: Laziness causes a deep sleep to fall, and a slack soul goes hungry.
19.16: He that is keeping the commandment is keeping his soul; he that is despising his ways will be put to death.
19.17: He that is showing favor to the lowly one is lending to Jehovah, and his treatment He will repay to him.
19.18: Chastise your son while there exists hope; and to the putting of him to death do not lift up your soul [ ful desire].
19.19: He that is of great rage will be bearing the fine; for if you would deliver I [ him], you will also keep doing it again and again.
19.20: Listen to counsel and accept discipline, in order that you may become wise in your future.
19.21: Many are the plans in the heart of a man, but the counsel of Jehovah is what will stand.
19.22: The desirable thing in earthling man is his loving - kindness; and one of little means is better than a lying man.
19.23: The fear of Jehovah tends toward life, and one will spend the night satisfied; one will not be visited with what is bad.
19.24: The lazy one has hidden his hand in the banquet bowl; he cannot bring it back even to his own mouth.
19.25: The ridiculer you should strike, that the inexperienced one may become shrewd; and there should be a reproving of the understanding one, that he may discern knowledge.
19.26: He that is maltreating a father I [ and] that chases a mother away is a son acting shamefully and disgracefully.
19.27: Cease, my son, to listen to discipline I [ and it will mean] to stray from the sayings of knowledge.
19.28: A good - for - nothing witness derides justice, and the very mouth of wicked people swallows down what is hurtful.
