19.29: Judgments have been firmly established for ridiculers, and strokes for the back of stupid ones.

20.1: Wine is a ridiculer, intoxicating liquor is boisterous, and everyone going astray by it is not wise.
20.2: The frightfulness of a king is a growling like that of a maned young lion. Anyone drawing his fury against himself is sinning against his own soul.
20.3: It is a glory for a man to desist from disputing, but everyone foolish will burst out I [ in it].
20.4: Because of winter the lazy one will not plow; he will be begging in reaping time, but there will be nothing.
20.5: Counsel in the heart of a man is as deep waters, but the man of discernment is one that will draw it up.
20.6: A multitude of men will proclaim each one his own loving - kindness, but a faithful man who can find?
20.7: The righteous is walking in his integrity. Happy are his sons after him.
20.8: The king is sitting upon the throne of judgment, scattering all badness with his own eyes.
20.9: Who can say: " I have cleansed my heart; I have become pure from my sin "?
20.10: Two sorts of weights and two sorts of e'phah measures - they are both of them together something detestable to Jehovah.
20.11: Even by his practices a boy makes himself recognized as to whether his activity is pure and upright.
20.12: The hearing ear and the seeing eye - Jehovah himself has made even both of them.
20.13: Do not love sleep, that you may not come to poverty. Open your eyes; be satisfied with bread.
20.14: " It is bad, bad! " says the buyer, and he is going his way. Then it is that he boasts about himself.
20.15: There exists gold, also an abundance of corals; but the lips of knowledge are precious vessels.
20.16: Take one's garment, in case one has gone surety for a stranger; and in the instance of a foreign woman, seize from him a pledge.
20.17: Bread I [ gained by] falsehood is pleasurable to a man, but afterward his mouth will be filled with gravel.
20.18: By counsel plans themselves are firmly established, and by skillful direction carry on your war.
20.19: He that is going about as a slanderer is uncovering confidential talk; and with one that is enticed with his lips you must have no fellowship.
20.20: As for anyone calling down evil upon his father and his mother, his lamp will be extinguished at the approach of darkness.
20.21: An inheritance is being got by greed at first, but its own future will not be blessed.
20.22: Do not say: " I will pay back evil! " Hope in Jehovah, and he will save you.
20.23: Two sorts of weights are something detestable to Jehovah, and a cheating pair of scales is not good.
20.24: From Jehovah are the steppings of an able - bodied man. As regards earthling man, how can he discern his way?
20.25: It is a snare when earthling man has rashly cried out, " Holy! " and after vows I [ he is disposed] to make examination.
20.26: A wise king is scattering wicked people, and he turns around upon them a wheel.
20.27: The breath of earthling man is the lamp of Jehovah, carefully searching all the innermost parts of the belly.
20.28: Loving - kindness and trueness - they safeguard the king; and by loving - kindness he has sustained his throne.
20.29: The beauty of young men is their power, and the splendor of old men is their gray - headedness.
20.30: Bruising wounds are what scours away the bad; and strokes, the innermost parts of the belly.

21.1: A king's heart is as streams of water in the hand of Jehovah. Everywhere that he delights to, he turns it.
21.2: Every way of a man is upright in his own eyes, but Jehovah is making an estimate of hearts.
21.3: To carry on righteousness and judgment is more preferable to Jehovah than sacrifice.
21.4: Haughty eyes and an arrogant heart, the lamp of the wicked ones, are sin.
21.5: The plans of the diligent one surely make for advantage, but everyone that is hasty surely heads for want.
21.6: The getting of treasures by a false tongue is an exhalation driven away, in the case of those seeking death.
21.7: The very despoiling by the wicked ones will drag them away, for they have refused to do justice.
21.8: A man, even a stranger, is crooked in I [ his] way; but the pure one is upright in his activity.
21.9: Better is it to dwell upon a corner of a roof than with a contentious wife, although in a house in common.
21.10: The very soul of the wicked one has craved what is bad; his fellow will be shown no favor in his eyes.
21.11: By the laying of a fine on the ridiculer the inexperienced becomes wise; and by one's giving insight to a wise person he gets knowledge.
21.12: The Righteous One is giving consideration to the house of the wicked one, subverting the wicked ones to I [ their] calamity.
21.13: As for anyone stopping up his ear from the complaining cry of the lowly one, he himself also will call and not be answered.
21.14: A gift made in secrecy subdues anger; and a bribe in the bosom, strong rage.
21.15: It is a rejoicing for the righteous one to do justice, but there is something terrible for those practicing what is hurtful.
21.16: As for a man wandering from the way of insight, he will rest in the very congregation of those impotent in death.
21.17: He that is loving merriment will be an individual in want; he that is loving wine and oil will not gain riches.
21.18: The wicked is a ransom for the righteous one; and the one dealing treacherously takes the place of the upright ones.
21.19: Better is it to dwell in a wilderness land than with a contentious wife along with vexation.
21.20: Desirable treasure and oil are in the abode of the wise one, but the man that is stupid will swallow it up.
21.21: He that is pursuing righteousness and loving - kindness will find life, righteousness and glory.
21.22: A wise one has scaled even the city of mighty men, that he might bring down the strength of its confidence.
21.23: He that is keeping his mouth and his tongue is keeping his soul from distresses.
21.24: Presumptuous, self - assuming braggart is the name of the one who is acting in a fury of presumptuousness.
21.25: The very craving of the lazy will put him to death, for his hands have refused to work.
21.26: All the day he has shown himself eagerly craving, but the righteous one gives and holds nothing back.
21.27: The sacrifice of the wicked ones is something detestable. How much more so when one brings it along with loose conduct.
21.28: A lying witness will perish, but the man that is listening will speak even forever.
21.29: A wicked man has put on a bold face, but the upright is the one that will firmly establish his ways.
21.30: There is no wisdom, nor any discernment, nor any counsel in opposition to Jehovah.
21.31: The horse is something prepared for the day of battle, but salvation belongs to Jehovah.

22.1: A name is to be chosen rather than abundant riches; favor is better than even silver and gold.
22.2: The rich one and the one of little means have met each other. The Maker of them all is Jehovah.
22.3: Shrewd is the one that has seen the calamity and proceeds to conceal himself, but the inexperienced have passed along and must suffer the penalty.
22.4: The result of humility I [ and] the fear of Jehovah is riches and glory and life.
22.5: Thorns I [ and] traps are in the way of the crooked one; he that is guarding his soul keeps far away from them.
22.6: Train up a boy according to the way for him; even when he grows old he will not turn aside from it.
22.7: The rich is the one that rules over those of little means, and the borrower is servant to the man doing the lending.
22.8: He that is sowing unrighteousness will reap what is hurtful, but the very rod of his fury will come to its end.
22.9: He that is kindly in eye will be blessed, for he has given of his food to the lowly one.
22.10: Drive away the ridiculer, that contention may go out and that legal contest and dishonor may cease.
22.11: The one loving purity of heart - for the charm of his lips the king will be his companion.
22.12: The eyes of Jehovah himself have safeguarded knowledge, but he subverts the words of the treacherous one.
22.13: The lazy one has said: " There is a lion outside! In the midst of the public squares I shall be murdered! "
22.14: The mouth of strange women is a deep pit. The one denounced by Jehovah will fall into it.
22.15: Foolishness is tied up with the heart of a boy; the rod of discipline is what will remove it far from him.
22.16: He that is defrauding the lowly one to supply many things to himself, he also that is giving to the rich one, is surely destined for want.
22.17: Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise ones, that you may apply your very heart to my knowledge.
22.18: For it is pleasant that you should keep them in your belly, that they may be firmly established together upon your lips.
22.19: For your confidence to come to be in Jehovah himself I have given you knowledge today, even you.
22.20: Have I not written you heretofore with counselings and knowledge,
22.21: to show you the truthfulness of true sayings, so as to return sayings that are the truth - to the one sending you forth?
22.22: Do not rob the lowly one because he is lowly, and do not crush the afflicted one in the gate.
22.23: For Jehovah himself will plead their cause, and he will certainly rob of soul those robbing them.
22.24: Do not have companionship with anyone given to anger; and with a man having fits of rage you must not enter in,
22.25: that you may not get familiar with his paths and certainly take a snare for your soul.
22.26: Do not get to be among those striking hands, among those who go security for loans.
22.27: If you have nothing to pay, why should he take your bed from under you?
22.28: Do not move back a boundary of long ago, which your forefathers have made.
22.29: Have you beheld a man skillful in his work? Before kings is where he will station himself; he will not station himself before commonplace men.

23.1: In case you should sit down to feed yourself with a king, you should diligently consider what is before you,
23.2: and you must put a knife to your throat if you are the owner of soul [ ful desire].
23.3: Do not show yourself craving his tasty dishes, as it is the food of lies.
23.4: Do not toil to gain riches. Cease from your own understanding.
23.5: Have you caused your eyes to glance at it, when it is nothing? For without fail it makes wings for itself like those of an eagle and flies away toward the heavens.
23.6: Do not feed yourself with the food of anyone of ungenerous eye, nor show yourself craving his tasty dishes.
23.7: For as one that has calculated within his soul, so he is. " Eat and drink, " he says to you, but his heart itself is not with you.
23.8: Your morsel that you have eaten, you will vomit it out, and you will have wasted your pleasant words.
23.9: Into the ears of a stupid one do not speak, for he will despise your discreet words.
23.10: Do not move back the boundary of long ago, and into the field of fatherless boys do not enter.
23.11: For their Redeemer is strong; he himself will plead their cause with you.
23.12: Do bring your heart to discipline and your ear to the sayings of knowledge.
23.13: Do not hold back discipline from the mere boy. In case you beat him with the rod, he will not die.
23.14: With the rod you yourself should beat him, that you may deliver his very soul from She'ol itself.
23.15: My son, if your heart has become wise, my heart will rejoice, even mine.
23.16: And my kidneys will exult when your lips speak uprightness.
23.17: Let your heart not be envious of sinners, but be in the fear of Jehovah all day long.
23.18: For in that case there will exist a future, and your own hope will not be cut off.
23.19: You, O my son, hear and become wise, and lead your heart on in the way.
23.20: Do not come to be among heavy drinkers of wine, among those who are gluttonous eaters of flesh.
23.21: For a drunkard and a glutton will come to poverty, and drowsiness will clothe one with mere rags.
23.22: Listen to your father who caused your birth, and do not despise your mother just because she has grown old.
23.23: Buy truth itself and do not sell it - wisdom and discipline and understanding.
23.24: The father of a righteous one will without fail be joyful; the one becoming father to a wise one will also rejoice in him.
23.25: Your father and your mother will rejoice, and she that gave birth to you will be joyful.
23.26: My son, do give your heart to me, and may those eyes of yours take pleasure in my own ways.
23.27: For a prostitute is a deep pit and a foreign woman is a narrow well.
23.28: Surely she, just like a robber, lies in wait; and among men she increases the treacherous ones.
23.29: Who has woe? Who has uneasiness? Who has contentions? Who has concern? Who has wounds for no reason? Who has dullness of eyes?
23.30: Those staying a long time with the wine, those coming in to search out mixed wine.
23.31: Do not look at wine when it exhibits a red color, when it gives off its sparkle in the cup, I [ when] it goes with a slickness.
23.32: At its end it bites just like a serpent, and it secretes poison just like a viper.
23.33: Your own eyes will see strange things, and your own heart will speak perverse things.
23.34: And you will certainly become like one lying down in the heart of the sea, even like one lying down at the top of a mast.
23.35: " They have struck me, but I did not become sick; they have smitten me, but I did not know it. When shall I wake up? I shall seek it yet some more. "

24.1: Do not be envious of bad men, and do not show yourself craving to get in with them.
24.2: For despoiling is what their heart keeps meditating, and trouble is what their own lips keep speaking.
24.3: By wisdom a household will be built up, and by discernment it will prove firmly established.
24.4: And by knowledge will the interior rooms be filled with all precious and pleasant things of value.
24.5: One wise in strength is an able - bodied man, and a man of knowledge is reinforcing power.
24.6: For by skillful direction you will carry on your war, and in the multitude of counselors there is salvation.
24.7: For a foolish one true wisdom is too high; in the gate he will not open his mouth.
24.8: As for anyone scheming to do bad, he will be called a mere master at evil ideas.
24.9: The loose conduct of foolishness is sin, and a ridiculer is something detestable to mankind.
24.10: Have you shown yourself discouraged in the day of distress? Your power will be scanty.
24.11: Deliver those who are being taken away to death; and those staggering to the slaughter, O may you hold I [ them] back.
24.12: In case you should say: " Look! We did not know of this, " will not he himself that is making an estimate of hearts discern it, and he himself that is observing your soul know and certainly pay back to earthling man according to his activity?
24.13: My son, eat honey, for it is good; and let sweet comb honey be upon your palate.
24.14: In the same way, do know wisdom for your soul. If you have found I [ it], then there exists a future, and your own hope will not be cut off.
24.15: Do not, as a wicked one, lie in wait for the abiding place of the righteous one; do not despoil his resting - place.
24.16: For the righteous one may fall even seven times, and he will certainly get up; but the wicked ones will be made to stumble by calamity.
24.17: When your enemy falls, do not rejoice; and when he is caused to stumble, may your heart not be joyful,
24.18: that Jehovah may not see and it be bad in his eyes and he certainly turn back his anger from against him.
24.19: Do not show yourself heated up at evildoers. Do not become envious of wicked people.
24.20: For there will prove to be no future for anyone bad; the very lamp of wicked people will be extinguished.
24.21: My son, fear Jehovah and the king. With those who are for a change, do not intermeddle.
24.22: For their disaster will arise so suddenly, that who is aware of the extinction of those who are for a change?
24.23: These I [ sayings] also are for the wise ones: The showing of partiality in judgment is not good.
24.24: He that is saying to the wicked one: " You are righteous, " the peoples will execrate him, national groups will denounce him.
24.25: But for those reproving I [ him] it will be pleasant, and upon them there will come the blessing of good.
24.26: Lips will he kiss who is replying in a straightforward way.
24.27: Prepare your work out of doors, and make it ready for yourself in the field. Afterward you must also build up your household.
24.28: Do not become a witness against your fellowman without grounds. Then you would have to be foolish with your lips.
24.29: Do not say: " Just as he did to me, so I am going to do to him. I shall repay to each one according to his acting. "
24.30: I passed along by the field of the lazy individual and by the vineyard of the man in need of heart.
24.31: And, look! all of it produced weeds. Nettles covered its very surface, and its stone wall itself had been torn down.
24.32: So I proceeded to behold, I myself; I began taking I [ it] to heart; I saw, I took the discipline:
24.33: A little sleeping, a little slumbering, a little folding of the hands to lie down,
24.34: and as a highwayman your poverty will certainly come and your neediness as an armed man.

25.1: These also are the proverbs of Sol'o·mon that the men of Hez·e·ki'ah the king of Judah transcribed:
25.2: The glory of God is the keeping of a matter secret, and the glory of kings is the searching through a matter.
25.3: The heavens for height and the earth for depth, and the heart of kings, that is unsearchable.
25.4: Let there be a removing of scummy dross from the silver, and all of it will come forth refined.
25.5: Let there be the removing of the wicked one before the king, and his throne will be firmly established by righteousness itself.
25.6: Do not do yourself honor before the king, and in the place of great ones do not stand.
25.7: For it is better I [ for him] to say to you: " Come up here, " than to abase you before a noble whom your eyes have seen.
25.8: Do not go forth to conduct a legal case hastily, that it may not be a question of what you will do in the culmination of it when your fellowman now humiliates you.
25.9: Plead your own cause with your fellowman, and do not reveal the confidential talk of another;
25.10: that the one listening may not put you to shame and the bad report by you can have no recall.
25.11: As apples of gold in silver carvings is a word spoken at the right time for it.
25.12: An earring of gold, and an ornament of special gold, is a wise reprover upon the hearing ear.
25.13: Just like the coolness of snow in the day of harvest is the faithful envoy to those sending him, for he restores the very soul of his masters.
25.14: As vaporous clouds and a wind without any downpour is a man boasting himself about a gift in falsehood.
25.15: By patience a commander is induced, and a mild tongue itself can break a bone.
25.16: Is it honey that you have found? Eat what is sufficient for you, that you may not take too much of it and have to vomit it up.
25.17: Make your foot rare at the house of your fellowman, that he may not have his sufficiency of you and certainly hate you.
25.18: As a war club and a sword and a sharpened arrow is a man testifying against his fellowman as a false witness.
25.19: As a broken tooth and a wobbling foot is the confidence in one proving treacherous in the day of distress.
25.20: He that is removing a garment on a cold day is as vinegar upon alkali and as a singer with songs upon a gloomy heart.
25.21: If the one hating you is hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
25.22: For coals are what you are raking together upon his head, and Jehovah himself will reward you.
25.23: The wind from the north brings forth as with labor pains a downpour; and a tongue I [ giving away] a secret, a denounced face.
25.24: Better is it to dwell upon a corner of a roof than with a contentious wife, although in a house in common.
25.25: As cold water upon a tired soul, so is a good report from a distant land.
25.26: A fouled spring and a ruined well is the righteous one when staggering before the wicked one.
25.27: The eating of too much honey is not good; and for people to search out their own glory, is it glory?
25.28: As a city broken through, without a wall, is the man that has no restraint for his spirit.

26.1: Like snow in summer and like rain in harvesttime, so glory is not fitting for a stupid one.
26.2: Just as a bird has cause for fleeing I [ and] just as a swallow for flying, so a malediction itself does not come without real cause.
26.3: A whip is for the horse, a bridle is for the ass, and the rod is for the back of stupid people.
26.4: Do not answer anyone stupid according to his foolishness, that you yourself also may not become equal to him.
26.5: Answer someone stupid according to his foolishness, that he may not become someone wise in his own eyes.
26.6: As one that is mutilating I [ his] feet, as one that is drinking mere violence, is he that is thrusting matters into the hand of someone stupid.
26.7: Have the legs of the lame one drawn up water? Then there is a proverb in the mouth of stupid people.
26.8: Like one shutting up a stone in a heap of stones, so is the one giving glory to a mere stupid one.
26.9: As a thorny weed has come up into the hand of a drunkard, so a proverb into the mouth of stupid people.
26.10: As an archer piercing everything is the one hiring someone stupid or the one hiring passersby.
26.11: Just like a dog returning to its vomit, the stupid one is repeating his foolishness.
26.12: Have you seen a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for the stupid one than for him.
26.13: The lazy one has said: " There is a young lion in the way, a lion in among the public squares. "
26.14: A door keeps turning upon its pivot, and the lazy one upon his couch.
26.15: The lazy one has hidden his hand in the banquet bowl; he has become too weary to bring it back to his mouth.
26.16: The lazy one is wiser in his own eyes than seven giving a sensible reply.
26.17: As one grabbing hold of the ears of a dog is anyone passing by that is becoming furious at the quarrel that is not his.
26.18: Just like someone mad that is shooting fiery missiles, arrows and death,
26.19: so is the man that has tricked his fellowman and has said: " Was I not having fun? "
26.20: Where there is no wood the fire goes out, and where there is no slanderer contention grows still.
26.21: As charcoal for the embers and wood for the fire, so is a contentious man for causing a quarrel to glow.
26.22: The words of a slanderer are like things to be swallowed greedily, which do go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
26.23: As a silver glazing overlaid upon a fragment of earthenware are fervent lips along with a bad heart.
26.24: With his lips the hater makes himself unrecognizable, but inside of him he puts deception.
26.25: Although he makes his voice gracious, do not believe in him, for there are seven detestable things in his heart.
26.26: Hatred is covered over by deceit. His badness will be uncovered in the congregation.
26.27: He that is excavating a pit will fall into the same, and he that is rolling away a stone - back to him it will return.
26.28: A tongue that is false hates the one crushed by it, and a flattering mouth causes an overthrow.

27.1: Do not make your boast about the next day, for you do not know what a day will give birth to.
27.2: May a stranger, and not your own mouth, praise you; may a foreigner, and not your own lips, do so.
27.3: The heaviness of a stone and a load of sand - but the vexation by someone foolish is heavier than both of them.
27.4: There is the cruelty of rage, also the flood of anger, but who can stand before jealousy?
27.5: Better is a revealed reproof than a concealed love.
27.6: The wounds inflicted by a lover are faithful, but the kisses of a hater are things to be entreated.
27.7: A soul that is satisfied will tread down comb honey, but to a hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
27.8: Just like a bird fleeing away from its nest, so is a man fleeing away from his place.
27.9: Oil and incense are what make the heart rejoice, also the sweetness of one's companion due to the counsel of the soul.
27.10: Do not leave your own companion or the companion of your father, and do not enter the house of your own brother on the day of your disaster. Better is a neighbor that is near than a brother that is far away.
27.11: Be wise, my son, and make my heart rejoice, that I may make a reply to him that is taunting me.
27.12: The shrewd one that has seen the calamity has concealed himself; the inexperienced that have passed along have suffered the penalty.
27.13: Take one's garment, in case one has gone surety for a stranger; and in the instance of a foreign woman, seize from him a pledge.
27.14: He that is blessing his fellowman with a loud voice early in the morning, as a malediction it will be accounted on his part.
27.15: A leaking roof that drives one away in the day of a steady rain and a contentious wife are comparable.
27.16: Anyone sheltering her has sheltered the wind, and oil is what his right hand encounters.
27.17: By iron, iron itself is sharpened. So one man sharpens the face of another.
27.18: He that is safeguarding the fig tree will himself eat its fruit, and he that is guarding his master will be honored.
27.19: As in water face corresponds with face, so the heart of a man with I [ that of] a man.
27.20: She'ol and I [ the place of] destruction themselves do not get satisfied; neither do the eyes of a man get satisfied.
27.21: The refining pot is for silver, and the furnace is for gold; and an individual is according to his praise.
27.22: Even if you should pound the foolish one fine with a pestle in a mortar, in among cracked grain, his foolishness will not depart from him.
27.23: You ought to know positively the appearance of your flock. Set your heart to your droves;
27.24: for treasure will not be to time indefinite, nor a diadem for all generations.
27.25: The green grass has departed, and the new grass has appeared, and the vegetation of the mountains has been gathered.
27.26: The young rams are for your clothing, and the he - goats are the price of the field.
27.27: And there is a sufficiency of goats' milk for your food, for the food of your household, and the means of life for your girls.

28.1: The wicked do flee when there is no pursuer, but the righteous are like a young lion that is confident.
28.2: Because of the transgression of a land many are its I [ successive] princes, but by a discerning man having knowledge of right I [ the prince] will remain long.
28.3: An able - bodied man that is of little means and that is defrauding the lowly ones is as a rain that washes away so that there is no food.
28.4: Those who are leaving the law praise the wicked one, but those who are keeping the law excite themselves against them.
28.5: Men given to badness cannot understand judgment, but those who are seeking Jehovah can understand everything.
28.6: Better is the one of little means who is walking in his integrity than anyone crooked in I [ his] ways, although he is rich.
28.7: An understanding son is observing the law, but one having companionship with gluttons humiliates his father.
28.8: He that is multiplying his valuables by interest and usury collects them merely for the one showing favor to the lowly ones.
28.9: He that is turning his ear away from hearing the law - even his prayer is something detestable.
28.10: He that is causing the upright ones to go astray into the bad way will himself fall into his own pit, but the faultless ones themselves will come into possession of good.
28.11: A rich man is wise in his own eyes, but the lowly one who is discerning searches him through.
28.12: When the righteous ones are exulting, there is abundant beauty; but when the wicked ones rise up, a man disguises himself.
28.13: He that is covering over his transgressions will not succeed, but he that is confessing and leaving I [ them] will be shown mercy.
28.14: Happy is the man that is feeling dread constantly, but he that is hardening his heart will fall into calamity.
28.15: As a growling lion and an onrushing bear is a wicked ruler over a lowly people.
28.16: A leader that is in want of true discernment is also abundant in fraudulent practices, but he that is hating unjust profit will prolong I [ his] days.
28.17: A man burdened with the bloodguilt for a soul will himself flee even to the pit. Let them not get hold of him.
28.18: He that is walking faultless will be saved, but he that is made crooked in I [ his] ways will fall at once.
28.19: He that is cultivating his own ground will have his sufficiency of bread, and he that is pursuing valueless things will have his sufficiency of poverty.
28.20: A man of faithful acts will get many blessings, but he that is hastening to gain riches will not remain innocent.
28.21: The showing of partiality is not good, nor that an able - bodied man should transgress over a mere piece of bread.
28.22: A man of envious eye is bestirring himself after valuable things, but he does not know that want itself will come upon him.
28.23: He that is reproving a man will afterward find more favor than he will that is flattering with his tongue.
28.24: He that is robbing his father and his mother and is saying: " It is no transgression, " is a partner of a man causing ruination.
28.25: He that is arrogant in soul stirs up contention, but he that is relying upon Jehovah will be made fat.
28.26: He that is trusting in his own heart is stupid, but he that is walking in wisdom is the one that will escape.
28.27: He that is giving to the one of little means will have no want, but he that is hiding his eyes will get many curses.
28.28: When the wicked rise up, a man conceals himself; but when they perish, the righteous become many.

29.1: A man repeatedly reproved but making his neck hard will suddenly be broken, and that without healing.
29.2: When the righteous become many, the people rejoice; but when anyone wicked bears rule, the people sigh.
29.3: A man that is loving wisdom makes his father rejoice, but he that is having companionship with prostitutes destroys valuable things.
29.4: By justice a king makes a land keep standing, but a man out for bribes tears it down.
29.5: An able - bodied man that is flattering his companion is spreading out a mere net for his steps.
29.6: In the transgression of a bad man there is a snare, but he that is righteous cries out joyfully and is glad.
29.7: The righteous one is knowing the legal claim of the lowly ones. He that is wicked does not consider such knowledge.
29.8: Men of boastful talk inflame a town, but those who are wise turn back anger.
29.9: A wise man having entered into judgment with a foolish man - he has become excited and has also laughed, and there is no rest.
29.10: Bloodthirsty men hate anyone blameless; and as for the upright ones, they keep seeking for the soul of each one.
29.11: All his spirit is what a stupid one lets out, but he that is wise keeps it calm to the last.
29.12: Where a ruler is paying attention to false speech, all those waiting on him will be wicked.
29.13: The one of little means and the man of oppressions have met each other; I [ but] Jehovah is lighting up the eyes of them both.
29.14: Where a king is judging the lowly ones in trueness, his throne will be firmly established for all time.
29.15: The rod and reproof are what give wisdom; but a boy let on the loose will be causing his mother shame.
29.16: When the wicked become many, transgression abounds; but those who are righteous will look on their very downfall.
29.17: Chastise your son and he will bring you rest and give much pleasure to your soul.
29.18: Where there is no vision the people go unrestrained, but happy are they that are keeping the law.
29.19: A servant will not let himself be corrected by mere words, for he understands but he is paying no heed.
29.20: Have you beheld a man hasty with his words? There is more hope for someone stupid than for him.
29.21: If one is pampering one's servant from youth on, in his later life he will even become a thankless one.
29.22: A man given to anger stirs up contention, and anyone disposed to rage has many a transgression.
29.23: The very haughtiness of earthling man will humble him, but he that is humble in spirit will take hold of glory.
29.24: He that is partner with a thief is hating his own soul. An oath involving a curse he may hear, but he reports nothing.
29.25: Trembling at men is what lays a snare, but he that is trusting in Jehovah will be protected.
29.26: Many are those seeking the face of a ruler, but the judgment of a man is from Jehovah.
29.27: A man of injustice is something detestable to the righteous ones, and one who is upright in his way is something detestable to a wicked one.

30.1: The words of A'gur the son of Ja'keh, the weighty message. The utterance of the able - bodied man to Ith'i·el, to Ith'i·el and U'cal.
30.2: For I am more unreasoning than anyone else, and I do not have the understanding of mankind;
30.3: and I have not learned wisdom; and the knowledge of the Most Holy One I do not know.
30.4: Who has ascended to heaven that he may descend? Who has gathered the wind in the hollow of both hands? Who has wrapped up the waters in a mantle? Who has made all the ends of the earth to rise? What is his name and what the name of his son, in case you know?
30.5: Every saying of God is refined. He is a shield to those taking refuge in him.
30.6: Add nothing to his words, that he may not reprove you, and that you may not have to be proved a liar.
30.7: Two things I have asked of you. Do not withhold them from me before I die.
30.8: Untruth and the lying word put far away from me. Give me neither poverty nor riches. Let me devour the food prescribed for me,
30.9: that I may not become satisfied and I actually deny I [ you] and say: " Who is Jehovah? " and that I may not come to poverty and I actually steal and assail the name of my God.
30.10: Do not slander a servant to his master, that he may not call down evil upon you, and that you may not have to be held guilty.
30.11: There is a generation that calls down evil even upon its father and that does not bless even its mother.
30.12: There is a generation that is pure in its own eyes but that has not been washed from its own excrement.
30.13: There is a generation whose eyes have become O how lofty! and whose beaming eyes are lifted up.
30.14: There is a generation whose teeth are swords and whose jawbones are slaughtering knives, to eat up the afflicted ones off the earth and the poor ones from among mankind.
30.15: The leeches have two daughters I [ that cry]: " Give! Give! " There are three things that do not get satisfied, four that have not said: " Enough! "
30.16: She'ol and a restrained womb, a land that has not been satisfied with water, and fire that has not said: " Enough! "
30.17: The eye that holds a father in derision and that despises obedience to a mother - the ravens of the torrent valley will pick it out and the sons of the eagle will eat it up.
30.18: There are three things that have proved too wonderful for me, and four that I have not come to know:
30.19: the way of an eagle in the heavens, the way of a serpent on a rock, the way of a ship in the heart of the sea and the way of an able - bodied man with a maiden.
30.20: Here is the way of an adulterous woman: she has eaten and has wiped her mouth and she has said: " I have committed no wrong. "
30.21: Under three things the earth has been agitated, and under four it is not able to endure:
30.22: under a slave when he rules as king, and someone senseless when he has his sufficiency of food;
30.23: under a hated woman when she is taken possession of as a wife, and a maidservant when she dispossesses her mistress.
30.24: There are four things that are the smallest of the earth, but they are instinctively wise:
30.25: the ants are a people not strong, and yet in the summer they prepare their food;
30.26: the rock badgers are a people not mighty, and yet upon a crag is where they put their house;
30.27: the locusts have no king, and yet they go forth all of them divided into groups;
30.28: the gecko lizard takes hold with its own hands and it is in the grand palace of a king.
30.29: There are three that do well in I [ their] pacing, and four that do well in I [ their] moving along:
30.30: the lion, which is the mightiest among the beasts and which does not turn back from before anyone;
30.31: the greyhound or the he - goat, and a king of a band of soldiers of his own people.
30.32: If you have acted senselessly by lifting yourself up, and if you have fixed your thought I [ upon it], I [ put] the hand to the mouth.
30.33: For the churning of milk is what brings forth butter, and the squeezing of the nose is what brings forth blood, and the squeezing out of anger is what brings forth quarreling.

31.1: The words of Lem'u·el the king, the weighty message that his mother gave to him in correction:
31.2: What I [ am I saying], O son of mine, and what, O son of my belly, and what, O son of my vows?
31.3: Do not give your vital energy to women, nor your ways to I [ what leads to] wiping out kings.
31.4: It is not for kings, O Lem'u·el, it is not for kings to drink wine or for high officials I [ to say: ] " Where is intoxicating liquor? "
31.5: that one may not drink and forget what is decreed and pervert the cause of any of the sons of affliction.
31.6: Give intoxicating liquor, YOU people, to the one about to perish and wine to those who are bitter of soul.
31.7: Let one drink and forget one's poverty, and let one remember one's own trouble no more.
31.8: Open your mouth for the speechless one, in the cause of all those passing away.
31.9: Open your mouth, judge righteously and plead the cause of the afflicted one and the poor one.
31.10: A capable wife who can find? Her value is far more than that of corals.
31.11: In her the heart of her owner has put trust, and there is no gain lacking.
31.12: She has rewarded him with good, and not bad, all the days of her life.
31.13: She has sought wool and linen, and she works at whatever is the delight of her hands.
31.14: She has proved to be like the ships of a merchant. From far away she brings in her food.
31.15: She also gets up while it is still night, and gives food to her household and the prescribed portion to her young women.
31.16: She has considered a field and proceeded to obtain it; from the fruitage of her hands she has planted a vineyard.
31.17: She has girded her hips with strength, and she invigorates her arms.
31.18: She has sensed that her trading is good; her lamp does not go out at night.
31.19: Her hands she has thrust out to the distaff, and her own hands take hold of the spindle.
31.20: Her palm she has stretched out to the afflicted one, and her hands she has thrust out to the poor one.
31.21: She does not fear for her household because of the snow, for all her household are clothed with double garments.
31.22: Coverlets she has made for herself. Her clothing is of linen and wool dyed reddish purple.
31.23: Her owner is someone known in the gates, when he sits down with the older men of the land.
31.24: She has made even undergarments and proceeded to sell I [ them], and belts she has given to the tradesmen.
31.25: Strength and splendor are her clothing, and she laughs at a future day.
31.26: Her mouth she has opened in wisdom, and the law of loving - kindness is upon her tongue.
31.27: She is watching over the goings - on of her household, and the bread of laziness she does not eat.
31.28: Her sons have risen up and proceeded to pronounce her happy; her owner I [ rises up], and he praises her.
31.29: There are many daughters that have shown capableness, but you - you have ascended above them all.
31.30: Charm may be false, and prettiness may be vain; I [ but] the woman that fears Jehovah is the one that procures praise for herself.

1.1: The words of the congregator, the son of David the king in Jerusalem.
1.2: " The greatest vanity! " the congregator has said, " the greatest vanity! Everything is vanity! "
1.3: What profit does a man have in all his hard work at which he works hard under the sun?
1.4: A generation is going, and a generation is coming; but the earth is standing even to time indefinite.
1.5: And the sun also has flashed forth, and the sun has set, and it is coming panting to its place where it is going to flash forth.
1.6: The wind is going to the south, and it is circling around to the north. Round and round it is continually circling, and right back to its circlings the wind is returning.
1.7: All the winter torrents are going forth to the sea, yet the sea itself is not full. To the place where the winter torrents are going forth, there they are returning so as to go forth.
1.8: All things are wearisome; no one is able to speak of it. The eye is not satisfied at seeing, neither is the ear filled from hearing.
1.9: That which has come to be, that is what will come to be; and that which has been done, that is what will be done; and so there is nothing new under the sun.
1.10: Does anything exist of which one may say: " See this; it is new "? It has already had existence for time indefinite; what has come into existence is from time prior to us.
1.11: There is no remembrance of people of former times, nor will there be of those also who will come to be later. There will prove to be no remembrance even of them among those who will come to be still later on.
1.12: I, the congregator, happened to be king over Israel in Jerusalem.
1.13: And I set my heart to seek and explore wisdom in relation to everything that has been done under the heavens - the calamitous occupation that God has given to the sons of mankind in which to be occupied.
1.14: I saw all the works that were done under the sun, and, look! everything was vanity and a striving after wind.
1.15: That which is made crooked cannot be made straight, and that which is wanting cannot possibly be counted.
1.16: I, even I, spoke with my heart, saying: " Look! I myself have greatly increased in wisdom more than anyone that happened to be before me in Jerusalem, and my own heart saw a great deal of wisdom and knowledge. "
1.17: And I proceeded to give my heart to knowing wisdom and to knowing madness, and I have come to know folly, that this too is a striving after wind.
1.18: For in the abundance of wisdom there is an abundance of vexation, so that he that increases knowledge increases pain.

2.1: I said, even I, in my heart: " Do come now, let me try you out with rejoicing. Also, see good. " And, look! that too was vanity.
2.2: I said to laughter: " Insanity! " and to rejoicing: " What is this doing? "
2.3: I explored with my heart by cheering my flesh even with wine, while I was leading my heart with wisdom, even to lay hold on folly until I could see what good there was to the sons of mankind in what they did under the heavens for the number of the days of their life.
2.4: I engaged in greater works. I built houses for myself; I planted vineyards for myself.
2.5: I made gardens and parks for myself, and I planted in them fruit trees of all sorts.
2.6: I made pools of water for myself, to irrigate with them the forest, springing up with trees.
2.7: I acquired menservants and maidservants, and I came to have sons of the household. Also, livestock, cattle and flocks in great quantity I came to have, more so than all those who happened to be before me in Jerusalem.
2.8: I accumulated also silver and gold for myself, and property peculiar to kings and the jurisdictional districts. I made male singers and female singers for myself and the exquisite delights of the sons of mankind, a lady, even ladies.
2.9: And I became greater and increased more than anyone that happened to be before me in Jerusalem. Moreover, my own wisdom remained mine.
2.10: And anything that my eyes asked for I did not keep away from them. I did not hold back my heart from any sort of rejoicing, for my heart was joyful because of all my hard work, and this came to be my portion from all my hard work.
2.11: And I, even I, turned toward all the works of mine that my hands had done and toward the hard work that I had worked hard to accomplish, and, look! everything was vanity and a striving after wind, and there was nothing of advantage under the sun.
2.12: And I, even I, turned to see wisdom and madness and folly; for what can the earthling man do who comes in after the king? The thing that people have already done.
2.13: And I saw, even I, that there exists more advantage for wisdom than for folly, just as there is more advantage for light than for darkness.
2.14: As regards anyone wise, his eyes are in his head; but the stupid one is walking on in sheer darkness. And I have come to know, I too, that there is one eventuality that eventuates to them all.
2.15: And I myself said in my heart: " An eventuality like that upon the stupid one will eventuate to me, yes, me. " Why, then, had I become wise, I overmuch so at that time? And I spoke in my heart: " This too is vanity. "
2.16: For there is no more remembrance of the wise one than of the stupid one to time indefinite. In the days that are already coming in, everyone is certainly forgotten; and how will the wise one die? Along with the stupid one.
2.17: And I hated life, because the work that has been done under the sun was calamitous from my standpoint, for everything was vanity and a striving after wind.
2.18: And I, even I, hated all my hard work at which I was working hard under the sun, that I would leave behind for the man who would come to be after me.
2.19: And who is there knowing whether he will prove to be wise or foolish? Yet he will take control over all my hard work at which I worked hard and at which I showed wisdom under the sun. This too is vanity.
2.20: And I myself turned around toward making my heart despair over all the hard work at which I had worked hard under the sun.
2.21: For there exists the man whose hard work has been with wisdom and with knowledge and with proficiency, but to a man that has not worked hard at such a thing will be given the portion of that one. This too is vanity and a big calamity.
2.22: For what does a man come to have for all his hard work and for the striving of his heart with which he is working hard under the sun?
2.23: For all his days his occupation means pains and vexation, also during the night his heart just does not lie down. This too is mere vanity.
2.24: With a man there is nothing better I [ than] that he should eat and indeed drink and cause his soul to see good because of his hard work. This too I have seen, even I, that this is from the hand of the I [ true] God.
2.25: For who eats and who drinks better than I do?
2.26: For to the man that is good before him he has given wisdom and knowledge and rejoicing, but to the sinner he has given the occupation of gathering and bringing together merely to give to the one that is good before the I [ true] God. This too is vanity and a striving after wind.

3.1: For everything there is an appointed time, even a time for every affair under the heavens:
3.2: a time for birth and a time to die; a time to plant and a time to uproot what was planted;
3.3: a time to kill and a time to heal; a time to break down and a time to build;
3.4: a time to weep and a time to laugh; a time to wail and a time to skip about;
3.5: a time to throw stones away and a time to bring stones together; a time to embrace and a time to keep away from embracing;
3.6: a time to seek and a time to give up as lost; a time to keep and a time to throw away;
3.7: a time to rip apart and a time to sew together; a time to keep quiet and a time to speak;
3.8: a time to love and a time to hate; a time for war and a time for peace.
3.9: What advantage is there for the doer in what he is working hard at?
3.10: I have seen the occupation that God has given to the sons of mankind in which to be occupied.
3.11: Everything he has made pretty in its time. Even time indefinite he has put in their heart, that mankind may never find out the work that the I [ true] God has made from the start to the finish.
3.12: I have come to know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice and to do good during one's life;
3.13: and also that every man should eat and indeed drink and see good for all his hard work. It is the gift of God.
3.14: I have come to know that everything that the I [ true] God makes, it will prove to be to time indefinite. To it there is nothing to add and from it there is nothing to subtract; but the I [ true] God himself has made it, that people may be afraid on account of him.
3.15: What has happened to be, it had already been, and what is to come to be has already proved to be; and the I [ true] God himself keeps seeking that which is pursued.
3.16: And I have further seen under the sun the place of justice where there was wickedness and the place of righteousness where wickedness was.
3.17: I myself have said in my heart: " The I [ true] God will judge both the righteous one and the wicked one, for there is a time for every affair and concerning every work there. "
3.18: I, even I, have said in my heart with regard to the sons of mankind that the I [ true] God is going to select them, that they may see that they themselves are beasts.
3.19: For there is an eventuality as respects the sons of mankind and an eventuality as respects the beast, and they have the same eventuality. As the one dies, so the other dies; and they all have but one spirit, so that there is no superiority of the man over the beast, for everything is vanity.
3.20: All are going to one place. They have all come to be from the dust, and they are all returning to the dust.
3.21: Who is there knowing the spirit of the sons of mankind, whether it is ascending upward; and the spirit of the beast, whether it is descending downward to the earth?
3.22: And I have seen that there is nothing better than that the man should rejoice in his works, for that is his portion; because who will bring him in to look on what is going to be after him?

4.1: And I myself returned that I might see all the acts of oppression that are being done under the sun, and, look! the tears of those being oppressed, but they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power, so that they had no comforter.
4.2: And I congratulated the dead who had already died rather than the living who were still alive.
4.3: So better than both of them I [ is] the one who has not yet come to be, who has not seen the calamitous work that is being done under the sun.
4.4: And I myself have seen all the hard work and all the proficiency in work, that it means the rivalry of one toward another; this also is vanity and a striving after the wind.
4.5: The stupid one is folding his hands and is eating his own flesh.
4.6: Better is a handful of rest than a double handful of hard work and striving after the wind.
4.7: I myself returned that I might see the vanity under the sun:
4.8: There exists one, but not a second one; also no son or brother does he have, but there is no end to all his hard work. Also, his eyes themselves are not satisfied with riches: " And for whom am I working hard and causing my soul to lack in good things? " This too is vanity, and it is a calamitous occupation.
4.9: Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their hard work.
4.10: For if one of them should fall, the other one can raise his partner up. But how will it be with just the one who falls when there is not another to raise him up?
4.11: Moreover, if two lie down together, they also will certainly get warm; but how can just one keep warm?
4.12: And if somebody could overpower one alone, two together could make a stand against him. And a threefold cord cannot quickly be torn in two.
4.13: Better is a needy but wise child than an old but stupid king, who has not come to know enough to be warned any longer.
4.14: For he has gone forth from the prison house itself to become king, although in the kingship of this one he had been born as one of little means.
4.15: I have seen all those alive who are walking about under the sun, I [ how it goes] with the child, who is second, that stands up in the other one's place.
4.16: There is no end to all the people, to all those before whom he happened to be; neither will people afterward rejoice in him, for this too is vanity and a striving after the wind.

5.1: Guard your feet whenever you go to the house of the I [ true] God; and let there be a drawing near to hear, rather than to give a sacrifice as the stupid ones do, for they are not aware of doing what is bad.
5.2: Do not hurry yourself as regards your mouth; and as for your heart, let it not be hasty to bring forth a word before the I [ true] God. For the I [ true] God is in the heavens but you are on the earth. That is why your words should prove to be few.
5.3: For a dream certainly comes in because of abundance of occupation, and the voice of a stupid one because of the abundance of words.
5.4: Whenever you vow a vow to God, do not hesitate to pay it, for there is no delight in the stupid ones. What you vow, pay.
5.5: Better is it that you vow not than that you vow and do not pay.
5.6: Do not allow your mouth to cause your flesh to sin, neither say before the angel that it was a mistake. Why should the I [ true] God become indignant on account of your voice and have to wreck the work of your hands?
5.7: For because of abundance I [ of occupation] there are dreams, and there are vanities and words in abundance. But fear the I [ true] God himself.
5.8: If you see any oppression of the one of little means and the violent taking away of judgment and of righteousness in a jurisdictional district, do not be amazed over the affair, for one that is higher than the high one is watching, and there are those who are high above them.
5.9: Also, the profit of the earth is among them all; for a field the king himself has been served.
5.10: A mere lover of silver will not be satisfied with silver, neither any lover of wealth with income. This too is vanity.
5.11: When good things become many, those eating them certainly become many. And what advantage is there to the grand owner of them, except looking I [ at them] with his eyes?
5.12: Sweet is the sleep of the one serving, regardless of whether it is little or much that he eats; but the plenty belonging to the rich one is not permitting him to sleep.
5.13: There exists a grave calamity that I have seen under the sun: riches being kept for their grand owner to his calamity.
5.14: And those riches have perished because of a calamitous occupation, and he has become father to a son when there is nothing at all in his hand.
5.15: Just as one has come forth from his mother's belly, naked will one go away again, just as one came; and nothing at all can one carry away for his hard work, which he can take along with his hand.
5.16: And this too is a grave calamity: exactly as one has come, so one will go away; and what profit is there to the one who keeps working hard for the wind?
5.17: Also, all his days he eats in darkness itself, with a great deal of vexation, with sickness on his part and I [ cause for] indignation.
5.18: Look! The best thing that I myself have seen, which is pretty, is that one should eat and drink and see good for all his hard work with which he works hard under the sun for the number of the days of his life that the I [ true] God has given him, for that is his portion.
5.19: Also every man to whom the I [ true] God has given riches and material possessions, he has even empowered him to eat from it and to carry off his portion and to rejoice in his hard work. This is the gift of God.
5.20: For not often will he remember the days of his life, because the I [ true] God is preoccupying I [ him] with the rejoicing of his heart.

6.1: There exists a calamity that I have seen under the sun, and it is frequent among mankind:
6.2: a man to whom the I [ true] God gives riches and material possessions and glory and who, for his soul, is in no need of anything that he shows himself longing for, and yet the I [ true] God does not enable him to eat from it, although a mere foreigner may eat it. This is vanity and it is a bad sickness.
6.3: If a man should become a father a hundred times, and he should live many years, so that numerous the days of his years should become, yet his own soul is not satisfied with good things and even the grave has not become his, I must say that one prematurely born is better off than he is.
6.4: For in vain has this one come and in darkness he goes away, and with darkness his own name will be covered.
6.5: Even the sun itself he has not seen, neither known. This one has rest rather than the former one.
6.6: Even supposing that he has lived a thousand years twice over and yet he has not seen what is good, is it not to just one place that everyone is going?
6.7: All the hard work of mankind is for their mouth, but even their own soul does not get filled.
6.8: For what advantage does the wise have over the stupid one? What does the afflicted one have in knowing how to walk in front of the living ones?
6.9: Better is the seeing by the eyes than the walking about of the soul. This too is vanity and a striving after the wind.
6.10: Whatever has come to be, its name has already been pronounced, and it has become known what man is; and he is not able to plead his cause with one that is more powerful than he is.
6.11: Because there exist many things that are causing much vanity, what advantage does a man have?
6.12: For who is there knowing what good a man has in life for the number of the days of his vain life, when he spends them like a shadow? For who can tell man what will happen after him under the sun?

7.1: A name is better than good oil, and the day of death than the day of one's being born.
7.2: Better is it to go to the house of mourning than to go to the banquet house, because that is the end of all mankind; and the one alive should take I [ it] to his heart.
7.3: Better is vexation than laughter, for by the crossness of the face the heart becomes better.
7.4: The heart of the wise ones is in the house of mourning, but the heart of the stupid ones is in the house of rejoicing.
7.5: Better is it to hear the rebuke of someone wise than to be the man hearing the song of the stupid ones.
7.6: For as the sound of thorns under the pot, so is the laughter of the stupid one; and this too is vanity.
7.7: For mere oppression may make a wise one act crazy, and a gift can destroy the heart.
7.8: Better is the end afterward of a matter than its beginning. Better is one who is patient than one who is haughty in spirit.
7.9: Do not hurry yourself in your spirit to become offended, for the taking of offense is what rests in the bosom of the stupid ones.
7.10: Do not say: " Why has it happened that the former days proved to be better than these? " for it is not due to wisdom that you have asked about this.
7.11: Wisdom along with an inheritance is good and is advantageous for those seeing the sun.
7.12: For wisdom is for a protection I [ the same as] money is for a protection; but the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom itself preserves alive its owners.
7.13: See the work of the I [ true] God, for who is able to make straight what he has made crooked?
7.14: On a good day prove yourself to be in goodness, and on a calamitous day see that the I [ true] God has made even this exactly as that, to the intent that mankind may not discover anything at all after them.
7.15: Everything I have seen during my vain days. There exists the righteous one perishing in his righteousness, and there exists the wicked one continuing long in his badness.
7.16: Do not become righteous overmuch, nor show yourself excessively wise. Why should you cause desolation to yourself?
7.17: Do not be wicked overmuch, nor become foolish. Why should you die when it is not your time?
7.18: It is better that you should take hold of the one, but from the other also do not withdraw your hand; for he that fears God will go forth with them all.
7.19: Wisdom itself is stronger for the wise one than ten men in power who happened to be in a city.
7.20: For there is no man righteous in the earth that keeps doing good and does not sin.
7.21: Also, do not give your heart to all the words that people may speak, that you may not hear your servant calling down evil upon you.
7.22: For your own heart well knows even many times that you, even you, have called down evil upon others.
7.23: All this I have tested with wisdom. I said: " I will become wise. " But it was far from me.
7.24: What has come to be is far off and exceedingly deep. Who can find it out?
7.25: I myself turned around, even my heart did, to know and to explore and to search for wisdom and the reason of things, and to know about the wickedness of stupidity and the foolishness of madness;
7.26: and I was finding out: More bitter than death I [ I found] the woman who is herself nets for hunting and whose heart is dragnets I [ and] whose hands are fetters. One is good before the I [ true] God if one escapes from her, but one is sinning if one is captured by her.
7.27: " See! This I have found, " said the congregator, " one thing I [ taken] after another, to find out the sum - up,
7.28: which my soul has continuously sought, but I have not found. One man out of a thousand I have found, but a woman among all these I have not found.
7.29: See! This only I have found, that the I [ true] God made mankind upright, but they themselves have sought out many plans. "

8.1: Who is there like the wise one? And who is there knowing the interpretation of a thing? The wisdom of a man itself causes his face to shine, and even the sternness of his face is changed I [ for the better].
8.2: I I [ say: ] " Keep the very order of the king, and that out of regard for the oath of God.
8.3: Do not hurry yourself, that you may go out from before him. Do not stand in a bad thing. For all that he delights I [ to do] he will do,
8.4: because the word of the king is the power of control; and who may say to him: 'What are you doing? ' "
8.5: He that is keeping the commandment will not know any calamitous thing, and the wise heart will know both time and judgment.
8.6: For there exists a time and judgment even for every affair, because the calamity of mankind is abundant upon them.
8.7: For there is no one knowing what will come to be, because who can tell him just how it will come to be?
8.8: There is no man having power over the spirit to restrain the spirit; neither is there any power of control in the day of death; nor is there any discharge in the war. And wickedness will provide no escape for those indulging in it.
8.9: All this I have seen, and there was an applying of my heart to every work that has been done under the sun, I [ during] the time that man has dominated man to his injury.
8.10: But, though this is so, I have seen the wicked ones being buried, how they came in and how they would go away from the holy place itself and be forgotten in the city where they acted that way. This too is vanity.
8.11: Because sentence against a bad work has not been executed speedily, that is why the heart of the sons of men has become fully set in them to do bad.
8.12: Although a sinner may be doing bad a hundred times and continuing a long time as he pleases, yet I am also aware that it will turn out well with those fearing the I [ true] God, because they were in fear of him.
8.13: But it will not turn out well at all with the wicked one, neither will he prolong his days that are like a shadow, because he is not in fear of God.
8.14: There exists a vanity that is carried out on the earth, that there exist righteous ones to whom it is happening as if for the work of the wicked ones, and there exist wicked ones to whom it is happening as if for the work of the righteous ones. I said that this too is vanity.
8.15: And I myself commended rejoicing, because mankind have nothing better under the sun than to eat and drink and rejoice, and that it should accompany them in their hard work for the days of their life, which the I [ true] God has given them under the sun.
8.16: In accord with this I applied my heart to know wisdom and to see the occupation that is carried on in the earth, because there is one seeing no sleep with his eyes, either by day or by night.
8.17: And I saw all the work of the I [ true] God, how mankind are not able to find out the work that has been done under the sun; however much mankind keep working hard to seek, yet they do not find out. And even if they should say they are wise enough to know, they would be unable to find out.

9.1: For I took all this to my heart, even to search out all this, that the righteous ones and the wise ones and their works are in the hand of the I [ true] God. Mankind are not aware of either the love or the hate that were all prior to them.
9.2: All are the same in what all have. One eventuality there is to the righteous one and the wicked one, the good one and the clean one and the unclean one, and the one sacrificing and the one that is not sacrificing. The good one is the same as the sinner; the one swearing is the same as whoever has been afraid of a sworn oath.
9.3: This is what is calamitous in all that has been done under the sun, that, because there is one eventuality to all, the heart of the sons of men is also full of bad; and there is madness in their heart during their lifetime, and after it - to the dead ones!
9.4: For as respects whoever is joined to all the living there exists confidence, because a live dog is better off than a dead lion.
9.5: For the living are conscious that they will die; but as for the dead, they are conscious of nothing at all, neither do they anymore have wages, because the remembrance of them has been forgotten.
9.6: Also, their love and their hate and their jealousy have already perished, and they have no portion anymore to time indefinite in anything that has to be done under the sun.
9.7: Go, eat your food with rejoicing and drink your wine with a good heart, because already the I [ true] God has found pleasure in your works.
9.8: On every occasion let your garments prove to be white, and let oil not be lacking upon your head.
9.9: See life with the wife whom you love all the days of your vain life that He has given you under the sun, all the days of your vanity, for that is your portion in life and in your hard work with which you are working hard under the sun.
9.10: All that your hand finds to do, do with your very power, for there is no work nor devising nor knowledge nor wisdom in She'ol, the place to which you are going.
9.11: I returned to see under the sun that the swift do not have the race, nor the mighty ones the battle, nor do the wise also have the food, nor do the understanding ones also have the riches, nor do even those having knowledge have the favor; because time and unforeseen occurrence befall them all.
9.12: For man also does not know his time. Just like fishes that are being taken in an evil net, and like birds that are being taken in a trap, so the sons of men themselves are being ensnared at a calamitous time, when it falls upon them suddenly.
9.13: Also this I saw as respects wisdom under the sun - and it was great to me:
9.14: There was a little city, and the men in it were few; and there came to it a great king, and he surrounded it and built against it great strongholds.
9.15: And there was found in it a man, needy I [ but] wise, and that one provided escape for the city by his wisdom. But no man remembered that needy man.
9.16: And I myself said: " Wisdom is better than mightiness; yet the wisdom of the needy one is despised, and his words are not listened to. "
9.17: The words of the wise ones in quietness are more to be heard than the cry of one ruling among stupid people.
9.18: Wisdom is better than implements for fighting, and merely one sinner can destroy much good.

10.1: Dead flies are what cause the oil of the ointment maker to stink, to bubble forth. I [ So] a little foolishness does to one who is precious for wisdom and glory.
10.2: The heart of the wise is at his right hand, but the heart of the stupid at his left hand.
10.3: And also in whatever way the foolish one is walking, his own heart is lacking, and he certainly says to everybody that he is foolish.
10.4: If the spirit of a ruler should mount up against you, do not leave your own place, for calmness itself allays great sins.
10.5: There exists something calamitous that I have seen under the sun, as when there is a mistake going forth on account of the one in power:
10.6: Foolishness has been put in many high positions, but the rich ones themselves keep dwelling merely in a low condition.
10.7: I have seen servants on horses but princes walking on the earth just like servants.
10.8: He that is digging a pit will himself fall right into it; and he that is breaking through a stone wall, a serpent will bite him.
10.9: He that is quarrying out stones will hurt himself with them. He that is splitting logs will have to be careful with them.
10.10: If an iron tool has become blunt and someone has not whetted its edge, then he will exert his own vital energies. So the using of wisdom to success means advantage.
10.11: If the serpent bites when no charming results, then there is no advantage to the one indulging in the tongue.
10.12: The words of the mouth of the wise one mean favor, but the lips of the stupid one swallow him up.
10.13: The start of the words of his mouth is foolishness, and the end afterward of his mouth is calamitous madness.
10.14: And the foolish one speaks many words. Man does not know what will come to be; and that which will come to be after him, who can tell him?
10.15: The hard work of the stupid ones makes them weary, because not one has come to know how to go to the city.
10.16: How will it be with you, O land, when your king is a boy and your own princes keep eating even in the morning?
10.17: Happy are you, O land, when your king is the son of noble ones and your own princes eat at the proper time for mightiness, not for mere drinking.
10.18: Through great laziness the beamwork sinks in, and through the letting down of the hands the house leaks.
10.19: Bread is for the laughter of the workers, and wine itself makes life rejoice; but money is what meets a response in all things.
10.20: Even in your bedroom do not call down evil upon the king himself, and in the interior rooms where you lie down do not call down evil upon anyone rich; for a flying creature of the heavens will convey the sound and something owning wings will tell the matter.

11.1: Send out your bread upon the surface of the waters, for in the course of many days you will find it again.
11.2: Give a portion to seven, or even to eight, for you do not know what calamity will occur on the earth.
11.3: If the clouds are filled I [ with water], they empty out a sheer downpour upon the earth; and if a tree falls to the south or if to the north, in the place where the tree falls there it will prove to be.
11.4: He that is watching the wind will not sow seed; and he that is looking at the clouds will not reap.
11.5: Just as you are not aware of what is the way of the spirit in the bones in the belly of her that is pregnant, in like manner you do not know the work of the I [ true] God, who does all things.
11.6: In the morning sow your seed and until the evening do not let your hand rest; for you are not knowing where this will have success, either here or there, or whether both of them will alike be good.
11.7: The light is also sweet, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun;
11.8: for if a man should live even many years, in all of them let him rejoice. And let him remember the days of darkness, though they could be many; every I [ day] that has come in is vanity.
11.9: Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart do you good in the days of your young manhood, and walk in the ways of your heart and in the things seen by your eyes. But know that on account of all these the I [ true] God will bring you into judgment.
11.10: So remove vexation from your heart, and ward off calamity from your flesh; for youth and the prime of life are vanity.

12.1: Remember, now, your Grand Creator in the days of your young manhood, before the calamitous days proceed to come, or the years have arrived when you will say: " I have no delight in them ";
12.2: before the sun and the light and the moon and the stars grow dark, and the clouds have returned, afterward the downpour;
12.3: in the day when the keepers of the house tremble, and the men of vital energy have bent themselves, and the grinding women have quit working because they have become few, and the ladies seeing at the windows have found it dark;
12.4: and the doors onto the street have been closed, when the sound of the grinding mill becomes low, and one gets up at the sound of a bird, and all the daughters of song sound low.
12.5: Also, they have become afraid merely at what is high, and there are terrors in the way. And the almond tree carries blossoms, and the grasshopper drags itself along, and the caper berry bursts, because man is walking to his long - lasting house and the wailers have marched around in the street;
12.6: before the silver cord is removed, and the golden bowl gets crushed, and the jar at the spring is broken, and the waterwheel for the cistern has been crushed.
12.7: Then the dust returns to the earth just as it happened to be and the spirit itself returns to the I [ true] God who gave it.
12.8: " The greatest vanity! " said the congregator, " Everything is vanity. "
12.9: And besides the fact that the congregator had become wise, he also taught the people knowledge continually, and he pondered and made a thorough search, that he might arrange many proverbs in order.
12.10: The congregator sought to find the delightful words and the writing of correct words of truth.
12.11: The words of the wise ones are like oxgoads, and just like nails driven in are those indulging in collections I [ of sentences]; they have been given from one shepherd.
12.12: As regards anything besides these, my son, take a warning: To the making of many books there is no end, and much devotion I [ to them] is wearisome to the flesh.
12.13: The conclusion of the matter, everything having been heard, is: Fear the I [ true] God and keep his commandments. For this is the whole I [ obligation] of man.
12.14: For the I [ true] God himself will bring every sort of work into the judgment in relation to every hidden thing, as to whether it is good or bad.

1.1: The superlative song, which is Sol'o·mon's:
1.2: " May he kiss me with the kisses of his mouth, for your expressions of endearment are better than wine.
1.3: For fragrance your oils are good. Like an oil that is poured out is your name. That is why maidens themselves have loved you.
1.4: Draw me with you; let us run. The king has brought me into his interior rooms! Do let us be joyful and rejoice in you. Do let us mention your expressions of endearment more than wine. Deservedly they have loved you.
1.5: " A black girl I am, but comely, O YOU daughters of Jerusalem, like the tents of Ke'dar, I [ yet] like the tent cloths of Sol'o·mon.
1.6: Do not YOU look at me because I am swarthy, because the sun has caught sight of me. The sons of my own mother grew angry with me; they appointed me the keeper of the vineyards, I [ although] my vineyard, one that was mine, I did not keep.
1.7: " Do tell me, O you whom my soul has loved, where you do shepherding, where you make the flock lie down at midday. Just why should I become like a woman wrapped in mourning among the droves of your partners? "
1.8: " If you do not know for yourself, O you most beautiful one among women, go out yourself in the footprints of the flock and pasture your kids of the goats alongside the tabernacles of the shepherds. "
1.9: " To a mare of mine in the chariots of Phar'aoh I have likened you, O girl companion of mine.
1.10: Your cheeks are comely among the hair braids, your neck in a string of beads.
1.11: Circlets of gold we shall make for you, along with studs of silver. "
1.12: " As long as the king is at his round table my own spikenard has given out its fragrance.
1.13: As a bag of myrrh my dear one is to me; between my breasts he will spend the night.
1.14: As a cluster of henna my dear one is to me, among the vineyards of En - ge'di. "
1.15: " Look! You are beautiful, O girl companion of mine. Look! You are beautiful. Your eyes are I [ those of] doves. "
1.16: " Look! You are beautiful, my dear one, also pleasant. Our divan also is one of foliage.
1.17: The beams of our grand house are cedars, our rafters juniper trees.

2.1: " A mere saffron of the coastal plain I am, a lily of the low plains. "
2.2: " Like a lily among thorny weeds, so is my girl companion among the daughters. "
2.3: " Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my dear one among the sons. His shade I have passionately desired, and there I have sat down, and his fruit has been sweet to my palate.
2.4: He brought me into the house of wine, and his banner over me was love.
2.5: Do YOU people refresh me with cakes of raisins, sustain me with apples; for I am lovesick.
2.6: His left hand is under my head; and his right hand - it embraces me.
2.7: I have put YOU under oath, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the female gazelles or by the hinds of the field, that YOU try not to awaken or arouse love I [ in me] until it feels inclined.
2.8: " The sound of my dear one! Look! This one is coming, climbing upon the mountains, leaping upon the hills.
2.9: My dear one is resembling a gazelle or the young of the stags. Look! This one is standing behind our wall, gazing through the windows, glancing through the lattices.
2.10: My dear one has answered and said to me, 'Rise up, you girl companion of mine, my beautiful one, and come away.
2.11: For, look! the rainy season itself has passed, the downpour itself is over, it has gone its way.
2.12: Blossoms themselves have appeared in the land, the very time of vine trimming has arrived, and the voice of the turtledove itself has been heard in our land.
2.13: As for the fig tree, it has gained a mature color for its early figs; and the vines are abloom, they have given I [ their] fragrance. Rise up, come, O girl companion of mine, my beautiful one, and come away.
2.14: O my dove in the retreats of the crag, in the concealed place of the steep way, show me your form, let me hear your voice, for your voice is pleasurable and your form is comely. ' "
2.15: " Do YOU people grab hold of the foxes for us, the little foxes that are making spoil of the vineyards, as our vineyards are abloom. "
2.16: " My dear one is mine and I am his. He is shepherding among the lilies.
2.17: Until the day breathes and the shadows have fled, turn around, O my dear one; be like the gazelle or like the young of the stags upon the mountains of separation.

3.1: " On my bed during the nights I have sought the one whom my soul has loved. I sought him, but I did not find him.
3.2: Let me rise up, please, and go round about in the city; in the streets and in the public squares let me seek the one whom my soul has loved. I sought him, but I did not find him.
