7.14: And they did not call to me for aid with their heart, although they kept howling on their beds. On account of their grain and sweet wine they kept loafing about; they kept turning against me.
7.15: And I, for my part, did disciplining; I strengthened their arms, but against me they kept scheming what was bad.
7.16: And they proceeded to return, not to anything higher; they had become like a loose bow. By the sword their princes will fall because of the denunciation of their tongue. This will be their derision in the land of Egypt. "

8.1: " To your mouth - a horn! I [ One comes] like an eagle against the house of Jehovah, for the reason that they have overstepped my covenant, and against my law they have transgressed.
8.2: To me they keep crying, 'O my God, we, Israel, have known you. '
8.3: " Israel has cast off good. Let one who is an enemy pursue him.
8.4: They themselves have set up kings, but not because of me. They have set up princes, but I did not know I [ it]. With their silver and their gold they have made for themselves idols, to the end that they may be cut off.
8.5: Your calf has been cast off, O Sa·mar'i·a. My anger has grown hot against them. How long will they be incapable of innocency?
8.6: For from Israel was even this. A mere craftsman made it, and it is not God; because the calf of Sa·mar'i·a will become mere splinters.
8.7: " For it is wind that they keep sowing, and a storm wind is what they will reap. Nothing has standing grain. No sprout produces flour. Should any perhaps produce I [ it], strangers themselves will swallow it down.
8.8: " Israel must be swallowed down. Now they must come to be among the nations, like a vessel in which there is no delight.
8.9: For they themselves have gone up to As·syr'i·a, as a zebra isolated to itself. In E'phra·im's case, they have hired lovers.
8.10: Also, although they keep hiring I [ them] among the nations, I shall now collect them together; and they will be a little while in severe pains because of the burden of king I [ and] princes.
8.11: " For E'phra·im has multiplied altars in order to sin. He has come to have altars in order to sin.
8.12: I proceeded to write for him many things of my law; just like something strange they have been accounted.
8.13: As my gift sacrifices they kept sacrificing flesh, and they kept eating what Jehovah himself took no pleasure in. Now he will remember their error and hold an accounting for their sins. To Egypt they themselves proceeded to return.
8.14: And Israel began forgetting his Maker and building temples; and Judah, for his part, multiplied fortified cities. And I shall certainly send fire into his cities and it must devour the dwelling towers of I [ each] one. "

9.1: " Do not rejoice, O Israel. Do not act joyful like the peoples. For by fornication you have gone from alongside your God. You have loved gifts of hire on all the threshing floors of grain.
9.2: Threshing floor and winepress do not feed them, and sweet wine itself proves disappointing to her.
9.3: They will not continue dwelling in the land of Jehovah, and E'phra·im must return to Egypt, and in As·syr'i·a they will eat what is unclean.
9.4: They will not continue pouring out wine to Jehovah. And their sacrifices will not be gratifying to him; they are like the bread of times of mourning to them; all those eating it will defile themselves. For their bread is for their own soul; it will not come into the house of Jehovah.
9.5: What will YOU people do in the day of meeting and in the day of the festival of Jehovah?
9.6: For, look! they will have to go because of despoiling. Egypt itself will collect them together; Mem'phis, for its part, will bury them. As for their desirable things of silver, nettles themselves will take possession of them; thorny bushes will be in their tents.
9.7: " The days of being given attention must come; the days of the due payment must come. Those of Israel will know I [ it]. The prophet will be foolish, the man of inspired expression will be maddened on account of the abundance of your error, even animosity being abundant. "
9.8: The watchman of E'phra·im was with my God. As regards a prophet, there is the trap of a birdcatcher on all his ways; there is an animosity in the house of his God.
9.9: They have gone down deep in bringing ruin, as in the days of Gib'e·ah. He will remember their error; he will give attention to their sins.
9.10: " Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel. Like the early fig on a fig tree in its beginning I saw the forefathers of YOU people. They themselves went in to Ba'al of Pe'or, and they proceeded to dedicate themselves to the shameful thing, and they came to be disgusting like I [ the thing of] their love.
9.11: As regards E'phra·im, like a flying creature their glory flies away, so that there is no giving birth, and no I [ pregnant] belly and no conception.
9.12: For although they bring up their sons, I will also bereave them of children so that there will be no man; because - woe also to them when I turn away from them!
9.13: E'phra·im, whom I have seen like Tyre planted in a pasture ground, even E'phra·im is destined to a bringing out of his sons even to a killer. "
9.14: Give to them, O Jehovah, what you should give. Give them a miscarrying womb and breasts shriveling up.
9.15: " All their badness was in Gil'gal, for there I had to hate them. On account of the evil of their dealings I shall drive them away from my own house. I will not continue on loving them. All their princes are acting stubborn.
9.16: E'phra·im must be struck down. Their very root must dry up. There will be no fruit that they produce. Also, in case they bring to birth, I will even put to death the desirable things of their belly. "
9.17: My God will reject them, for they have not listened to him, and they will become fugitives among the nations.

10.1: " Israel is a degenerating vine. Fruit he keeps putting forth for himself. In proportion to the abundance of his fruit he has multiplied I [ his] altars. In proportion to the goodness of his land, they put up good pillars.
10.2: Their heart has become hypocritical; now they will be found guilty. " There is one who will break their altars; he will despoil their pillars.
10.3: For now they will say, 'We have no king, for we have not feared Jehovah. And as regards the king, what will he do for us? '
10.4: " They speak words, making false oaths, concluding a covenant; and judgment has sprouted like a poisonous plant in the furrows of the open field.
10.5: For the calf I [ idol] of Beth - a'ven the residents of Sa·mar'i·a will get frightened; for over it its people will certainly mourn, as well as its foreign - god priests I [ who] used to be joyful over it, on account of its glory, because it will have gone into exile away from it.
10.6: Even it someone will bring to As·syr'i·a itself as a gift to a great king. Shame is what E'phra·im himself will get, and Israel will be ashamed of its counsel.
10.7: Sa·mar'i·a I [ and] her king will certainly be silenced, like a snapped - off twig on the surface of waters.
10.8: And the high places of I [ Beth - ]a'ven, the sin of Israel, will actually be annihilated. Thorns and thistles themselves will come up upon their altars. And people will in fact say to the mountains, 'Cover us! ' and to the hills, 'Fall over us! '
10.9: " From the days of Gib'e·ah you have sinned, O Israel. There they stood still. In Gib'e·ah war against the sons of unrighteousness did not get to overtake them.
10.10: When it is my craving I shall also discipline them. And against them peoples will certainly be gathered when there is a harnessing of them to their two errors.
10.11: " And E'phra·im was a trained heifer loving to thresh; and I, for my part, passed over her good - looking neck. I make I [ someone] ride E'phra·im. Judah plows; Jacob harrows for him.
10.12: Sow seed for yourselves in righteousness; reap in accord with loving - kindness. Till for yourselves arable land, when there is time for searching for Jehovah until he comes and gives instruction in righteousness to YOU.
10.13: " YOU people have plowed wickedness. Unrighteousness is what YOU have reaped. YOU have eaten the fruitage of deception, for you have trusted in your way, in the multitude of your mighty ones.
10.14: And an uproar has risen among your people, and your own fortified cities will all be despoiled, as with the despoiling by Shal'man of the house of Ar'bel, in the day of battle I [ when] a mother herself was dashed to pieces alongside I [ her] own sons.
10.15: In this way one will certainly do to YOU people, O Beth'el, because of YOUR extreme badness. In the dawn the king of Israel will positively have to be silenced. "

11.1: " When Israel was a boy, then I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.
11.2: " They called them. To that same extent they went away from before them. To the Ba'al images they took up sacrificing, and to the graven images they began making sacrificial smoke.
11.3: But as for me, I taught E'phra·im to walk, taking them upon I [ my] arms; and they did not recognize that I had healed them.
11.4: With the ropes of earthling man I kept drawing them, with the cords of love, so that I became to them as those lifting off a yoke on their jaws, and gently I brought food to I [ each] one.
11.5: He will not return to the land of Egypt, but As·syr'i·a will be his king, because they refused to return.
11.6: And a sword will certainly whirl about in his cities and make an end of his bars and devour because of their counsels.
11.7: And my people are tending toward unfaithfulness to me. And upward they call it; no one at all does any rising up.
11.8: " How can I give you up, O E'phra·im? I [ How] can I deliver you up, O Israel? How can I set you as Ad'mah? I [ How] can I place you like Ze·boi'im? My heart has changed within me; at the same time my compassions have grown hot.
11.9: I shall not express my burning anger. I shall not bring E'phra·im to ruin again, for I am God and not man, the Holy One in the midst of you; and I shall not come in excitement.
11.10: After Jehovah they will walk. Like a lion he will roar; for he himself will roar, and sons will come trembling from the west.
11.11: Like a bird they will come trembling out of Egypt, and like a dove out of the land of As·syr'i·a; and I shall certainly make them dwell in their houses, " is the utterance of Jehovah.
11.12: " With lying, E'phra·im has surrounded me, and with deception the house of Israel. But Judah is yet roaming with God, and with the Most Holy One he is trustworthy. "

12.1: " E'phra·im is feeding on wind and chasing after the east wind all day long. Lying and despoiling are what he multiplies. And a covenant with As·syr'i·a they conclude, and to Egypt oil itself is brought.
12.2: " And Jehovah has a legal case with Judah, even to hold an accounting against Jacob according to his ways; according to his dealings he will repay him.
12.3: In the belly he seized his brother by the heel, and with his dynamic energy he contended with God.
12.4: And he kept contending with an angel and gradually prevailed. He wept, that he might implore favor for himself. " At Beth'el He got to find him, and there He began talking with us.
12.5: And Jehovah the God of the armies, Jehovah is his memorial.
12.6: " And as respects you, to your God you should return, keeping loving - kindness and justice; and let there be a hoping in your God constantly.
12.7: As regards I [ the] tradesman, in his hand are the scales of deception; to defraud is what he has loved.
12.8: And E'phra·im keeps saying, 'Indeed, I have become rich; I have found valuable things for myself. As regards all my toiling, they will find, on my part, no error that is sin. '
12.9: " But I am Jehovah your God from the land of Egypt. Yet I shall make you dwell in the tents as in the days of an appointed time.
12.10: And I spoke to the prophets, and visions I myself multiplied, and by the hand of the prophets I kept making likenesses.
12.11: " With Gil'e·ad what is uncanny, also untruth, have occurred. In Gil'gal they have sacrificed even bulls. Moreover, their altars are like piles of stones in the furrows of the open field.
12.12: And Jacob proceeded to run away to the field of Syria, and Israel kept serving for a wife, and for a wife he guarded I [ sheep].
12.13: And by a prophet Jehovah brought up Israel out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was guarded.
12.14: E'phra·im caused offense to bitterness, and his deeds of bloodshed he leaves upon his own self, and his reproach his grand Master will repay to him. "

13.1: " When E'phra·im spoke, there was trembling; he himself carried I [ weight] in Israel. But he proceeded to become guilty in regard to Ba'al and die.
13.2: And now they commit additional sin and make for themselves a molten statue from their silver, idols according to their own understanding, the work of craftsmen, all of it. To them they are saying, 'Let the sacrificers who are men kiss mere calves. '
13.3: Therefore they will become like the clouds of morning and like the dew that early goes away; like chaff that is stormed away from the threshing floor and like smoke from the I [ roof] hole.
13.4: " But I am Jehovah your God from the land of Egypt, and there was no God except me that you used to know; and there was no savior but I.
13.5: I myself knew you in the wilderness, in the land of fevers.
13.6: According to their pasturage they also came to be satisfied. They became satisfied and their heart began to be exalted. That is why they forgot me.
13.7: And I shall become to them like a young lion. Like a leopard by I [ the] way I shall keep looking.
13.8: I shall encounter them like a bear that has lost its cubs, and I shall rip apart the enclosure of their heart. And I shall devour them there like a lion; a wild beast of the field itself will tear them to pieces.
13.9: It will certainly bring you to ruin, O Israel, because it was against me, against your helper.
13.10: " Where, then, is your king, that he may save you in all your cities, and your judges, I [ concerning] whom you said, 'Do give me a king and princes'?
13.11: I proceeded to give you a king in my anger, and I shall take I [ him] away in my fury.
13.12: " The error of E'phra·im is wrapped up, his sin is treasured up.
13.13: The labor pangs of a woman giving birth are what will come to him. He is a son not wise, for in season he will not stand still at the breaking forth of sons I [ from the womb].
13.14: " From the hand of She'ol I shall redeem them; from death I shall recover them. Where are your stings, O Death? Where is your destructiveness, O She'ol? Compassion itself will be concealed from my eyes.
13.15: " In case he himself as the son of reed plants should show fruitfulness, an east wind, the wind of Jehovah, will come. From a wilderness it is coming up, and it will dry up his well and drain his spring. That one will pillage the treasure of all desirable articles.
13.16: " Sa·mar'i·a will be held guilty, for she is actually rebellious against her God. By the sword they will fall. Their own children will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women themselves will be ripped up. "

14.1: " Do come back, O Israel, to Jehovah your God, for you have stumbled in your error.
14.2: Take with yourselves words and come back to Jehovah. Say to him, all YOU people, 'May you pardon error; and accept what is good, and we will offer in return the young bulls of our lips.
14.3: As·syr'i·a itself will not save us. Upon horses we shall not ride. And no more shall we say: " O our God! " to the work of our hands, because it is by you that a fatherless boy is shown mercy. '
14.4: " I shall heal their unfaithfulness. I shall love them of I [ my] own free will, because my anger has turned back from him.
14.5: I shall become like the dew to Israel. He will blossom like the lily, and will strike his roots like Leb'a·non.
14.6: His twigs will go forth, and his dignity will become like that of the olive tree, and his fragrance will be like that of Leb'a·non.
14.7: They will again be dwellers in his shadow. They will grow grain, and will bud like the vine. His memorial will be like the wine of Leb'a·non.
14.8: " E'phra·im I [ will say], 'What do I have to do any longer with the idols? ' " I myself shall certainly give an answer and I shall keep looking on him. I am like a luxuriant juniper tree. From me must fruit for you be found. "
14.9: Who is wise, that he may understand these things? Discreet, that he may know them? For the ways of Jehovah are upright, and the righteous are the ones who will walk in them; but the transgressors are the ones who will stumble in them.

1.1: The word of Jehovah that occurred to Joel the son of Pe·thu'el:
1.2: " Hear this, YOU older men, and give ear, all YOU inhabitants of the land. Has this occurred in YOUR days, or even in the days of YOUR forefathers?
1.3: Concerning it give an account to YOUR own sons, and YOUR sons to their sons, and their sons to the following generation.
1.4: What was left by the caterpillar, the locust has eaten; and what was left by the locust, the creeping, unwinged locust has eaten; and what the creeping, unwinged locust has left, the cockroach has eaten.
1.5: " Wake up, YOU drunkards, and weep; and howl, all YOU wine drinkers, on account of sweet wine, for it has been cut off from YOUR mouths.
1.6: For there is a nation that has come up into my land, mighty and without number. Its teeth are the teeth of a lion, and it has the jawbones of a lion.
1.7: It has set my vine as an object of astonishment, and my fig tree as a stump. It has positively stripped it bare and thrown I [ it] away. The twigs of it have become white.
1.8: Wail, as a virgin girded with sackcloth does over the owner of her youth.
1.9: " Grain offering and drink offering have been cut off from the house of Jehovah; the priests, the ministers of Jehovah, have mourned.
1.10: I [ The] field has been despoiled, I [ the] ground has gone to mourning; for I [ the] grain has been despoiled, I [ the] new wine has been dried up, I [ the] oil has faded away.
1.11: Farmers have felt shame; vinedressers have howled, on account of wheat and on account of barley; for the harvest of I [ the] field has perished.
1.12: The vine itself has shown dryness, and even the fig tree has faded away. As for I [ the] pomegranate tree, also I [ the] palm tree and I [ the] apple tree, all the trees of the field, they have dried up; for exultation has gone ashamed away from the sons of mankind.
1.13: " Gird yourselves, and beat YOUR breasts, YOU priests. Howl, YOU ministers of I [ the] altar. Come in, spend the night in sackcloth, YOU ministers of my God; for from the house of YOUR God grain offering and drink offering have been withheld.
1.14: Sanctify a time of fasting. Call together a solemn assembly. Gather together I [ the] older men, all the inhabitants of the land, to the house of Jehovah YOUR God, and cry to Jehovah for aid.
1.15: " Alas for the day; because the day of Jehovah is near, and like a despoiling from the Almighty One it will come!
1.16: Has not food itself been cut off before our very eyes; from the house of our God, rejoicing and joyfulness?
1.17: Dried figs have shriveled under their shovels. Storehouses have been laid desolate. Barns have been torn down, for I [ the] grain has dried up.
1.18: O how the domestic animal has sighed! I [ How] the droves of cattle have wandered in confusion! For there is no pasturage for them. Also, the droves of the sheep have been the ones made to bear guilt.
1.19: " To you, O Jehovah, I shall call; for fire itself has devoured the pasture grounds of I [ the] wilderness, and a very flame has consumed all the trees of the field.
1.20: The beasts of the field also keep longing for you, because the channels of water have dried up, and fire itself has devoured the pasture grounds of the wilderness. "

2.1: " Blow a horn in Zion, O men, and shout a war cry in my holy mountain. Let all the inhabitants of the land get agitated; for the day of Jehovah is coming, for it is near!
2.2: It is a day of darkness and gloominess, a day of clouds and thick gloom, like light of dawn spread out upon the mountains. " There is a people numerous and mighty; one like it has not been made to exist from the indefinite past, and after it there will be none again to the years of generation after generation.
2.3: Ahead of it a fire has devoured, and behind it a flame consumes. Like the garden of E'den the land is ahead of it; but behind it is a desolate wilderness, and there has also proved to be nothing thereof escaping.
2.4: " Its appearance is like the appearance of horses, and like steeds is the way they keep running.
2.5: As with the sound of chariots on the tops of the mountains they keep skipping about, as with the sound of a flaming fire that is devouring stubble. It is like a mighty people, drawn up in battle order.
2.6: Because of it, peoples will be in severe pains. As for all faces, they will certainly collect a glow I [ of excitement].
2.7: " Like powerful men they run. Like men of war they go up a wall. And they go each one in his own ways, and they do not alter their paths.
2.8: And one another they do not shove. As an able - bodied man in his course, they keep going; and should some fall even among the missiles, the I [ others] do not break off course.
2.9: " Into the city they rush. On the wall they run. On the houses they go up. Through the windows they go in like the thief.
2.10: Before it I [ the] land has become agitated, I [ the] heavens have rocked. Sun and moon themselves have become dark, and the very stars have withdrawn their brightness.
2.11: And Jehovah himself will certainly give forth his voice before his military force, for his camp is very numerous. For he who is carrying out his word is mighty; for the day of Jehovah is great and very fear - inspiring, and who can hold up under it? "
2.12: " And now also, " the utterance of Jehovah is, " come back to me with all YOUR hearts, and with fasting and with weeping and with wailing.
2.13: And rip apart YOUR hearts, and not YOUR garments; and come back to Jehovah YOUR God, for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abundant in loving - kindness, and he will certainly feel regret on account of the calamity.
2.14: Who is there knowing whether he will turn back and actually feel regret and let remain after it a blessing, a grain offering and a drink offering for Jehovah YOUR God?
2.15: " Blow a horn in Zion, O men. Sanctify a time of fasting. Call together a solemn assembly.
2.16: Gather I [ the] people together. Sanctify a congregation. Collect I [ the] old men together. Gather children and those sucking the breasts together. Let I [ the] bridegroom go forth from his interior room, and I [ the] bride from her nuptial chamber.
2.17: " Between the porch and the altar let the priests, the ministers of Jehovah, weep and say, 'Do feel sorry, O Jehovah, for your people, and do not make your inheritance a reproach, for nations to rule over them. Why should they say among the peoples: " Where is their God? " '
2.18: And Jehovah will be zealous for his land and will show compassion upon his people.
2.19: And Jehovah will answer and say to his people, 'Here I am sending to YOU the grain and the new wine and the oil, and YOU people will certainly be satisfied with it; and I shall not make YOU anymore a reproach among the nations.
2.20: And the northerner I shall put far away from upon YOU, and I shall actually disperse him to a waterless land and desolated waste, with his face to the eastern sea and his rear section to the western sea. And the stink from him will certainly ascend, and the stench from him will keep ascending; for He will actually do a great thing in what He does. '
2.21: " Do not be fearful, O ground. Be joyful and rejoice; for Jehovah will actually do a great thing in what He does.
2.22: Do not be fearful, YOU beasts of the open field, for the pasture grounds of I [ the] wilderness will certainly grow green. For the tree will actually give its fruitage. The fig tree and the vine must give their vital energy.
2.23: And, YOU sons of Zion, be joyful and rejoice in Jehovah YOUR God; for he will be bound to give YOU the autumn rain in right measure, and he will bring down upon YOU people a downpour, autumn rain and spring rain, as at the first.
2.24: And the threshing floors must be full of I [ cleansed] grain, and the press vats must overflow with new wine and oil.
2.25: And I will make compensation to YOU for the years that the locust, the creeping, unwinged locust, and the cockroach and the caterpillar have eaten, my great military force that I have sent among YOU.
2.26: And YOU will certainly eat, eating and becoming satisfied, and YOU will be bound to praise the name of Jehovah YOUR God, who has done with YOU so wonderfully; and my people will not be ashamed to time indefinite.
2.27: And YOU people will have to know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am Jehovah YOUR God and there is no other. And my people will not be ashamed to time indefinite.
2.28: " And after that it must occur that I shall pour out my spirit on every sort of flesh, and YOUR sons and YOUR daughters will certainly prophesy. As for YOUR old men, dreams they will dream. As for YOUR young men, visions they will see.
2.29: And even on the menservants and on the maidservants in those days I shall pour out my spirit.
2.30: " And I will give portents in the heavens and on the earth, blood and fire and columns of smoke.
2.31: The sun itself will be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the coming of the great and fear - inspiring day of Jehovah.
2.32: And it must occur that everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will get away safe; for in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will prove to be the escaped ones, just as Jehovah has said, and in among the survivors, whom Jehovah is calling. "

3.1: " For, look! in those days and in that time, when I shall bring back the captive ones of Judah and Jerusalem,
3.2: I will also collect together all the nations and bring them down to the low plain of Je·hosh'a·phat; and I will put myself on judgment with them there on account of my people and my inheritance Israel, whom they scattered among the nations; and they apportioned out my own land.
3.3: And for my people they kept casting lots; and they would give the male child for a prostitute, and the female child they sold for wine, that they might drink.
3.4: " And, also, what do YOU have to do with me, O Tyre and Si'don and all YOU regions of Phi·lis'ti·a? Is it the treatment that YOU are giving me as a reward? And if YOU are giving such treatment to me, swiftly, speedily I shall pay back YOUR treatment upon YOUR heads.
3.5: Because YOU men have taken my own silver and my own gold, and YOU have brought my own desirable good things into YOUR temples;
3.6: and the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem YOU have sold to the sons of the Greeks, for the purpose of removing them far from their own territory;
3.7: here I am arousing them I [ to come] from the place where YOU have sold them, and I will pay back YOUR treatment upon YOUR own heads.
3.8: And I will sell YOUR sons and YOUR daughters into the hand of the sons of Judah, and they must sell them to the men of She'ba, to a nation far away; for Jehovah himself has spoken I [ it].
3.9: " Proclaim this, YOU people, among the nations, 'Sanctify war! Arouse the powerful men! Let them draw near! Let them come up, all the men of war!
3.10: Beat YOUR plowshares into swords and YOUR pruning shears into lances. As for the weak one, let him say: " I am a powerful man. "
3.11: Lend YOUR aid and come, all YOU nations round about, and collect yourselves together. ' " To that place, O Jehovah, bring your powerful ones down.
3.12: " Let the nations be aroused and come up to the low plain of Je·hosh'a·phat; for there I shall sit in order to judge all the nations round about.
3.13: " THRUST in a sickle, for harvest has grown ripe. Come, descend, for I [ the] winepress has become full. The press vats actually overflow; for their badness has become abundant.
3.14: Crowds, crowds are in the low plain of the decision, for the day of Jehovah is near in the low plain of the decision.
3.15: Sun and moon themselves will certainly become dark, and the very stars will actually withdraw their brightness.
3.16: And out of Zion Jehovah himself will roar, and out of Jerusalem he will give forth his voice. And heaven and earth certainly will rock; but Jehovah will be a refuge for his people, and a fortress for the sons of Israel.
3.17: And YOU people will have to know that I am Jehovah YOUR God, residing in Zion my holy mountain. And Jerusalem must become a holy place; and as regards strangers, they will no more pass through her.
3.18: " And it must occur in that day that the mountains will drip with sweet wine, and the very hills will flow with milk, and the very streambeds of Judah will all flow with water. And out of the house of Jehovah there will go forth a spring, and it must irrigate the torrent valley of the Acacia Trees.
3.19: As regards Egypt, a desolate waste it will become; and as regards E'dom, a wilderness of desolate waste it will become, because of the violence to the sons of Judah, in whose land they shed innocent blood.
3.20: But as for Judah, to time indefinite it will be inhabited, and Jerusalem to generation after generation.
3.21: And I will consider innocent their blood that I had not considered innocent; and Jehovah will be residing in Zion. "

1.1: The words of A'mos, who happened to be among the sheep raisers from Te·ko'a, which he visioned concerning Israel in the days of Uz·zi'ah the king of Judah and in the days of Jer·o·bo'am the son of Jo'ash, the king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
1.2: And he proceeded to say: " Jehovah - out of Zion he will roar, and out of Jerusalem he will give forth his voice; and the pasture grounds of the shepherds must go to mourning, and the summit of Car'mel must dry up. "
1.3: " This is what Jehovah has said, ' " On account of three revolts of Damascus, and on account of four, I shall not turn it back, on account of their threshing Gil'e·ad even with iron threshing instruments.
1.4: And I will send a fire onto the house of Haz'a·el, and it must devour the dwelling towers of Ben - ha'dad.
1.5: And I will break the bar of Damascus and cut off I [ the] inhabitant from Bik'ath - a'ven, and the holder of I [ the] scepter from Beth - e'den; and the people of Syria will have to go as exiles to Kir, " Jehovah has said. '
1.6: " This is what Jehovah has said, ' " On account of three revolts of Ga'za, and on account of four, I shall not turn it back, on account of their taking into exile a complete body of exiles to hand over to E'dom.
1.7: And I will send a fire onto the wall of Ga'za, and it must devour her dwelling towers.
1.8: And I will cut off I [ the] inhabitant from Ash'dod, and the holder of I [ the] scepter from Ash'ke·lon; and I will turn my hand back upon Ek'ron, and the remaining ones of the Phi·lis'tines must perish, " the Sovereign Lord Jehovah has said. '
1.9: " This is what Jehovah has said, 'On account of three revolts of Tyre, and on account of four, I shall not turn it back, on account of their handing over a complete body of exiles to E'dom, and I [ because] they did not remember the covenant of brothers.
1.10: And I will send a fire onto the wall of Tyre, and it must devour her dwelling towers. '
1.11: " This is what Jehovah has said, 'On account of three revolts of E'dom, and on account of four, I shall not turn it back, on account of his pursuing his own brother with the sword, and I [ because] he ruined his I [ own] merciful qualities, and his anger keeps tearing away forever; and his fury - he has kept it perpetually.
1.12: And I will send a fire into Te'man, and it must devour the dwelling towers of Boz'rah. '
1.13: " This is what Jehovah has said, ' " On account of three revolts of the sons of Am'mon, and on account of four, I shall not turn it back, on account of their slitting open the pregnant women of Gil'e·ad, for the purpose of widening out their own territory.
1.14: And I will set fire to the wall of Rab'bah, and it must devour her dwelling towers, with an alarm signal in the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of storm wind.
1.15: And their king must go into exile, he and his princes together, " Jehovah has said. '

2.1: " This is what Jehovah has said, ' " On account of three revolts of Mo'ab, and on account of four, I shall not turn it back, on account of his burning the bones of the king of E'dom for lime.
2.2: And I will send a fire into Mo'ab, and it must devour the dwelling towers of Ke'ri·oth; and with noise Mo'ab must die, with an alarm signal, with the sound of a horn.
2.3: And I will cut off I [ the] judge from the midst of her, and all her princes I shall kill with him, " Jehovah has said. '
2.4: " This is what Jehovah has said, 'On account of three revolts of Judah, and on account of four, I shall not turn it back, on account of their rejecting the law of Jehovah, and I [ because] they did not keep his own regulations; but their lies, after which their forefathers had walked, kept making them wander.
2.5: And I will send a fire into Judah, and it must devour the dwelling towers of Jerusalem. '
2.6: " This is what Jehovah has said, 'On account of three revolts of Israel, and on account of four, I shall not turn it back, on account of their selling someone righteous for mere silver, and someone poor for I [ the price of] a pair of sandals.
2.7: They are panting for the dust of I [ the] earth on the head of lowly persons; and the way of meek people they turn aside; and a man and his own father have gone to the I [ same] girl, for the purpose of profaning my holy name.
2.8: And on garments seized as a pledge they stretch themselves out beside every altar; and the wine of those who have been fined they drink at the house of their gods. '
2.9: " 'But as for me, I had annihilated the Am'or·ite on account of them, whose height was like the height of cedars, and who was vigorous like the massive trees; and I went annihilating his fruitage above and his roots below.
2.10: And I myself brought YOU people up out of the land of Egypt, and I kept making YOU walk through the wilderness forty years, in order to take possession of the land of the Am'or·ite.
2.11: And I kept raising up some of YOUR sons as prophets and some of YOUR young men as Naz'i·rites. Should this really not be, O sons of Israel? ' is the utterance of Jehovah.
2.12: " 'But YOU kept giving the Naz'i·rites wine to drink, and upon the prophets YOU laid a command, saying: " YOU must not prophesy. "
2.13: Here I am making what is under YOU sway, just as the wagon sways that is full up with a row of newly cut grain.
2.14: And a place to which to flee must perish from the swift one, and no one strong will reinforce his power, and no mighty man will provide his soul with escape.
2.15: And no one handling the bow will stand, and no one swift on his feet will escape, and no rider of the horse will provide his soul with escape.
2.16: And as for one strong in his heart among the mighty men, naked is how he will flee in that day, ' is the utterance of Jehovah. "

3.1: " Hear this word that Jehovah has spoken concerning YOU, O sons of Israel, concerning the whole family that I brought up out of the land of Egypt, saying,
3.2: 'YOU people only have I known out of all the families of the ground. That is why I shall hold an accounting against YOU for all YOUR errors.
3.3: " 'Will two walk together unless they have met by appointment?
3.4: Will a lion roar in the forest when it has no prey? Will a young maned lion give forth its voice from its hiding place if it has caught nothing at all?
3.5: Will a bird fall into a trap on the earth when there is no snare for it? Does a trap go up from the ground when it has absolutely caught nothing?
3.6: If a horn is blown in a city, do not also the people themselves tremble? If a calamity occurs in the city, is it not also Jehovah who has acted?
3.7: For the Sovereign Lord Jehovah will not do a thing unless he has revealed his confidential matter to his servants the prophets.
3.8: There is a lion that has roared! Who will not be afraid? The Sovereign Lord Jehovah himself has spoken! Who will not prophesy? '
3.9: " 'PUBLISH it on I [ the] dwelling towers in Ash'dod and on I [ the] dwelling towers in the land of Egypt, and say: " Be gathered together against the mountains of Sa·mar'i·a, and see the many disorders in the midst of her and cases of defrauding inside her.
3.10: And they have not known how to do what is straightforward, " is the utterance of Jehovah, " those who are storing up violence and despoiling in their dwelling towers. " '
3.11: " Therefore this is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah has said, 'There is an adversary even round about the land, and he will certainly bring your strength down from you, and your dwelling towers will actually be plundered. '
3.12: " This is what Jehovah has said, 'Just as the shepherd snatches away from the mouth of the lion two shanks or a piece of an ear, so the sons of Israel will be snatched away, those sitting in Sa·mar'i·a on a splendid couch and on a Dam·a·scene' divan. '
3.13: " 'HEAR and give witness in the house of Jacob, ' is the utterance of the Sovereign Lord Jehovah, the God of the armies.
3.14: 'For, in the day of my holding an accounting for the revolts of Israel against him, I will also hold an accounting against the altars of Beth'el; and the horns of the altar will certainly be cut off and must fall to the earth.
3.15: And I will strike down the winter house in addition to the summer house. ' " 'And the houses of ivory will have to perish, and many houses will have to come to their finish, ' is the utterance of Jehovah. "

4.1: " Hear this word, YOU cows of Ba'shan, who are on the mountain of Sa·mar'i·a, who are defrauding the lowly ones, who are crushing the poor ones, who are saying to their masters, 'Do bring, and let us drink! '
4.2: The Sovereign Lord Jehovah has sworn by his holiness, ' " Look! There are days coming upon YOU, and he will certainly lift YOU up with butcher hooks and the last part of YOU with fishhooks.
4.3: And I [ by] breaches YOU will go forth, each one straight ahead; and YOU will certainly be thrown out to Har'mon, " is the utterance of Jehovah. '
4.4: " 'Come, YOU people, to Beth'el and commit transgression. At Gil'gal be frequent in committing transgression, and bring YOUR sacrifices in the morning; on the third day, YOUR tenth parts.
4.5: And from what is leavened make a thanksgiving sacrifice to smoke, and proclaim voluntary offerings; publish I [ it], for that is the way YOU have loved, O sons of Israel, ' is the utterance of the Sovereign Lord Jehovah.
4.6: " 'And I also, for my part, gave YOU people cleanness of teeth in all YOUR cities and want of bread in all YOUR places; but YOU did not come back to me, ' is the utterance of Jehovah.
4.7: " 'And as for me, I also withheld from YOU people the downpour when there were yet three months to the harvest; and I made it rain on one city, but on another city I would not make it rain. There was one tract of land that would be rained on, but a tract of land on which I would not make it rain would be dried up.
4.8: And two or three cities staggered to one city in order to drink water, and they would not get satisfied; but YOU did not come back to me, ' is the utterance of Jehovah.
4.9: " 'I struck YOU people with scorching and mildew. There was a multiplying of YOUR gardens and of YOUR vineyards, but YOUR fig trees and YOUR olive trees the caterpillar would devour; yet YOU did not come back to me, ' is the utterance of Jehovah.
4.10: " 'I sent among YOU people a pestilence in the nature of that of Egypt. With the sword I killed YOUR young men, along with the taking captive of YOUR horses. And I kept making the stink of YOUR camps ascend even into YOUR nostrils; but YOU did not come back to me, ' is the utterance of Jehovah.
4.11: " 'I caused an overthrow among YOU people, like God's overthrow of Sod'om and Go·mor'rah. And YOU came to be like a log snatched out of I [ the] burning; but YOU did not come back to me, ' is the utterance of Jehovah.
4.12: " Therefore that is what I shall do to you, O Israel. As a consequence of the fact that I shall do this very thing to you, get ready to meet your God, O Israel.
4.13: For, look! the Former of I [ the] mountains and the Creator of I [ the] wind, and the One telling to earthling man what his mental concern is, the One making dawn into obscurity, and the One treading on earth's high places, Jehovah the God of armies is his name. "

5.1: " Hear this word that I am taking up over YOU people as a dirge, O house of Israel:
5.2: " The virgin, Israel, has fallen; She cannot get up again. She has been forsaken upon her own ground; There is no one raising her up.
5.3: " For this is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah has said, 'The very city that was going forth with a thousand will have a hundred left; and the one going forth with a hundred will have ten left, for the house of Israel. '
5.4: " For this is what Jehovah has said to the house of Israel, 'Search for me, and keep living.
5.5: And do not search for Beth'el, and to Gil'gal YOU must not come, and to Be'er - she'ba YOU must not pass over; because Gil'gal itself will without fail go into exile; and as regards Beth'el, it will become something uncanny.
5.6: Search for Jehovah, and keep living, that he may not become operative just like fire, O house of Joseph, and it may not actually devour, and Beth'el may not be with no one to extinguish I [ it],
5.7: O YOU who are turning justice into mere wormwood, and the ones who have cast righteousness itself to the earth.
5.8: The Maker of the Ki'mah constellation and the Ke'sil constellation, and the One turning deep shadow into the morning itself, and the One who has made day itself dark as night, the One calling for the waters of the sea, that he may pour them out upon the surface of the earth - Jehovah is his name;
5.9: he who is causing a despoiling to flash forth upon someone strong, that despoiling itself may come upon even a fortified place.
5.10: " 'In the gate they have hated a reprover, and a speaker of perfect things they detest.
5.11: Therefore, for the reason that YOU are extracting farm rent from someone lowly, and the tribute of grain YOU keep taking from him; houses of hewn stone YOU have built, but YOU will not keep dwelling in them; and desirable vineyards YOU have planted, but YOU will not keep drinking the wine of them.
5.12: For I have known how many YOUR revolts are and how mighty YOUR sins are, O YOU who are showing hostility toward someone righteous, YOU who are taking hush money, and the ones who have turned aside poor people even in the gate.
5.13: Therefore the very one having insight will in that time keep silent, for it will be a calamitous time.
5.14: " 'Search for what is good, and not what is bad, to the end that YOU people may keep living; and that thus Jehovah the God of armies may come to be with YOU, just as YOU have said.
5.15: Hate what is bad, and love what is good, and give justice a place in the gate. It may be that Jehovah the God of armies will show favor to the remaining ones of Joseph. '
5.16: " Therefore this is what Jehovah the God of armies, Jehovah, has said, 'In all the public squares there will be wailing, and in all the streets people will be saying: " Ah! Ah! " And they will have to call a farmer to mourning, and to wailing those experienced in lamentation. '
5.17: 'And in all vineyards there will be wailing; for I shall pass through the midst of you, ' Jehovah has said.
5.18: " 'Woe to those who are craving the day of Jehovah! What, then, will the day of Jehovah mean to YOU people? It will be darkness, and no light,
5.19: just as when a man flees because of the lion, and the bear actually meets him; and I [ as when] he went into the house and supported his hand against the wall, and the serpent bit him.
5.20: Will not the day of Jehovah be darkness, and not light; and will it not have gloom, and not brightness?
5.21: I have hated, I have rejected YOUR festivals, and I shall not enjoy the smell of YOUR solemn assemblies.
5.22: But if YOU people offer up to me whole burnt offerings, even in YOUR gift offerings I shall find no pleasure, and on YOUR communion sacrifices of fatlings I shall not look.
5.23: Remove from me the turmoil of your songs; and the melodious sound of your stringed instruments may I not hear.
5.24: And let justice roll forth just like waters, and righteousness like a constantly flowing torrent.
5.25: Was it sacrifices and gift offerings that YOU people brought near to me in the wilderness for forty years, O house of Israel?
5.26: And YOU will certainly carry Sak'kuth YOUR king and Kai'wan, YOUR images, the star of YOUR god, whom YOU made for yourselves.
5.27: And I will cause YOU to go into exile beyond Damascus, ' he whose name is Jehovah the God of armies has said. "

6.1: " Woe to those who are at ease in Zion and to those trusting in the mountain of Sa·mar'i·a! They are the distinguished ones of the chief part of the nations, and to them the house of Israel have come.
6.2: Make YOUR way over to Cal'neh, and see; and go from there to populous Ha'math, and go down to Gath of the Phi·lis'tines. Are they better than these kingdoms, or is their territory bigger than YOUR territory?
6.3: I [ Are YOU] putting out of I [ YOUR] mind the calamitous day, and do YOU bring near the dwelling of violence?
6.4: I [ YOU men] that are lying down on couches of ivory and are sprawling on their divans, and are eating the rams out of a flock and the young bulls from among fattened calves;
6.5: that are improvising according to the sound of the stringed instrument; that, like David, have devised for themselves instruments for song;
6.6: that are drinking out of bowls of wine, and that with the choicest oils do their anointing, and that have not been made sick at the catastrophe of Joseph.
6.7: " Therefore now they will go into exile at the head of those going into exile, and the revelry of sprawling ones must depart.
6.8: " 'The Sovereign Lord Jehovah has sworn by his own soul, ' is the utterance of Jehovah the God of armies, ' " I am detesting the pride of Jacob, and his dwelling towers I have hated, and I will deliver up I [ the] city and what fills it.
6.9: And it must occur that if ten men should be left remaining in one house, they must also die.
6.10: And his father's brother will have to carry them forth one by one, and will be burning them one by one, in order to bring out I [ the] bones from the house. And he will have to say to whoever is in the innermost parts of the house, 'Are there any more with you? ' And he will certainly say, 'Nobody! ' And he will have to say, 'Keep silence! For it is not the occasion for making any mention of the name of Jehovah. ' "
6.11: " 'For here is Jehovah commanding, and he will certainly strike down the great house into rubble and the small house into debris.
6.12: " 'On a crag will horses run, or will one plow I [ there] with cattle? For into a poisonous plant YOU people have turned justice, and the fruitage of righteousness into wormwood,
6.13: I [ YOU who] are rejoicing in a thing that is not; who are saying: " Have we not in our strength taken horns to ourselves? "
6.14: Look! I am raising up against YOU, O house of Israel, ' is the utterance of Jehovah the God of the armies, 'a nation, and they must oppress YOU people from the entering in of Ha'math down to the torrent valley of the Ar'a·bah. ' "

7.1: This is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah caused me to see, and, look! he was forming a I [ locust] swarm at the start of the coming up of the later sowing. And, look! it was the later sowing after the mown grass of the king.
7.2: And it occurred that when it had finished eating up the vegetation of the land, I proceeded to say: " O Sovereign Lord Jehovah, forgive, please. Who will rise up of Jacob? For he is small! "
7.3: Jehovah felt regret over this. " It shall not occur, " Jehovah said.
7.4: This is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah caused me to see, and, look! the Sovereign Lord Jehovah was calling for a contention by means of fire; and it went eating up the vast watery deep and ate up the tract of land.
7.5: And I proceeded to say: " O Sovereign Lord Jehovah, hold off, please. Who will rise up of Jacob? For he is small! "
7.6: Jehovah felt regret over this. " That, too, will not occur, " the Sovereign Lord Jehovah said.
7.7: This is what he caused me to see, and, look! Jehovah was stationed on a wall I [ made with] a plummet, and there was a plummet in his hand.
7.8: Then Jehovah said to me: " What are you seeing, A'mos? " So I said: " A plummet. " And Jehovah went on to say: " Here I am setting a plummet in the midst of my people Israel. I shall no more do any further excusing of it.
7.9: And the high places of Isaac will certainly be laid desolate, and the sanctuaries themselves of Israel will be devastated; and I will rise up against the house of Jer·o·bo'am with a sword. "
7.10: And Am·a·zi'ah the priest of Beth'el proceeded to send to Jer·o·bo'am the king of Israel, saying: " A'mos has conspired against you right inside the house of Israel. The land is not able to put up with all his words.
7.11: For this is what A'mos has said, 'By the sword Jer·o·bo'am will die; and as regards Israel, it will without fail go into exile from its own ground. ' "
7.12: And Am·a·zi'ah proceeded to say to A'mos: " O visionary, go, run your way off to the land of Judah, and there eat bread, and there you may prophesy.
7.13: But at Beth'el you must no longer do any further prophesying, for it is the sanctuary of a king and it is the house of a kingdom. "
7.14: Then A'mos answered and said to Am·a·zi'ah: " I was not a prophet, neither was I the son of a prophet; but I was a herdsman and a nipper of figs of sycamore trees.
7.15: And Jehovah proceeded to take me from following the flock, and Jehovah went on to say to me, 'Go, prophesy to my people Israel. '
7.16: And now hear the word of Jehovah, 'Are you saying: " You must not prophesy against Israel, and you must let no I [ word] drop against the house of Isaac "?
7.17: Therefore this is what Jehovah has said: " As regards your wife, in the city she will become a prostitute. And as regards your sons and your daughters, by the sword they will fall. And as regards your ground, by the measuring rope it will be apportioned out. And as regards you yourself, on unclean ground you will die; and as regards Israel, it will without fail go into exile from its own ground. " ' "

8.1: This is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah caused me to see, and, look! there was a basket of summer fruit.
8.2: Then he said: " What are you seeing, A'mos? " So I said: " A basket of summer fruit. " And Jehovah went on to say to me: " The end has come to my people Israel. I shall no more do any further excusing of them.
8.3: 'And the songs of I [ the] temple will actually be a howling in that day, ' is the utterance of the Sovereign Lord Jehovah. 'There will be many a carcass. In every place one will certainly throw I [ them] out - hush! '
8.4: " Hear this, YOU men snapping at someone poor, even in order to cause the meek ones of the earth to cease,
8.5: saying, 'How long will it be before the new moon passes and we may sell cereals? Also, the sabbath, and we may offer grain for sale; in order to make the e'phah small and to make the shekel great and to falsify the scales of deception;
8.6: in order to buy lowly people for mere silver and someone poor for I [ the price of] a pair of sandals, and that we may sell mere refuse of grain? '
8.7: " Jehovah has sworn by the Superiority of Jacob, 'Never will I forget all their works.
8.8: Will it not be on this account that the land will be agitated, and every inhabitant in it will have to mourn; and it will, all of it, certainly come up just like the Nile and be tossed and sink down like the Nile of Egypt? '
8.9: " 'And it must occur in that day, ' is the utterance of the Sovereign Lord Jehovah, 'that I will make the sun go down at high noon, and I will cause darkness for the land on a bright day.
8.10: And I will turn YOUR festivals into mourning and all YOUR songs into a dirge, and I will bring up upon all hips sackcloth and upon every head baldness; and I will make the situation like the mourning for an only I [ son], and the end result of it as a bitter day. '
8.11: " 'Look! There are days coming, ' is the utterance of the Sovereign Lord Jehovah, 'and I will send a famine into the land, a famine, not for bread, and a thirst, not for water, but for hearing the words of Jehovah.
8.12: And they will certainly stagger from sea all the way to sea, and from north even to the sunrise. They will keep roving about while searching for the word of Jehovah, but they will not find I [ it].
8.13: In that day the pretty virgins will swoon away, also the young men, because of the thirst;
8.14: those who are swearing by the guiltiness of Sa·mar'i·a, and who actually say: " As your god is alive, O Dan! " and, " As the way of Be'er - she'ba is alive! " And they will certainly fall, and they will rise up no more. ' "

9.1: I saw Jehovah stationed above the altar, and he proceeded to say: " Strike the pillar head, so that the thresholds will rock. And cut them off at the head, all of them. And the last part of them I shall kill with the sword itself. No one fleeing of them will make good his flight, and no one escaping of them will make his getaway.
9.2: If they dig down into She'ol, from there my own hand will take them; and if they go up to the heavens, from there I shall bring them down.
9.3: And if they hide themselves on the top of Car'mel, from there I shall carefully search and be certain to take them. And if they conceal themselves from in front of my eyes on the floor of the sea, down there I shall command the serpent, and it must bite them.
9.4: And if they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I shall command the sword, and it must kill them; and I will set my eyes upon them for bad, and not for good.
9.5: And the Sovereign Lord, Jehovah of the armies, is the One touching the land, so that it melts; and all the inhabitants in it will have to mourn; and it will certainly come up like the Nile, all of it, and sink down like the Nile of Egypt.
9.6: " 'He who is building in the heavens his stairs, and his structure over the earth that he founded; he who is calling for the waters of the sea, that he may pour them out upon the surface of the earth - Jehovah is his name. '
9.7: " 'Are YOU not like the sons of the Cush'ites to me, O sons of Israel? ' is the utterance of Jehovah. 'Did I not bring Israel itself up out of the land of Egypt, and the Phi·lis'tines out of Crete, and Syria out of Kir? '
9.8: " 'Look! The eyes of the Sovereign Lord Jehovah are upon the sinful kingdom, and he will certainly annihilate it from upon the surface of the ground. Nevertheless, I shall not completely annihilate the house of Jacob, ' is the utterance of Jehovah.
9.9: 'For, look! I am commanding, and I will jiggle the house of Israel among all the nations, just as one jiggles the sieve, so that not a pebble falls to the earth.
9.10: By the sword they will die - all the sinners of my people, those who are saying: " The calamity will not come near or reach as far as us. " '
9.11: " 'In that day I shall raise up the booth of David that is fallen, and I shall certainly repair their breaches. And its ruins I shall raise up, and I shall certainly build it up as in the days of long ago,
9.12: to the end that they may take possession of what is left remaining of E'dom, and all the nations upon whom my name has been called, ' is the utterance of Jehovah, who is doing this.
9.13: " 'Look! There are days coming, ' is the utterance of Jehovah, 'and the plowman will actually overtake the harvester, and the treader of grapes, the carrier of the seed; and the mountains must drip with sweet wine, and the very hills will all find themselves melting.
9.14: And I will gather back the captive ones of my people Israel, and they will actually build I [ the] desolated cities and inhabit I [ them], and plant vineyards and drink the wine of them, and make gardens and eat the fruit of them. '
9.15: " 'And I shall certainly plant them upon their ground, and they will no more be uprooted from their ground that I have given them, ' Jehovah your God has said. "

1.1: The vision of O·ba·di'ah: This is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah has said regarding E'dom: " There is a report that we have heard from Jehovah, and there is an envoy that has been sent among the nations, 'Rise up, YOU people, and let us rise up against her in battle. ' "
1.2: " Look! Small is what I have made you among the nations. You are despised very much.
1.3: The presumptuousness of your heart is what has deceived you, you who are residing in the retreats of the crag, the height where he dwells, saying in his heart, 'Who will bring me down to I [ the] earth? '
1.4: If you should make your position high like the eagle, or if among the stars there were a placing of your nest, down from there I would bring you, " is the utterance of Jehovah.
1.5: " If it were thieves that came in to you, if despoilers I [ came in] by night, to what extent would you have been silenced? Would they not steal as much as they wanted? Or if it were grape gatherers that came in to you, would they not let some gleanings remain?
1.6: O the extent to which those of E'sau have been searched out! I [ How] his concealed treasures have been sought out!
1.7: As far as the boundary they have sent you. The very men in covenant with you have all deceived you. The men at peace with you have prevailed against you. Those I [ eating] food with you will place a net under you as one in whom there is no discernment.
1.8: Will it not be in that day? " is the utterance of Jehovah. " And I shall certainly destroy the wise ones out of E'dom, and discernment out of the mountainous region of E'sau.
1.9: And your mighty men must become terrified, O Te'man, for the reason that each one will be cut off from the mountainous region of E'sau, because of a killing.
1.10: Because of the violence to your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will have to be cut off to time indefinite.
1.11: In the day when you stood off on the side, in the day when strangers took his military force into captivity and I [ when] outright foreigners entered his gate and over Jerusalem they cast lots, you also were like one of them.
1.12: " And you ought not to watch the sight in the day of your brother, in the day of his misfortune; and you ought not to rejoice at the sons of Judah in the day of their perishing; and you ought not to maintain a big mouth in the day of I [ their] distress.
1.13: You ought not to come into the gate of my people in the day of their disaster. You, even you, ought not to peer at his calamity in the day of his disaster; and you ought not to thrust out a hand upon his wealth in the day of his disaster.
1.14: And you ought not to stand at the parting of the ways, in order to cut off his escapees; and you ought not to hand over his survivors in the day of distress.
1.15: For the day of Jehovah against all the nations is near. In the way that you have done, it will be done to you. Your sort of treatment will return upon your own head.
1.16: For in the way that YOU people have drunk upon my holy mountain, all the nations will keep drinking constantly. And they will certainly drink and gulp down and become as though they had never happened to be.
1.17: " And in Mount Zion is where those escaping will prove to be, and it must become something holy; and the house of Jacob must take possession of the things for them to possess.
1.18: And the house of Jacob must become a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of E'sau as stubble; and they must set them ablaze and devour them. And there will prove to be no survivor to the house of E'sau; for Jehovah himself has spoken I [ it].
1.19: And they must take possession of the Neg'eb, even of the mountainous region of E'sau, and of the She·phe'lah, even of the Phi·lis'tines. And they must take possession of the field of E'phra·im and of the field of Sa·mar'i·a; and Benjamin I [ must take possession of] Gil'e·ad.
1.20: And as for the exiles of this rampart, to the sons of Israel will belong what the Ca'naan·ites I [ possessed] as far as Zar'e·phath. And the exiles of Jerusalem, who were in Se·phar'ad, will take possession of the cities of the Neg'eb.
1.21: " And saviors will certainly come up onto Mount Zion, in order to judge the mountainous region of E'sau; and the kingship must become Jehovah's. "

1.1: And the word of Jehovah began to occur to Jo'nah the son of A·mit'tai, saying:
1.2: " Get up, go to Nin'e·veh the great city, and proclaim against her that their badness has come up before me. "
1.3: And Jo'nah proceeded to get up and run away to Tar'shish from before Jehovah; and he finally came down to Jop'pa and found a ship going to Tar'shish. So he paid its fare and went down into it, in order to go with them to Tar'shish from before Jehovah.
1.4: And Jehovah himself hurled forth a great wind at the sea, and there came to be a great tempest on the sea; and as for the ship, it was about to be wrecked.
1.5: And the mariners began to fear and to call for aid, each one to his god. And they kept hurling out the articles that were in the ship to the sea, in order to lighten I [ it] of them. But Jo'nah himself had gone down to the innermost parts of the decked vessel, and he proceeded to lie down and go fast asleep.
1.6: At length the ship captain came near to him and said to him: " What is the matter with you, sleeper? Get up, call out to your god! Perhaps the I [ true] God will show himself caring about us, and we shall not perish. "
1.7: And they began to say to one another: " Come, and let us cast lots, that we may know on whose account we have this calamity. " And they kept casting lots, and finally the lot fell upon Jo'nah.
1.8: So they said to him: " Do tell us, please, on whose account it is that we are having this calamity? What is your work, and from where do you come? What is your country, and from which people are you? "
1.9: At that he said to them: " I am a Hebrew, and Jehovah the God of the heavens I am fearing, the One who made the sea and the dry land. "
1.10: And the men began to fear greatly, and they went on to say to him: " What is this that you have done? " For the men had come to know that it was from before Jehovah that he was running away, because he had told them.
1.11: Finally they said to him: " What should we do to you, in order that the sea may become still for us? " For the sea was continually growing more tempestuous.
1.12: So he said to them: " Lift me up and hurl me into the sea, and the sea will become still for YOU; because I am aware that it is on my account that this great tempest is upon YOU. "
1.13: But the men tried to work their way through, in order to bring I [ the ship] back to the dry land; yet they were unable, because the sea was continually growing more tempestuous against them.
1.14: And they proceeded to call out to Jehovah and to say: " Ah, now, O Jehovah, may we, please, not perish because of the soul of this man! And do not put upon us innocent blood, since you yourself, O Jehovah, have done according to what you have delighted in! "
1.15: Then they lifted up Jo'nah and hurled him into the sea; and the sea began to halt from its raging.
1.16: At that the men began to fear Jehovah greatly, and so they offered a sacrifice to Jehovah and made vows.
1.17: Now Jehovah appointed a great fish to swallow Jo'nah, so that Jo'nah came to be in the inward parts of the fish three days and three nights.

2.1: Then Jo'nah prayed to Jehovah his God from the inward parts of the fish
2.2: and said: " Out of my distress I called out to Jehovah, and he proceeded to answer me. Out of the belly of She'ol I cried for help. You heard my voice.
2.3: When you threw me I [ to] the depths, into the heart of the open sea, Then a very river encircled me. All your breakers and your waves - over me they passed on.
2.4: And as for me, I said, 'I have been driven away from in front of your eyes! How shall I gaze again upon your holy temple? '
2.5: Waters encircled me clear to I [ the] soul; the watery deep itself kept enclosing me. Weeds were wound around my head.
2.6: To the bottoms of I [ the] mountains I went down. As for the earth, its bars were upon me for time indefinite. But out of I [ the] pit you proceeded to bring up my life, O Jehovah my God.
2.7: When my soul fainted away within me, Jehovah was the One whom I remembered. Then my prayer came in to you, into your holy temple.
2.8: As for those who are observing the idols of untruth, they leave their own loving - kindness.
2.9: But as for me, with the voice of thanksgiving I will sacrifice to you. What I have vowed, I will pay. Salvation belongs to Jehovah. "
2.10: In time Jehovah commanded the fish, so that it vomited out Jo'nah onto the dry land.

3.1: Then the word of Jehovah occurred to Jo'nah the second time, saying:
3.2: " Get up, go to Nin'e·veh the great city, and proclaim to her the proclamation that I am speaking to you. "
3.3: At that, Jo'nah got up and went to Nin'e·veh in accord with the word of Jehovah. Now Nin'e·veh herself proved to be a city great to God, with a walking distance of three days.
3.4: Finally Jo'nah started to enter into the city the walking distance of one day, and he kept proclaiming and saying: " Only forty days more, and Nin'e·veh will be overthrown. "
3.5: And the men of Nin'e·veh began to put faith in God, and they proceeded to proclaim a fast and to put on sackcloth, from the greatest one of them even to the least one of them.
3.6: When the word reached the king of Nin'e·veh, then he rose up from his throne and put off his official garment from himself and covered himself with sackcloth and sat down in the ashes.
3.7: Furthermore, he had the cry made, and he had it said in Nin'e·veh, by the decree of the king and his great ones, saying: " No man and no domestic animal, no herd and no flock, should taste anything at all. None should take food. Even water they should not drink.
3.8: And let them cover themselves with sackcloth, man and domestic animal; and let them call out to God with strength and come back, each one from his bad way and from the violence that was in their hands.
3.9: Who is there knowing whether the I [ true] God may turn back and actually feel regret and turn back from his burning anger, so that we may not perish? "
3.10: And the I [ true] God got to see their works, that they had turned back from their bad way; and so the I [ true] God felt regret over the calamity that he had spoken of causing to them; and he did not cause I [ it].

4.1: To Jo'nah, though, it was highly displeasing, and he got to be hot with anger.
4.2: Hence he prayed to Jehovah and said: " Ah, now, O Jehovah, was not this an affair of mine, while I happened to be on my own ground? That is why I went ahead and ran away to Tar'shish; for I knew that you are a God gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abundant in loving - kindness, and feeling regret over the calamity.
4.3: And now, O Jehovah, take away, please, my soul from me, for my dying is better than my being alive. "
4.4: In turn Jehovah said: " Have you rightly become hot with anger? "
4.5: Then Jo'nah went out of the city and sat down east of the city; and gradually he made for himself there a booth, that he might sit under it in the shade until he would see what would become of the city.
4.6: Accordingly Jehovah God appointed a bottle - gourd plant, that it should come up over Jo'nah, in order to become a shade over his head, to deliver him from his calamitous state. And Jo'nah began to rejoice greatly over the bottle - gourd plant.
4.7: But the I [ true] God appointed a worm at the ascending of the dawn on the next day, that it should strike the bottle - gourd plant; and it gradually dried up.
4.8: And it came about that, as soon as the sun shone forth, God also went on to appoint a parching east wind, and the sun kept striking upon the head of Jo'nah, so that he was swooning away; and he kept asking that his soul might die, and he repeatedly said: " My dying off is better than my being alive. "
4.9: And God proceeded to say to Jo'nah: " Have you rightly become hot with anger over the bottle - gourd plant? " At that he said: " I have rightly become hot with anger, to the point of death. "
4.10: But Jehovah said: " You, for your part, felt sorry for the bottle - gourd plant, which you did not toil upon or make get big, which proved to be a mere growth of a night and perished as a mere growth of a night.
4.11: And, for my part, ought I not to feel sorry for Nin'e·veh the great city, in which there exist more than one hundred and twenty thousand men who do not at all know the difference between their right hand and their left, besides many domestic animals? "

1.1: The word of Jehovah that occurred to Mi'cah of Mo'resh·eth, in the days of Jo'tham, A'haz, Hez·e·ki'ah, kings of Judah, that he visioned concerning Sa·mar'i·a and Jerusalem:
1.2: " Hear, O YOU peoples, all of YOU; pay attention, O earth and what fills you, and let the Sovereign Lord Jehovah serve against YOU as a witness, Jehovah from his holy temple.
1.3: For, look! Jehovah is going forth from his place, and he will certainly come down and tread upon earth's high places.
1.4: And the mountains must melt under him, and the low plains themselves will split apart, like wax because of the fire, like waters being poured down a steep place.
1.5: " It is because of the revolt of Jacob that there is all this, even because of the sins of the house of Israel. What is the revolt of Jacob? Is it not Sa·mar'i·a? And what are the high places of Judah? Are they not Jerusalem?
1.6: And I shall certainly make Sa·mar'i·a a heap of ruins of the field, the planting places of a vineyard; and I will pour down into the valley her stones, and her foundations I shall lay bare.
1.7: And her graven images will all be crushed to pieces, and all the gifts I [ made] to her as her hire will be burned in the fire; and all her idols I shall make a desolate waste. For from the things given as the hire of a prostitute she collected I [ them], and to the thing given as the hire of a prostitute they will return. "
1.8: On this account I will wail and howl; I will walk barefoot and naked. I shall make a wailing like the jackals, and a mourning like female ostriches.
1.9: For the stroke upon her is unhealable; for it has come as far as Judah, I [ the] plague as far as the gate of my people, as far as Jerusalem.
1.10: " In Gath do not YOU men tell I [ it] out; positively do not weep. " In the house of Aph'rah wallow in the very dust.
1.11: Make your way across, O inhabitress of Sha'phir, in shameful nudity. The inhabitress of Za'a·nan has not gone forth. The wailing of Beth - e'zel will take from YOU people its standing place.
1.12: For the inhabitress of Ma'roth has waited for good, but what is bad has come down from Jehovah to the gate of Jerusalem.
1.13: Attach the chariot to the team of horses, O inhabitress of La'chish. The beginning of sin was what she was to the daughter of Zion, for in you the revolts of Israel have been found.
1.14: Therefore you will give parting gifts to Mo'resh·eth - gath. The houses of Ach'zib were as something deceitful to the kings of Israel.
1.15: The dispossessor I shall yet bring to you, O inhabitress of Ma·re'shah. As far as A·dul'lam the glory of Israel will come.
1.16: Cause baldness, and shear I [ your hair] off on account of your sons of exquisite delight. Broaden out your baldness like I [ that of] the eagle, because they have gone away from you into exile. "

2.1: " Woe to those who are scheming what is harmful, and to those practicing what is bad, upon their beds! By the light of the morning they proceed to do it, because it is in the power of their hand.
2.2: And they have desired fields and have seized I [ them]; also houses, and have taken I [ them]; and they have defrauded an able - bodied man and his household, a man and his hereditary possession.
2.3: " Therefore this is what Jehovah has said, 'Here I am thinking up against this family a calamity from which YOU people will not remove YOUR necks, so that YOU will not walk haughtily; because it is a time of calamity.

2.16: You will certainly be satiated with dishonor instead of glory. Drink also, you yourself, and be considered uncircumcised. The cup of the right hand of Jehovah will come around to you, and there will be disgrace upon your glory;
2.17: because the violence I [ done] to Leb'a·non is what will cover you, and the rapacity upon I [ the] beasts that terrifies them, because of the shedding of blood of mankind and the violence I [ done] to I [ the] earth, the town and all those dwelling in it.
2.18: Of what benefit has a carved image been, when the former of it has carved it, a molten statue, and an instructor in falsehood? when the former of its form has trusted in it, to the extent of making valueless gods that are speechless?
2.19: " 'Woe to the one saying to the piece of wood: " O do awake! " to a dumb stone: " O wake up! It itself will give instruction "! Look! It is sheathed in gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in the midst of it.
2.20: But Jehovah is in his holy temple. Keep silence before him, all the earth! ' "

3.1: The prayer of Ha·bak'kuk the prophet in dirges:
3.2: O Jehovah, I have heard the report about you. I have become afraid, O Jehovah, of your activity. In the midst of I [ the] years O bring it to life! In the midst of I [ the] years may you make it known. During the agitation, to show mercy may you remember.

3.4: As for I [ his] brightness, it got to be just like the light. He had two rays I [ issuing] out of his hand, and there the hiding of his strength was.
3.5: Before him pestilence kept going, and burning fever would go forth at his feet.
