7.6: So Jesus started off with them. But when he was not far from the house, the army officer had already sent friends to say to him: " Sir, do not bother, for I am not fit to have you come in under my roof.
7.7: For that reason I did not consider myself worthy to come to you. But say the word, and let my servant be healed.
7.8: For I too am a man placed under authority, having soldiers under me, and I say to this one, 'Be on your way! ' and he is on his way, and to another, 'Come! ' and he comes, and to my slave, 'Do this! ' and he does it. "
7.9: Well, when Jesus heard these things he marveled at him, and he turned to the crowd following him and said: " I tell YOU, Not even in Israel have I found so great a faith. "
7.10: And those that had been sent, on getting back to the house, found the slave in good health.
7.11: Closely following this he traveled to a city called Na'in, and his disciples and a great crowd were traveling with him.
7.12: As he got near the gate of the city, why, look! there was a dead man being carried out, the only - begotten son of his mother. Besides, she was a widow. A considerable crowd from the city was also with her.
7.13: And when the Lord caught sight of her, he was moved with pity for her, and he said to her: " Stop weeping. "
7.14: With that he approached and touched the bier, and the bearers stood still, and he said: " Young man, I say to you, Get up! "
7.15: And the dead man sat up and started to speak, and he gave him to his mother.
7.16: Now fear seized them all, and they began to glorify God, saying: " A great prophet has been raised up among us, " and, " God has turned his attention to his people. "
7.17: And this news concerning him spread out into all Ju·de'a and all the surrounding country.
7.18: Now John's disciples reported to him about all these things.
7.19: So John summoned a certain two of his disciples and sent them to the Lord to say: " Are you the Coming One or are we to expect a different one? "
7.20: When they came up to him the men said: " John the Baptist dispatched us to you to say, 'Are you the Coming One or are we to expect another? ' "
7.21: In that hour he cured many of sicknesses and grievous diseases and wicked spirits, and granted many blind persons the favor of seeing.
7.22: Hence in answer he said to the I [ two]: " Go YOUR way, report to John what YOU saw and heard: the blind are receiving sight, the lame are walking, the lepers are being cleansed and the deaf are hearing, the dead are being raised up, the poor are being told the good news.
7.23: And happy is he who has not stumbled over me. "
7.24: When the messengers of John had gone away, he started to say to the crowds concerning John: " What did YOU go out into the wilderness to behold? A reed being tossed by the wind?
7.25: What, then, did YOU go out to see? A man dressed in soft outer garments? Why, those in splendid dress and existing in luxury are in royal houses.
7.26: Really, then, what did YOU go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell YOU, and far more than a prophet.
7.27: This is he concerning whom it is written, 'Look! I am sending forth my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way ahead of you. '
7.28: I tell YOU, Among those born of women there is none greater than John; but a person that is a lesser one in the kingdom of God is greater than he is. "
7.29: ( And all the people and the tax collectors, when they heard I [ this], declared God to be righteous, they having been baptized with the baptism of John.
7.30: But the Pharisees and those versed in the Law disregarded the counsel of God to them, they not having been baptized by him. )
7.31: " With whom, therefore, shall I compare the men of this generation, and whom are they like?
7.32: They are like young children sitting in a marketplace and crying out to one another, and who say, 'We played the flute for YOU, but YOU did not dance; we wailed, but YOU did not weep. '
7.33: Correspondingly, John the Baptist has come neither eating bread nor drinking wine, but YOU say, 'He has a demon. '
7.34: The Son of man has come eating and drinking, but YOU say, 'Look! A man gluttonous and given to drinking wine, a friend of tax collectors and sinners! '
7.35: All the same, wisdom is proved righteous by all its children. "
7.36: Now a certain one of the Pharisees kept asking him to dine with him. Accordingly he entered into the house of the Pharisee and reclined at the table.
7.37: And, look! a woman who was known in the city to be a sinner learned that he was reclining at a meal in the house of the Pharisee, and she brought an alabaster case of perfumed oil,
7.38: and, taking a position behind at his feet, she wept and started to wet his feet with her tears and she would wipe them off with the hair of her head. Also, she tenderly kissed his feet and greased them with the perfumed oil.
7.39: At the sight the Pharisee that invited him said within himself: " This man, if he were a prophet, would know who and what kind of woman it is that is touching him, that she is a sinner. "
7.40: But in reply Jesus said to him: " Simon, I have something to say to you. " He said: " Teacher, say it! "
7.41: " Two men were debtors to a certain lender; the one was in debt for five hundred de·nar'i·i, but the other for fifty.
7.42: When they did not have anything with which to pay back, he freely forgave them both. Therefore, which of them will love him the more? "
7.43: In answer Simon said: " I suppose it is the one to whom he freely forgave the more. " He said to him: " You judged correctly. "
7.44: With that he turned to the woman and said to Simon: " Do you behold this woman? I entered into your house; you gave me no water for my feet. But this woman wet my feet with her tears and wiped them off with her hair.
7.45: You gave me no kiss; but this woman, from the hour that I came in, did not leave off tenderly kissing my feet.
7.46: You did not grease my head with oil; but this woman greased my feet with perfumed oil.
7.47: By virtue of this, I tell you, her sins, many though they are, are forgiven, because she loved much; but he who is forgiven little, loves little. "
7.48: Then he said to her: " Your sins are forgiven. "
7.49: At this those reclining at the table with him started to say within themselves: " Who is this man who even forgives sins? "
7.50: But he said to the woman: " Your faith has saved you; go your way in peace. "

8.1: Shortly afterwards he went journeying from city to city and from village to village, preaching and declaring the good news of the kingdom of God. And the twelve were with him,
8.2: and certain women that had been cured of wicked spirits and sicknesses, Mary the so - called Mag'da·lene, from whom seven demons had come out,
8.3: and Jo·an'na the wife of Chu'za, Herod's man in charge, and Su·san'na and many other women, who were ministering to them from their belongings.
8.4: Now when a great crowd had collected together with those that went to him from city after city, he spoke by means of an illustration:
8.5: " A sower went out to sow his seed. Well, as he was sowing, some of it fell alongside the road and was trampled down, and the birds of heaven ate it up.
8.6: Some other landed upon the rock - mass, and, after sprouting, it dried up because of not having moisture.
8.7: Some other fell among the thorns, and the thorns that grew up with it choked it off.
8.8: Some other fell upon the good soil, and, after sprouting, it produced fruit a hundredfold. " As he told these things, he proceeded to call out: " Let him that has ears to listen, listen. "
8.9: But his disciples began to ask him what this illustration might mean.
8.10: He said: " To YOU it is granted to understand the sacred secrets of the kingdom of God, but for the rest it is in illustrations, in order that, though looking, they may look in vain and, though hearing, they may not get the meaning.
8.11: Now the illustration means this: The seed is the word of God.
8.12: Those alongside the road are the ones that have heard, then the Devil comes and takes the word away from their hearts in order that they may not believe and be saved.
8.13: Those upon the rock - mass are the ones who, when they hear it, receive the word with joy, but these have no root; they believe for a season, but in a season of testing they fall away.
8.14: As for that which fell among the thorns, these are the ones that have heard, but, by being carried away by anxieties and riches and pleasures of this life, they are completely choked and bring nothing to perfection.
8.15: As for that on the fine soil, these are the ones that, after hearing the word with a fine and good heart, retain it and bear fruit with endurance.
8.16: " No one, after lighting a lamp, covers it with a vessel or puts it underneath a bed, but he puts it on a lampstand, that those stepping in may behold the light.
8.17: For there is nothing hidden that will not become manifest, neither anything carefully concealed that will never become known and never come into the open.
8.18: Therefore, pay attention to how YOU listen; for whoever has, more will be given him, but whoever does not have, even what he imagines he has will be taken away from him. "
8.19: Now his mother and brothers came toward him, but they were unable to get to him because of the crowd.
8.20: However, it was reported to him: " Your mother and your brothers are standing outside wanting to see you. "
8.21: In reply he said to them: " My mother and my brothers are these who hear the word of God and do it. "
8.22: In the course of one of the days he and his disciples got into a boat, and he said to them: " Let us cross to the other side of the lake. " So they set sail.
8.23: But as they were sailing he fell asleep. Now a violent windstorm descended upon the lake, and they began to fill up with I [ water] and to be in danger.
8.24: Finally they went to him and roused him, saying: " Instructor, Instructor, we are about to perish! " Rousing himself, he rebuked the wind and the raging of the water, and they subsided, and a calm set in.
8.25: Then he said to them: " Where is YOUR faith? " But struck with fear, they marveled, saying to one another: " Who really is this, for he orders even the winds and the water, and they obey him? "
8.26: And they put in to shore in the country of the Ger'a·senes, which is on the side opposite Gal'i·lee.
8.27: But as he got out onto land a certain man from the city who had demons met him. And for a considerable time he had not worn clothing, and he was staying, not at home, but among the tombs.
8.28: At the sight of Jesus he cried aloud and fell down before him, and with a loud voice he said: " What have I to do with you, Jesus Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me. "
8.29: ( For he had been ordering the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For over a long time it had held him fast, and he was repeatedly bound with chains and fetters under guard, but he would burst the bonds and be driven by the demon into the lonely places. )
8.30: Jesus asked him: " What is your name? " He said: " Legion, " because many demons had entered into him.
8.31: And they kept entreating him not to order them to go away into the abyss.
8.32: Now a herd of a considerable number of swine was feeding there on the mountain; so they entreated him to permit them to enter into those. And he gave them permission.
8.33: Then the demons went out of the man and entered into the swine, and the herd rushed over the precipice into the lake and drowned.
8.34: But when the herders saw what had happened, they fled and reported it to the city and to the countryside.
8.35: Then people turned out to see what had happened, and they came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons came out, clothed and in his sound mind, sitting at the feet of Jesus; and they became fearful.
8.36: Those who had seen it reported to them how the demon - possessed man had been made well.
8.37: So all the multitude from the surrounding country of the Ger'a·senes asked him to get away from them, because they were in the grip of great fear. Then he went aboard the boat and turned away.
8.38: However, the man from whom the demons had gone out kept begging to continue with him; but he dismissed the man, saying:
8.39: " Be on your way back home, and keep on relating what things God did for you. " Accordingly he went away, proclaiming throughout the whole city what things Jesus did for him.
8.40: When Jesus got back, the crowd received him kindly, for they were all expecting him.
8.41: But, look! a man named Ja'i·rus came, and this man was a presiding officer of the synagogue. And he fell at the feet of Jesus and began to entreat him to enter into his house,
8.42: because he had an only - begotten daughter about twelve years old and she was dying. As he was going the crowds thronged him.
8.43: And a woman, subject to a flow of blood for twelve years, who had not been able to get a cure from anyone,
8.44: approached from behind and touched the fringe of his outer garment, and instantly her flow of blood stopped.
8.45: So Jesus said: " Who was it that touched me? " When they were all denying it, Peter said: " Instructor, the crowds are hemming you in and closely pressing you. "
8.46: Yet Jesus said: " Someone touched me, for I perceived that power went out of me. "
8.47: Seeing that she had not escaped notice, the woman came trembling and fell down before him and disclosed before all the people the cause for which she touched him and how she was healed instantly.
8.48: But he said to her: " Daughter, your faith has made you well; go your way in peace. "
8.49: While he was yet speaking, a certain representative of the presiding officer of the synagogue came, saying: " Your daughter has died; do not bother the teacher any longer. "
8.50: On hearing this, Jesus answered him: " Have no fear, only put forth faith, and she will be saved. "
8.51: When he reached the house he did not let anyone go in with him except Peter and John and James and the girl's father and mother.
8.52: But people were all weeping and beating themselves in grief for her. So he said: " STOP weeping, for she did not die but is sleeping. "
8.53: At this they began to laugh at him scornfully, because they knew she had died.
8.54: But he took her by the hand and called, saying: " Girl, get up! "
8.55: And her spirit returned, and she rose instantly, and he ordered something to be given her to eat.
8.56: Well, her parents were beside themselves; but he instructed them to tell no one what had happened.

9.1: Then he called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all the demons and to cure sicknesses.
9.2: And so he sent them forth to preach the kingdom of God and to heal,
9.3: and he said to them: " Carry nothing for the trip, neither staff nor food pouch, nor bread nor silver money; neither have two undergarments.
9.4: But wherever YOU enter into a home, stay there and leave from there.
9.5: And wherever people do not receive YOU, on going out of that city shake the dust off YOUR feet for a witness against them. "
9.6: Then starting out they went through the territory from village to village, declaring the good news and performing cures everywhere.
9.7: Now Herod the district ruler heard of all the things happening, and he was in great perplexity because of its being said by some that John had been raised up from the dead,
9.8: but by others that E·li'jah had appeared, but by still others that a certain one of the ancient prophets had risen.
9.9: Herod said: " John I beheaded. Who, then, is this about whom I am hearing such things? " So he was seeking to see him.
9.10: And when the apostles returned they recounted to him what things they had done. With that he took them along and withdrew to privacy into a city called Beth·sa'i·da.
9.11: But the crowds, getting to know it, followed him. And he received them kindly and began to speak to them about the kingdom of God, and he healed those needing a cure.
9.12: Then the day started to decline. The twelve now came up and said to him: " Dismiss the crowd, that they may go into the villages and countryside round about and procure lodging and find provisions, because out here we are in a lonely place. "
9.13: But he said to them: " YOU give them something to eat. " They said: " We have nothing more than five loaves and two fishes, unless perhaps we ourselves go and buy foodstuffs for all these people. "
9.14: They were, in fact, about five thousand men. But he said to his disciples: " Have them recline as at meals, in groups of about fifty each. "
9.15: And they did so and had them all recline.
9.16: Then taking the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, blessed them and broke them up and began to give them to the disciples to set before the crowd.
9.17: So they all ate and were satisfied, and the surplus that they had was taken up, twelve baskets of fragments.
9.18: Later, while he was praying alone, the disciples came together to him, and he questioned them, saying: " Who are the crowds saying that I am? "
9.19: In reply they said: " John the Baptist; but others, E·li'jah, and still others, that one of the ancient prophets has risen. "
9.20: Then he said to them: " YOU, though, who do YOU say I am? " Peter said in reply: " The Christ of God. "
9.21: Then in a stern talk to them he instructed them not to be telling this to anybody,
9.22: but said: " The Son of man must undergo many sufferings and be rejected by the older men and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and on the third day be raised up. "
9.23: Then he went on to say to all: " If anyone wants to come after me, let him disown himself and pick up his torture stake day after day and follow me continually.
9.24: For whoever wants to save his soul will lose it; but whoever loses his soul for my sake is the one that will save it.
9.25: Really, what does a man benefit himself if he gains the whole world but loses his own self or suffers damage?
9.26: For whoever becomes ashamed of me and of my words, the Son of man will be ashamed of this one when he arrives in his glory and that of the Father and of the holy angels.
9.27: But I tell YOU truthfully, There are some of those standing here that will not taste death at all until first they see the kingdom of God. "
9.28: In actual fact, about eight days after these words, he took Peter and John and James along and climbed up into the mountain to pray.
9.29: And as he was praying the appearance of his face became different and his apparel became glitteringly white.
9.30: Also, look! two men were conversing with him, who were Moses and E·li'jah.
9.31: These appeared with glory and began talking about his departure that he was destined to fulfill at Jerusalem.
9.32: Now Peter and those with him were weighed down with sleep; but when they got fully awake they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.
9.33: And as these were being separated from him, Peter said to Jesus: " Instructor, it is fine for us to be here, so let us erect three tents, one for you and one for Moses and one for E·li'jah, " he not realizing what he was saying.
9.34: But as he was saying these things a cloud formed and began to overshadow them. As they entered into the cloud, they became fearful.
9.35: And a voice came out of the cloud, saying: " This is my Son, the one that has been chosen. Listen to him. "
9.36: And as the voice occurred Jesus was found alone. But they kept quiet and did not report to anyone in those days any of the things they saw.
9.37: On the succeeding day, when they got down from the mountain, a great crowd met him.
9.38: And, look! a man cried out from the crowd, saying: " Teacher, I beg you to take a look at my son, because he is my only - begotten,
9.39: and, look! a spirit takes him, and suddenly he cries out, and it throws him into convulsions with foam, and it scarcely withdraws from him after bruising him.
9.40: And I begged your disciples to expel it, but they could not. "
9.41: In response Jesus said: " O faithless and twisted generation, how long must I continue with YOU and put up with YOU? Lead your son over here. "
9.42: But even as he was approaching, the demon dashed him to the ground and violently convulsed him. However, Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit and healed the boy and delivered him to his father.
9.43: Well, they all began to be astounded at the majestic power of God. Now as they were all marveling at all the things he was doing, he said to his disciples:
9.44: " Give lodgment to these words in YOUR ears, for the Son of man is destined to be delivered into the hands of men. "
9.45: But they continued without understanding of this saying. In fact, it was concealed from them that they might not see through it, and they were afraid to question him about this saying.
9.46: Then a reasoning entered among them as to who would be the greatest of them.
9.47: Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their hearts, took a young child, set it beside him
9.48: and said to them: " Whoever receives this young child on the basis of my name receives me I [ too], and whoever receives me receives him I [ also] that sent me forth. For he that conducts himself as a lesser one among all of YOU is the one that is great. "
9.49: In response John said: " Instructor, we saw a certain man expelling demons by the use of your name and we tried to prevent him, because he is not following with us. "
9.50: But Jesus said to him: " Do not YOU men try to prevent I [ him], for he that is not against YOU is for YOU. "
9.51: As the days were now coming to the full for him to be taken up, he firmly set his face to go to Jerusalem.
9.52: So he sent forth messengers in advance of him. And they went their way and entered into a village of Sa·mar'i·tans, to make preparation for him;
9.53: but they did not receive him, because his face was set for going to Jerusalem.
9.54: When the disciples James and John saw this they said: " Lord, do you want us to tell fire to come down from heaven and annihilate them? "
9.55: But he turned and rebuked them.
9.56: So they went to a different village.
9.57: Now as they were going on the road, someone said to him: " I will follow you to wherever you may depart. "
9.58: And Jesus said to him: " Foxes have dens and birds of heaven have roosts, but the Son of man has nowhere to lay down his head. "
9.59: Then he said to another: " Be my follower. " The man said: " Permit me first to leave and bury my father. "
9.60: But he said to him: " Let the dead bury their dead, but you go away and declare abroad the kingdom of God. "
9.61: And still another said: " I will follow you, Lord; but first permit me to say good - bye to those in my household. "
9.62: Jesus said to him: " No man that has put his hand to a plow and looks at the things behind is well fitted for the kingdom of God. "

10.1: After these things the Lord designated seventy others and sent them forth by twos in advance of him into every city and place to which he himself was going to come.
10.2: Then he began to say to them: " The harvest, indeed, is great, but the workers are few. Therefore beg the Master of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.
10.3: Go forth. Look! I am sending YOU forth as lambs in among wolves.
10.4: Do not carry a purse, nor a food pouch, nor sandals, and do not embrace anybody in greeting along the road.
10.5: Wherever YOU enter into a house say first, 'May this house have peace. '
10.6: And if a friend of peace is there, YOUR peace will rest upon him. But if there is not, it will turn back to YOU.
10.7: So stay in that house, eating and drinking the things they provide, for the worker is worthy of his wages. Do not be transferring from house to house.
10.8: " Also, wherever YOU enter into a city and they receive YOU, eat the things set before YOU,
10.9: and cure the sick ones in it, and go on telling them, 'The kingdom of God has come near to YOU. '
10.10: But wherever YOU enter into a city and they do not receive YOU, go out into its broad ways and say,
10.11: 'Even the dust that got stuck to our feet from YOUR city we wipe off against YOU. Nevertheless, keep this in mind, that the kingdom of God has come near. '
10.12: I tell YOU that it will be more endurable for Sod'om in that day than for that city.
10.13: " Woe to you, Cho·ra'zin! Woe to you, Beth·sa'i·da! because if the powerful works that have taken place in YOU had taken place in Tyre and Si'don, they would long ago have repented sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
10.14: Consequently it will be more endurable for Tyre and Si'don in the judgment than for YOU.
10.15: And you, Ca·per'na·um, will you perhaps be exalted to heaven? Down to Ha'des you will come!
10.16: " He that listens to YOU listens to me I [ too]. And he that disregards YOU disregards me I [ too]. Moreover, he that disregards me disregards I [ also] him that sent me forth. "
10.17: Then the seventy returned with joy, saying: " Lord, even the demons are made subject to us by the use of your name. "
10.18: At that he said to them: " I began to behold Satan already fallen like lightning from heaven.
10.19: Look! I have given YOU the authority to trample underfoot serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will by any means do YOU hurt.
10.20: Nevertheless, do not rejoice over this, that the spirits are made subject to YOU, but rejoice because YOUR names have been inscribed in the heavens. "
10.21: In that very hour he became overjoyed in the holy spirit and said: " I publicly praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have carefully hidden these things from wise and intellectual ones, and have revealed them to babes. Yes, O Father, because to do thus came to be the way approved by you.
10.22: All things have been delivered to me by my Father, and who the Son is no one knows but the Father; and who the Father is, no one I [ knows] but the Son, and he to whom the Son is willing to reveal him. "
10.23: With that he turned to the disciples by themselves and said: " Happy are the eyes that behold the things YOU are beholding.
10.24: For I say to YOU, Many prophets and kings desired to see the things YOU are beholding but did not see them, and to hear the things YOU are hearing but did not hear them. "
10.25: Now, look! a certain man versed in the Law rose up, to test him out, and said: " Teacher, by doing what shall I inherit everlasting life? "
10.26: He said to him: " What is written in the Law? How do you read? "
10.27: In answer he said: " 'You must love Jehovah your God with your whole heart and with your whole soul and with your whole strength and with your whole mind, ' and, 'your neighbor as yourself. ' "
10.28: He said to him: " You answered correctly; 'keep on doing this and you will get life. ' "
10.29: But, wanting to prove himself righteous, the man said to Jesus: " Who really is my neighbor? "
10.30: In reply Jesus said: " A certain man was going down from Jerusalem to Jer'i·cho and fell among robbers, who both stripped him and inflicted blows, and went off, leaving him half - dead.
10.31: Now, by coincidence, a certain priest was going down over that road, but, when he saw him, he went by on the opposite side.
10.32: Likewise, a Levite also, when he got down to the place and saw him, went by on the opposite side.
10.33: But a certain Sa·mar'i·tan traveling the road came upon him and, at seeing him, he was moved with pity.
10.34: So he approached him and bound up his wounds, pouring oil and wine upon them. Then he mounted him upon his own beast and brought him to an inn and took care of him.
10.35: And the next day he took out two de·nar'i·i, gave them to the innkeeper, and said, 'Take care of him, and whatever you spend besides this, I will repay you when I come back here. '
10.36: Who of these three seems to you to have made himself neighbor to the man that fell among the robbers? "
10.37: He said: " The one that acted mercifully toward him. " Jesus then said to him: " Go your way and be doing the same yourself. "
10.38: Now as they were going their way he entered into a certain village. Here a certain woman named Martha received him as guest into the house.
10.39: This woman also had a sister called Mary, who, however, sat down at the feet of the Lord and kept listening to his word.
10.40: Martha, on the other hand, was distracted with attending to many duties. So, she came near and said: " Lord, does it not matter to you that my sister has left me alone to attend to things? Tell her, therefore, to join in helping me. "
10.41: In answer the Lord said to her: " Martha, Martha, you are anxious and disturbed about many things.
10.42: A few things, though, are needed, or just one. For her part, Mary chose the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her. "

11.1: Now on the occasion of his being in a certain place praying, when he stopped, a certain one of his disciples said to him: " Lord, teach us how to pray, just as John also taught his disciples. "
11.2: Then he said to them: " Whenever YOU pray, say, 'Father, let your name be sanctified. Let your kingdom come.
11.3: Give us our bread for the day according to the day's requirement.
11.4: And forgive us our sins, for we ourselves also forgive everyone that is in debt to us; and do not bring us into temptation. ' "
11.5: Further, he said to them: " Who of YOU will have a friend and will go to him at midnight and say to him, 'Friend, loan me three loaves,
11.6: because a friend of mine has just come to me on a journey and I have nothing to set before him'?
11.7: And that one from inside says in reply, 'Quit making me trouble. The door is already locked, and my young children are with me in bed; I cannot rise up and give you anything. '
11.8: I tell YOU, Although he will not rise up and give him anything because of being his friend, certainly because of his bold persistence he will get up and give him what things he needs.
11.9: Accordingly I say to YOU, Keep on asking, and it will be given YOU; keep on seeking, and YOU will find; keep on knocking, and it will be opened to YOU.
11.10: For everyone asking receives, and everyone seeking finds, and to everyone knocking it will be opened.
11.11: Indeed, which father is there among YOU who, if his son asks for a fish, will perhaps hand him a serpent instead of a fish?
11.12: Or if he also asks for an egg, will hand him a scorpion?
11.13: Therefore, if YOU, although being wicked, know how to give good gifts to YOUR children, how much more so will the Father in heaven give holy spirit to those asking him! "
11.14: Later he was expelling a dumb demon. After the demon came out, the dumb man spoke. And the crowds marveled.
11.15: But certain ones of them said: " He expels the demons by means of Be·el'ze·bub the ruler of the demons. "
11.16: However, others, to tempt him, began seeking a sign out of heaven from him.
11.17: Knowing their imaginations he said to them: " Every kingdom divided against itself comes to desolation, and a house I [ divided] against itself falls.
11.18: So if Satan is also divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? Because YOU say I expel the demons by means of Be·el'ze·bub.
11.19: If it is by means of Be·el'ze·bub I expel the demons, by whom do YOUR sons expel them? Because of this they will be judges of YOU.
11.20: But if it is by means of God's finger I expel the demons, the kingdom of God has really overtaken YOU.
11.21: When a strong man, well armed, guards his palace, his belongings continue in peace.
11.22: But when someone stronger than he is comes against him and conquers him, he takes away his full armament in which he was trusting, and he divides out the things he despoiled him of.
11.23: He that is not on my side is against me, and he that does not gather with me scatters.
11.24: " When an unclean spirit comes out of a man, it passes through parched places in search of a resting - place, and, after finding none, it says, 'I will return to my house out of which I moved. '
11.25: And on arriving it finds it swept clean and adorned.
11.26: Then it goes its way and takes along seven different spirits more wicked than itself, and, after getting inside, they dwell there; and the final circumstances of that man become worse than the first. "
11.27: Now as he was saying these things a certain woman out of the crowd raised her voice and said to him: " Happy is the womb that carried you and the breasts that you sucked! "
11.28: But he said: " No, rather, Happy are those hearing the word of God and keeping it! "
11.29: When the crowds were massing together, he started to say: " This generation is a wicked generation; it looks for a sign. But no sign will be given it except the sign of Jo'nah.
11.30: For just as Jo'nah became a sign to the Nin'e·vites, in the same way will the Son of man be also to this generation.
11.31: The queen of the south will be raised up in the judgment with the men of this generation and will condemn them; because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Sol'o·mon, but, look! something more than Sol'o·mon is here.
11.32: The men of Nin'e·veh will rise in the judgment with this generation and will condemn it; because they repented at what Jo'nah preached; but, look! something more than Jo'nah is here.
11.33: After lighting a lamp, a person puts it, not in a vault nor under a measuring basket, but upon the lampstand, that those stepping in may behold the light.
11.34: The lamp of the body is your eye. When your eye is simple, your whole body is also bright; but when it is wicked, your body is also dark.
11.35: Be alert, therefore. Perhaps the light that is in you is darkness.
11.36: Therefore, if your whole body is bright with no part at all dark, it will all be as bright as when a lamp gives you light by its rays. "
11.37: When he had spoken this, a Pharisee requested him to dine with him. So he went in and reclined at the table.
11.38: However, the Pharisee was surprised at seeing that he did not first wash before the dinner.
11.39: But the Lord said to him: " Now YOU Pharisees, YOU cleanse the outside of the cup and dish, but the inside of YOU is full of plunder and wickedness.
11.40: Unreasonable persons! He that made the outside made also the inside, did he not?
11.41: Nevertheless, give as gifts of mercy the things that are inside, and, look! all I [ other] things are clean about YOU.
11.42: But woe to YOU Pharisees, because YOU give the tenth of the mint and the rue and of every I [ other] vegetable, but YOU pass by the justice and the love of God! These things YOU were under obligation to do, but those other things not to omit.
11.43: Woe to YOU Pharisees, because YOU love the front seats in the synagogues and the greetings in the marketplaces!
11.44: Woe to YOU, because YOU are as those memorial tombs which are not in evidence, so that men walk upon them and do not know I [ it]! "
11.45: In answer a certain one of those versed in the Law said to him: " Teacher, in saying these things you also insult us. "
11.46: Then he said: " Woe also to YOU who are versed in the Law, because YOU load men with loads hard to be borne, but YOU yourselves do not touch the loads with one of YOUR fingers!
11.47: " Woe to YOU, because YOU build the memorial tombs of the prophets, but YOUR forefathers killed them!
11.48: Certainly YOU are witnesses of the deeds of YOUR forefathers and yet YOU give consent to them, because these killed the prophets but YOU are building I [ their tombs].
11.49: On this account the wisdom of God also said, 'I will send forth to them prophets and apostles, and they will kill and persecute some of them,
11.50: so that the blood of all the prophets spilled from the founding of the world may be required from this generation,
11.51: from the blood of Abel down to the blood of Zech·a·ri'ah, who was slain between the altar and the house. ' Yes, I tell YOU, it will be required from this generation.
11.52: " Woe to YOU who are versed in the Law, because YOU took away the key of knowledge; YOU yourselves did not go in, and those going in YOU hindered! "
11.53: So when he went out from there the scribes and the Pharisees started in to press upon him terribly and to ply him with questions about further things,
11.54: lying in wait for him, to catch something out of his mouth.

12.1: In the meantime, when the crowd had gathered together in so many thousands that they were stepping upon one another, he started out by saying first to his disciples: " Watch out for the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
12.2: But there is nothing carefully concealed that will not be revealed, and secret that will not become known.
12.3: Wherefore what things YOU say in the darkness will be heard in the light, and what YOU whisper in private rooms will be preached from the housetops.
12.4: Moreover, I say to YOU, my friends, Do not fear those who kill the body and after this are not able to do anything more.
12.5: But I will indicate to YOU whom to fear: Fear him who after killing has authority to throw into Ge·hen'na. Yes, I tell YOU, fear this One.
12.6: Five sparrows sell for two coins of small value, do they not? Yet not one of them goes forgotten before God.
12.7: But even the hairs of YOUR heads are all numbered. Have no fear; YOU are worth more than many sparrows.
12.8: " I say, then, to YOU, Everyone that confesses union with me before men, the Son of man will also confess union with him before the angels of God.
12.9: But he that disowns me before men will be disowned before the angels of God.
12.10: And everyone that says a word against the Son of man, it will be forgiven him; but he that blasphemes against the holy spirit will not be forgiven it.
12.11: But when they bring YOU in before public assemblies and government officials and authorities, do not become anxious about how or what YOU will speak in defense or what YOU will say;
12.12: for the holy spirit will teach YOU in that very hour the things YOU ought to say. "
12.13: Then a certain one of the crowd said to him: " Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me. "
12.14: He said to him: " Man, who appointed me judge or apportioner over YOU persons? "
12.15: Then he said to them: " Keep YOUR eyes open and guard against every sort of covetousness, because even when a person has an abundance his life does not result from the things he possesses. "
12.16: With that he spoke an illustration to them, saying: " The land of a certain rich man produced well.
12.17: Consequently he began reasoning within himself, saying, 'What shall I do, now that I have nowhere to gather my crops? '
12.18: So he said, 'I will do this: I will tear down my storehouses and build bigger ones, and there I will gather all my grain and all my good things;
12.19: and I will say to my soul: " Soul, you have many good things laid up for many years; take your ease, eat, drink, enjoy yourself. " '
12.20: But God said to him, 'Unreasonable one, this night they are demanding your soul from you. Who, then, is to have the things you stored up? '
12.21: So it goes with the man that lays up treasure for himself but is not rich toward God. "
12.22: Then he said to his disciples: " On this account I say to YOU, Quit being anxious about YOUR souls as to what YOU will eat or about YOUR bodies as to what YOU will wear.
12.23: For the soul is worth more than food and the body than clothing.
12.24: Mark well that the ravens neither sow seed nor reap, and they have neither barn nor storehouse, and yet God feeds them. Of how much more worth are YOU than birds?
12.25: Who of YOU by being anxious can add a cubit to his life span?
12.26: If, therefore, YOU cannot do the least thing, why be anxious about the remaining things?
12.27: Mark well how the lilies grow; they neither toil nor spin; but I tell YOU, Not even Sol'o·mon in all his glory was arrayed as one of these.
12.28: If, now, God thus clothes the vegetation in the field that today exists and tomorrow is cast into an oven, how much rather will he clothe YOU, YOU with little faith!
12.29: So quit seeking what YOU might eat and what YOU might drink, and quit being in anxious suspense;
12.30: for all these are the things the nations of the world are eagerly pursuing, but YOUR Father knows YOU need these things.
12.31: Nevertheless, seek continually his kingdom, and these things will be added to YOU.
12.32: " Have no fear, little flock, because YOUR Father has approved of giving YOU the kingdom.
12.33: Sell the things belonging to YOU and give gifts of mercy. Make purses for yourselves that do not wear out, a never - failing treasure in the heavens, where a thief does not get near nor moth consumes.
12.34: For where YOUR treasure is, there YOUR hearts will be also.
12.35: " Let YOUR loins be girded and YOUR lamps be burning,
12.36: and YOU yourselves be like men waiting for their master when he returns from the marriage, so that at his arriving and knocking they may at once open to him.
12.37: Happy are those slaves whom the master on arriving finds watching! Truly I say to YOU, He will gird himself and make them recline at the table and will come alongside and minister to them.
12.38: And if he arrives in the second watch, even if in the third, and finds them thus, happy are they!
12.39: But know this, that if the householder had known at what hour the thief would come, he would have kept watching and not have let his house be broken into.
12.40: YOU also, keep ready, because at an hour that YOU do not think likely the Son of man is coming. "
12.41: Then Peter said: " Lord, are you saying this illustration to us or also to all? "
12.42: And the Lord said: " Who really is the faithful steward, the discreet one, whom his master will appoint over his body of attendants to keep giving them their measure of food supplies at the proper time?
12.43: Happy is that slave, if his master on arriving finds him doing so!
12.44: I tell YOU truthfully, He will appoint him over all his belongings.
12.45: But if ever that slave should say in his heart, 'My master delays coming, ' and should start to beat the menservants and the maidservants, and to eat and drink and get drunk,
12.46: the master of that slave will come on a day that he is not expecting I [ him] and in an hour that he does not know, and he will punish him with the greatest severity and assign him a part with the unfaithful ones.
12.47: Then that slave that understood the will of his master but did not get ready or do in line with his will will be beaten with many strokes.
12.48: But the one that did not understand and so did things deserving of strokes will be beaten with few. Indeed, everyone to whom much was given, much will be demanded of him; and the one whom people put in charge of much, they will demand more than usual of him.
12.49: " I came to start a fire on the earth, and what more is there for me to wish if it has already been lighted?
12.50: Indeed, I have a baptism with which to be baptized, and how I am being distressed until it is finished!
12.51: Do YOU imagine I came to give peace on the earth? No, indeed, I tell YOU, but rather division.
12.52: For from now on there will be five in one house divided, three against two and two against three.
12.53: They will be divided, father against son and son against father, mother against daughter and daughter against I [ her] mother, mother - in - law against I [ her] daughter - in - law and daughter - in - law against I [ her] mother - in - law. "
12.54: Then he went on to say also to the crowds: " When YOU see a cloud rising in western parts, at once YOU say, 'A storm is coming, ' and it turns out so.
12.55: And when YOU see that a south wind is blowing, YOU say, 'There will be a heat wave, ' and it occurs.
12.56: Hypocrites, YOU know how to examine the outward appearance of earth and sky, but how is it YOU do not know how to examine this particular time?
12.57: Why do YOU not judge also for yourselves what is righteous?
12.58: For example, when you are going with your adversary at law to a ruler, get to work, while on the way, to rid yourself of the dispute with him, that he may never hale you before the judge, and the judge deliver you to the court officer, and the court officer throw you into prison.
12.59: I tell you, You will certainly not get out from there until you pay over the last small coin of very little value. "

13.1: At that very season there were certain ones present that reported to him about the Gal·i·le'ans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
13.2: So in reply he said to them: " Do YOU imagine that these Gal·i·le'ans were proved worse sinners than all other Gal·i·le'ans because they have suffered these things?
13.3: No, indeed, I tell YOU; but, unless YOU repent, YOU will all likewise be destroyed.
13.4: Or those eighteen upon whom the tower in Si·lo'am fell, thereby killing them, do YOU imagine that they were proved greater debtors than all other men inhabiting Jerusalem?
13.5: No, indeed, I tell YOU; but, unless YOU repent, YOU will all be destroyed in the same way. "
13.6: Then he went on to tell this illustration: " A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came looking for fruit on it, but found none.
13.7: Then he said to the vinedresser, 'Here it is three years that I have come looking for fruit on this fig tree, but have found none. Cut it down! Why really should it keep the ground useless? '
13.8: In reply he said to him, 'Master, let it alone also this year, until I dig around it and put on manure;
13.9: and if then it produces fruit in the future, I [ well and good]; but if not, you shall cut it down. ' "
13.10: Now he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath.
13.11: And, look! a woman with a spirit of weakness for eighteen years, and she was bent double and was unable to raise herself up at all.
13.12: When he saw her, Jesus addressed her and said to her: " Woman, you are released from your weakness. "
13.13: And he laid his hands on her; and instantly she straightened up, and began to glorify God.
13.14: But in response the presiding officer of the synagogue, indignant because Jesus did the cure on the sabbath, began to say to the crowd: " There are six days on which work ought to be done; on them, therefore, come and be cured, and not on the sabbath day. "
13.15: However, the Lord answered him and said: " Hypocrites, does not each one of YOU on the sabbath untie his bull or his ass from the stall and lead it away to give it drink?
13.16: Was it not due, then, for this woman who is a daughter of Abraham, and whom Satan held bound, look! eighteen years, to be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day? "
13.17: Well, when he said these things, all his opposers began to feel shame; but all the crowd began to rejoice at all the glorious things done by him.
13.18: Therefore he went on to say: " What is the kingdom of God like, and with what shall I compare it?
13.19: It is like a mustard grain that a man took and put in his garden, and it grew and became a tree, and the birds of heaven took up lodging in its branches. "
13.20: And again he said: " With what shall I compare the kingdom of God?
13.21: It is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three large measures of flour until the whole mass was fermented. "
13.22: And he journeyed through from city to city and from village to village, teaching and continuing on his journey to Jerusalem.
13.23: Now a certain man said to him: " Lord, are those who are being saved few? " He said to them:
13.24: " Exert yourselves vigorously to get in through the narrow door, because many, I tell YOU, will seek to get in but will not be able,
13.25: when once the householder has got up and locked the door, and YOU start to stand outside and to knock at the door, saying, 'Sir, open to us. ' But in answer he will say to YOU, 'I do not know where YOU are from. '
13.26: Then YOU will start saying, 'We ate and drank in front of you, and you taught in our broad ways. '
13.27: But he will speak and say to YOU, 'I do not know where YOU are from. Get away from me, all YOU workers of unrighteousness! '
13.28: There is where I [ YOUR] weeping and the gnashing of I [ YOUR] teeth will be, when YOU see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but yourselves thrown outside.
13.29: Furthermore, people will come from eastern parts and western, and from north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.
13.30: And, look! there are those last who will be first, and there are those first who will be last. "
13.31: In that very hour certain Pharisees came up, saying to him: " Get out and be on your way from here, because Herod wants to kill you. "
13.32: And he said to them: " Go and tell that fox, 'Look! I am casting out demons and accomplishing healing today and tomorrow, and the third day I shall be finished. '
13.33: Nevertheless, I must go on my way today and tomorrow and the following day, because it is not admissible for a prophet to be destroyed outside of Jerusalem.
13.34: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, the killer of the prophets and stoner of those sent forth to her - how often I wanted to gather your children together in the manner that a hen gathers her brood of chicks under her wings, but YOU people did not want I [ it]!
13.35: Look! YOUR house is abandoned to YOU. I tell YOU, YOU will by no means see me until YOU say, 'Blessed is he that comes in Jehovah's name. ' "

14.1: And on an occasion when he went into the house of a certain one of the rulers of the Pharisees on the sabbath to eat a meal, they were closely watching him.
14.2: And, look! there was before him a certain man who had dropsy.
14.3: So in response Jesus spoke to those versed in the Law and to the Pharisees, saying: " Is it lawful on the sabbath to cure or not? "
14.4: But they kept silent. With that he took hold of I [ the man], healed him and sent I [ him] away.
14.5: And he said to them: " Who of YOU, if his son or bull falls into a well, will not immediately pull him out on the sabbath day? "
14.6: And they were not able to answer back on these things.
14.7: He then went on to tell the invited men an illustration, as he marked how they were choosing the most prominent places for themselves, saying to them:
14.8: " When you are invited by someone to a marriage feast, do not lie down in the most prominent place. Perhaps someone more distinguished than you may at the time have been invited by him,
14.9: and he that invited you and him will come and say to you, 'Let this man have the place. ' And then you will start off with shame to occupy the lowest place.
14.10: But when you are invited, go and recline in the lowest place, that when the man that has invited you comes he will say to you, 'Friend, go on up higher. ' Then you will have honor in front of all your fellow guests.
14.11: For everyone that exalts himself will be humbled and he that humbles himself will be exalted. "
14.12: Next he proceeded to say also to the man that invited him: " When you spread a dinner or evening meal, do not call your friends or your brothers or your relatives or rich neighbors. Perhaps sometime they might also invite you in return and it would become a repayment to you.
14.13: But when you spread a feast, invite poor people, crippled, lame, blind;
14.14: and you will be happy, because they have nothing with which to repay you. For you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous ones. "
14.15: On hearing these things a certain one of the fellow guests said to him: " Happy is he who eats bread in the kingdom of God. "
14.16: I [ Jesus] said to him: " A certain man was spreading a grand evening meal, and he invited many.
14.17: And he sent his slave out at the hour of the evening meal to say to the invited ones, 'Come, because things are now ready. '
14.18: But they all in common started to beg off. The first said to him, 'I bought a field and need to go out and see it; I ask you, Have me excused. '
14.19: And another said, 'I bought five yoke of cattle and am going to examine them; I ask you, Have me excused. '
14.20: Still another said, 'I just married a wife and for this reason I cannot come. '
14.21: So the slave came up and reported these things to his master. Then the householder became wrathful and said to his slave, 'Go out quickly into the broad ways and the lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor and crippled and blind and lame. '
14.22: In time the slave said, 'Master, what you ordered has been done, and yet there is room. '
14.23: And the master said to the slave, 'Go out into the roads and the fenced - in places, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.
14.24: For I say to YOU people, None of those men that were invited shall have a taste of my evening meal. ' "
14.25: Now great crowds were traveling with him, and he turned and said to them:
14.26: " If anyone comes to me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, yes, and even his own soul, he cannot be my disciple.
14.27: Whoever is not carrying his torture stake and coming after me cannot be my disciple.
14.28: For example, who of YOU that wants to build a tower does not first sit down and calculate the expense, to see if he has enough to complete it?
14.29: Otherwise, he might lay its foundation but not be able to finish it, and all the onlookers might start to ridicule him,
14.30: saying, 'This man started to build but was not able to finish. '
14.31: Or what king, marching to meet another king in war, does not first sit down and take counsel whether he is able with ten thousand troops to cope with the one that comes against him with twenty thousand?
14.32: If, in fact, he cannot do so, then while that one is yet far away he sends out a body of ambassadors and sues for peace.
14.33: Thus, you may be sure, none of YOU that does not say good - bye to all his belongings can be my disciple.
14.34: " Salt, to be sure, is fine. But if even the salt loses its strength, with what will it be seasoned?
14.35: It is suitable neither for soil nor for manure. People throw it outside. Let him that has ears to listen, listen. "

15.1: Now all the tax collectors and the sinners kept drawing near to him to hear him.
15.2: Consequently both the Pharisees and the scribes kept muttering, saying: " This man welcomes sinners and eats with them. "
15.3: Then he spoke this illustration to them, saying:
15.4: " What man of YOU with a hundred sheep, on losing one of them, will not leave the ninety - nine behind in the wilderness and go for the lost one until he finds it?
15.5: And when he has found it he puts it upon his shoulders and rejoices.
15.6: And when he gets home he calls his friends and his neighbors together, saying to them, 'Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost. '
15.7: I tell YOU that thus there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner that repents than over ninety - nine righteous ones who have no need of repentance.
15.8: " Or what woman with ten drachma coins, if she loses one drachma coin, does not light a lamp and sweep her house and search carefully until she finds it?
15.9: And when she has found it she calls the women who are her friends and neighbors together, saying, 'Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma coin that I lost. '
15.10: Thus, I tell YOU, joy arises among the angels of God over one sinner that repents. "
15.11: Then he said: " A certain man had two sons.
15.12: And the younger of them said to his father, 'Father, give me the part of the property that falls to my share. ' Then he divided his means of living to them.
15.13: Later, after not many days, the younger son gathered all things together and traveled abroad into a distant country, and there squandered his property by living a debauched life.
15.14: When he had spent everything, a severe famine occurred throughout that country, and he started to be in need.
15.15: He even went and attached himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to herd swine.
15.16: And he used to desire to be filled with the carob pods which the swine were eating, and no one would give him I [ anything].
15.17: " When he came to his senses, he said, 'How many hired men of my father are abounding with bread, while I am perishing here from famine!
15.18: I will rise and journey to my father and say to him: " Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.
15.19: I am no longer worthy of being called your son. Make me as one of your hired men. " '
15.20: So he rose and went to his father. While he was yet a long way off, his father caught sight of him and was moved with pity, and he ran and fell upon his neck and tenderly kissed him.
15.21: Then the son said to him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you. I am no longer worthy of being called your son. Make me as one of your hired men. '
15.22: But the father said to his slaves, 'Quick! bring out a robe, the best one, and clothe him with it, and put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
15.23: And bring the fattened young bull, slaughter it and let us eat and enjoy ourselves,
15.24: because this my son was dead and came to life again; he was lost and was found. ' And they started to enjoy themselves.
15.25: " Now his older son was in the field; and as he came and got near the house he heard a music concert and dancing.
15.26: So he called one of the servants to him and inquired what these things meant.
15.27: He said to him, 'Your brother has come, and your father slaughtered the fattened young bull, because he got him back in good health. '
15.28: But he became wrathful and was unwilling to go in. Then his father came out and began to entreat him.
15.29: In reply he said to his father, 'Here it is so many years I have slaved for you and never once did I transgress your commandment, and yet to me you never once gave a kid for me to enjoy myself with my friends.
15.30: But as soon as this your son who ate up your means of living with harlots arrived, you slaughtered the fattened young bull for him. '
15.31: Then he said to him, 'Child, you have always been with me, and all the things that are mine are yours;
15.32: but we just had to enjoy ourselves and rejoice, because this your brother was dead and came to life, and he was lost and was found. ' "

16.1: Then he went on to say also to the disciples: " A certain man was rich and he had a steward, and this one was accused to him as handling his goods wastefully.
16.2: So he called him and said to him, 'What is this I hear about you? Hand in the account of your stewardship, for you can no longer manage the house. '
16.3: Then the steward said to himself, 'What am I to do, seeing that my master will take the stewardship away from me? I am not strong enough to dig, I am ashamed to beg.
16.4: Ah! I know what I shall do, so that, when I am put out of the stewardship, people will receive me into their homes. '
16.5: And calling to him each one of the debtors of his master he proceeded to say to the first, 'How much are you owing my master? '
16.6: He said, 'A hundred bath measures of olive oil. ' He said to him, 'Take your written agreement back and sit down and quickly write fifty. '
16.7: Next, he said to another one, 'Now you, how much are you owing? ' He said, 'A hundred cor measures of wheat. ' He said to him, 'Take your written agreement back and write eighty. '
16.8: And his master commended the steward, though unrighteous, because he acted with practical wisdom; for the sons of this system of things are wiser in a practical way toward their own generation than the sons of the light are.
16.9: " Also, I say to YOU, Make friends for yourselves by means of the unrighteous riches, so that, when such fail, they may receive YOU into the everlasting dwelling places.
16.10: The person faithful in what is least is faithful also in much, and the person unrighteous in what is least is unrighteous also in much.
16.11: Therefore, if YOU have not proved yourselves faithful in connection with the unrighteous riches, who will entrust YOU with what is true?
16.12: And if YOU have not proved yourselves faithful in connection with what is another's, who will give YOU what is for yourselves?
16.13: No house servant can be a slave to two masters; for, either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will stick to the one and despise the other. YOU cannot be slaves to God and to riches. "
16.14: Now the Pharisees, who were money lovers, were listening to all these things, and they began to sneer at him.
16.15: Consequently he said to them: " YOU are those who declare yourselves righteous before men, but God knows YOUR hearts; because what is lofty among men is a disgusting thing in God's sight.
16.16: " The Law and the Prophets were until John. From then on the kingdom of God is being declared as good news, and every sort of person is pressing forward toward it.
16.17: Indeed, it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for one particle of a letter of the Law to go unfulfilled.
16.18: " Everyone that divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery, and he that marries a woman divorced from a husband commits adultery.
16.19: " But a certain man was rich, and he used to deck himself with purple and linen, enjoying himself from day to day with magnificence.
16.20: But a certain beggar named Laz'a·rus used to be put at his gate, full of ulcers
16.21: and desiring to be filled with the things dropping from the table of the rich man. Yes, too, the dogs would come and lick his ulcers.
16.22: Now in course of time the beggar died and he was carried off by the angels to the bosom I [ position] of Abraham. " Also, the rich man died and was buried.
16.23: And in Ha'des he lifted up his eyes, he existing in torments, and he saw Abraham afar off and Laz'a·rus in the bosom I [ position] with him.
16.24: So he called and said, 'Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Laz'a·rus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am in anguish in this blazing fire. '
16.25: But Abraham said, 'Child, remember that you received in full your good things in your lifetime, but Laz'a·rus correspondingly the injurious things. Now, however, he is having comfort here but you are in anguish.
16.26: And besides all these things, a great chasm has been fixed between us and YOU people, so that those wanting to go over from here to YOU people cannot, neither may people cross over from there to us. '
16.27: Then he said, 'In that event I ask you, father, to send him to the house of my father,
16.28: for I have five brothers, in order that he may give them a thorough witness, that they also should not get into this place of torment. '
16.29: But Abraham said, 'They have Moses and the Prophets; let them listen to these. '
16.30: Then he said, 'No, indeed, father Abraham, but if someone from the dead goes to them they will repent. '
16.31: But he said to him, 'If they do not listen to Moses and the Prophets, neither will they be persuaded if someone rises from the dead. ' "

17.1: Then he said to his disciples: " It is unavoidable that causes for stumbling should come. Nevertheless, woe to the one through whom they come!
17.2: It would be of more advantage to him if a millstone were suspended from his neck and he were thrown into the sea than for him to stumble one of these little ones.
17.3: Pay attention to yourselves. If your brother commits a sin give him a rebuke, and if he repents forgive him.
17.4: Even if he sins seven times a day against you and he comes back to you seven times, saying, 'I repent, ' you must forgive him. "
17.5: Now the apostles said to the Lord: " Give us more faith. "
17.6: Then the Lord said: " If YOU had faith the size of a mustard grain, YOU would say to this black mulberry tree, 'Be uprooted and planted in the sea! ' and it would obey YOU.
17.7: " Who of YOU is there that has a slave plowing or minding the flock who will say to him when he gets in from the field, 'Come here at once and recline at the table'?
17.8: Rather, will he not say to him, 'Get something ready for me to have my evening meal, and put on an apron and minister to me until I am through eating and drinking, and afterward you can eat and drink'?
17.9: He will not feel gratitude to the slave because he did the things assigned, will he?
17.10: So YOU, also, when YOU have done all the things assigned to YOU, say, 'We are good - for - nothing slaves. What we have done is what we ought to have done. ' "
17.11: And while he was going to Jerusalem he was passing through the midst of Sa·mar'i·a and Gal'i·lee.
17.12: And as he was entering into a certain village ten leprous men met him, but they stood up afar off.
17.13: And they raised their voices and said: " Jesus, Instructor, have mercy on us! "
17.14: And when he got sight of them he said to them: " Go and show yourselves to the priests. " Then as they were going off their cleansing occurred.
17.15: One of them, when he saw he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice.
17.16: And he fell upon his face at I [ Jesus'] feet, thanking him; furthermore, he was a Sa·mar'i·tan.
17.17: In reply Jesus said: " The ten were cleansed, were they not? Where, then, are the other nine?
17.18: Were none found that turned back to give glory to God but this man of another nation? "
17.19: And he said to him: " Rise and be on your way; your faith has made you well. "
17.20: But on being asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God was coming, he answered them and said: " The kingdom of God is not coming with striking observableness,
17.21: neither will people be saying, 'See here! ' or, 'There! ' For, look! the kingdom of God is in YOUR midst. "
17.22: Then he said to the disciples: " Days will come when YOU will desire to see one of the days of the Son of man but YOU will not see I [ it].
17.23: And people will say to YOU, 'See there! ' or, 'See here! ' Do not go out or chase after I [ them].
17.24: For even as the lightning, by its flashing, shines from one part under heaven to another part under heaven, so the Son of man will be.
17.25: First, however, he must undergo many sufferings and be rejected by this generation.
17.26: Moreover, just as it occurred in the days of Noah, so it will be also in the days of the Son of man:
17.27: they were eating, they were drinking, men were marrying, women were being given in marriage, until that day when Noah entered into the ark, and the flood arrived and destroyed them all.
17.28: Likewise, just as it occurred in the days of Lot: they were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, they were building.
17.29: But on the day that Lot came out of Sod'om it rained fire and sulphur from heaven and destroyed them all.
17.30: The same way it will be on that day when the Son of man is to be revealed.
17.31: " On that day let the person that is on the housetop but whose movable things are in the house not come down to pick these up, and the person out in the field, let him likewise not return to the things behind.
17.33: Whoever seeks to keep his soul safe for himself will lose it, but whoever loses it will preserve it alive.
17.34: I tell YOU, In that night two I [ men] will be in one bed; the one will be taken along, but the other will be abandoned.
17.35: There will be two I [ women] grinding at the same mill; the one will be taken along, but the other will be abandoned. "
17.37: So in response they said to him: " Where, Lord? " He said to them: " Where the body is, there also the eagles will be gathered together. "

18.1: Then he went on to tell them an illustration with regard to the need for them always to pray and not to give up,
18.2: saying: " In a certain city there was a certain judge that had no fear of God and had no respect for man.
18.3: But there was a widow in that city and she kept going to him, saying, 'See that I get justice from my adversary at law. '
18.4: Well, for a while he was unwilling, but afterward he said to himself, 'Although I do not fear God or respect a man,
18.5: at any rate, because of this widow's continually making me trouble, I will see that she gets justice, so that she will not keep coming and pummeling me to a finish. ' "
18.6: Then the Lord said: " HEAR what the judge, although unrighteous, said!
18.7: Certainly, then, shall not God cause justice to be done for his chosen ones who cry out to him day and night, even though he is long - suffering toward them?
18.8: I tell YOU, He will cause justice to be done to them speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of man arrives, will he really find the faith on the earth? "
18.9: But he spoke this illustration also to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and who considered the rest as nothing:
18.10: " Two men went up into the temple to pray, the one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
18.11: The Pharisee stood and began to pray these things to himself, 'O God, I thank you I am not as the rest of men, extortioners, unrighteous, adulterers, or even as this tax collector.
18.12: I fast twice a week, I give the tenth of all things I acquire. '
18.13: But the tax collector standing at a distance was not willing even to raise his eyes heavenward, but kept beating his breast, saying, 'O God, be gracious to me a sinner. '
18.14: I tell YOU, This man went down to his home proved more righteous than that man; because everyone that exalts himself will be humiliated, but he that humbles himself will be exalted. "
18.15: Now people began to bring him also their infants for him to touch these; but on seeing it the disciples began to reprimand them.
18.16: However, Jesus called the I [ infants] to him, saying: " Let the young children come to me, and do not try to stop them. For the kingdom of God belongs to suchlike ones.
18.17: Truly I say to YOU, Whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a young child will by no means get into it. "
18.18: And a certain ruler questioned him, saying: " Good Teacher, by doing what shall I inherit everlasting life? "
18.19: Jesus said to him: " Why do you call me good? Nobody is good, except one, God.
18.20: You know the commandments, 'Do not commit adultery, Do not murder, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honor your father and mother. ' "
18.21: Then he said: " All these I have kept from youth on. "
18.22: After hearing that, Jesus said to him: " There is yet one thing lacking about you: Sell all the things you have and distribute to poor people, and you will have treasure in the heavens; and come be my follower. "
18.23: When he heard this, he became deeply grieved, for he was very rich.
18.24: Jesus looked at him and said: " How difficult a thing it will be for those having money to make their way into the kingdom of God!
18.25: It is easier, in fact, for a camel to get through the eye of a sewing needle than for a rich man to get into the kingdom of God. "
18.26: Those who heard this said: " Who possibly can be saved? "
18.27: He said: " The things impossible with men are possible with God. "
18.28: But Peter said: " Look! We have left our own things and followed you. "
18.29: He said to them: " Truly I say to YOU, There is no one who has left house or wife or brothers or parents or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
18.30: who will not in any way get many times more in this period of time, and in the coming system of things everlasting life. "
18.31: Then he took the twelve aside and said to them: " Look! We are going up to Jerusalem, and all the things written by means of the prophets as to the Son of man will be completed.
18.32: For instance, he will be delivered up to I [ men of] the nations and will be made fun of and be treated insolently and spit upon;
18.33: and after scourging him they will kill him, but on the third day he will rise. "
18.34: However, they did not get the meaning of any of these things; but this utterance was hidden from them, and they were not knowing the things said.
18.35: Now as he was getting near to Jer'i·cho a certain blind man was sitting beside the road begging.
18.36: Because he heard a crowd moving through he began to inquire what this might mean.
18.37: They reported to him: " Jesus the Naz·a·rene' is passing by! "
18.38: At that he cried out, saying: " Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me! "
18.39: And those going in advance began to tell him sternly to keep quiet, but that much more he kept shouting: " Son of David, have mercy on me. "
18.40: Then Jesus stood still and commanded the I [ man] to be led to him. After he got near, I [ Jesus] asked him:
18.41: " What do you want me to do for you? " He said: " Lord, let me recover sight. "
18.42: So Jesus said to him: " Recover your sight; your faith has made you well. "
18.43: And instantly he recovered sight, and he began to follow him, glorifying God. Also, all the people, at seeing I [ it], gave praise to God.

19.1: And he entered Jer'i·cho and was going through.
19.2: Now here there was a man called by the name Zac·chae'us; and he was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.
19.3: Well, he was seeking to see who this Jesus was, but he could not for the crowd, because he was small in size.
19.4: So he ran ahead to an advance position and climbed a fig - mulberry tree in order to see him, because he was about to go through that way.
19.5: Now when Jesus got to the place, he looked up and said to him: " Zac·chae'us, hurry and get down, for today I must stay in your house. "
19.6: With that he hurried and got down and with rejoicing he received him as guest.
19.7: But when they saw I [ it], they all fell to muttering, saying: " With a man that is a sinner he went in to lodge. "
19.8: But Zac·chae'us stood up and said to the Lord: " Look! The half of my belongings, Lord, I am giving to the poor, and whatever I extorted from anyone by false accusation I am restoring fourfold. "
19.9: At this Jesus said to him: " This day salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.
19.10: For the Son of man came to seek and to save what was lost. "
19.11: While they were listening to these things he spoke in addition an illustration, because he was near Jerusalem and they were imagining that the kingdom of God was going to display itself instantly.
19.12: Therefore he said: " A certain man of noble birth traveled to a distant land to secure kingly power for himself and to return.
19.13: Calling ten slaves of his he gave them ten mi'nas and told them, 'Do business till I come. '
19.14: But his citizens hated him and sent out a body of ambassadors after him, to say, 'We do not want this I [ man] to become king over us. '
19.15: " Eventually when he got back after having secured the kingly power, he commanded to be called to him these slaves to whom he had given the silver money, in order to ascertain what they had gained by business activity.
19.16: Then the first one presented himself, saying, 'Lord, your mi'na gained ten mi'nas. '
19.17: So he said to him, 'Well done, good slave! Because in a very small matter you have proved yourself faithful, hold authority over ten cities. '
19.18: Now the second came, saying, 'Your mi'na, Lord, made five mi'nas. '
19.19: He said to this one also, 'You, too, be in charge of five cities. '
19.20: But a different one came, saying, 'Lord, here is your mi'na, that I kept laid away in a cloth.
19.21: You see, I was in fear of you, because you are a harsh man; you take up what you did not deposit and you reap what you did not sow. '
19.22: He said to him, 'Out of your own mouth I judge you, wicked slave. You knew, did you, that I am a harsh man, taking up what I did not deposit and reaping what I did not sow?
19.23: Hence why is it you did not put my silver money in a bank? Then on my arrival I would have collected it with interest. '
19.24: " With that he said to those standing by, 'Take the mi'na from him and give it to him that has the ten mi'nas. '
19.25: But they said to him, 'Lord, he has ten mi'nas! ' -
19.26: 'I say to YOU, To everyone that has, more will be given; but from the one that does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
19.27: Moreover, these enemies of mine that did not want me to become king over them BRING here and slaughter them before me. ' "
19.28: So, after he had said these things, he began to go on ahead, going up to Jerusalem.
19.29: And when he got near to Beth'pha·ge and Beth'a·ny at the mountain called Mount of Olives, he sent forth two of the disciples,
19.30: saying: " Go into the village that is within sight of YOU, and in it after YOU pass in YOU will find a colt tied, on which none of mankind ever sat. Loose it and bring it.
19.31: But if anyone asks YOU, 'Why is it YOU are loosing it? ' YOU must speak in this way, 'The Lord needs it. ' "
19.32: So those who were sent forth departed and found it just as he said to them.
19.33: But as they were loosing the colt the owners of it said to them: " Why are YOU loosing the colt? "
19.34: They said: " The Lord needs it. "
19.35: And they led it to Jesus, and they threw their outer garments upon the colt and set Jesus upon I [ it].
19.36: As he moved along they kept spreading their outer garments on the road.
19.37: As soon as he got near the road down the Mount of Olives all the multitude of the disciples started to rejoice and praise God with a loud voice concerning all the powerful works they had seen,
19.38: saying: " Blessed is the One coming as the King in Jehovah's name! Peace in heaven, and glory in the highest places! "
19.39: However, some of the Pharisees from the crowd said to him: " Teacher, rebuke your disciples. "
19.40: But in reply he said: " I tell YOU, If these remained silent, the stones would cry out. "
19.41: And when he got nearby, he viewed the city and wept over it,
19.42: saying: " If you, even you, had discerned in this day the things having to do with peace - but now they have been hid from your eyes.
19.43: Because the days will come upon you when your enemies will build around you a fortification with pointed stakes and will encircle you and distress you from every side,
19.44: and they will dash you and your children within you to the ground, and they will not leave a stone upon a stone in you, because you did not discern the time of your being inspected. "
19.45: And he entered into the temple and started to throw out those who were selling,
19.46: saying to them: " It is written, 'And my house will be a house of prayer, ' but YOU made it a cave of robbers. "
19.47: Furthermore, he went teaching daily in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes and the principal ones of the people were seeking to destroy him;
19.48: and yet they did not find the effective thing for them to do, for the people one and all kept hanging onto him to hear him.

20.1: On one of the days while he was teaching the people in the temple and declaring the good news, the chief priests and the scribes with the older men came near,
20.2: and they spoke up, saying to him: " Tell us by what authority you do these things, or who it is that gave you this authority. "
20.3: In reply he said to them: " I will also ask YOU a question, and YOU tell me:
20.4: Was the baptism of John from heaven or from men? "
20.5: Then among themselves they drew conclusions, saying: " If we say, 'From heaven, ' he will say, 'Why is it YOU did not believe him? '
20.6: But if we say, 'From men, ' the people one and all will stone us, for they are persuaded that John was a prophet. "
20.7: So they replied that they did not know its source.
20.8: And Jesus said to them: " Neither am I telling YOU by what authority I do these things. "
